### 484. A `\bibitem` outside an open bibliography opens the kernel's bibliography, closed at its environment's end (Perl: the current `\thebibliography`, open to the end)

**Perl behavior**: `\lx@mung@bibliography` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4109-4122) closes an enclosing
`enumerate`/`itemize`/`description` and invokes `\thebibliography`, whatever it currently is; the bibliography stays open
until something closes it (the document's end, the next sectioning unit).
**Rust behavior** (sect11.rs `\lx@mung@bibliography`): it opens the kernel's own bibliography,
`\lx@kernel@thebibliography`: a class's list `\let` over `\thebibliography` no longer reopens per `\bibitem` (KPE #569).
In `{thebibliography}` (that class list), the class's `\endthebibliography` first ends its list, and the kernel's end is
the environment's; in another environment (a class's `{references}`, an author's `\begin{list}{}{}`), the environment's end
closes the bibliography first and then runs as its own (the class's `\endlist` ending its list frame), so text and floats
after `\end{references}` follow the bibliography, as pdflatex prints them, instead of landing in the last entry.
**Why**: content placement and the PushbackLimit loops (run 336: ajour, cjour, IEEE-Con-Sys-mag; 0711.2301,
astro-ph0005341, 2310.12571, astro-ph0002202, gr-qc0207046). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch64p::{class_lets_its_own_bibliography,
class_references_list_with_bibitems, class_references_list_followed_by_text, bibitem_in_an_environment_without_an_end_macro}`. Residuals (synthetic, RED repros): a class
end that prints text after its list prints it before the entries (`class_bibliography_end_prints_text`); a class
bibliography built on `{enumerate}` leaves a group open (`class_bibliography_as_enumerate`); a `{references}` inside an
`{itemize}` and an `\item[]` before the first `\bibitem` still misplace the list item and the bibliography; an
environment whose end is a constructor (`\end{multicols}`, `minipage`; `quote`/`center` close by autoclose) and a
bibliography opened inside a group nested in the environment (a command-form `\references … \endreferences` in `{small}`)
leave what follows in the last entry, as before. For an environment with no `\end<env>` (`{small}`) its end closes the bibliography, the saved
end being `\relax`.

### 486. ar5iv's archival `\today` is the paper's source date (Perl: `\relax` at begin-document)

**Perl behavior**: ar5iv.sty.ltxml:23-25 locks `\today` to `\relax` `AtBeginDocument`, so an archival conversion prints
no date where the paper printed `\today` (`\date{\today}` gives an empty `<date>`). A preamble or class reading of
`\today` still sees the conversion's day (KPE #575). `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` sets `\year`/`\month`/`\day`/`\time` on the
UTC clock (`gmtime`, TeX_Job.pool.ltxml:42-46), else the local clock.
**Rust behavior**: under the ar5iv preload the job's clock (`\year`, `\month`, `\day`, `\time`, hence LaTeX's and
babel's `\today`, `\pdfcreationdate` and the l3kernel's `\c_sys_*_int`) is the paper's own date: the newest recorded
modification time among the TeX source files of its bundle (`latexml::source_date`: `.tex .ltx .latex .sty .cls .clo
.def .cfg .fd .bbl .bib` and the main file; a zip entry's Info-ZIP UT timestamp, else its DOS time read as UTC; a tar
entry's mtime; a directory's or single file's filesystem mtimes; a time at the DOS epoch is no date), on the UTC clock,
set before the format loads (`latex.rs` runs `\__kernel_sys_everyjob:`, which copies the clock into `\c_sys_*_int`).
Only the bundle's date counts: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (exported by Nix shells and Debian builds, often as 315532800) never
dates an ar5iv `\today`; it seeds tex_job's registers only. The CLI and `cortex_worker` read the date from the input
(`Config::source_date_epoch`); stdin, `literal:` input, the library API and the LSP have none. With no date (stdin, an
editor buffer, the ~30% of arXiv zips that are single-file submissions with undated entries) the locked `\relax`
`\today` stays, bound at load time. The `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` clock moved from local time to UTC to match Perl's
`gmtime`, which shifts the manual sweeps' pinned 1767225600 by one date word (2025-12-31 → 2026-01-01 on a US-Eastern
host).
**Why**: user ruling 2026-10-10: `\today` prints what arXiv's PDF shows, and a class that parses `\today` gets a date —
ptapap.cls:322-325 splits the `\edef`'d `\today` with `\def\next#1#2#3#4\relax`, which on `\relax` ran away
("Paragraph ended before \next was complete", 95 papers of run 336, 1801.05985); 1811.05851's `\item[] \today` gives
"November 14, 2018". A/B: the 95 ptapap papers lose that error (203 → 108 errors, the rest is a separate
`\oldfnum@figure` cluster) with unchanged XML; of 60 random dated papers using `\today`, 48 change, every change a date
where `\today` was (43 `<date>` elements filled), none worse; 10 undated papers unchanged. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch64s::{ptapap_splits_the_source_date, title_block_today_is_the_source_date,
pdf_creation_date_keeps_the_source_clock, undated_source_keeps_the_empty_today}`, `source_date::tests`.
Deterministic per zip/tar bundle only: directory and single-file inputs read filesystem mtimes, which a checkout or copy
resets. A dated plain-TeX document now raises `Error:undefined:\today` (plain has no `\today`, as pdftex; before, ar5iv
defined it as `\relax`); a document defining its own `\today` now prints it. Residual (as Perl, the ruling covers
`\today` only): an undated bundle's `\time`, `\pdfcreationdate`, `\the\year` and `\c_sys_*_int` still read the
conversion's clock. Known limits of the date: an entry dated in the future wins (no clock is consulted); a directory
walk skips `.git`/`.svn`/`.hg`/`CVS`; a single-file input counts only that file, not what it `\input`s; a `.tar.gz` is
decompressed a second time for its dates. A non-numeric `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` falls back to the local clock (Perl's `gmtime("abc")` would give 1970-01-01; as
before this batch); `\pdfcreationdate` appends `Z` also when the registers hold the local clock (an undated bundle under
a non-UTC `TZ`; pdftex.rs).

### 488. IEEEproof's QED follows IEEEtran's own switch (Perl: the QED stack amsthm shares)

**Perl behavior**: `\IEEEproof` pushes `\qed` on `QED@stack`, `\endIEEEproof` pops and digests it, and `\IEEEQEDhere`

**Rust behavior**: IEEEtran.cls:5543-5556 — `\newif\if@IEEEQEDshow` true at class load, `\IEEEproof` sets it true
locally, `\endIEEEproof` typesets the document's `\IEEEQED` while it is true, `\IEEEQEDoff` = `\global\@IEEEQEDshowfalse`,
`\IEEEQEDhere` = `\IEEEQEDoff\IEEEQED`. An IEEEQED command in an amsthm proof leaves amsthm's ∎, amsthm's `\qedhere` in an
IEEEproof leaves IEEEproof's (2001.04812), a nested IEEEproof's `\IEEEQEDhere` suppresses the outer QED (the false is
global), a document's `\IEEEQED` or `\@IEEEQEDshowfalse` applies.
**Why**: faithful to IEEEtran (2201.01339, 2201.11150, 1410.7694); Perl's stack lost amsthm's QED.

**Perl behavior**: Stomach.pm:343-375 errors on a `}`/`\endgroup` that meets an environment's mode frame and keeps the
frame, so `{\thm …}`, `{\quote …}`, `\begingroup\rem …\endgroup` and `\begin{flushleft} … \endgroup` (valid LaTeX: a bare
`\X` opens no group, latex.ltx:15346-15355; `\begin`'s group is closed by any `\endgroup`) swallow the rest of the
document (KPE #583).
**Rust behavior**: stomach.rs `close_environment_frame` ends the environment first, in the shape of tex.web §1064
`off_save`: a bare `\X` frame back-inputs the closer and inserts `\endX`; a `\begin{X}` frame met by `\endgroup` runs
`\end{X}` in the `\endgroup`'s place. The diagnostic follows the kind of group the environment's begin code leaves open
(DefEnvironment `tex_group` = none | semi_simple | box, tex.web §269): none → Info; semi_simple → Error for `}` (§1069
`extra_right_brace`) and for `\endgroup` against a `\begin{X}` frame (`\begin`'s own group stays open), Info for a bare
`\X` met by `\endgroup` (§1063 unsave: `\endX` takes its place and the enclosing group stays open); box → Error for
`\endgroup` (§1064 `off_save`) and for `}` (§1068 packages the box early; TeX reports the mismatch later). The kind is a
frame value, cleared where raw end code closes `\@xfloat`'s box (`\lx@endfloatbox@close`). `}` against a `\begin{X}`
frame and math-mode frames keep their Errors. End code TeX never runs when a group ends an environment is skipped

`\lx@checkend` (latex.ltx `\@checkend`, which Perl's `\end` does not run; KPE #584), reporting "\begin{X} on input line N
ended by \end{Y}" when the frames and `\@currenvir` both disagree. The 71 environments whose begin code opens a group
are marked with their source lines (audit in `agent_reports/payload_64y_ab/envlist2.tsv`).
**Why**: content: the rest of the document after such a closer. Witnesses 1210.5866, 2412.14057, 1702.01612,
1909.03158; 17/17 witnesses clean (139 → 0 errors); 150 of the ≈2,060 run-336 papers with that first error: 141 → 82

### 500. A locked binding owns its calls: a document's parameterless redefinition is the meaning for every use without an argument (Perl: every TeX-source redefinition refused)

**Perl behavior**: `installDefinition` refuses every redefinition of a `:locked` name from TeX sources
(State.pm:502-517), logging `Info:ignore` "Ignoring redefinition of \cs". A document that uses a locked name as a
plain value then has the binding read the next token as its argument. A pgffor loop variable
`\foreach \i/\text in {…}` gives 15 errors (Perl 17; 2405.18512, 1406.2544). `\@for\text:=…` is a Fatal runaway (Perl
102 errors). `\def\title{On Widgets}` then `\section*{\title}` gives 1 error and an empty title (1511.05179).
**Rust behavior** (policy D1, user rulings 2026-10-11): `install_definition` (state.rs) installs a redefinition
instead of refusing it when it is all of the following:
- of Document origin;
- a **parameterless** Expandable — `defines_value`: a robust wrapper `\protect \cs␣` is judged by its inner `\cs␣`,
  and an ltcmd wrapper `\__cmd_start…` by its signature — braced in `\__cmd_start:nNNnnn`/`\__cmd_start_expandable:nNNNNn`,
  and for `\__cmd_start_optimized:` the argument count in `\l__cmd_current_arg_int`, set before ltcmd rebuilds
  `\cs code` (latex.ltx:1963-1983; `\cs code` itself is still the previous declaration's then) — so
  `\DeclareRobustCommand\mathit[1]{…}` and `\RenewDocumentCommand\mathbf{m}{…}` are commands (2306.08511,
  2306.10719, 2306.05287), while `\DeclareRobustCommand\text{V}`, `\RenewDocumentCommand\text{}{V}` and a robust or
  ltcmd `{V}` after a `[1]`/`{m}` declaration are values. `def_macro` installs a robust macro's inner `\cs␣` before its
  wrapper, the reverse of Perl's DefMacroI, so the wrapper's install can judge what it wraps; unobservable otherwise;
- of a binding that `owns_calls`, i.e. its first mandatory parameter reads a braced argument (Plain, Semiverbatim,
  Digested, Undigested, …) after optional ones only, or it is itself an earlier override (loop iterations).

The installed definition carries `Expandable::yields_calls`. The binding is kept globally as `\lx@locked@<cs>`, and
expanding the override first peeks one raw token:
- an explicit catcode-1 `{`, or a `[`/`*` the binding's signature opens with, runs the binding;
- anything else expands the document's definition, as pdflatex does.

`\ifx`, `\meaning` and `\let` see the document's macro, since `PartialEq` compares `paramlist`/`expansion` only.
A `\let` copy also carries `yields_calls` and the call owner, so `\let\c=\cite` after a value makes `\c{k}` a
citation where pdflatex prints the value (accepted residual since 64zb; eplain's `\@oldatcatcode` is such a copy,
harmless there because the next token is `\let`).
Reversions and `tex=` still name `<cs>`. The refusal records (`\lx@dropped@<cs>`, `<cs>:redefined`,
`<cs>:redefined@nargs`, empty internals) are written as before, so calls behave as today. One `Info:lock` per cs per
document replaces the per-iteration "Ignoring redefinition".

Scope of the rule:
- **Commands stay refused.** A redefinition with parameters — `\renewcommand\cite[1]`, `\def\author(s)`, robust and
  ltcmd forms included — defines a command, not a value. It stays refused as in Perl, and the binding keeps every
  use, `\mathbf x` included.
- **Absolutely locked.**
  - Bindings with no braced interface: sectioning (whose 0-parameter macro reads its argument downstream in
    `\@startsection`), `\footnote`, `\url`, `\maketitle`, `\abstract`, environments, font defaults, `\def`.
  - Every name containing `@`, LaTeX's internal namespace (clsguide.tex:187, latex.ltx:1797): `\alloc@`,
    `\@startsection`, `\@caption`, `\@lbibitem`, ….
- **A robust binding owns its calls by what it wraps** (user ruling 2026-10-15, "extend D1 to robust"): its own meaning is
  the parameterless `\protect \cs␣`, so `owns_calls` reads the inner `\cs␣`'s parameter list, and `call_openers`
  takes the `[`/`*` openers from it. The one robust locked binding is the kernel `\cite` without natbib
  (sect11.rs, `[] Semiverbatim`): a group-local `\def\cite{CITEV}` used as `[\cite]` prints the value, and
  `\cite[p.~3]{x}`/`\cite{x}` stay the binding's citations (67n; was RED `macro-state/m5_robust_cite_value_in_group`).
  eplain's btxmac borrows `\cite` as scratch — `\edef\cite{\the\catcode`@}`, `\let\@oldatcatcode=\cite`
  (eplain.tex:346-348), read back by `\catcode`@ = \@oldatcatcode` (:666) — and its own `\def\cite{\@getoptionalarg
  \@cite}` (:445) becomes an override whose calls keep the binding. Refused, the scratch left `@` at catcode 0 and
  ended in Fatal `ParamSpec` at :721 (math0308041, math0612670, 0705.2148, 0802.3843, 1207.1752, 1401.4197; Perl's
  `\cite` is not locked). A wrapper whose inner macro the document replaced (`\DeclareRobustCommand\cite{V}` installs
  `\cite␣` first, only file-locked, #568) takes every use of `\cite`, calls included — `B \cite{k}` gives `Vk`, as in
  pdflatex and Perl — and a parameterless value declared after it is refused, because `owns_calls` then judges the
  replacement (`\renewcommand\cite{W}` after it gives `[V]`, pdflatex `[W]`; RED
  `macro-state/m5_robust_cite_declare_robust_then_value`), while the log still says "Ignoring redefinition of \cite".
- **Unchanged paths.** Class/package code (File origin) stays refused with records and replay; `replay_class_setter`
  and the `\maketitle` deposit run under File origin. So do `\newcommand` (LaTeX refuses a defined name too), `\font`,
  `\newenvironment`, and `\let`, which bypasses the lock as in Perl.

The derived classes under article+amsmath,amssymb,natbib,url,hyperref are pinned in `locked_names_derived_classes`: 25
owners, 110 absolute.
- **Machinery without `@` owns its calls too.** `\newcounter`, `\DeclareTextAccentDefault`,
  `\Declare{Lower,Upper,Titlecase}Mapping` and `\multicolumn` follow ruling 3 and the `@`-only exclusion; there is no
  name list. Their braced calls are unchanged. Only a parameterless document redefinition used without braces runs the
  author's code, which is pdflatex's behaviour.
- **"Document origin" covers package code run while the document is read.** pgf's diamond shape defines its anchor
  macro as `\savedanchor\text` (pgflibraryshapes.geometric.code.tex:277) at node time. That is now the meaning inside
  the node, and 2006.09271 logs `Info:lock:\text`. Definitions made while a package is loaded keep File origin
  (ruling 2).
- **The peek is raw and may read past the end of a macro body.** `\def\wrap{\text}\wrap{x}` runs the binding on
  `{x}`, as TeX's argument scan would read `{x}`.

Accepted residuals:
- **(a) Unbraced use of a parameterless forwarder.** It runs the author's code, as pdflatex does; author code is not
  analysed. Examples: `\def\mathcal{\mathscr}` with `\mathcal C` (script, while a braced `\mathcal{C}` stays
  calligraphic: 1004.3646, 1407.2007); `\renewcommand\mathbf{\boldsymbol}` with `\mathbf a` (1806.00338); the
  `\mathpalette` `\sqrt` hack with `\sqrt\rho` (an hbox/vrule rendering around the binding's root: 1806.09639,
  1904.10871).
- **(b) The binding's kept name leaks in expansion-only contexts.** `\edef\y{\text{z}}` gives `\meaning\y` =
  `macro:->\lx@locked@text {z}`, and `\typeout{[\text{a}]}` prints `\lx@locked@text{a}`. `tex=` and reversions are
  clean. RED `macro-state/m5_locked_name_in_expansion_only_context`; review probes p1/p6.
- A robust value followed by a robust command (`\DeclareRobustCommand\text{V}` then `\DeclareRobustCommand\text[1]{X#1}`)
  gives `[X]` for `[\text]`, as pdflatex does: the value's wrapper `\protect \text␣` stays the meaning (the command's
  wrapper is refused), and its inner `\text␣`, which is not locked, is now `X#1` and reads `]`; `\text{c}` stays the
  binding's.
- **(c) Deferred, rulings 4/5.** e2 `{\def\section{Sec.}…}` and d2 `\let\text\relax\def\text{v}` stay as Perl;
  m5_e2/m5_d2 are RED-deferred.

**Why**: the lock exists to keep the semantic markup of a call (Perl acb3b27e, "commonly redefined macros that lose
semantics when redefined"). A use without an argument cannot produce that markup; it only made the binding consume the
wrong token. D1 keeps every call's markup and gives the document TeX's meaning everywhere else. The full study is in
OXIDIZED_DESIGN.md "Locked definitions".

A/B vs 8542e1b1a5:
- the M5 cluster (369 papers): errors 11,882 → 2,500, 140 papers fewer, 125 to zero, none more, no Fatal change;
- census 314/320 identical, the 6 changes intended or residual (a);
- restyle 100/100 identical;
- random 298/300 identical (2 fewer errors);
- witnesses 2405.18512 45 → 0 (its appendices now `<appendix>`), 1406.2544 31 → 0, 1511.05179 1 → 0.

Guards `perfect_kernel_batch64zb::*`, `perfect_kernel_batch67n::*` (robust bindings); repros `macro-state/m5_*`.

### 501. An email or web address a class sets in typewriter type is `<text font="typewriter">` in its contact, its `_` and `~` as typed (Perl: roman, `˙` and `˜`)

**Perl behavior**: every class binding's address (`\email`, `\homepage`, `\urladdr`, `\ead`) is a Semiverbatim argument
digested in the current font (revtex4_support.sty.ltxml:55, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:655-659): in OT1 roman its
catcode-12 `_` and `~` are slots 0x5F/0x7E, the dot and tilde accents (TeX_Fonts.pool.ltxml:214), "ann˙able@a.edu",
and the HTML `mailto:` link is made of that text (KPE #586).
**Rust behavior**: a binding whose class sets the address with `\url`, `\texttt` or `\ttfamily` passes it through the
kernel `\lx@address@urlfont` (url.sty's `\UrlFont`: the ASCII encoding, the typewriter family): REVTeX 4.0
(revtex4.cls:4476-4493), amsart/amsproc/amsbook (amsart.cls:538-546), llncs (:897), JHEP.cls (:806), jheppub
(:127-131), iopart (:354-355), aa (:600, :824), elsarticle (:215-219, :232-235), cas (cas-common.sty:362), imsart
(imsart.sty:1162). The contact holds `<text font="typewriter">ann_able@a.edu</text>`; the author block's contacts made
of such a command's call (`\institute{… \\ \email{x}}`, `E-mail: \email{x}`) are set the same (`email_command_address`).
The accent of an empty letter (`\~{}`) is the current font's, so a typewriter address keeps its `~` in the run
(1601.03451), and the HTML link of an address held in typewriter runs is all of its text (`contact-address`). The
ASCII fontmap's 0x10/0x11 are the dotless ı/ȷ (Perl: none), so `\'{\i}` in an address is "í".
Perl's own golden `tests/structure/amsarticle.xml` has `joe@blow` in roman; ours carries the typewriter font.
REVTeX 4.0 with the paper's own `\usepackage{hyperref}` sets the address with hyperref's `\href`, in roman ('˙' in OT1);
revtex4_support always loads hyperref (as Perl's, revtex4_support.sty.ltxml:23), so the binding cannot tell, and every
REVTeX 4.0 address is typewriter (user ruling 2026-10-11, 3 of 41 sampled revtex4 underscore papers). AASTeX 6+, which
loads under the revtex4 binding, sets `\homepage` in roman (revtex4-1.cls:2387-2390, aastex701.cls:2213-2216) and keeps
it so (#502); AASTeX 5.x's `\email` is typewriter (aastex.cls:903-905, `\tt`; 1001.0026).
**Why**: the address as the PDF prints it, and a working `mailto:` link. Witnesses 1001.1076 (40 of 41 sampled revtex4
papers), 2101.10462, 2501.04035. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch64zc::*`.

### 502. An email or web address a class sets in roman keeps its `_` (Perl and pdflatex: `˙` in OT1)

**Perl behavior**: as #501; the address in the OT1 roman font prints `_` as the dot accent.
**Rust behavior**: a binding whose class sets the address in the current roman font — REVTeX 4.1/4.2 (`\href` without
hyperref is `\@href`, revtex4-1.cls:1959-1961), AASTeX 6+, emulateapj (on REVTeX 4.1, emulateapj.cls:151-167),
svjour3/svmult, quantumarticle, jmlr, pasj00, ptephy —
passes it through the kernel `\lx@address@textfont` (the ASCII encoding, the current font): roman, its `_` and `~` as
typed, no element added.
**Why**: pdflatex prints "ann˙able@a.edu" there too; the address is the author's, not the accident of the font (user
ruling 2026-10-11). 12 of 175 sampled underscore papers (revtex4-2 9, revtex4-1 3). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch64zc::revtex4_2_ot1_email_keeps_its_underscore`, `class_email_paths_keep_their_font_and_underscore`.

### 503. The accent of an empty letter is the current font's, one run with the text around it (Perl: the same font; `˜`/`ˆ` in typewriter type)

**Perl behavior**: `applyAccent` (TeX_Character.pool.ltxml:62-87) takes the font of the digested letter (:67); an
empty letter has none, so the typewriter replacement (:80-83, which would give `~`) is skipped and the standalone
accent (:84-87) is a Box with no font, which takes the current one (Box.pm:31). `\textsf{a\~{}b}` is one sansserif run;
in typewriter type `\~{}`/`\^{}` are `˜`/`ˆ`, one run per font.
**Rust behavior**: an empty letter (or one without a font) takes the current font, as Perl's: one run (the port's
font-less split was a port bug: SYNC "Rust Error Fixes"). Beyond Perl, in typewriter type or the ASCII encoding `\~{}`/`\^{}` give `~`/`^`, cmtt's 0x7E/0x5E
as pdflatex prints them under OT1 (a typewriter address keeps its `~` in its run, 1601.03451, 1601.06529). Under T1
pdflatex's `\texttt{\~{}}` is ectt slot 3, the raised `˜`; we print the author's ASCII `~`.
**Why**: Perl parity for the font, and the character the author typed. Body text changes on 6 of 13 sampled `\~{}`
papers, each a run joined or a `~`: 1001.1367, 1001.1793, 1301.6104, 1301.6221, 1901.07113, 2101.11048. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch64zc::accent_of_empty_letter_keeps_the_run`.

### 504. → Bindings beyond Perl's tree: REVTeX 3 (`revtex3_support_sty.rs`)

### 505. → #408 (OmniBus loaded for a missing `\documentstyle` option only provides (Perl: loaded whole over the class))

### 506. A bibliography a `\bibitem` opens outside any bibliography takes the author's heading line as its title, else none (Perl: `\refname`)

User ruling 2026-10-10. Perl titles every bibliography `\refname`. For a bibliography a `\bibitem` opens outside any
bibliography (kernel and natbib), ours takes the author's heading line before it as the title and removes it from the
body. A heading line is a paragraph whose only content is one run of ≤4 words (a full stop only after one word), with
only text runs inside, styled apart from the paragraph's font: bold, small caps, ≥1.15× size (`\large`+) or underlined,
not italic. Otherwise the bibliography has no visible title and no table-of-contents entry (`toc` dropped from
`inlist`). Either way the lists its `\bibitem`s were taken from, emptied, go. Section headings are absorbed as OD #456;
an explicit `{thebibliography}` is unchanged. Trigger: `\noindent{\bf Literature}\begin{enumerate}\bibitem{a}
A.\end{enumerate}`. Open: heading styles the paragraph's own font already carries are not absorbed (fail safe).

### 507. `ltx:biblist` reopens, and the phantom-entry prune runs at the bibliography's and the document's close (Perl: autoClose only)

`ltx:biblist` has `auto_open => 0.5` (Perl autoClose only); `TagOptions.auto_open` carries Perl's fraction. The OD #155
phantom-entry prune runs at the bibliography's close and at the document's close over every keyless blank
`ltx:bibitem` inside (lists, floats, tables, tags, nested entries, or outside any bibliography), followed by the removal
of auto-opened `ltx:biblist`s left empty. No hook removes the node it closes (Document.pm:1243-1247 stops there).

### 508. AMS-TeX `\end` ends the document unless followed by `{`

**Rule.** In an AMS-TeX document `\end` is `\lx@end@document`, except before a `{`, where it stays LaTeX's `\end{<env>}`
(`latexml_engine/src/amstex.rs:193-208`). **Perl** reads an amsppt document plain, where `\end` is `\lx@end@document`
(plain_constructs.pool.ltxml:284) and amsppt's `\enddocument` reaches it through `\plainend` (amsppt.sty:1090-1098); we
read it through LaTeX (converter.rs `compile_route`), where a bare `\end` took what followed for an environment name (an
`unexpected:\endgroup` Error per document: 1505.02369, 1901.01055, 2410.05768, math-ph9812020, q-alg9510020). The `{`
exception keeps a LaTeX document that loads AMS-TeX working. Witness 1008.3855 (4 entries written after `\end` are, as
in TeX, not typeset).

### 509. `\endabstract` is locked against redefinition from files (Perl: unlocked)

`\endabstract:locked@files`: a package's `\endabstract` no longer replaces the kernel's (Perl's is unlocked).
Witness 1606.05599 (its bibliography and abstract are reached again).

### 510. Only a TeX `\item` or `\bibitem` steps the bibliography counter (Perl: recovery entries are numbered)

As pdflatex: the entry the recovery opens for a paragraph (`\lx@pseudo@bibitem`, Perl `\save@bibitem{}`) takes an
unnumbered id and no label; `\par@in@bibliography` makes no entry before an `\item`; no number is given back on a prune
(an author's `\item` before `\bibitem{d}` prints an empty [4] and d is [5], as pdflatex). natbib's `\bibitem` keeps its
place (opens no bibliography) only among its list's own items: an itemization is bound, the environment that bound it
(`itemization_environment`, set by `begin_itemize`) is the current one, and it has an `\item` already (RED repro
index-bib/natbib_bibitem_among_list_items, SYNC K21). Id shift (user ruling 2026-10-11, accepted): on
ACM-Reference-Format `.bbl`-preamble papers (2106.12714, 2605.03143; ~78% of 2020+ acmart papers) entries move from
`bib.bib(N+1)` to `bib.bibN`, so ids and tags match pdflatex's printed numbers; Perl numbers the pseudo entry
(`\save@bibitem{}`, latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4058); `bib.bibxN` is Perl's unnumbered scheme (Package.pm:857-872).

### 511. natbib's `\bibitem` outside any list reports Lonely `\item` and still recovers a bibliography; `\bibliography` is given back after it

natbib's `\bibitem` outside any list (no itemization bound, current environment not center, flushleft, flushright,
quote, quotation or verse) reports Perl's `Error:malformed:ltx:bibitem` with its own wording "\bibitem outside any list
(LaTeX: Lonely \item--perhaps a missing list environment); opening a bibliography", once per `\bibitem` (pdflatex's
Lonely `\item`, latex.ltx:16041-16043; Perl reports the misplaced element instead), and the bibliography is still
recovered. A sectioning command or `\maketitle` ends that bibliography at digestion (`\lx@bibliography@unlonely` on
`\@startsection@hook`), dropping natbib's pending `\@bibstop`, as a bibliography's own setup now also does. Every
bibliography `\lx@mung@bibliography` opens (in the document body or another environment, out of an author's
`{enumerate}`/`{itemize}`/`{description}`, or in a class's `\let` of `\thebibliography`) gives
`\bibliography`/`\bibliographystyle` back right after its setup (Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3839-3840 leaves them
no-ops to the end of the enclosing group): a later `.bbl` bibliography prints, and a `\bibliography` inside such a list
runs, as in pdflatex. The end of the environment it opens in is saved once, by a marker of its own
(`\lx@mung@saved@<env>@done`), an environment without `\end<env>` (`{small}`) included. Witnesses 1108.2593 (40 Lonely
Errors, bibliography structure kept), 1411.7266 (CS18's open `\acknowledgments` list: 10 → 0). Trigger:
`\usepackage{natbib}\begin{document}x\bibitem{a} A.\bibitem{b} B.\end{document}` → 2 Errors (pdflatex 2). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch64x::{natbib_bibitem_in_the_document_body_is_reported,
natbib_bibitem_in_a_class_references_environment, bibliography_after_an_implicit_one_is_printed,
lonely_bibliography_does_not_reach_the_next_document}`.

### 514. `\noalign\\` is an empty noalign and the row end; "Missing { inserted" unless the kernel's text tabular newline (Perl: Missing `{` and a cascade)

`\noalign` followed by `\\` (or `\tabularnewline`, past spaces and `\relax`, as §785 `scan_left_brace` reads) is read
as an empty noalign and the row end (it was a noalign group that never closed, and the rest of the document was lost).
In TeX the kernel text `tabular`'s `\\` (and `\tabularnewline`, latex.ltx:16576 `\let`) is `\@tabularcr`
(latex.ltx:16590), `{\ifnum0=`}\fi…`: the brace `\noalign` scans is the one `\\` opens and its `\ifnum0=`{\fi}` closes,
before the `\cr` that ends an empty row, so pdflatex is clean (2309.15248, svmult's `\svhline\noalign\\`;
`\tabular…\endtabular` the same). Every other `\\` (array.sty's and the kernel's `\@arraycr`, `\relax\iffalse{\fi…`,
longtable's `\LT@tabularcr`, amsmath's `\math@cr`) opens with no brace: "Missing { inserted" and a cascade. Ours expands
every `\\` to `\lx@hidden@cr{…}`, so the shape is told before expansion: the token is `\ifx`-equal to `\@tabularcr` (a
`\let` copy too), the alignment's binding names `\@tabularcr` as its `\\` (`row_end`: the kernel's `tabular_bindings`;
longtable names `\LT@tabularcr`, longtable.sty:133) and array.sty is not loaded. Then it is silent; otherwise it raises
`Error:expected:{` "Missing { inserted" once (math `array`, amsmath `align`, array.sty `tabular`, longtable, tabularx;
pdflatex: 5-114 cascaded errors). Witness 2309.15248 (its 44 bibitems restored). Residuals (GA4N, post-merge): every
`\\` here is one `\lx@alignment@newline` (latex_constructs/sect10.rs `\let`s `\@tabularcr` and `\@arraycr` to it), so
`\ifx` cannot tell them apart — a kernel text tabular's `\noalign\@arraycr` is silent where pdflatex errs (RED
kernel-alignment/noalign_arraycr_in_a_kernel_tabular_red) — and a macro that expands to the row end
(`\def\tnl{\tabularnewline}`, RED kernel-alignment/noalign_tabularcr_through_a_macro_red) errs where pdflatex is clean,
TeX's brace not being readable; `\noalign\cr` still cascades.

### 515. Kernel `\lx@startsection@afterhook{<type>}{<inlist>}` after a heading (Perl: none; svmult `\motto`/`\chapauthor` undefined)

A binding may define `\lx@startsection@afterhook`; the kernel reads it after a sectional heading (the kernel defines
none, so it costs nothing). svmult uses it: `\chapauthor` becomes a creator of the next numbered chapter and `\motto` a
quote opening the next chapter (starred chapters take the motto only, svmult.cls:649 `\@makeschapterhead`). Witnesses
0911.4644, 1010.1304. Residual: svmult numbers front-matter chapters (svmult.cls:592-594), ours does not (RED
class-bindings/svmult_frontmatter_chapter_numbered).

### 517. quantumarticle's REVTeX-compatibility `\pacs`/`\preprint` are kept as RDFa metadata (Perl: undefined)

quantumarticle.cls (:1462-1471) accepts and discards `\pacs` and `\preprint` in its REVTeX-compatibility mode. Per the
rulings (#6 2026-10-10, F8 2026-10-09) they are kept as RDFa, not displayed: one `dcterms:subject` per `\pacs` (beside
the author's `pdfkeywords`) and `dcterms:identifier` per `\preprint`. hyperref is loaded at `\begin{document}` as the
class does (:1392-1394), and natbib with `numbers,sort&compress` (:1428-1429) unless natbib or biblatex is loaded.
Witnesses 1705.03968, 1704.06662, 1709.01098, 2212.01355. Guards `quantumarticle_revtex_compatibility`,
`quantumarticle_pacs_keep_the_authors_keywords`.

### 518. An undefined `@string` macro is reported for entries that reach the bibliography; the `.bst`'s `MACRO`s define them (Perl: every entry, Perl's defaults, `at String; line 0`)

Perl's BibTeX parser reports an undefined macro in any entry of the `.bib` (BibTeX.pm:307-310); bibtex warns only for
cited entries. Ours reports it ("The BibTeX macro 'x' is not defined", `Error:unexpected:x`, its value the name
itself as in Perl) for entries that are digested (cited) and for `@string`/`@preamble`, located at the `.bib` line
(`<stem>; line N`), where Perl's report says `at String; line 0 col 1`. The bibliography style's `MACRO {name} {"value"}` commands (quote-aware: a value with TeX
braces is read to its closing quote) override Perl's built-in month/journal defaults, as bibtex does; with no
`\bibliographystyle`, REVTeX's implicit style supplies its own. With no style (no `\bibliographystyle` and no
class-implicit one), or one that is not found, an undefined macro is a Warning (the style may define it; Perl:
`Error:unexpected` at `String; line 0 col 1`). Witnesses 2606.21799, 2603.22119. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch64zf::{bib_parse_errors_are_reported,
revtex_implicit_bibstyle_defines_its_macros, bst_macros_after_a_braced_value_resolve}`. KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #600.

### 519. Numbers and dimensions out of TeX's range clamp at its bounds with an Error (Perl: the raw value, silently)

An integer constant past 2^31−1 is 2^31−1 with "Number too big" (tex.web §445); a dimension past `\maxdimen` is
`\maxdimen`, negated only for the scan's own sign, with "Dimension too large" (§460); an e-TeX expression out of range
is 0 with "Arithmetic overflow" (etex.ch `\numexpr`/`\dimexpr`). TeX errs on each, and its recovery value (TeX's bound
or 0) is not the author's: an Error, the
recovery value kept (the staged severity rule (3), DG 2026-11-11; 64zf's Warnings until DTL1d). pgfmath's parser result
past `\maxdimen` errs with Perl's `Error:pgfmath:overflow` (pgfmath.code.tex.ltxml:342-344, :391-393), on the dimension
TeX holds and never on the fpu's floats (#1012). Replaces
batch 56bq's i64-only clamp. Still silent: `\multiply` past the bound (it computes on in the i64 headroom; TeX errs and
keeps the register) and pgfmath's function results (clamped) (REDs expansion-primitives/multiply_overflow_keeps_the_register_red, graphics-tikz/
pgfmath_function_overflow_clamped_silently_red); a calc sum past the bound (`calc_expression_dimension_not_clamped_red`); outside
the fpu, pgfmath's unitless operands and its operations' results past the bound (`pgfmath_unitless_and_intermediate_overflow_red`). Not
yet TeX's: an e-TeX expression checks only its final value, so an intermediate overflow that comes back in range is silent
and a product past the i64 range keeps the bound (`clamp_arith_overflow`, one report per multiply) where etex.ch's
`scan_expr` latches one error and returns 0 (`etex_expression_overflow_latched_once_red`). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch64zf::{number_and_dimension_overflow_clamp_and_err,
integer_constant_overflow_is_infinity}`, `error_boundary::perfect_kernel_error_boundary` (both sides); repro
expansion-primitives/dimension_overflow_max_dimen. The one exception (DG 2026-11-13, SBX1): an overflow in the measure of a
`breakable` tcolorbox, which we set as one box where TeX breaks it (Perl tcolorbox.sty.ltxml:21), is a Warning naming the
box, the overflows it cascades into an Info (`common::error::approximated_measure`, read by the box's own
`\iftcb@isbreakable` when tcolorbox.sty:2006 `\tcb@draw@color@box` measures it; 2605.05949 2605.19136 2605.24941
2605.28003 2605.30434 2606.07718: 4 Errors each → 1 Warning; a tcolorbox before 3.x has no such flag, so its boxes are
not breakable: 1606.02242 ships 2.80), cleared at the measure's end (`\lx@tcb@measure@done`:
the command form `\tcolorbox…\endtcolorbox`, tcolorbox.sty:1150, opens no group); a box of its own unbreakable, also
one inside the breakable one, and an overflow after the box keep the Error (`error_boundary::perfect_kernel_error_boundary`,
five rows; the 2.80 shape a sixth, 0 Errors). Open (BRKC, post-merge): a breakable box in a minipage or a float, which TeX does not break, is downgraded
too (`tcolorbox_breakable_box_in_{minipage,float}_overflow_red`).

### 520. setspace's `\onehalfspace`/`\doublespace` switches are checked no-ops (Perl: an environment frame)

setspace.sty:534-547 makes each switch a `\begingroup` plus the spacing, ended by its `\end…` (`\restore@spacing`'s
`\endgroup`, :516-523). The spacing is presentational and the group is not modelled: a real `\begingroup` keeps every
word since 65c but nests a later sibling environment inside the earlier one at `\end{document}`, so the checked no-op
keeps the author's sibling structure. What the group does to TeX is reported where TeX reports it: one
`Error:unexpected` per group that ends with a switch still open, at the innermost open switch.
- A brace group, or an environment whose frame binds `\hsize` (a box: floats, minipage, subfigure, wrapfigure,
  algorithm): "Extra }, or forgotten \endgroup", object `}` (witness 2310.08233's `{\doublespace text}`).
- Another environment: "\end{X} closes \<switch>'s \begingroup instead of {X}'s group; {X} stays open (LaTeX:
  \begin{X} … ended by \end{<enclosing>})", naming the enclosing environment's end, or `\end{document}`.
- A plain `\begingroup … \endgroup`: its `\endgroup` closes the innermost switch's group and the plain group stands
  open in its place, so every switch of the group re-arms on the enclosing one, outermost first (stomach.rs
  `pop_stack_frame` honours the `\aftergroup` a group-end hook queues, as Perl's popStackFrame does, Stomach.pm:
  308-314). At the document level that is no error, as in TeX ("(\end occurred inside a group at level 1)";
  KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #602).
- An `\end…` closes the innermost switch of its own group (a frame-local stack; the next one out names the report).
- A group digested twice (a `\section` title: heading and toc) reports twice, like any error there (RED
  sectioning-frontmatter/section_title_errors_reported_twice, shared with Perl).
- Groups abandoned at `\end{document}` run no check (`lx@ending@document`, OD #207). At a bounded body's terminal
  the check runs, but the re-arm it queues is discarded (guard `abandoned_group_discards_hook_queued_aftergroup`).

Residuals, erring toward flagging: a switch closed by `\end<name>` from inside a nested plain group still reports
(RED boxes-groups/doublespace_end_in_a_nested_plain_group: review probes r9, h5, h9 pdflatex 0, ours 1; h7 pdflatex 1,
ours 2). The closer named is the enclosing environment's end only when no group intervenes; with one between

setspace_switch_reports_where_tex_errs, setspace_switch_is_quiet_where_tex_is, setspace_switches_in_one_group_are_one_error,
setspace_switch_in_a_plain_group_rearms_on_the_enclosing_group, setspace_box_environments_are_known_by_their_frame,
setspace_report_names_the_enclosing_end, setspace_end_closes_only_a_switch_of_its_own_group,
