### 552. A `\label[type]{key}` keeps its key wherever a caption reads its label — after `\caption`, in its text, in a longtable — with or without cleveref (Perl: `[` is read as the label)

`\@caption` moves a `\label` that follows the caption into it (`\@caption@postlabel … SkipMatch:\label Semiverbatim`,
latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3172), reading the label's key as the next argument. cleveref's `\label` takes an optional
type, `\label[appendixtable]{tab:a_b}`, so the key read was `[`: `labels="LABEL:["`, the rest `appendixtable]tab:a_b`
typeset in the float, and a `_` in the key an Error (Perl the same). **Rust** (batch 65m): `\@caption@postlabel` reads
the optional and passes only the key on, as our cleveref binding's `\lx@cleverref@label[]` drops the type anyway.
**Witness**: 2404.11739 8 → 0 (`labels="LABEL:tab:_app_sim_baranov_binM"`). The type itself goes on as `\lx@label@type`,
which the cleveref binding makes the object's reference type (77s, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #998): `\cref` shows "Appendix
Table 1" as pdflatex. Open: a procedure's `\cref` shows our refnum `Proc` where pdflatex shows "Procedure -" (predates
65m). The two other sites that move a trailing `\label` the same way read the optional too: algorithm2e's procedure
caption (`\lx@algocf@proccaption@postlabel`, algorithm2e_sty.rs) and caption.sty's `\captionof`
(`\@captionof@postlabel`, caption_sty.rs; Perl caption.sty.ltxml:122 the same as pool:3172). subeqn's
`\@lab@subeqnarray` (subeqn.sty:57 `[2]`, so pdflatex reads `[` too) is left as TeX has it. The label-mapping peek
`maybe_peek_label` (counter/dialect.rs; Perl Package.pm:819ff the same) also reads `[` as the key, but runs only under a
label-mapping hook, which only the test helper `labelled_tex.rs` sets. Since 77s r2 two more sites read it: a `\label`
inside the caption's text (`\@@@hack@caption@`, latex_constructs/sect09.rs; 1412.3542, 1901.00405, 2008.03354,
2201.04036) and longtable's label (`\lx@longtable@label`, longtable_sty.rs, the type applied after the table by
`\lx@longtable@labeltype`; 2508.14936). **Divergence without cleveref**: all five sites read the optional `[type]`
whether or not cleveref is loaded; the kernel `\label` takes no optional, so pdflatex reads `[` as the key and typesets
the rest — a longtable's `\caption{Long}\label[appendixtable]{lt}` prints "appendixtable]lt" after the caption and
every `\ref{lt}` is "??" (0 errors). We label the key and drop the `[type]` text, so the reference resolves (77s r2
re-review probe l2). Kept by main-session decision 2026-10-20 as a semantic gain (content and markup before PDF fidelity:
the key labels the object and its references resolve, where pdflatex prints bracket text and "??"); reading the type
only with cleveref loaded would match pdflatex. **Guards**:
`perfect_kernel_batch65m::cleveref_label_type_after_caption` (repros
captions-floats/cleveref_label_type_after_{caption,procedure_caption,captionof}),
`perfect_kernel_batch77s::label_type_in_caption_text` (repro package-bindings/cleveref_label_type_in_caption_text).

### 553. TeX's math-group recovery for an inline formula outside alignments: a math shift closes the groups opened in it, `\par` ends it unless the math after it goes on (then it is kept open, as Perl's), an environment's end ends it, a `}` at its math shift ends it when it closes a construct digested as a unit, else is deleted (Perl: none of the three)

tex.web: a math shift with `cur_group` not the math shift group goes through `off_save` (§1193 `mmode+math_shift`,
§1064-1065): "Missing } inserted" for a `{`/`\bgroup` group (`simple_group`), "Missing \endgroup inserted" for
`\begingroup` (`semi_simple_group`), "Missing \right. inserted" for `\left`, and the shift is read again. A `\par` in
math mode is `insert_dollar_sign` (§1046-1047 `mmode+par_end`): "Missing $ inserted" and the `\par` read again; LaTeX's
`\end{X}` gets the same through its `\par` or its `\endgroup` meeting the math shift group (§1064). A `}` meeting the
math shift group is `extra_right_brace` (§1068-1069): "Extra }, or forgotten $", the brace deleted. Perl has none of
these: `$` in a group inside the formula is "Attempt to end mode math" with the frame left open, `\par` in math is
silent, and a `}` at the formula's frame closes it with an Error.

**Rust** (batch 65n), for an *inline formula outside alignments* — one `\lx@begin@inline@math` opened with no alignment
current (frame value `stomach::INLINE_FORMULA`), reached from the innermost frame through groups `off_save` closes only
(`stomach::inline_formula_reachable`):
- tex_math.rs `end_math_or_defer`: the math ender meeting a `{`/`\bgroup` or `\begingroup` group inserts its closer
  (`stomach::off_save_closer`), Error "Missing } inserted" / "Missing \endgroup inserted" (TeX's error, and Perl's
  "Attempt to end mode math"), the closer owed by the group as 65d's `\right` path owes it (`owe_inserted_closer`), and
  the ender read again; the ender met first reverts as nothing. Before, the math end was deferred to the group's end,
  which an unbalanced paper never reaches, and the rest of the paper was digested as math. The deferral stays for a
  constructor's argument frame (`$\bm{\hat{m}$} b`, kblocks-doc; nicefrac; titlecaps — TeX has no group there), for
  formulas in alignments and for display math.
- stomach.rs `insert_dollar_sign`, called by `\lx@normal@par` (before digest; only where the math after the `\par` does
  not go on, 66w below) and by `digest_next_body` at a DefEnvironment's own end: Error "Missing $ inserted",
  `\lx@end@inline@math@inserted` (the ender, reverting to nothing) and the command read again; the `\par` whatsit left in
  the formula reverts as nothing (`lx@par@void`).
- stomach.rs `digest_next_body`: a `}` meeting the formula's math shift group, one rule (`formula_ends_with_its_unit`).
  The `}` **ends the formula** when it closes a construct digested as a unit that holds the formula: a box body (the
  mode frame just outside the formula switched by a command on its own `{` — `\mbox{$x}`, `\hbox{$x}`, `\fbox{$x}`; not
  an environment `\begin{X}`) or an argument digested on its own (`\caption{$x} cap}`, `\section{$x} sec}`: the `}` is
  the argument's own closing brace, gullet.rs `isolated_input_ends_here` — only `}`s left in the isolated context's
  pushback and its mouth exhausted). The formula cannot escape such a construct: its end is inserted, the `}` read again
  ends the construct, and the text after it stays text. **Every other `}` is deleted**, as TeX deletes it (§1069), and
  the formula goes on to its own `$` — or, missing that, to the `\par` or environment end where §1047 inserts it:
  `Before $x} y$ after.` at the paragraph's level or in an environment, `{\it a $x}$ y} after one.` and
  `{\bf $x} y$ after one.` in a plain group (pdflatex's shape and count, 1 error, "after one." text; 65d review a1, a2,
  a8, a16). One Error either way, TeX's message "Extra }, or forgotten $" — also where a display formula or a formula
  in an alignment cell ends at the `}` (below). The `}` a `\right`/`\middle` delimiter scan put back (#530,
  `$\left\{ x \right}$`, `\mbox{$\left\{ x \right}$}`) is deleted before the rule is asked: the author wrote it as a
  delimiter, never as a construct's closer (the box's own `}` follows the `$`), as pdflatex deletes it (65d review g1).

**Content first, against TeX, for a unit construct** (main session decision 2026-10-12): pdflatex deletes the `}` there
too and runs the formula on — `\mbox{$x} after one.` swallows "after one." and the next paragraph into the box (3
errors, pdftotext "Before xafterone.Second para."), and a macro argument's formula ends at the box's or heading's end
(§1047, `\caption{$x}`, `\footnote{note $x}`, `\parbox`, `\makebox`, `\raisebox`: "Missing $ inserted"). Ours ends the
formula at the `}` with one Error, so the text after the construct stays text (65d review a6, a7, a9, a10, a14).
A round-2 draft extended the ending to every `}` whose `{` partner lies outside the formula (a plain `{…}` group
included); it gained nothing on the probe set and lost the shapes where the author did write the closing `$` after the
stray `}` (a1, a2, a16: "after one." became math, 2-3 errors) — settled, not to be re-attempted without evidence.

**Residual, as pdflatex**: in a plain `{…}` group a forgotten `$` (`Before {\bf see $x} more text.`) has its `}`
deleted, and the formula runs the text on as math to the paragraph's end ("Missing $ inserted" at the `\par`; Math
"xmoretext.", 2 errors + the open group at the document's end — pdflatex's count and shape). Possible refinement (RED
paragraph-mode/forgotten_dollar_in_a_plain_group_keeps_the_text, SYNC_STATUS row MS): `$`-parity evidence in the rest
of the paragraph — odd, the author's closing `$` exists, so delete; even, the `$` was forgotten, so end at the `}`.

**`\par` ends the formula only where no math follows** (user ruling 2026-10-14, batch 66w). tex.web pairs §1047's
ending with §1046's re-opening: a math-only token in the text after it inserts a `$` again, so a formula split by a blank
line is two formulas and the paragraph's `$`s stay in step. 65n had only the ending, and every later `$` of the
paragraph opened where it should close: hep-th9402135 (`$Z_{YM}(\epsilon) =` ⏎⏎ `\int_{\cal A} … D A$`, eleven such splits)
went Fatal TooManyErrors where Perl, whose `\par` in math is silent, has 0 errors and the formulas whole — the K1 cluster
of run 345, 31 papers (agent_reports/2026-10-14_ef345_regressions.md, `_k1_arxiv_pdf_study.md`). The ruling keeps Perl's
content where the formula clearly continues and §1047 where it does not, and **any doubt ends the formula**.
stomach.rs `formula_continues_past_par`, asked by `\lx@normal@par` before `insert_dollar_sign`: the input is looked at,
not read (`gullet::peek_upcoming_tokens`: the pushback, then the current mouth's next 40 source lines tokenized lazily by
a scratch mouth under the current catcodes — nothing expanded, consumed or frozen), up to the formula's would-be closer
(the next `$`, or `\)`), within 2,000 tokens and 16,000 copied characters (so a `\par` costs the same however long its
line: the 66w review's one-line 3,000/6,000-repetition probes had grown quadratically). A math-only token before it
keeps the formula open and the `\par` reverts as nothing (no Error; Perl's `tex=` keeps `\par`, which is no formula's
TeX): a sub/sup mark, or a control sequence by its current meaning (`stomach.rs lookahead_command`) — a `\let` to a
mark, a DefMath symbol, a constructor or primitive requiring math, one of tex.web §1046's math-only primitives
(`\left`/`\right`, `\over`, `\mathchar`, the math classes and styles…). Otherwise §1047 ends it as before: no math-only
token first (that `$` opens the next paragraph's own formula), or a doubt:
- the paragraph or the formula ends first, by name or by meaning (`\par`/`\endgraf`, `\end`, `\begin`, `\vskip`,
  `\hrule`…, `\cr`, an `&`, `\(`, `\[`, a definition that leaves horizontal mode), also inside a macro's body
  (`\medskip`'s `\vskip`, `\section`'s `\par`), the closer sits in a group, a bracket or a `$$`, a `}` closes a group
  the look-ahead did not see open, or a bound runs out;
- a command the look-ahead cannot follow: a parameter verbatim, semi-verbatim or delimited by its type (`\url{…}`,
  `\ref{…}`, `\label`, `\def\a#1.{…}`), a macro whose expansion is code (`\verb`, which reads its own delimited
  argument), a macro whose body holds one (`\lstinline` = `\leavevmode\lx@lstinline`, url.sty's `\url`), a `$` or `&`
  in a macro's body, or a macro nested past 3 levels / 512 body tokens.
A command's arguments are not looked into, their scripts being a key's or a file name's, never typeset: a `*` right
after a command that is not math-only (a math-only one's groups are math: `\left[0,1\right)`, `\in [0,1)`), then
every `[…]` and `{…}` in a row (`\cite[p.~2]{smith_2001}`, `\ref*{eq_1}`,
`\includegraphics[width=1cm]{fig_1}`, `\citep[e.g.][]{a_b}`, `\hyperref[sec_a]{there}`; the 66w review's blocker, where
66w had read the key's `_` as math and, for p_cite, run the next formula through `\begin{thebibliography}` — Perl's
failure, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #679); any other group is looked into (hep-th9402135's `{\cf^{1}/G}$`). The look-ahead
starts after the judged `\par`: a current line read to its end adds nothing (`Mouth::peek_text`), and leading tokens
that mean `\par` are skipped (`means_par`) — under `\obeylines` a line end in a formula is an active `^^M` let to
`\par`, and the math on the next line keeps the formula open as after a blank line (hep-ph9809328, hep-ph9706250,
whose MTeXsis `\unobeylines` is missing; repro paragraph-mode/formula_split_by_an_obeyed_line_end_continues). A continuing
formula's `\par` still clears `\parshape` and `\interlinepenalties`, as every `\par` (TeX_Paragraph.pool.ltxml:118-119);
the rest of Perl's after-digest (:121-145: the `next_para_class` hand-over, the `\vadjust` material) is left to the
`\par` that does end the paragraph — Perl runs it inside the formula, where a class meant for the next `ltx:para` and
vertical material do not belong. Not done: §1046's re-opening itself (a stray `_` in text still takes Perl's "Script _
can only appear in math mode" — the 66i draft, 32 papers worse on our wrong modes upstream); a continuation with no
math-only token (`$a =` ⏎⏎ `b$, where $c$`) still ends at the `\par`, as pdflatex; a `\par` from a macro body
(hep-th9402135's `\def\bull{\vrule height 1.5ex` ⏎⏎ `width …}` in `$\bull$`) is looked past like any other, and ends
the formula there as pdflatex does (2 errors per use; Perl 0). Repros paragraph-mode/
formula_split_by_blank_line_continues_with_math, formula_split_by_blank_line_braced_continuation,
script_in_text_after_par_closed_formula_reenters_math (GREEN), par_in_inline_math_before_a_text_paragraph_ends_the_formula,
par_in_inline_math_before_a_label_argument_ends_the_formula, and the 66w r1 controls
par_in_inline_math_before_{a_cite_with_a_note,a_starred_ref,verb,includegraphics,citep_with_two_notes,hyperref,
unfollowable_commands}_ends_the_formula; guards `perfect_kernel_batch66w::*`.

**Display math is tolerant of `\par`** (main session decision 2026-10-12): no §1047 for display math, a blank line in
an `equation` being common and tolerated.

**Why only there**: a cell's `$` may be its template's (`align*`'s `$\displaystyle…$`): math9805003's undefined
`{Sb}` in an `align*`, whose row template `$` closed the environment's `\begingroup`, lost the whole alignment
(repro paragraph-mode/alignment_cell_formula_keeps_its_recovery, CONTROL). Display math has no §1047 (above), so a deleted brace would run `{\equation x=1}` on through the document.
Open (SYNC_STATUS row MS): an author's formula in a cell (RED paragraph-mode/cell_end_in_inline_math_inserts_dollar;
1210.0368, 1907.09124, whose deferrals sit in alignments) needs the template's `$` told from the author's.

**Diagnostics given up for TeX's**: `$x} after one.` with no closing `$` at the paragraph's level now sets "after
one." as math to the paragraph's end, as pdflatex ("xaf terone."); 65a's inserted `$` had guessed "forgotten $" and
kept it text, but swapped text and math wherever the `$` came later (`$x} y$ after.`). Open (SYNC_STATUS row MS): a `}`
meeting a `\left` group in an inline formula is not yet deleted (RED
paragraph-mode/brace_meeting_left_group_in_inline_math_is_deleted).

**Witnesses** (65int2 → 65n; errors / warnings / text words outside math / runs of 20+ letters): 2007.11971 13 / 2,643 /
5,268 / 179 → 1 / 43 / 9,865 / 0; 1710.02165 29 / 35 / 12,121 / 1 → 21 / 27 / 12,501 / 0; 2008.11762 14 → 15 (a
pre-existing `$` desync in the paragraph now ends at its `\par`, content unchanged); 1210.0368, 1907.09124,
math9805003, hep-lat9811036, nucl-th0401019 unchanged. Probes `~/data/pk_wt/scratch_65n/` (pdflatex oracle per probe).

**Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batch65n::{math_shift_closes_a_group_opened_in_the_formula,
par_in_inline_math_ends_the_formula, environment_end_in_inline_math_ends_the_formula,
stray_brace_in_a_formula_is_deleted, stray_brace_ending_a_unit_construct_ends_the_formula,
alignment_cell_formula_keeps_its_recovery}`, `perfect_kernel_batch56::box_end_over_leaked_math_closes_it_into_the_box`;
repros `paragraph-mode/*` (REDs cell_end_in_inline_math_inserts_dollar, brace_meeting_left_group_in_inline_math_is_deleted,
forgotten_dollar_in_a_plain_group_keeps_the_text), boxes-groups/mbox_math_stray_brace_ends_box_not_math (GREEN).

### 556. `\lefteqn` in a first column is one cell that spans the empty cells after it (Perl: `\multicolumn{3}`)

latex.ltx:15800 defines `\lefteqn#1` as `\rlap{$\displaystyle #1$}`: a zero-width box inside its column's own u/v
template (tex.web §788 `init_col`, §789), its ink printed over the columns to its right. TeX does not span there: each
`&` closes the cell and opens the next preamble column whatever either holds (tex.web §791 `fin_col`), so the common
`\lefteqn{lhs}&&\nonumber\\` and `\lefteqn{lhs}&\\` rows are three-cell rows, 0 errors in pdflatex. Perl
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2194-2197) makes a first-column `\lefteqn` a `\multicolumn{3}{l}`, so those `&` overflow
the row (`Error:unexpected:&`, Perl and Rust alike; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #624), and the cells after it hold what they
held as overflow cells (text-mode math, nucl-th9512020).

**Rust** (batch 65o): the first-column `\lefteqn` is `\multicolumn{1}{l}{\lx@alignment@cell@overprint{ltx_eqn_lefteqn}
…}`. `\lx@alignment@cell@overprint` (tex_tables.rs, Rust-only) marks the current cell `Cell::overprint` and classes it;
`normalize_overprint_spans` (alignment/normalize.rs, between the cell sizes and `normalize_mark_spans`) extends an
overprinting cell's span, since HTML cannot overprint, over the cells after it that TeX shows nothing for, up to the
first that is not structurally skippable (`Digested::is_skippable`: spaces, empty or invisible boxes such as a
`\phantom`, the template's empty `$\displaystyle$` shell), spans or is spanned, and on over the cells a short row lacks
(amsmath's repeating templates; a row ended early has no boxes there, tex.web §§800-810) to the table's width. A cell
measuring under 1pt is not therefore empty: an `\index` or a `\hypertarget` anchor ends the span (a covered cell is
never absorbed). So the HTML keeps Perl's intent where the row is empty after the `\lefteqn` (one cell over the row:
`colspan="3"` in an eqnarray, `2` in an `array{ll}` or an `align*`, where Perl's 3 overran the two columns), and a cell
with content keeps its own column. The eqnarray's `_Capture_` carries the class, so `equationgroup_join_rows` classes
the row `ltx_eqn_lefteqn` as Perl Base_XMath.pool.ltxml:956-957 means to; in Perl it never fires. The class is in the
XML only: LaTeXML-block-xhtml.xsl writes the HTML row's own class (:703, :883), so LaTeXML.css's
`tr.ltx_eqn_lefteqn + tr` rule never meets it. Run 340's `&` cluster R1 (about 2,050 papers, 29 of 55 sampled): the 31
erroring witnesses go to 0 errors (0707.3929, 0801.4655, 0806.1442, 1103.1986, 1209.6494, 1409.4633, nucl-th9512020,
0810.2247, 0810.2511, 1104.3567, 1109.2680, 1203.3852, 1301.5488, 1411.3238, 1503.01263, 1701.08456, 1704.07012,
1706.08792, 1806.07473, 1903.02286, 2201.13255, astro-ph0111262, astro-ph0203455, cond-mat0209129, cond-mat9710308,
hep-lat9711012, math0102211, math0407427, math9806075, 2411.04274, 2609.03020; 2205.04522 stays at 0).

The `\multicolumn` cell of an eqnarray is text (its `$` is the template's): where more of the cell follows the
`\lefteqn` (`\lefteqn{\widehat G}\hphantom{G}^{(r)} &=&`, 2411.17699), the rest is math in TeX, so there the
`\lefteqn` is latex.ltx's `\rlap{$\displaystyle #1$}` inside the cell's math, still overprinting. An `array`'s or
amsmath's span keeps the rest in math, so they keep the span.

The decision rule (68z, sect07.rs `\lefteqn`, `LefteqnLookAhead`): the macro looks ahead without expanding the
input, as TeX would read the rest of the cell, and the `\lefteqn` is the whole cell when, past what prints nothing the
cell's math would hold, the next token is a tab or `\cr`, or has the meaning of `\\`, `\nonumber`, `\notag`, `\label`,
`\end` or `\tabularnewline`. Passed over: spaces, braces (`{}`, and into `{\nonumber}`), `\quad`, `\qquad`, `\,`,
`\;`, `\:`, `\!`, `\ `, `\enspace`, `\hfil`, `\hfill`, `\relax`, `\protect` (so a `\DeclareRobustCommand\nn
{\nonumber}` is followed to its inner macro), `\strut`, `\mathstrut`, `\hspace` with its `*` and argument
(2210.09695's `\hspace{1cm}\\`), `\vphantom` with its argument, `\hskip` with its glue and `\kern` with its dimension
(read by keyword, tex.web §448/§461: signs, a register or a factor and unit, `true`, `plus`/`minus` with `fil`). A
macro it meets is followed into its body, which is read the same way and then the input after it (`\def\nn
{\nonumber}`, `\def\eeq{\end{eqnarray}}`, `\def\rnn{\relax\nonumber}`, `\def\eq{&=&}`: the cell end is tested first,
so a body opening with a tab ends the cell; hep-ph0607130), through 8 expansions and at most 256 tokens. An end
command that is undefined or `\relax` (`\notag` without amsmath; latex.ltx's top-level `\tabularnewline`) matches only
by name, since `\protect` would equal it. Anything else, `\lefteqn{X}\quad y^2` and `\lefteqn{X}\hskip 1cm y^2`
included, keeps the cell's math. Known limits: the look-ahead does not expand conditionals or primitives other than
these (`\ifx`, `\csname`, `\@ifnextchar`-headed macros, `\@plus` in a glue read as letters: each keeps the in-cell
form); a macro with parameters is followed into its body without its arguments; any other unexpandable command
before the row end (`\lefteqn{X}\displaystyle\\`) keeps the in-cell form. That form, where the cell does end,
is a right-aligned cell that holds the zero-width box (round 1's layout); deciding at the cell end would need the
digested cell rewritten from the in-cell form to the span: not done. Repros alignment/lefteqn_then_script,
alignment/lefteqn_row_end_by_meaning, alignment/lefteqn_cell_end_forms; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch68z::{a_first_column_lefteqn_keeps_the_rest_of_its_cell_in_math,
a_lefteqn_before_a_row_end_macro_is_the_whole_cell, every_lefteqn_cell_end_form_is_the_whole_cell}`.

Residuals (RED repros): `\multicolumn{1}{l}` replaces column 1's template, so its `@{…}` material and `|` rules are
lost, which TeX's `\rlap`, inside the template, keeps (alignment/lefteqn_overprint_keeps_template_material; Perl's
`\multicolumn{3}` loses them too). An `\index` or anchor alone in the cell after the `\lefteqn` keeps its column but
is still dropped, by the alignment's size-based skip that every eqnarray cell meets (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #625,
alignment/eqnarray_side_content_only_cell); 65int2 kept it only as an overflow cell.

**Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batch65o::{lefteqn_spans_empty_cells, lefteqn_spans_empty_cell, lefteqn_array_two_columns,
lefteqn_cells_with_content, lefteqn_then_amp, lefteqn_stops_at_side_content}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch61::eqnarray_continuation_after_lefteqn_does_not_panic`, `53_alignment::eqnarray_test`; repros
`alignment/lefteqn_*`.

**Bounded overprint** (issue 736): nicematrix's `\Block{i-j}{text}` sets its text over an i×j rectangle whose other
source cells are empty (nicematrix.sty:7258-7300). `\lx@nicematrix@block@span` marks the anchor cell overprinting with
`Cell::overprint_columns = j`, which caps the span at `j` columns (a covered cell with text still ends it), and gives it
`rowspan = i` as `\multirow` does (`normalize_mark_spans` truncates it at a covered cell with text); `*` leaves that
side unspanned. Witness 2206.12224; guard `perfect_kernel_batchi736::nicematrix_body_features_keep_the_table`.

### 557. eqnarray has latex.ltx's fourth column, the equation number's (Perl: three columns)

latex.ltx:15756-15766 gives eqnarray's `\halign` four columns: the three of the equation and
`\hb@xt@\z@\bgroup\hss##\egroup`, the zero-width number column that `\@@eqncr` (:15789-15796) fills with `\@eqnnum`.
Columns 2-4 set `\@eqcnt` in their u-part; `\@@eqncr` reads it, pads the row with `&` to the number column, or raises
"Too many columns in eqnarray environment" if the row reached it, and resets it. A row ended by `\cr` may write in the
number column (`a &=& b &\cr`, 1804.05059; the text prints at the number's place, the row unnumbered). A fifth `&` is
tex.web §792's "Extra alignment tab", which TeX turns into `\cr`. Perl's eqnarray template
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2231-2236) has three columns, so the fourth `&` overflows (`Error:unexpected:&`) wherever
the row ends (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #624).

**Rust** (batch 65o): `eqnarray_columns` adds the text column (`\hfil` before: right-aligned, as `\hss##`), the
alignment records the equations' three columns (`eqnarray_columns` property; `_ncolumns` stays 3, so
`rearrange_eqnarray` reads the rows as Perl), and, for eqnarray only (`_number_column` on the group; an
`\IEEEeqnarray`'s cells are its specification's and stay as written), `drop_empty_number_cells` drops the trailing run
of empty cells past the third column, ending a span that reaches into it at the third column: eqnarray rows keep their
three `td`. An empty cell before a later one with content stays, since each `&` opens the next column whatever the
cell holds (tex.web §791), so `k &=& l & & EXTRA` keeps `EXTRA` in the fifth `td`; a trailing empty cell is an empty
unset box, set by `fin_align` as a row that ended before it (§§800-810), so dropping the run leaves what TeX prints. A
written fourth cell keeps its text in a fourth `td`, where Perl's overflow cell put it (now `align="right"`, was
`center`). `\lx@eqnarray@number@check` (sect07.rs), run by the eqnarray's `\\` (`\lx@eqnarray@newline`) and by
`\endeqnarray` / `\endeqnarray*`, raises latex.ltx's error, `Error:unexpected:eqnarray Too many columns in eqnarray
environment`, where the row has reached the fourth column; in the look-ahead before a cell the current column is the
one before, so `&\\` counts the cell it opens, as TeX's u-part does (pdflatex's three errors on the repro, ours three).
IEEEeqnarray (`eqnarray_bindings_with_columns`) has no number column and no check.

Known residual: the check reads the current row's column, which is pdflatex's count only for rows ended by `\\` or the
environment's end. A raw `\cr` skips `\@@eqncr`, so TeX's `\@eqcnt` is not reset and the next `\\` or end counts the
`\cr` row's column (pdflatex 2 errors, ours 0: RED alignment/eqnarray_cr_row_column_count); for the same reason a
`\cr`-ended row is unnumbered in TeX and numbered here, as in Perl (RED alignment/eqnarray_cr_row_unnumbered).

**Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batch65o::{eqnarray_number_column, eqnarray_number_column_too_many,
eqnarray_empty_cell_keeps_later_column}`, `perfect_kernel_batch64ra::eqnarray_extra_tab_keeps_three_columns`; repros
`alignment/eqnarray_number_column*`, `alignment/eqnarray_empty_cell_keeps_later_column`.

### 559. A `\multicolumn` paragraph cell lets `\\` to a line break inside its box; its nested alignments keep their own `\\` (Perl: the cell's `\\` ends the outer row)

latex.ltx `\multicolumn` (:16603) splices the column's whole `\@preamble` after `\omit`, so a `\\` (`\@tabularcr`)
in a `p{}`/`m{}`/`b{}`/`X` cell puts its `\cr` inside the open `\vtop` group: "Missing } inserted" in pdflatex, unless a
`\centering`/`\raggedright` in the cell has let `\\` to `\@centercr`, which makes it a line break of the cell's
paragraph (`\multicolumn{2}{|p{1cm}|}{\centering A\\ B}`: A and B stack in the merged cell). Perl's live
`\lx@alignment@multicolumn` is the second of its two definitions (TeX_Tables.pool.ltxml:704-713):
`\lx@alignment@altcolumn{<template>}\relax <body>`, whose `replaceColumn` makes the multicolumn's column the cell's
template, so the column's before and after tokens wrap the body; its `\\` ends the outer row: B becomes a new row
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #626). The cell's local changes end with it in TeX (latex.ltx:16603-16607 sets it in `\begingroup…\endgroup`): here `\\` is saved after the `\omit`s (`\let\lx@multicolumn@cr\\`) and put back after the cell, so a `\centering` in it does not reach the row's `\\` (1511.05496; repro `alignment/multicolumn_centering_then_row_end`); a whole group is not used, as it would also end the alignment state the cell reads at its close.

**Rust** (`tex_tables.rs` `\lx@alignment@multicolumn`) ports the first, overridden definition (:693-702), the column's
before tokens (through `beforeCellUnlist`), the body and the after tokens (through `afterCellUnlist`) spliced after the
`\omit`s (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #474), with `\let\\\lx@newline\let\tabularnewline\lx@newline` inside the box
group the before tokens open when the column is a paragraph column (`align=Justify`): after the column type's own
before tokens, ahead of its `>{…}` tokens (`Cell::prefix_at`, set by `Template::add_column`), so a prefix macro that
takes arguments takes the `\ignorespaces` and the body, not the `\let`, and an `\arraybackslash` there keeps the same
recovery (pdflatex: `\arraybackslash` lets `\\` to `\tabularnewline`, i.e. `\@tabularcr`, array.sty:247 and
latex.ltx:16576, so pdflatex errs as without it, "Missing \endgroup inserted" with array.sty loaded: tex.web do_endv
meets the cell box's group). The cell's `\\` is a line break, what pdflatex prints with `\centering` and the recovery of its error
without (that error is not yet a Warning: repro `kernel-alignment/multicolumn_pcol_plain_newline_unwarned`, RED); a
nested `tabular`/`array`/`tabularx` lets `\\` to its own row end and keeps its rows, and so does a math alignment in the
cell (`pmatrix`, `cases`, `array`, `aligned` collapsed into one row). This replaces a rewrite of the body's brace-depth-0 `\\`
tokens to `\lx@newline`, which also rewrote the row ends of a nested `\begin{tabular}…\end{tabular}` (an environment is
no brace group): its rows collapsed into one cell, a multi-column one overflowed ("Extra alignment tab", then "\noalign
cannot be used here" at the next `\hline`) and a one-column one lost its rows silently. And it replaces a re-boxing of
tabularx `X`/tabulary `J`/tabu `X` cells as `\lx@tabular@p t{}{…}`, whose empty width was a "Missing number" Warning and
`width="0.0pt"`; their `\vtop{` is spliced as Perl splices it, as in their ordinary cells. Witnesses 2607.14806
(4 → 0 errors), 2010.13561 (29 → 0), 1808.05579 (18 → 0), unchanged 1610.00974 and 1805.01525 (`L{5cm}` =
`>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}m{5cm}`).

**Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batch65p::{multicolumn_pcol_nested_tabular_keeps_its_rows,
multicolumn_pcol_nested_one_column_tabular_keeps_its_rows, multicolumn_x_nested_ruled_tabular_keeps_its_rows,
multicolumn_pcol_text_then_nested_ptabular_keeps_its_rows, multicolumn_pcol_embedded_newline_is_a_line_break,
multicolumn_pcol_pmatrix_keeps_its_rows, multicolumn_pcol_prefix_with_arguments_reads_the_body}`; repros
`kernel-alignment/multicolumn_*`. Open: pdflatex's `>{\two}p{3cm}` reads `[|]xy` (array.sty `\insert@pcolumn`'s
`\relax`), ours `[|x]y` as before 65p (RED repro `kernel-alignment/pcol_prefix_argument_takes_relax`).

### 562. A repeat load of hyperref takes its new options through `\hypersetup`; a package that requires its requirer back ends the cycle with an Info (Perl: the options are dropped; Perl marks the package loaded first)

A class binding may load a package its real class does not: revtex4_support (revtex4_support.sty.ltxml:23),
elsarticle (elsarticle.cls.ltxml:52), PoS, jmlr and sagej load hyperref. The author's later
`\usepackage[colorlinks]{hyperref}` is then a repeat load, which LaTeX would refuse with "Option clash" — but in real
LaTeX it is the first hyperref load, and colorlinks loads color (hyperref.sty:4532-4537). Perl drops the options
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #628), so `\textcolor`, `\color` and `\definecolor` are undefined (about 860 run-340 first errors).

**Rust** (batch 65r, `binding/content.rs` `apply_new_options_on_reload`): a binding may name its key-value setter in
`<file>_keyval_setter`; the options a repeat load has that the first did not are digested as `<setter>{options}`, with
an Info ("Applying options … from a repeat load"). hyperref names `\hypersetup`, whose `colorlinks` loads color. The
"Option clash" Info stays. Witnesses 2609.24844, 2609.13110, 1711.02465, 1904.06989 (PoS). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch65r::hyperref_colorlinks_after_class_preload`.

A binding-load re-entrance — a package required while it is itself being loaded — was a Warning. LaTeX ends such a
cycle silently: `\ProvidesPackage` defines `\ver@<file>` before the body runs, and Perl marks `<request>_loaded` before
`do $pathname` (Package.pm:2332). thm-restate.sty:26 and thmtools.sty:47-49 require each other, so a `.sty`/`.cls`
re-entrance is now an Info; any other (a pool, task #260's natbib loop) keeps the Warning. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch65r::thm_restate_loads_thmtools`.

### 563. amsrefs loads what amsrefs.sty loads, and `\bibselect` reads its database, printing the cited entries (Perl: no loads, no `\bibselect`)

amsrefs.sty loads url (:45-46), rkeyval (:213) and, unless `lite` (:179, :214-218), textcmds and mathscinet, so a
`\bib` entry's `\cprime`, `\germ`, `\scr`, `\Dbar` and `\url`, and a document's `\DefineSimpleKey`, are defined. Its
`\bibselect{db}` (:1291-1340) reads the records of `db.ltb` (`.ltx`, `.tex`) that start with `\bib`, writes the cited
ones (`\bibselect*`: all) to `\jobname.bbl` and inputs it. Perl's amsrefs binding loads nothing and has no
`\bibselect` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #627; about 1,860 run-340 first errors).

**Rust** (batch 65r, `amsrefs_sty.rs`): the loads as amsrefs.sty (rkeyval and textcmds, which have no binding, only
where raw loading is on); `\bibselect` reads the database records as `\ReadBibLoop` does (a record is a line extended
while its braces are open) and digests them; with no database shipped it inputs the author's `\jobname.bbl` (the
selection of their run). A non-starred selection marks its entries `class="ltx_bib_library"` (`bibtex.rs`
`{bib@entry}`), and the bibliography (`latexml_post` make_bibliography) prints those when cited, as the entries of a
`.bib` — an amsrefs `biblist`'s own `\bib`s stay printed whether cited or not (#57, 1012.2719). Also `{biblist}[…]`
and `{biblist*}` take their settings (`\resetbiblist`, :569, :651), `\BibSpecAlias` is ignored as `\BibSpec` is,
`\bysame` is its rule, `\ocite`/`\ocites` cite. Witnesses 1907.08888, 2602.02342, math0410226 (`\cprime`, `\germ`),
1904.05225 (`CF.ltb`), 2103.06687 (`.bbl`), 2604.08274 (`\DefineSimpleKey`), 1904.00652 (`\resetbiblist`). **Guards**:
`perfect_kernel_batch65r::{amsrefs_loads_mathscinet_url, amsrefs_lite_rkeyval}`,
`06_cluster_bibliography::{amsrefs_bibselect_database, amsrefs_bibselect_star_database}`.

### 567. `\newcommand` with an optional argument also defines LaTeX's internal `\\cs` (Perl: only `\cs`)

latex.ltx:1245-1257 `\@xargdef` makes `\cs` `\@protected@testopt\cs\\cs{<default>}` and puts the macro reading `[#1]`
under the internal `\\cs` (`\csname\string\cs\endcsname`). Perl's `\newcommand` builds one macro that reads its optional
argument itself (`convertLaTeXArgs`), so code that calls the internal directly found it undefined: the amsart idiom
`\edef\cs{\@dblarg\csname\string\cs\endcsname}`, copied by bcp.cls:151-153 for `\abtitle` and cmfne.cls:460,483, left
`\@abtitle` unset, and `\uppercasenonmath\@abtitle` then built a definition containing itself (Fatal
`Stomach:Recursion`; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #638).

**Rust** (batch 66b, sect08.rs `define_optional_internal`): every declarator built on `\@xargdef` with an optional
argument also defines `\\cs` with the same body, its first parameter the bracketed one: `\newcommand`, `\renewcommand`,
`\providecommand`, the begin macro of `\newenvironment`/`\renewenvironment` (`\@newenv`'s `\new@command`,
latex.ltx:1324-1331), and `\DeclareRobustCommand`'s inner `\cs␣` (:1412-1428; internal `\\cs␣`); a starred
declarator's internal is not `\long` (`\l@ngrel@x`). `\cs` itself is unchanged. A `\renewcommand`,
`\DeclareRobustCommand` or `\newenvironment` the lock refuses still defines its internal, as `\@xargdef` does: only the
class's own `\csname\string\cs\endcsname` reaches it, and the replay of a refused class setter goes through it
(cmfne.cls:462-483 `\renewcommand{\author}[2][]` + the `\@dblarg` `\edef`, whose `\enddoc@text` prints
`\firstshortauthor`: 2210.02246 lost its two author lines while the internal was skipped). No binding defines or calls a
`\\cs` internal; a locked `\renewenvironment` is refused whole (its stores recorded), and a `\newcommand` of a defined
name defines none, as LaTeX's. Residuals: the internal reads `[…]` as
an optional argument, as our `\@yargdef` does, where LaTeX's requires the brackets; an active character gets none (its
`\string` names another control sequence). The internal is named as `\string` prints the command: the null control
sequence's is `\\csname\endcsname` (tex.web §263) — named `"\\" + "\"`, it was `\\` itself, so
`\expandafter\newcommand\expandafter{\csname\endcsname}[1][x]{…}` (changes' `\csname\Changes@commandname\endcsname`
with its `\Changes@commandname` undefined in our binding) replaced the line break, and a `{#1\\}` body recursed to a
Fatal (2410.07647: F 1 → 0, 870 → 23,196 words; int131fix, guard
`perfect_kernel_batch131fix::null_cs_optional_internal_keeps_the_line_break`). Witnesses 1510.00296, 1704.01336, 1207.2066, 2003.00661 (Fatal → 0 errors), 2210.02246 (cmfne's author lines).
Guards `perfect_kernel_batch66b::{newcommand_optional_argument_defines_its_internal_macro,
every_xargdef_declarator_defines_the_internal_macro, refused_dblarg_setter_reaches_its_internal}`; repros
`macro-state/newcommand_optional_internal_cs`, `sectioning-frontmatter/refused_dblarg_setter_reaches_its_internal`.

### 568. A locked robust binding locks its inner `\cs␣` against the files (Perl: the wrapper only)

A robust binding is the wrapper `\protect\cs␣` around its body under `\cs␣` (Package.pm `defRobustCS`); the lock was
recorded for `\cs` alone, so code that defines the inner by name took over every call. cmfne.cls:1772-1778 (cite.sty's
code, copied) runs `\@namedef{cite }{…\@citex…}` with `\def\@citex[#1]#2{\@cite{\citen{#2}}{#1}}`; under our cite
binding's `\let\citen\cite` (Perl cite.sty.ltxml) the kernel `\cite` reached the class's inner, which called `\cite`
again (Fatal `Stomach:Recursion`).

**Rust** (batch 66b, `def_macro`): a locked robust macro records `"\cs␣:locked@files"` as well, so raw class and package
code redefining the inner is refused as the wrapper is; the document's own definition of the inner (its
`\DeclareRobustCommand\cite`, or `\@namedef{cite }` in the preamble) stays its own, as in Perl. A file's `\let` of a locked
robust binding to another robust command (a class's `\let\cite\mycite`) takes `\let`'s plain path rather than #315's body
copy, which wrote the inner past the lock (guard `robust_let_over_a_locked_binding_keeps_its_inner`). A locked binding
whose inner is free (a constructor: the kernel `\LaTeX`) keeps the copy, whose wrapper the lock refuses, at every
origin but where D1 accepts the document's own override (`owns_calls` and a copied body that takes no argument):
bera.sty:12-23 `\let\LaTeX=\fveLaTeX` keeps the logo (the enumitem, colorspace and mathador manuals lost it while
every locked binding took the plain path, which leaves plain `:locked` to `\let`; guard
`robust_let_over_a_locked_constructor_keeps_it`, repro `macro-state/robust_let_over_locked_constructor`). Perl's `Let`
(Package.pm:383-390) checks no lock and takes bera's logo, as pdflatex does; a `\let` to a non-robust meaning takes the
plain path here too (bera.sty:10-11 `\def\fveTeX`, `\let\TeX=\fveTeX`, replaces `\TeX`), so the outcome follows the target's
kind — 65int8f's behaviour, kept. Residual: the refused wrapper records `:redefined@nargs` 0 (state.rs, the dropped
definition) even when the copied body takes arguments, so a class's `\let\abstract\myabs` (robust, `[1]`) is not read as a
stored-argument setter. Only the kernel
`\cite` is a locked robust macro today. The robust constructor path (`def_constructor`) records the lock under
the inner name only, the other half of the same asymmetry; no witness needs it. Witnesses 2210.02246, 2303.09770 (Fatal
→ 0 errors). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch66b::locked_robust_cite_keeps_its_inner_definition`; repro
`macro-state/locked_robust_inner_cite`.

### 569. A lock against the files holds for their `\let` too; a binding's read-to-end environment locks both halves

`:locked@files` (#453: the kernel minipage; the abstract's end half, sect05.rs) refuses a class's or package's
redefinition while leaving the document free; `install_definition` applied it to a `\def`, but `\let` checked nothing (as
Perl's `Let`, Package.pm:383-390, checks no lock). arabtex's asect.sty:297 `\let\endabstract\endquotation`, called by its
own raw `\end` (alatex.sty:105-109), closed the kernel abstract's body as a quotation (2401.14559, 2 errors).

**Rust** (batch 66c, `state::let_i`, TeX's `\let`): a `\let` from a class or package file of a name carrying
`:locked@files` is refused; a plain `:locked` is still left to `\let`, as in Perl, and so are the engine's own meaning
writes (`assign_meaning`: `\csname`'s `\relax`, `with_let` restores). A `\let` to an undefined token (expl3's
`\cs_undefine:N`) only clears the name and is kept: projlib-author.sty:243-246 backs up and undefines
`\abstract`/`\endabstract` before its `\newenvsc{abstract}`, whose `\NewDocumentEnvironment` errs "End of environment
'abstract' already defined" on a name still defined (the homework and jwjournal manuals). The binding is kept aside
(`"\cs:locked@cleared"`) and put back when the file's new meaning for the name is refused (`restore_cleared_binding`, from
`install_definition` and `let_i`), whether the name is still undefined or `\csname` has made it `\relax` on the way
(`\@namedef`, ltcmd's `\cs_set_eq:cc`), so the binding's other callers (a raw `\end`) still meet it. The lock is read at
the origins `install_definition` reads it at (all but the document's). The binding comes back once: the stash is
consumed, so a `\relax` the document gives the name later stays its own (guard `a_cleared_binding_is_restored_once`). The same rule for a
binding whose begin half reads its body to the end: mn2e_support's `{keywords}` (`\lx@begin@keywords`) locks both
`\keywords` and `\endkeywords` against the files, since mn2e-breakabs.sty:87-95 (shipped by MNRAS papers) redefines the
end half alone as mn2e.cls's `\endlist` (1403.3615, 1607.03149), and a file redefining both halves would otherwise have
its begin half taken and its end half refused; mn2e.cls:992 `\ifSFB@keywords` is defined. Residual shared with #453: the
lock reads the origin at run time, so a class's `\AtBeginDocument{\let…}` runs as the document's. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch66b::{file_let_*, refused_*_of_a_cleared_name_restores_the_binding, mn2e_*}`; repros
`macro-state/{file_let_of_locked_end_half, file_let_clearing_locked_name}`.

68x extends the keeping aside to a plain `:locked` binding: a file's `\let` that clears one goes through, as in Perl,
and the binding comes back when a refused new meaning finds the name still cleared (state.rs `let_i`):
eulerpx.sty:130-132 `\let\mathscr=\undefined` then `\DeclareMathAlphabet\mathscr{U}{zeus}{m}{n}`, refused by the lock
on the kernel's `\mathscr` (sect07.rs), left `\mathscr` undefined (2311.14793, 2501.10505, 2510.26876: 1 Error each;
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #863). The binding, not the refused redefinition, is what comes back: the lock keeps the kernel's
semantic markup, and Euler Script is a script alphabet as the binding's is. Repro
macro-state/plain_locked_binding_cleared_by_a_file_comes_back; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68x::a_plain_locked_binding_a_file_cleared_comes_back`. The plain lock refuses the document's
redefinition as it refuses a file's, so the document's own clearing `\let` keeps the binding aside too (68x r2; the
`:locked@files` branch keeps its origin test, since that lock leaves the document free): `\let\mathcal\undefined
\DeclareMathAlphabet{\mathcal}{OMS}{cmsy}{m}{n}` left `\mathcal` undefined, `\let\mathscr\relax` before
`\DeclareMathAlphabet{\mathscr}{U}{rsfs}{m}{n}` lost the script font; a binding a package's group-local clear set aside
is replaced by the current one. A document value-definition after the restore still reaches the binding's call owner
(#500). Repro macro-state/plain_locked_binding_cleared_by_the_document_comes_back; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68x::a_plain_locked_binding_the_document_cleared_comes_back`. The lock still wins
over the document's own new meaning after its clearing `\let`: `\let\footnote\relax\newcommand\footnote[1]{}` keeps
the kernel's footnote, which pdflatex drops, as a plain locked `\renewcommand\footnote` is refused (Perl
State.pm:507-515; review 68x r2 probe p12).

### 575. AMS-TeX's `\tag` recovers where TeX errs

AMS-TeX's `\tag` takes its text to the display's `$$` (`\def\tag#1$$`, amstex.tex:597-605) or, in a row, opens the
row's tag cell without an argument (`\def\tag{\global\tag@true…&&}` in `\align`, :633-635; `\def\tag{&}` in `\gather`,
:797). Perl's `\let\tag\eqno` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #643) errs on these shapes too, in its own way. Measured with pdftex
(TL 2025, `\input amstex`, `\input amsppt.sty`, `\document`; each shape followed by a paragraph and `\enddocument`):

| shape (in `$$\align … \endalign$$`) | pdftex | ours |
|---|---|---|
| `a&=b\tag 1\displaybreak c&=d` | 4 errors ("Extra alignment tab has been changed to \cr" twice, "Misplaced \crcr", "Misplaced \noalign": the measuring pass's tag cell is `\eat@{##}`, :655); tag "(1c)" | 0 errors, tag "(1)" on its row |
| `a&=b\tag 4\par\\ c&=d` | 8 errors, from "Paragraph ended before \align was complete" (`\csname align \endcsname#1\endalign`, :667/:687, not `\long`); the alignment is lost | 0 errors: the `\par` ends the tag cell |
| `a&=b\tag{3\par}\\ c&=d` | 9 errors (the same, and "Too many }'s") | 0 errors: the `\par` stays in the tag's text, `(3)` |
| `a&={b\tag 2} c\\ e&=f` | 100 errors ("Argument of \maketag@@@@ has an extra }" and "Paragraph ended before \maketag@@@@" twice each, 47 "Missing \cr inserted", 46 "Misplaced \cr", …), Fatal, no PDF | 0 errors: the `}` ends the tag cell, `(2)` |
| `a&=b\tag{5\\ c&=d` | 3 errors ("Paragraph ended before \align was complete", "Missing $ inserted", "Display math should end with $$"; "Forbidden control sequence found while scanning use of \align" when the `\outer` `\enddocument` follows the display); the alignment is lost | 1 error ("Missing } inserted before the row's end in \tag"); see below |
| `{\it … $$\align a&=b\tag{5\\ c&=d\endalign$$ …}` | 3 errors, as the row above; the alignment is lost | 1 error, as the row above; the `{\it` group and its text after the display kept |
| `\vbox{… $$\align a&=b\tag{5\\ c&=d\endalign$$ …}` | 4 errors (the same three, then "You can't use `\end' in internal vertical mode"), then Emergency stop; Fatal, no PDF | 1 error, as the row above; the `\vbox` and its text kept |
| `a&=b\tag{{3\par}5\\ c&=d` | 9 errors, as `\tag{3\par}\\` | 1 error, as `\tag{5\\`; the tag is "(35)" |
| `a&=b\tag{{5\\ 6}\par c&=d` | 7 errors (as `\tag 4\par\\`, less "Invalid use of \\"); the alignment is lost | 3 errors: "Missing } inserted …" twice, then "Missing { inserted" at the second row's `&`; the `}` after the row's end closes the next row's cell-template `{` (`$\displaystyle{##}$`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #908, 69c), and the `&` meeting the count −1 gets its `{` (tex.web §1127 `align_error`, 70b), so both rows are kept, "(5)" on the first (before 69c: 3, that `}` closing the display, the alignment lost; 69c: 2, the `&` taken for the cell end with no v-part) |
| `a&=b\\ c&=d\tag{5 e` and `\enddocument`, no `\endalign` | 3 errors ("Forbidden control sequence found while scanning use of \align" at the `\outer` `\enddocument`, amsppt.sty:1091; "Missing $ inserted", "Display math should end with $$"); the alignment is lost | 1 error ("Missing } inserted …"); the document ends; the open row's last cells are dropped, with or without a tag (RED `amstex/amstex_align_unclosed_at_enddocument`) |

On rows 1-3 and 5-10 TeX's errors are not `\tag`'s: they come from `\align` reading its body as a non-`\long` argument
and from the measuring pass. On row 4 they are the tag cell's own: its template reads the cell as `\maketag@##\maketag@`
(amstex.tex:678, :700), and `\maketag@@@@#1\maketag@` (:604) meets the `}` closing the group opened before the tag
("Argument of \maketag@@@@ has an extra }", then its runaway). Content comes first, so the row tag keeps the author's text
and errs only where the tag's text cannot end.

**Rust** (batch 66e, amstex.rs `amstex_tag`): in a row (an AMS-TeX alignment's, or a LaTeX equation row's when the
AmSTeX pool is loaded, which no `\tag#1$$` governs either) a `\par` outside the tag's own groups, or a `}` closing a
group opened before the tag (an enclosing group's `}` too), ends the tag cell with the text read so far and no error; it
is never read into the tag. A `\par` inside a group of the tag stays in its text if that group closes before the row's
end (`\tag{3\par}\\`, `\tag{{3\par}5…`). A row's or environment's end (`\\`, a token meaning `\cr`, `\endalign`, a
display end, `$$`, the document's end `\enddocument` or `\bye`) read while a group of the tag is open stops the scan at once (`\tag{5\\ c&=d\endalign$$`): TeX's
`\cr` inside a cell's braces is "Missing } inserted" (tex.web §1126-1127), so the tag raises it once per open group
(TeX does so at depth 1 and 2 only: at depth 3 or more `align_error`, tex.web:21562-21563, finds `abs(align_state)>2`
and reports "Misplaced \cr", dropping the `\cr`), or TeX's runaway error ("Paragraph ended before \tag was complete") when a `\par` was read in a group still open there;
it keeps the text up to the earlier of that `\par` and that end, closes its groups, and the input is read again from
there (`close_runaway_row_tag`, which retracts the kept braces from the alignment ledger). The file's end raises "File
ended while scanning use of \tag" with the same recovery. A `$` opening inline math inside a row's tag cell or a group
of the tag is paired with the `$` closing it, which is never the start of `$$` (`\tag{$a$$b$}\\`, `\tag $a$$b$\\`:
two inline maths, as in TeX's restricted horizontal mode, tex.web §1138); only the `$$` form's own level matches `$$` as
tokens (`\def\tag#1$$`). The document's end (`\enddocument`, amsppt.sty:1091, and `\bye`, both `\outer` in TeX) is never
read into a tag: in a row it is a row end as above; in the `$$` form it is TeX's "Forbidden control sequence found while
scanning use of \tag" and the call is dropped (tex.web §336-339). The next row, the alignment, an enclosing group, every later
paragraph and `\enddocument` are kept. Trade-off of this fail-safe rule: a row tag whose braces hold an inner
alignment's row end (`\tag{$\matrix a\\b\endmatrix$}\\`, which TeX sets, the inner `\halign` resetting `align_state`)
stops at that `\\`; no braced tag holding a row end, a `\par` or `matrix` occurs in a scan of 10,000 arXiv source zips
(9204-9608, about 1,000 braced tags). The `$$` form keeps TeX's errors (tex.web §395-396). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch66e::{amstex_row_tag_ends_at_every_row_ender,
amstex_row_tag_cell_ends_at_par_and_extra_brace, amstex_row_tag_open_group_stops_at_the_row_end,
amstex_tag_in_latex_equation_row_ends_at_extra_brace, amstex_tag_stops_at_the_document_end,
amstex_tag_inline_maths_are_not_a_display_end}`; repros `amstex/amstex_row_tag_runaway_group`,
`amstex/amstex_row_tag_open_group_in_enclosing_group`.

### 576. `\begin{document}` opens the `.aux` under the job's name, as latex.ltx's `\document` does (Perl: none)

latex.ltx's `\document` (:9491-9494) does `\if@filesw \immediate\openout\@mainaux\jobname.aux
\immediate\write\@mainaux{\relax}\fi`, so the `.aux` exists from then on. Perl's `\begin{document}` opens none; its only
open is `latex_base`'s `\openout\@mainaux\jobname.aux` (latex_base.pool.ltxml:722), run when LaTeX.pool loads. Without
a preload that is at `\documentclass` (TeX.pool.ltxml:33-39), after `\jobname` is installed (Core.pm:152), and the
in-memory `.aux` (TeX_FileIO.pool.ltxml:120-126) is found by a later `\input` (Package.pm:2104). With the format
preloaded (a preload such as `ar5iv.sty`, as on arXiv) it runs when the state is initialized (Core.pm:143), before
`\jobname`, so the stream is not under the job's name. Ours (latex_base.rs:743) ran at that early point too, or, under a
dump, at the dump's build, whose `output_file:*` streams the dump does not keep. A class or package `\enddocument` that does `\input
\jobname.aux` under `\if@filesw` (jpsj3.cls:90-96, bio.cls, lamuphys.sty:1240-1247, caosp.sty:916) then met
`Error:missing_file:<jobname>.aux`. Ours opens it in `\begin{document}`'s after-digest (latex_constructs/sect02.rs) in
latex.ltx's place, so the `\input` reads the in-memory `.aux` (its `\relax` and whatever the document wrote). `\nofiles`
stays Perl's no-op (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3773, sect11.rs), so `\if@filesw` stays true. Witnesses 2605.24927,
2605.04825, 2605.28673, 2605.20125, cond-mat9607109, astro-ph9805185 (each 1 error → 0, text unchanged). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66f::jobname_aux_exists_after_begin_document`; repro `loader/jobname_aux_exists_after_begin_document`.

### 577. nicematrix `[opacity=…]` fills are flattened against a white page

nicematrix.sty:5605-5616 (`\__nicematrix_color_opacity:w`) reads a `\CodeBefore` color command's optional argument as
keys: `opacity=` sets the PDF fill opacity (`\pgfsetfillopacity`) over whatever lies beneath. Our cell and row fills are
plain CSS background colors, so `opacity=o` is rendered as the color mixed with white at `o` — what the PDF shows on a
white page and the same on a white HTML page, but not over a colored or dark background. Perl has no nicematrix binding.
Witness 2605.25123 (`\columncolor[opacity=0.2]{blue}{3}`, "Unrecognized color model" Error before). Code
latexml_contrib/src/nicematrix_sty.rs (`nice_color`); guard `perfect_kernel_batch66f::nicematrix_color_opacity_key`.

### 578. `\hypertarget` in math: an empty anchor, its text after the mode test

hyperref.sty:4805-4811 (nesting off, its default :323) sets the destination and then `#2` in every mode
(`\hyper@@anchor{#1}{\relax}#2`); Perl (hyperref.sty.ltxml:258-266) digests `#2` as the anchor's own text in every mode.
In text ours keeps Perl's shape (the anchor holds its text, `anchor_own_text`). In math, where an `ltx:anchor` holds no
math, the anchor is empty and `#2` follows it in place, so a brace-less call takes one token there and a formula opened
by it stays whole (`\hypertarget{e1}` before `\left( \frac{n}{p}\right)`: 2606.15438's `\left(` read as the anchor's
text was closed at that argument's end, its `\right)` "Extra"). `#2` comes after the conditional: hyperref's own `#2`
sits before its `\fi`, so a brace-less `\hypertarget{e2}\frac{n}{p}` has `\frac` read `\fi` as its numerator
(pdflatex `\showbox`: the destination, an empty-over-n fraction, then p); ours renders n over p. A `\relax` before
`\ifmmode` (amstex.tex:72's `\RIfM@`) keeps a row-initial call in `align`/`aligned`/`array` on the math branch, where
TeX is still expanding in search of `\omit` before the cell's math begins. Open: the math anchor's `xml:id` is generated,
not the target's name, so a `\hyperlink` to it dangles, and the anchor parses as an operand (RED
`package-bindings/hypertarget_math_anchor_keeps_its_id`). Code hyperref_sty.rs `\hypertarget`/`\lx@hypertarget`; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66f::hypertarget_braceless_in_math`.

### 579. The article/report/book bindings define `\fnum@figure`/`\fnum@table` as the tag LaTeXML composes (Perl: undefined)

article.cls:457/469 (report, book alike) define `\fnum@figure`/`\fnum@table`; Perl defines neither and composes the
tag in `\lx@@fnum@@` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:1041-1056), which an undefined `\fnum@<type>` falls back to. Code that
takes their current body then found nothing: babel's ini caption templates (babel.sty:2959-2965
`\gdef\fnum@table{…{\[fnum@table]}…}`, for a language loaded on demand such as Lithuanian) captured the undefined token
itself, and the new `\fnum@table` called itself at the first caption (2605.29738: Fatal IfLimit; Perl loops too, KPE
#654). Ours defines each as `\lx@@fnum@@{figure}`/`{table}` in the article, report and book bindings, where LaTeX's
classes define them, and every caption's tag is the one composed before; a class or package `\def`/`\renewcommand` of
them works as in LaTeX. Residual: letter.cls, without floats, defines neither, but has no binding, and the OmniBus it
falls back to loads the article binding; so a letter-based class's `\newcommand` of them (newlfm.cls:1006/1012), which
LaTeX accepts, is ignored with an Info `Ignoring redefinition`, and its captions keep the composed tag. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66h::babel_ini_caption_template_needs_fnum`.

### 580. The algorithm2e binding loads no float package (Perl: float)

algorithm2e.sty loads no float package: its float is its own `\@float{algocf}` (algorithm2e.sty:2487-2488). Perl's
binding requires float (algorithm2e.sty.ltxml:37), and so did ours, which put float's binding where TeX has none. Beside
floatrow (floatrow.sty:34 marks float loaded and carries its interface) that replaced floatrow's `\float@end` with
float_sty.rs's no-op whichever came first — after floatrow, float's binding redefined it; before, floatrow's
`\newcommand`s were refused — and every restyled float's box stayed open (`\endgroup` errors; 1811.04370, 2007.08784,
1609.05867, 1910.09976, 1807.05059: five of the nine floatrow papers of the run-347 `\endgroup` drill-down; the other
four load float themselves after floatrow, which floatrow.sty:34 makes a no-op in LaTeX, KPE #668, open). The binding's
float frames and top caption are float_sty.rs's Rust helpers (`add_float_frames`, `reposition_caption_top`), which need
no load. A document using float's commands (`\restylefloat`, `\newfloat`) with algorithm2e and without
`\usepackage{float}` now finds them undefined, as in LaTeX. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66m::algorithm2e_beside_floatrow_keeps_floatrows_end`.

### 581. `\lstinline` is robust (Perl: expandable)

listings.sty:1941 `\newcommand\lstinline[1][]{…}` is `\@protected@testopt`: under `\@unexpandable@protect` it stays
unexpanded. Perl's `\lstinline` (listings.sty.ltxml:54) is an expandable macro, and ours was too: its expansion opens
the inline listing's group (listings_sty.rs `\lx@lstinline` `bgroup()`, as Perl's `$STATE->getStomach->bgroup`), so in
our engine an `\edef`/`\xdef` that should keep it ran it. ifthen's `\ifthenelse{\equal{\lstinline|N|}{}}` evaluates
its test in an `\xdef` (ifthen.sty:101-110), and the group it opened met the `\endgroup` after it (ours: 1406.5453
729 errors, 1605.05104 89; Perl's run of the repro gives 0, its recovery not traced). Ours defines it `protected`. Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch66m::lstinline_robust_in_ifthen_equal`.

### 587. A MetaPost figure gets the fonts dvips would download (Perl: the figure fails to convert)

MetaPost's default PostScript (`prologues:=0`) is not self-contained: its text is `(S) cmmi10 9.96265 fshow`, the fonts
are named by their TeX names and listed only in `%*Font:` header comments, which dvips reads to download them when it
includes the figure (`finclude.pro` supplies `fshow`) — so arXiv's PDF shows them. Ghostscript alone stops at
`/undefined in cmmi10`; Perl's ImageMagick path and ours reported `Error:imageprocessing:failed_to_convert` and left the
figure out (about two thirds of the run-349 image-conversion Error papers; 40/40 sampled were MetaPost). Before converting,
ours does what dvips does (`latexml_post/src/postscript_fonts.rs`, called from `graphics.rs` `convert_image`): a copy of
the figure gets, before its `%%EndProlog`, each listed font's Type1 program (TeX Live's `pdftex.map` entry, the `.pfb`
through kpathsea, inlined as PFA), its TeX name bound to the font, and MetaPost's own `prologues:=1` `fshow`; the copy is
converted and removed. Fonts whose map entry re-encodes (`ptmr8r`) or is missing are not supplied — the figure fails as
before. Witnesses gr-qc0001079 (`foliation.ps`), math0102124 (38 figures), cs0005010 (34): each E → 0; guard
`postscript_fonts::tests::metapost_figure_gets_the_fonts_dvips_would_download`.

### 588. Under the ar5iv preload, `\url`/`\href` are hyperref's when nothing defined them (Perl: undefined)

arXiv's build loads hyperref into every paper (a 00README `nohypertex` opts out; 2101.07380's PDF says "LaTeX with
hyperref" though its source never loads it), so a paper that uses `\url` or `\href` with neither url.sty nor hyperref
loaded builds there; pdflatex alone, Perl and we stopped at "Undefined control sequence" (812 `\url` + 473 `\href`
papers live in run 349, ~80% of a 40-paper sample loading neither package). Provide-only (user ruling 2026-10-14): the
ar5iv preload (`latexml_contrib/src/ar5iv_sty.rs`) queues `\lx@arxiv@provide@hyper@urls` at `\begin{document}`, which
defines whichever of the two is still undefined as hyperref's (`hyperref_sty.rs` `define_hyper_urls`, shared with the
hyperref binding), with url.sty's default `\UrlFont`/`\UrlLeft`/`\UrlRight` where missing. A paper that loads either
package, or defines the command itself in its preamble or in an `\AtBeginDocument` hook, keeps its own; nothing is
supplied without the ar5iv preload, and hyperref is not loaded for every paper (the rejected option). The supplied `\url`
is locked as the hyperref binding's is (OD #500), so a `\renewcommand\url` in the document body is ignored with an Info.
hyperref loads url.sty, so url.sty is then loaded provide-only too (67q): its `\path`, `\urlstyle`, `\urldef` and `\Url`
for the names still undefined. An elsarticle-num `.bbl` defines `\path` only when `\href` is undefined, and its
`{\path{doi:…}}` entries were undefined once `\href` was supplied (2605.07373, 2605.08166, 2605.12003). Witnesses
cond-mat0407333, cs0409028, hep-th0411273, 1001.4826 (`\doi` → `\href`); guards `perfect_kernel_batch67a`.

### 592. A binding standing in for a class or package takes the algorithm packages from the paper's copy of that file

The algorithm packages differ between copies of one class or package, by version and by the paper's own edits: every
ICML style as distributed loads `algorithm` and `algorithmic` (icml2016.sty:70-71 … icml2025.sty:95-96), and papers
that use algpseudocode comment `algorithmic` out of their copy (icml2024.sty:94 "removed due to conflict with
algpseudocode", 2402.05403), since loading it first bails algorithmicx (algorithmicx.sty.ltxml:9-12, Perl alike) and
leaves `\State`/`\For` undefined; WileyNJD-v2.cls:3331 and WileyNJDv5.cls:6820 load `algorithm, algorithmicx,
algpseudocode` (one copy `algorithm2e`, 2002.02812); bmvc2k.cls `algorithm` with `algorithmic` or with `algpseudocode`
by year; pnas-new.cls:110-111 `algorithm` and `algpseudocode[noend]`; edited copies of neurips_2023.sty (2402.18905)
and siamltex.cls (2210.03478) load them where the distributed files load none. Perl has no binding for the classes and
scans the paper's copy from OmniBus (Package.pm:2776-2813), so for them this is Perl's own behaviour. For icml20xx.sty
it is beyond Perl (as pdflatex): Perl's `FindFile_aux` tries the versioned-name fallback binding before a raw copy it
is not interpreting (Package.pm:2135-2138; the glued suffix `[vV]?[-_.\d]+`, :2180, maps icml2017 to icml.sty.ltxml),
which loads the distributed pair whatever the copy says (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #684). Our bindings
stand in for them (icml_support_sty.rs `load_icml_style` for icml2016-2025, icml2019_sty.rs after its raw read, icml_sty.rs
when it answers a versioned fallback such as `icml2026` or `./icml2018`; wileynjd_cls.rs, bmvc2k_cls.rs, pnas_new_cls.rs,
siamltex_cls.rs, neurips_sty.rs), and loaded either the distributed ICML pair or no algorithm package at all. Now each
calls `shipped_class::require_shipped_algorithm_packages`: the dependency scan (`require_dependencies_only`,
content.rs) of the file being loaded (the load's `\@currname`, or the request a versioned fallback answers,
`fallback_request`), kept to `ALGORITHM_PACKAGES`, so the copy's choice, order and options win; without a copy, the
ICML binding keeps the distributed pair and the others load none (as OmniBus has nothing to scan).
Perl's icml_support.sty.ltxml, reached by name from icml.sty.ltxml for `\usepackage{icml}`, still loads the pair; Perl's
neurips.sty.ltxml loads none, and a shipped neurips.sty copy now adds its algorithm packages (beyond Perl, as
pdflatex). The scan's comment pattern also drops a comment on a last line without its newline (Perl's `s/%[^\n]*\n//gs` keeps it), which a
`{filecontents}` copy has. Run 349: `\State` 560, `\For` 470, `{algorithm}` 544 papers. Witnesses 1706.03643,
1706.04918, 1706.04933, 1706.04964, 2002.06473, 2106.05074 (icml); 1810.03033, 1810.12033, 2106.06046, 2402.13183,
2506.07013 (Wiley); 2210.06270, 2210.01640 (bmvc2k); 2402.10236 (pnas-new). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch67l::{icml_style_copy_decides_the_algorithm_packages, icml_style_without_a_copy_keeps_the_distributed_pair,
wileynjd_class_copy_loads_its_algorithm_packages, wileynjd_class_copy_with_algorithm2e,
bmvc2k_class_copy_loads_its_algorithm_packages, icml_versioned_fallback_follows_the_copy,
neurips_copy_loads_its_algorithm_packages}`.

### 593. In maths an old font command switches the math alphabet to the group's end, as latex.ltx's `\@fontswitch` (Perl: the alphabet takes the next token)

latex.ltx's `\DeclareOldFontCommand#1#2#3` is `\DeclareRobustCommand#1{\@fontswitch{#2}{#3}}` (14309-14311), and
`\@fontswitch` (14312-14321) in maths lets `\math@bgroup` to `\relax` before `#2\relax`: the alphabet `\mathrm\relax`
reads the `\relax` as its argument and selects its math group to the end of the enclosing group, so `{\rm LP-HF}` is
`LP-HF` upright. Article/book/report/letter's `\cal` and `\mit` are `\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal` / `\mathnormal`.
Perl's `\@fontswitch` (`\ifmmode #2\relax\else #1 \fi`, latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:5200) and `\DeclareOldFontCommand`
(a closure returning the bare `#3`, :5315-5320) run the alphabet with its own grouping, so it reads the next token
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #685). We follow latex.ltx: `\@fontswitch` is `\ifmmode\lx@math@alphabet@switch{}{#2}\else#1\fi`
(sect13.rs), and an old font command's maths branch is `\lx@math@alphabet@switch{<its name>}{#3}`. The switch merges the
font an alphabet's binding carries (`font => {…}` on the constructor or primitive, kept on the definition as
`Definition::declared_font`: `\mathrm`, `\mathbf`, `\mathcal`, `\mathbb`, every `\DeclareMathAlphabet`'d one) into the
current font, as the native `\rm`/`\bf` primitives do in maths (plain_constructs.rs), and reverts as the old command's
name (`{\rm LP-HF}`; through `\@fontswitch` directly, as the alphabet: `{\mathcal H}`). The name travels as a character
string, so an `\edef` in maths cannot expand the command into itself. In TeX the `\relax`'d `\math@bgroup` makes
any alphabet `#2` expands to a switch, so the switch looks through parameterless macros with a token body and
`\protect` (a robust command's `\protect\X␣`) up to 16 deep (`math_alphabet_font`): `\newcommand\Bbbx{\mathbb}`
`\DeclareOldFontCommand{\bbx}{\normalfont}{\Bbbx}` makes `{\bbx RZ}` a blackboard R and Z, as pdflatex sets them
(`\U/msb/m/n/10`). A `#2` that reaches no font-carrying alphabet that way — a macro with an argument, a closure-bodied
macro, a body that begins with anything else (`\def\Bbbx{\relax\mathbb}`) — is TeX's `#2\relax`, which is
latex.ltx's behaviour when `#2` is not an alphabet and a residual when it is one reached otherwise. The text branch is latex.ltx's `#1` (Perl's `#1 ` set a space after `{\cal x}`'s `\relax`). It shows when a
raw-loaded class or package re-declares the old font commands: under the ar5iv rawclasses lever 511 outputs had an
empty `\math..{}` (ptptex 306, jpsj2 98, paper 71, artikel1 12) and about 8 papers new errors; under the bound article
classes `\rm` is the native switch and was already right. Witnesses jpsj2 cond-mat0510381, 0711.1066, 1004.2823;
ptptex gr-qc0605108, 0804.3840, 1101.1147, hep-th0507073; paper math0405417. Repro
fonts-nfss/old_font_command_switches_math_alphabet; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch67r::{old_font_command_switches_the_math_alphabet,
old_font_command_switches_package_and_declared_alphabets, old_font_command_alphabet_through_a_macro}` (repro
fonts-nfss/old_font_command_alphabet_through_a_macro).

Residual (deferred): through `\@fontswitch` directly the box reverts as the alphabet, so a multi-token group's `tex=`
does not round-trip: `{\cal AB}` reverts as `{\mathcal AB}`, which TeX reads as `\mathcal{A}B` (base: `{\mathcal{}AB}`,
with the content wrong too). There is no standard switch form of `\mathcal`, and `\@fontswitch\relax\mathcal` round-trips
only under `\makeatletter`. The only direct `\@fontswitch` users in TeX Live's standard classes are article.cls:497-498
`\cal`/`\mit` (and the book/report/letter copies), which the kernel binds natively (reverting as `\cal`); a sound
round-trip would revert as `\cal`/`\mit` when `#2` is `\mathcal`/`\mathnormal` and that command's current robust body is
exactly `\@fontswitch\relax<alphabet>`.

### 596. amsthm's `{proof}` is kept against a class or package that copies it (Perl: the file's environment replaces it)

amsthm_sty.rs locks `\proof` and `\endproof` against the class and package files (`:locked@files`, state.rs
`name_carries_lock`), as the kernel's `\endabstract` (sect05.rs) and `\minipage` (sect12.rs) are, but only against a
COPY of amsthm's interface (`\proof:locked@copies`, state.rs `files_lock_holds`): a redefinition whose first parameter
is an optional argument with a non-empty default (`takes_optional_first`) — amsthm.sty:431's own
`{proof}[1][\proofname]`, which smfart.cls:1194, smfbook.cls:1281, ijmart.cls:336 or thuthesis.cls:4052
(`[1][\thu@proof@name]`) re-implement over a `\trivlist`. A robust copy (`\DeclareRobustCommand\proof[1][\proofname]`)
is judged by its inner `\proof␣`, as `owns_calls` judges a robust binding (its own meaning is the parameterless
`\protect\proof␣`); an ltcmd copy (`\RenewDocumentEnvironment{proof}{O{\proofname}}`) is not read as one and goes
through (no TeX Live file defines the proof either way). Perl locks nothing there (amsthm.sty.ltxml:146-192,
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #690). A copy's `\renewenvironment{proof}` is skipped (`\renewenvironment` reads `lock_holds_against`,
sect08.rs), its `\newenvironment` after a clearing `\let\proof\relax` is refused and the binding put back
(`install_definition`, `let_i`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch67s::package_redefined_proof_keeps_the_binding`), and the
proof stays `<ltx:proof>`, titled from the optional argument or else the refused copy's own default
(`record_redefined_default`, `\proof:redefined@default`, recorded only under this lock; it is never empty, an empty
default not being a copy), so the class's language and name still title it (smfart.cls:1288 "Démonstration",
thuthesis's `\thu@proof@name`); with no copy refused, `\proofname`. A redefinition with a head of its own — no optional argument, or an empty default
(fascicules.sty:142 "Démonstration:", NotesTeX.sty:124, beautybook.cls:1211, thmbox.sty:214 `[1][]` with `\proofname\
#1`, a raw `\def\proof{…}`) — goes through with the head text and end mark it wrote; the end half `\endproof` follows
its begin half (locked while `\proof` is still the binding's). The lock keeps the binding only while its proof is in
force: once the document (or a definition the lock let through) has replaced or undefined `\proof`, it lapses and later
definitions go through as in LaTeX (amsart, the document's `\let\proof\undefined\let\endproof\undefined`, then a
package's `\newenvironment{proof}[1][Nachweis]`: pdflatex "Nachweis."; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch67ps::proof_lock_lapses_once_the_document_undefines_it`). 0705.0545 (the same `\let`, then the
author's nccthm.sty:173 `\newcommand*{\proof}[1][]`) goes through on the copy rule alone, its default being empty
(`perfect_kernel_batch67ps::proof_lock_passes_an_empty_default`). It is not set by a borrow (`require_package_borrowed`, theorem.sty's and
ntheorem.sty's bindings: LaTeX has no amsthm proof there, so a class's `\def\proof` after `\RequirePackage{theorem}`
stays its own), nor by the real load that follows a borrow when a file or the document has already put its own proof in
place (amsthm.sty:431's `\newenvironment{proof}` fails over it in LaTeX; the binding then leaves `\proof`/`\endproof`
alone, with an `Info:ignore`). The document's own `\newenvironment{proof}`/`\renewenvironment{proof}` is honoured, as in
LaTeX and Perl (an author `{proof}` in paper.cls papers), and so is a class's redefinition made from an
`\AtBeginDocument` hook, which runs with the document's origin (rawclasses study R7): GT.cls:1469-1470 `\let\proof
\relax` at class level, then its copy `\newenvironment{proof}[1][\proofname]` inside `\AtBeginDocument` (:1488-1494),
so 2503.05183 keeps the class's trivlist (as on a03442572a), a residual of this rule. apxproof builds on the binding's
proof: its parameterless wrappers (apxproof.sty:393-417 `\def \proof`, sending a `theoremrep`'s proof to the appendix,
read back as `\begin{axp@oldproof}`) are not copies and go through, so apxproof_sty.rs needs no lift of the lock
(witness 2502.18805, whose 53 proofs otherwise stayed in the body). Residuals of a kept copy: its head layout, font,
case and punctuation do not carry (smfart's ` — ` after the head, ijmart's slanted head, isamms's small caps;
theoretics.cls:418's `\MakeTextUppercase{#1}`, so 1609.05867's "PROOF SKETCH." is "Proof Sketch."), and its end mark is
the binding's ∎ (theoretics's red `\blacksquare` `\qedsymbol`; a copy that prints no QED gets one). The lock covers the
names `\proof`/`\endproof` only: a file's `\newtheorem{proof}` after amsthm still defines the `\begin{proof}` that
`\begin` looks up first and makes a `<theorem>`. Under the raw-class lever 86 papers had lost every proof (smfart 72,
ijmart 11, smfbook 3; witnesses 1711.11547, 1902.02049, 2108.12000); without the lever the copies in papers' own classes
keep their proofs (jloganal.cls 1202.3460, theoretics.cls 1609.05867, gtart_h.cls math0003189, gtart.cls math0203159,
math0302254, math0412216, smfart.cls 2309.14926; not GT.cls 2503.05183, the `\AtBeginDocument` residual above). Repros
package-bindings/{amsthm_proof_kept_against_a_class_renewenvironment, amsthm_proof_lock_lets_a_hardcoded_head_through,
amsthm_proof_copy_titled_by_its_default, amsthm_proof_lock_lapses_after_the_document_undefines_it,
amsthm_proof_lock_passes_an_empty_default, amsthm_proof_lock_holds_against_a_robust_copy,
theorem_borrowed_proof_yields_to_a_class_def}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch67s::{class_renewed_proof_keeps_the_binding,

The older sn-jnl.cls copies load program (sn-jnl.cls:311 of 1812.02207's copy, :621 of 1911.08756's; 106 of 148
sampled copies), and sn_jnl_cls.rs's scan of the class now loads it, for the `\gt`/`\lt`/`\union` its papers use
(138 run-353 papers). program.sty:175-176 also redefines `\(` as `\begin{programbox}` (a `\textwidth` minipage around
a `{program}`, :165-173), which the papers of these copies write as inline maths; pdflatex sets them in the line
(2112.05038 on 413 lines: "For a domain Y ⊂ Rn, there exists…"), where the raw emulation made each an `ltx_minipage`
inline-block holding a one-item `ltx_trivlist` list (1331 in 2112.05038). sn_jnl_cls.rs puts the kernel's `\(`/`\)`
(`\lx@begin@inline@math`, sect07.rs) back after the class's loads when program loaded; program's other definitions,
the active `;` included, stay. Program loaded under another class, or by the document's own later
`\usepackage{program}` (the test sits in the class binding, right after its scan), keeps the programbox. The faithful
alternative was to drop the two lines (every `\(…\)` an inline-block). Approved by the main session 2026-10-15: the

`perfect_kernel_batch67u::snjnl_class_copy_loads_program`.

### 605. The dependency scan skips a package the document marked loaded (`\ver@<name>.<ext>`; Perl: records only)

A binding's dependency scan (`content.rs::require_dependencies_filtered`, Perl `maybeRequireDependencies`,
Package.pm:2776-2810) stands in for the scanned file's own `\usepackage`/`\RequirePackage`/`\LoadClass` lines, and LaTeX
skips such a line when `\ver@<name>.<ext>` is defined and not `\relax` (latex.ltx:18750 `\@onefilewithoptions` →
`\@ifl@aded`, :18397-18402). The scan now does the same for a candidate our own records (`_loaded`/`_raw_loaded`) say
is not loaded, with `Info:dependencies:<file> Skipping dependency <file>: it is marked loaded`
(`marked_loaded_unrecorded`). The marker may come from the document, from a class or package read raw (memoir's
`\EmulatedPackage`, imakeidx.sty:61 `ver@makeidx.sty`, xcolor.sty:315 `ver@color.sty`) or from a binding (biblatex's);
LaTeX skips the line for each alike. Perl tests only its records (Package.pm:2328-2330), so it would load the package — the
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #780 gap, latent there. Witness 2201.11056: sn-jnl-setup.sty suppresses sn-jnl.cls:311's
`\usepackage{program}` through `\AddToHook{class/sn-jnl/before}`, which our scan loaded (active `|`, pgf broken,
`oom`). Scan-only by ruling (main session 2026-10-16): `\usepackage`/`\RequirePackage` keep the records-only test (user
ruling 2026-10-14, no general loader `\ver@` rule — floatrow_sty.rs records float/rotfloat loaded rather than setting
their markers, ams_support_sty.rs reads amsart.cls's own `\ver@amsthm.sty`, subcaption_sty.rs describes a document's
`\@namedef{ver@subfig.sty}`). Repro loader/scan_skips_document_marked_loaded_package; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch68f::scan_skips_a_package_the_document_marked_loaded`.
