### 720. tkz-euclide's pre-v3 `\usetkzobj`/`\usetkztool` are defined over the current package (TL 2025: undefined)

tkz-euclide v1-v2 loaded its object files with `\usetkzobj{all|<objects>}` (tkz-tools-eu-modules.tex:18-58, still in
TeX Live but no longer read); since v3 the package loads every object itself (tkz-euclide.sty:173-199) and the loaders
are gone, so a paper written for the old API errs under TL 2025 ("Undefined control sequence"). User ruling 2026-10-17:
the binding serves both versions. The contrib binding (tkz_euclide_sty.rs) reads the real package and defines the two
loaders, where neither is defined (a paper's own older copy keeps its own), as macros that take their arguments and load
nothing, since everything is loaded. Witnesses 1506.03598, 1612.05374, 2005.14485, 1906.04134, 1608.04592; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch71a::tkz_euclide_old_usetkzobj`.

### 721. A TeX macro's undelimited argument that is a command reading a mandatory argument is read with its own arguments, the call the author wrote, with a Warning that TeX errs there (amsmath/amsfonts accents, mathstyle scripts; TeX: an error; Perl: no diagnostic)

amsmath's accents (amsmath.sty:754-797, `\mathaccentV`'s fifth argument, `\mathaccent"…{#5}`), amsfonts' `\widehat#1`/
`\widetilde#1` (amsfonts.sty:78-87) and breqn/mathstyle's `\sb`/`\sp` (mathstyle.sty:126-127,
`\mathsub{\protect\subsupstyle#1}`, the math-active `_`/`^`) take their accentee or script as an undelimited macro
argument and brace it, so a macro after them is the item with its whole expansion (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #945; breqn's, SYNC
71a (7)). The bindings pass that argument to LaTeXML's own accent or script through one helper (amsmath_sty.rs
`undelimited_argument`: `\lx@ams@mathaccentV` for amsmath, `\lx@undelimited@argument` for the others), which reads a
single command by its definition, never its name (user ruling 2026-10-17; `classify_undelimited_argument`, looking
through a robust wrapper's parameterless `\protect <cs>` to `<cs>` — a robust command's `\protect \cs␣`, the binding's
`\ensuremath` = `\protect\@ensuremath` (`\hat\ensuremath{x}`: pdflatex 5 errors) — and an alias's one-token body,
amsmath.sty:892 `\def\Hat{\hat}`):
- **no mandatory argument** (`\alpha`, `\nabla`, `\infty`, `\relax`, `\bf`, `\muu`, `\newcommand{\tasknum}[1][]{…}`, an
  undefined command): braced, as TeX braces it, with no diagnostic — `\hat\relax x` is the hat over an empty nucleus
  and x after it, as TeX's `\showlists`. Under amsmath's `\mathaccentV` an amsmath accent (`\hat\vec x`) is the nested
  accent: braced, itself over an empty nucleus (`\macc@nested`, :832-870; `\showlists`: the hat over the vec over an
  empty box, x outside). Only that reader nests: under amsfonts' `\widehat#1` or breqn's `\sb#1` an amsmath accent is a
  command reading a mandatory argument (`\widehat\hat z`: pdflatex 7 errors; breqn's `y^\hat z`: 6, "Argument of
  \mathaccentV has an extra }"), read as the next case;
- **a mandatory argument** (`\mathbf`, `\text`, `\mathrm`, `\newcommand\nv[1]`, `\DeclareRobustCommand\vv[1]`, amsfonts'
  `\widehat`): the command read with its own arguments, the call the author wrote. A macro's arguments are read by its
  parameters (an ltcmd command's by its signature: `m`, `o`/`O{…}`, `s`, through the `\cs code` of an all-`m` one) and
  reverted, and the call braced, so the accent or script takes the call's whole expansion: `\hat\foo x+y`
  (`\def\foo#1{}`) is the hat over `\foo x`'s empty expansion and `+y` after it, `\hat\pair{a}{b}` over `(a,b)`,
  `\hat\nv x` (`\nv[1]{#1_1}`) over `x_1`, `\hat\vq[a]{x}` (`{om}`) over `\vq[a]{x}`. A primitive or constructor
  (`\mathbf`, `\sqrt`, `\text`) is left unbraced: the item it makes is the call, its arguments read at digestion
  (`\hat\mathbf{x}` a hat over the bold x, breqn's `x_\text{abc}` a subscript "abc"). A call missing an undelimited
argument where the next token ends or structures the current list (`read_call_arguments`, `ends_the_list`: by meaning a
column end — `&` or a `\let` copy, `\cr`, `\crcr`, `\span` — and a catcode-6 token; by name `\par`, `\\`, `\end`, `\]`,
`\)`; the end of the input) is left unbraced, its arguments read so far put back, as TeX leaves the tokens: the braced
call would take a cell's `&` or a row's `\\` into its group (`\hat\pair{a} & x` in `cases` keeps both cells, `\hat\nv
& = 1` and `a &= \hat\nv \\ y &= 2` in `align` their cells and rows). A `\def` with a leading delimiter
  (`\def\lp(#1)`), an ltcmd signature with a delimited or embellishment argument and a binding closure without a
  parameter list are left unbraced for the item to read with what follows. Each occurrence gets one
  `Warning:malformed:<reader>` naming the reading made, e.g. "amsmath's \hat takes \pair alone as its argument, where
  TeX errs: \pair reads an argument of its own; read as \hat{\pair{a}{b}}" ("read as \hat{\mathbf…}, \mathbf with its
  argument" for a constructor; breqn's names `_`/`^`, what the author types), located at the source line (a heading's,
  item's or theorem's text is digested from a token list; the innermost source mouth's location is given). pdflatex:
  "Argument of \select@group has an extra }", "Argument of \text@ has an extra }", 5-9 errors for one such accent;
- **a binding closure** (an expandable definition without a token body, or a conditional): unbraced as before, since
  a closure may read past the brace; the Warning only where it declares a mandatory parameter, the one case in which
  TeX's macro would err.
One Warning per source occurrence: a digestion that re-reads a source the document typesets where it stands gives none
(`tex_math::REREAD_COPY`, set by `\lx@reread@copy`): the toc copy of a heading or caption without a `[short]` (sect04.rs;
`\lx@toc@copy@text` for the kernel's, longtable's and listings' captions, where a `[short]` the same as the caption — as
`\@dblarg` gives it — counts as the caption), the reference forms of a tag (`\lx@make@tags`: an `\item[…]` label's
typerefnum, a `\tag{…}`'s refnum), natbib's label copies (written to the .aux; a full compile errs nowhere — pdflatex run three times on
`\bibitem[{$\hat\mathbf{x}$}(2000)]` gives 0 errors — so no Warning is TeX's own count). A
`[short]` title or caption is its own source, digested once, into the toc: TeX errs on it only when the list is typeset
(`\tableofcontents`, `\listoffigures`), and it warns once regardless, because we digest and keep it.
Why not error as TeX does: content before PDF fidelity (priority order 2026-10-06), where TeX's recovery loses the
formula — under the braced form 2210.10207 lost 11,424 words — and the shape is rare (7 occurrences in 7,500 sampled
1505/1905/2305 papers, most of them in unused macros: 1905.01764 7, 1505.00442 1); why the Warning: the source is not
valid TeX, and the reading is ours (ruling: never an Error, never silent). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch71a::{amsmath_accent_macro_argument, amsmath_accent_ltcmd_argument,
undelimited_argument_reads_the_whole_call, undelimited_argument_call_stops_at_the_list_end,
undelimited_argument_through_a_robust_wrapper, amsfonts_widehat_macro_argument, breqn_script_macro_argument,
undelimited_argument_warning_once_per_occurrence}`.

### 725. latex209.def's LaTeX2e-command traps apply to `\usepackage`, `\listfiles`, `\lrbox` and `\@xargdef`; the `\ensuremath` trap is held while bindings call it where their 2.09-era originals do not

**TeX**: `\documentstyle` inputs latex209.def, whose :79-91 wrap `\usepackage`, `\listfiles`, `\ensuremath`, `\lrbox`
and `\@xargdef` in `\@latex@e@error`, enabled by `\@documentclasshook` (:137): each use after the class errs "LaTeX2e
command … in LaTeX 2.09 document" and then runs; :105-123 let the document define the 2e-only names it lists.

**Perl**: none of latex209.def is applied (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #925).

**Rust** (int20, user ruling 2026-10-17): tex_job.rs `\lx@latex@ix@definitions` applies :79-123 and :137 except the
`\ensuremath` wrapper. Our bindings call `\ensuremath` in code their originals write without it — AASTeX 4
aaspp4.sty (1995, shipped with astro-ph9606031) `\def\fd{\hbox{$.\!\!^{\rm d}$}}` against aas_support_sty.rs
`\ensuremath{\@fd}` (Perl-origin aas_support.sty.ltxml L499), REVTeX 3, emulateapj — so the trap fired on binding code
pdflatex never runs: astro-ph9606143 7 → 9, astro-ph9701025 1 → 15, cond-mat9906271 0 → 6, astro-ph9809336 45 → 48,
astro-ph9806372 2 → 4 (A/B over the 250 `\documentstyle` papers of the census sample, none of them calling
`\ensuremath` in the source). The trap lands with a kernel-internal ensure-math for binding code (SYNC row). Residual:
latex.ltx's "`\usepackage` before `\documentclass`" (`\@fileswithoptions`) that pdflatex adds is not reproduced. No census paper uses
`\usepackage` after `\documentstyle` (0806.0904 redefines it: `\def\usepackage#1{\input{#1.sty}}`, no trap in pdflatex either). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch70b::documentstyle_usepackage_errs_as_latex209`.

### 731. A stand-in binding is followed by the paper's copy of its file, which only provides ("a stand-in's copy provides") — absorbs #732 #733 #736 #744

**The one rule.** After a stand-in binding has loaded, the copy of its file the paper ships is read raw at the same point
and provides only what the binding lacks: a name the binding owns keeps the binding's meaning for the document (the
copy's own code sees its own), a locked name is refused, a counter, a text default or a saved meaning the binding's
load did not make is the copy's (`binding/content.rs:2518 read_stand_in_copy`, `:2945 copy_is_the_stood_in_file`;
`state.rs:2178 note_copy_provides_assignment`, `:2805 leave_copy_provides_frame`, `:2258 copy_provides_refuses_locked`).
Rules 0-14 below are its sub-rules; the members after them are #732, #733, #736 and #744.

**TeX**: `\documentclass{svjour3}`, `\usepackage{aas_macros}`, `\input tcilatex` read the author's file the paper ships;
every definition in it, and everything it registers for later, takes effect.

**Perl**: `FindFile` prefers the `.ltxml` (Package.pm:2113-2133): the binding loads and the copy is never read, so an
extra command the copy defines and the paper uses is undefined (aas_macros.sty:94-97 `\kms`, 1309.5950).

**Rust** (72a, user ruling 2026-10-17, memory `feedback_rulings_2026_10_17_od721_h1`): after a binding on
`AUTHOR_FILE_STAND_INS` (author_files.rs) has loaded, the copy the paper ships — the request as the paper wrote it
(`fallback_request` for a versioned fallback: `icml2026` → icml2025.sty), found in the paper's source directory or a
`{filecontents}` file, never TeX Live's — is read raw at the same point, origin `File` (content.rs `read_stand_in_copy`,
from `input_definitions_impl` after the binding's `\ver@` and from `input`'s `.tex` route), before the load's
`\AtEndOfClass`/`\AtEndOfPackage` code runs. The rules:
0. *Identity.* The copy is read only when it is the file the binding stands in for (content.rs
   `copy_is_the_stood_in_file`; 72a r3 rule): (a) its `\Provides(Expl)?(Class|Package|File)` names the binding that
   answered (the file itself when the binding is of its name; #744), or a file the binding is built on — one its own code loads (`state::note_stand_in_file`,
   `stand_in_built_on`) —, a declared macro read as its definition in the copy says, as `\ProvidesClass` expands its
   argument (r4: cimart.cls:13-14 `\def\ClassName@CiM{cimart}\ProvidesClass{\ClassName@CiM}`, 2412.00032), whatever
   the version (1609.03892's fcs.cls of 2016, older than the `\fcssetup` the binding
   models; 2308.11432's `\ProvidesExplClass{fcs}`; 2011.13564's IEEEtai.cls, IEEE's own, `\ProvidesClass{IEEEtran}`, the
   class the binding loads; apjfonts.sty, 1202.3442); else (b) it defines at least a quarter of the binding's public
   command set, the letters-only names its own code assigned with those of a stand-in its own code loads
   (`state::stand_in_public_names`, `State::stand_in_last_load`, merged at `end_stand_in_load`: the diagrams binding's
   diagrams.tex; not a file it loads otherwise, `StandInLoadGuard::suspend`, nor a stand-in such a file loads —
   `StandInLoadGuard::loaded_by`, r4: OmniBus's `RequirePackage!("aas_macros")`, omnibus_cls.rs:71, swelled asme2ej's
   set from 22 names to 87 and nature-pre's from 3 to 68, so 2309.12017, 2102.01782 and 2111.09589 went unread). A binding with no public name of its own
   reads no undeclared copy (aipcheck.tex, mssymb.tex, citesort.sty, revtex.sty: 45 of the simulation's copies). The quarter is the
   gap of a bimodal distribution: over the reviewer's simulation of the census's 4,346 distinct copies
   (`scratch_356a0c47/rev72a/ident_sim2.json`; approximate: the binding's `.rs` names, no nested stand-ins), the
   undeclared copies' shares fall 124 under a tenth, 28 between a tenth and four tenths, 1,028 above; the quarter
   admits the 1,047 the r2 rule read by names, and its absolute (20 names) and copy-side (a quarter of the copy's
   names) clauses admitted none beyond it, so they are gone. Per clause on the simulation under the r4 rule
   (`scratch_72a/r4/tools/ident_r4.py`): declaration 3,071 (2,987, and 84 of a binding whose public set is empty),
   names 1,046 (cimart's one copy now by declaration), empty set and no matching declaration 45 not read, 133
   rejected (107 arxiv/PRIMEarxiv/icml2019 copies their binding reads raw itself, rule 4), 51 whose binding file the
   simulation could not map; the one copy near the quarter (0.225-0.275) was cimart's. The simulation's public sets
   approximate the runtime's (nature-pre: 5 there, 3 here, so its two copies read at 1 of 3). An author's own
   file that only shares the name is not read (base behaviour): hep-ph9609379's diagrams.sty, fifteen `\special`
   PostScript macros sharing one name (`\diagram`) of the diagrams binding's 270 (r1: its `\Bullet` called the
   binding's `\diagram`, 1 → 101 Errors and a Fatal); 2411.02780's equations.sty, which is annotate-equations.sty
   renamed (`\ProvidesPackage{annotate-equations}`; r1: 2 → 99 Errors over xkeyval's `\usevalue`). Logged at Info.
   Reading such a file raw, as TeX does, is an open row.
1. *Ownership* (a routed copy's declared text names: rule 14; a copy under the binding's own name supplies none). A
   name is the binding's when it was assigned while the stand-in binding loaded (origin.rs `StandInLoadGuard`,
   `State::stand_in_meanings`: its `DefMacro!`s, `Let!`s, `RawTeX`, the bindings it required) at an origin of
   LaTeXML's own, its guesses included (`Fallback`: the OmniBus base a class binding loads, whose `\received`
   WileyNJDv5.cls:5071 replaced, dropping 2609.19994's dated frontmatter — OD #408's yielding is to the document, and
   the copy is not the document), or its meaning is a definition made under that very name at origin `Unknown`, `Pool`
   or `Binding` (a pool's `\maketitle`, another binding's `\citep`), or under one of the semantic layer's own `\lx@`
   names (79i: the pool's `\let\label\lx@label`, sect11.rs — no file defines an `\lx@` name; a shipped aastex7.cls's
   `\def\label` writing the `.aux`, aastex7.cls:635, aastex701.cls, siamltex.cls, emulateapj.cls, jasatex.cls, stood
   for the document and recorded no label: 2508.00291, 2510.05388, 2604.27071, 1205.2995, 1409.5957, 1412.0148; 16 of
   24 such proj98 papers now resolve every reference, 519 → 158 dangling; guard
   `perfect_kernel_batch79i::a_copy_redefining_label_keeps_the_documents_labels`); an environment is owned when `\begin{X}` or
   `\end{X}` is, or `\X` or `\endX` with them, and its names are decided together (r5): once the copy's code has kept
   one aside, the others it defines are kept too, though the first now carries the copy's meaning (cimart.cls:295-315's
   `\newtheorem{theorem}` left the binding's `\begin{theorem}` with the copy's `\end{theorem}`, a group open at the
   end: 2412.00032, 2408.07575's `{example}`); a plain macro's `\end…` partner alone does not make it owned (plain's
   `\endgroup`, a copy's `\group`). OmniBus's theorem autoload stubs (`\begin{theorem}` … `\begin{alg}`, which step
   aside for an environment declared since) are `Stub`, not a definition of the environment, so a copy's `\newtheorem`
   declares it whole (omnibus_cls.rs; pdflatex "Definition 1.1", "Theorem 1.2" on the reviewer's probe thm_copy).
   *Text defaults* (main-session ruling 2026-10-17, 72a r5): a public macro without parameters expanding to text
   (`\refname`, `\bibname`, `\abstractname`, `\contentsname`) that the base class the binding loads assigned last —
   a class its own code loads, and the classes that class loads, the pool's article/report/book and the OmniBus guess
   (`StandInLoadGuard::suspend_for`, `State::stand_in_base_defaults`) — or LaTeXML's kernel before the binding, is not
   owned (`state::unowned_text_default`): the copy's `\def`/`\renewcommand` of it holds, and its `\newcommand` defines
   it (`copy_provides_text_default_yields`, sect08.rs), as the real class's would over article.cls's — MRM.cls:3191
   `\def\refname{REFERENCES}` (2506.14995's PDF), ws-rv9x6.cls:91 `\newcommand\bibname{References}` (2301.03442).
   One the binding's own code assigns, or a binding it requires (natbib's), stays owned; natbib's `\bibname`/`\refname`
   are provided as natbib.sty:1093-1094 provides them (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #960). The format's names (`Plain`, `LatexDump`, `Format`), the document's world (`File`, `Document`), the
   other guesses that yield (`Fallback`, `Stub`, `Borrowed`) and `\let` copies of such meanings are not — except a
   `\let` LaTeXML's own code made while a stand-in binding loads, recorded as it is made (`State::binding_lets`,
   `let_i`, r4: not every pool `\newif` flag; the object a `\let` copies carries its source's name; aas_support_sty.rs's
   `\let\subjectheadings\keywords`, astro-ph0011001). Measured and
   declined (72a r2): narrowing ownership to the binding's own code, so that a copy's redefinition of a macro a package
   the binding loaded defined stands as in TeX, released the class bindings' frontmatter and layout macros to the copy
   (`\title`, `\author`, `\thanks`, `\keywords`, `\@makecaption` in 146 of 400 census papers, the NFSS size commands,
   the `\the<counter>`s) and brought back aastex7's three Fatals; constructors and primitives kept owned did not
   cover them (they are macros). The case it was for, 2411.02780, is rule 0's.
2. *Assignments.* Every meaning assignment of the read (`install_definition`, `assign_meaning`: the `\def` family,
   `\let`, `\chardef`…, the LaTeX declarators) to an owned name holds only inside the copy's own code: the binding's
   meaning is kept aside and put back when the read ends (state.rs `note_copy_provides_assignment`,
   `leave_copy_provides_frame`), so for the document it acted as `\providecommand`, while the copy's load-time logic
   sees what it defined, as in TeX — aipproc.cls:559 `\ifnum\pageref>0` after its option's `\chardef\pageref`
   (astro-ph0105128), epl2.cls:1317-1318's save-and-wrap of `\bibitem`, which the epl binding makes too and which a
   kept `\let` would turn into a self-call (0906.2627, 1102.2776, 1203.4765: Fatal loops before the rule). This
   refines the brief's "declined" by mechanism (the census hazard 4: a declined scratch name changed the copy's
   load-time logic); a name the code leaves as it found it (`\protected@edef`'s `\protect`) is not logged. Everything
   else stands as TeX makes it: the copy's extras, kernel scratch, earlier raw files' names. Not while the state is
   unlocked (a binding's `before`/`after` code run for the copy, an `AddToMacro!` append); the copy's own code runs
   locked, as a raw read does, also its `\AtEndOfClass` code run inside `\documentclass`'s unlocked after-digestion
   (asme2ej.cls:1230-1244 `\AtEndOfClass{… \def\newtheorem …}`, 2210.14434). A name the copy `\let`s to its own
   version of an owned name takes the binding's meaning back with it (`CopyProvidesFrame::assigned`): emulateapj5.sty:386
   `\def\keywords`, :394 `\let\subjectheadings=\keywords` (astro-ph0011001, a "Subject headings:" paragraph where the
   binding makes `<keywords>`). *Counters* (main-session call 2026-10-17, 72a r3): a counter's representation
   (`\the<ctr>`, `\p@<ctr>`) and reset list (`\cl@<ctr>`; `\@addtoreset`, `\numberwithin`, `\counterwithin`, a
   re-`\newcounter`) are owned only when the stand-in binding's own load assigned them (`counter_part`,
   `copy_provides_keeps_counter`): the pool's article defaults yield to the copy, as article.cls's own would to the real
   class — jheppub.sty:313-314 `\renewcommand{\theequation}{\thesection.\arabic{equation}}` and
   `\numberwithin{equation}{section}` number (2.1) as its PDF does (2112.14648, 2607.20603; r2: "(1)" … "(60)"). The
   read is no raw class read for K11 (`\lx@class@loaded@raw`): the binding owns the title page. *A command saved again*
   (77w): a `\let\org\X` of the copy, where `\org` already holds an earlier meaning of `\X` (a `\let` copy made under
   `\X`'s name) that the binding's load assigned, while `\X` still holds the binding's later meaning (the copy's read
   has not assigned `\X` itself) and that meaning reaches `\org` (its body, or a body it names, transitively:
   `state::meaning_reaches`), is declined in the copy's own code too (`state::copy_provides_keeps_saved_meaning`, Info):
   `\org` keeps the meaning TeX gives it, `\X` before the redefinition. The binding (or a file it read) made the same
   save-and-wrap, and the wrapper saved into `\org` calls itself when the copy's own code uses it: myjmlr.cls and
   jmlr_mod.cls (jmlr.cls copies, rule 12) run `\let\jmlr@org@newtheorem\newtheorem` (jmlr.cls:753-754; the jmlr
   binding's jmlrutils.sty makes the same wrap) before their own `\newtheorem{example}`, which looped to the timeout
   (1506.02582, 2304.14217). A `\let` whose new meaning does not reach the name, or whose source the copy's read has
   just assigned, is no such wrap and stands: pgf's scratch `\let\pgfutil@reserved@c\pgfutil@reserved@b`, run by
   `\usetikzlibrary` while a self-named sn-jnl.cls copy is read, was declined at int40a and the copy's
   `\usetikzlibrary{snakes}` lost (2207.07492: 0 → 6 Errors), and where `@b`'s loop body names `@c` the declined `\let`
   left pgf's recursion spinning to the timeout (2101.08181's lmcs.cls copy: 3 s → Fatal Timeout); guards
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::{copy_loads_a_tikz_library, copy_runs_its_own_loop}`.
3. *Locks.* A locked name is refused as for any file, but without the records a raw class's takeover leaves
   (`\lx@dropped@<name>`, `<cs>:redefined`, defaults; OD #265, #500): `copy_provides_refuses_locked`, so no replay of the
   copy's `\maketitle` body.
4. *No second read.* A copy already read raw — by its canonical path (content.rs `RAW_READ_PATHS`, kept out of the
   dumped state; `load_tex_definitions`) or as `<file>_raw_loaded` — is not read again: the 17 stand-ins whose
   bindings `InputDefinitions!` their copy (arxiv,
   cvpr, iccv, PRIMEarxiv, wacv, icml2019, pasj00/01/02, tlp, cimento, JINST, aistats2026, compositio, hha, jhrs,
   czjphys; iccvw by source).
5. *Hooks.* `\AtEndOfClass`/`\AtEndOfPackage` code the copy registers runs at the end of its load inside the copy's
   mode (`\lx@copy@provides@begin{N}` … `\lx@copy@provides@end`, `copy_provides_wrap`; aa.cls:71's `{abstract}`).
   Code it defers to the document — `\AtBeginDocument`, `\AtEndDocument`, `\AtEndPreamble`, `\AfterEndPreamble`,
   `\AfterEndDocument`, `\AddToHook` (lthooks' `\AddToHook code` stands in while the copy is read) — is not registered
   (`copy_provides_defers`, one Info per copy and seam): it is the class's document-time machinery the binding has taken
   over. On the census sample it fixed no Error and caused 3 Fatals (aastex7.cls:459's `\AddToHook{enddocument}` patch
   reads the kernel's `\enddocument` up to `\@checkend`: 2504.00922, 2605.15371, 2607.03848), 5 Error rows (PoS.cls,
   JHEP.cls "\abstract{...} should appear before \begin{document}"; ieeeaccess.cls's `\EOD`; aipproc.cls's
   `\layoutstyle`) and printed layout checks ("The page layout violates the ICML style", 2407.02750). The 72a brief's
   rule 5 asked for the hooks to run under the rule; main-session decision 2026-10-17 (72a r2, on this evidence: 0
   papers fixed, 3 aastex7 Fatals, junk text): they stay unregistered, the binding owning the document-time machinery.
   Likewise decided: the copy-local overlay of rule 2 stays, nested loads are real loads (rule 6) with the `\ver@` test
   scoped to the copy's own `\usepackage` lines, and (72a r3) counter ownership follows the stand-in binding's own load
   only (rule 2). *Direct hook writes* (77w): the copy's own write to LaTeX's hook macros — `\g@addto@macro
   \@begindocumenthook{…}`, ltxgrid's `\prepdef\@begindocumenthook` (qm2008_abs.cls:3233, snp.cls) or a `\def` of
   `\@begindocumenthook`/`\@enddocumenthook` — is the same document-time code and is not registered either
   (`state::copy_provides_defers_hook_write`, from `install_definition`): ltxgrid's page grid ran over the revtex4
   binding's names at `\begin{document}`, 7 "Missing number" Warnings each in 0805.2253, 0806.0481, 0805.4759 (guard
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::copy_writes_document_hook`, which pins "UNHOOKED" where pdflatex prints "HOOKED"). Its cost
   is `\AtBeginDocument`'s: a hook body that defines names the document uses loses them.
6. *Nested loads.* A package or class the copy loads (`\RequirePackage`, `\usepackage`, `\LoadClass`) is a real load,
   the mode suspended for it (`input_definitions`; a file it pulls in by `\input` is part of the copy, #744): a package the binding did not load loads whole (bmvc2k.cls:139's
   `tabularx`, colm's `multirow`, ws-rv9x6.cls's `ws-crop9x6`), a loaded one is the usual no-op, and `\LoadClass` of
   the loaded class is quiet. These are the lines the binding's dependency scan stands in for, so the copy's
   `\usepackage`/`\RequirePackage` takes the scan's `\ver@` test (`require_package` → `marked_loaded_unrecorded`,
   latex.ltx:18750 `\@ifl@aded`; DIVERGENCES #605): a package the document marked loaded is skipped (sn-jnl.cls:311
   `\usepackage{program}` under sn-jnl-setup.sty's `\AddToHook{class/sn-jnl/before}`, 2201.11056). Every other
   `\usepackage` keeps the records-only test (rulings 2026-10-14/16). Unlike `end_provide_only` (OmniBus's provide-only load, OD #408), these files are not
   marked unloaded after: OmniBus loads part of a file that a later request must load whole; the copy's nested load
   is that file's whole load.
7. *Options.* The copy's `\DeclareOption`s and `\ProcessOptions` run its own handlers inside its code (a handler
   name the binding declared is the binding's, rule 2, and comes back as the binding left it: run and `\relax`ed); its
   `\NeedsTeXFormat`/`\ProvidesClass` are quiet, `\ProvidesClass` recording its version.
8. *Diagnostics.* An Error raised in the copy's own code stays an Error (user ruling 2026-10-17, "Keep as Errors";
   round 1's demotion to a Warning is removed). The copies' Errors became binding work: pnas-new.cls:229
   `\RequirePackage[explicit]{titlesec}` (the binding now passes `explicit` where the copy does: 1907.12289,
   2509.24970, 7 Errors each), ieeeaccess.cls:21-23's `\@IEEEusingAfourpapertrue` (IEEEtran.cls:268-270's flags, now
   in the IEEEtran binding: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #957), ieeeaccess.cls:131 `\definecolor{accessblue}{spotcolor}
   {PANTONE3015C,1.0}` (color.sty:117-122 accepts a model whose `\color@<model>` exists, which spotcolor.sty:71
   defines: the colour keeps its earlier definition — the ieeeaccess binding's CMYK, ieeeaccess_cls.rs:32 —, at Info;
   a name the driver's model defines first takes the alternate the model's binding gives, `\lx@color@alternate@<model>`
   — the spotcolor binding keeps each `\AddSpotColor`'s CMYK, spotcolor.sty:31-41, scaled by the tint —, else black;
   color_sty.rs `driver_color_model`, `driver_alternate_color`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #957; 2007.03025, 2009.04554,
   2011.07807, 2209.03883, 2209.12464, 2609.20467). Open: aipcheck.tex:53-54 reads
   `\fmtversion` as `#1/#2/#3` (pre-2020 LaTeX; TL 2025's is `2024-11-01`, pdflatex errs the same: 0806.2199, 3
   Errors).
9. *Not covered.* An extra macro's body, run later in the document, is the author's command and keeps TeX's effect,
   calling the binding's meanings of owned names (neurips_2024.sty's `\TEST`, defined inside its `\@maketitle`, stays
   unreachable: 2406.07381).
10. *Setter defaults* (72a r3). A frontmatter setter the copy calls (`\author`, `\date`, a binding's `\copyrightinfo`)
   stores the class's default, as in TeX, rather than adding an element: while the copy is read, the frontmatter queue
   is the copy's defaults (base_utilities/frontmatter/queue.rs `frontmatter_queue_name`, `frontmatter_copy_defaults`; a removal applies to
   the same queue, so atlasdoc.cls:824's `\date{}` under `cernpreprint` clears its `\date{\today}`). At `\maketitle`
   (`\lx@store@defaults` → `hand_copy_frontmatter_defaults`) a default is handed to the frontmatter only when the
   document did not set its kind — decided by the call, whatever its value (r4): a setter of the kernel's fields
   (`\author`, `\date`, `\title`, whichever binding defines it) called outside the copy's read, observed from the
   copy's first default on (`definition::origin::watch_setter_calls`, `state::note_setter_call` in
   `Expandable::invoke`: inst_support's accumulating `\author{}` queues and clears nothing), or an entry of its tag and
   role queued or removed (`\date{}`'s `\lx@clear@frontmatter`) — and, for the kernel's fields (`\@author`, `\@date`,
   `\@title`), only when the copy's own title page prints the store (`frontmatter_stores::copy_title_page_prints`: the
   `\maketitle`/`\@maketitle` it defined — `\renewcommand`, refused or overlaid, or `\DeclareRobustCommand`'d — and
   the raw page styles, read as K11's `ClassReaders` reads a raw class's title page, `reads_of`, so a
   `\csname…\endcsname` or `\@nameuse` name is followed; a branch of a `\newif`/kvoptions switch that is now false is
   skipped, `\unless` inverting it, and a conditional written as data, `\let\ifX\iftrue` or `\newif\ifX`, opens no
   level; a title-page name with neither a copy's nor a raw file's meaning is the binding's, which prints the
   frontmatter: a copy's `\renewcommand\maketitle{\begingroup\@maketitle\endgroup}`); the binding's title page prints
   them when the copy defines none. The walk is `ClassReaders`' reading, not its survey: the survey indexes the
   meanings in force, while a copy's own versions of owned names live in its overlay. Without `\maketitle` none shows, as in pdflatex. atlasdoc.cls:189-190 (r2: two
   identical `<creator>`s in 1805.01649, 1806.07355, 1807.02012, 1902.05892, 1904.03536; a `<date>` the 2019 class
   prints only in `\ATLAS@TitleHeader` under `datetop`, :567, which `cernpreprint` skips: 1902.05892, 1904.03536).
   jgcc.cls:397's `\copyrightinfo{}{}` (2309.03819, 2401.15504) prints nothing, as amsart.cls:723-727's
   `\@setcopyright` prints no copyright without a year (ams_support_sty.rs `\lx@ams@add@copyright`, the one test
   of both `\copyrightinfo`s; Perl's ams_support.sty.ltxml:139 adds ", ", KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #958). The walk's roots
   are broad and err toward keeping a default: every raw `\ps@…` page style and `\@oddhead`/`\@evenhead`, so a default
   a copy prints only in a running head shows in the document, which LaTeXML has no running heads for.
11. *Renamed natbib copies* (72a r4, main-session scope). A class copy that loads a renamed copy of natbib —
   NJDnatbib.sty (WileyNJD-v2/v5/MRM.cls, `\ProvidesPackage{NJDnatbib}` :29) and bmvc2k_natbib.sty (bmvc2k.cls:710,
   `\ProvidesPackage{bmvc2k_natbib}` :29) — read it raw: its `\bibsection`'s `\@ifundefined{chapter}` took the
   `\chapter*{\bibname}` branch under LaTeXML's always-defined `\chapter` (Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:557), a
   "Bibliography" heading and `bib.bibxN` ids in 14 papers (2412.14509, 2212.00057, 2210.06270, 1501.07873, 2311.17607,
   2406.08486; 2101.06297, 2211.16474, 2411.11493, 2206.08798, 2602.03829, 2408.07575, 2609.08425, 2506.14995). Each
   fork is now a stand-in binding (contrib `njdnatbib_sty.rs`, `bmvc2k_natbib_sty.rs`) that loads the natbib binding
   with the options the class gave it (`njdnatbib_sty::natbib_fork_options`); the copy, read after, provides only.
   Options that reach a natbib loaded already take effect as natbib's options do (natbib.sty:238-262: `numbers` is also
   `square,comma`; `natbib.sty_keyval_setter` → `\lx@natbib@repeat@options`, content.rs `apply_new_options_on_reload`,
   the mechanism hyperref's `\hypersetup` uses), at Info, only where TeX would see them (r6, `natbib.sty_repeat_clash`):
   the first load was a compiled binding's own early one (`<file>:requested_by_binding`, the requester's `Binding`
   origin, recorded at the first load: sv_support's natbib, which svjour3.cls:67-68 loads only under its `natbib`
   option, 2604.22515; sn-jnl's, which sn-jnl.cls:1654-1665 loads with the style's options, 1012.4730, 2604.20688,
   2107.02450, 2409.07188), or the request carries a renamed copy's own options (`natbib.sty:options_of_a_renamed_copy`,
   set by `natbib_fork_options`: in TeX the fork's own `\ProcessOptions` runs). Otherwise the first load was the
   document's world's — the document's, a raw class's, or a class binding's that records its load as the class's own
   (jmlr.cls:150, acmart.cls:299-300: `natbib.sty:requested_by_binding` false) — and LaTeX keeps the first options and
   stops with "Option clash for package natbib", an Error here as there (the reviewer's probes nat_twice, jmlr_numbers,
   pdflatex author-year); elsarticle (elsarticle.cls:1243), jheppub (jheppub.sty:37) and acmart under its `natbib`
   boolkey (acmart.cls:131-138) record theirs too (r7). A raw file's own repeat after an early binding load — a copy
   that loads natbib itself — is the load TeX sees and ends the early-load state (r7, #733). jheppub's binding loads
   natbib with jheppub.sty:37's `[numbers,sort&compress]` (2112.14648, 2607.20603); jcappub's natbib is
   jcappub.sty:32's, read from the copy (2405.09762). Residual: the repeat rule sets only natbib's style options
   (`numbers`, `authoryear`, `super`, brackets, separators, `nobibstyle`/`bibstyle`), in natbib's declaration order
   (r8); `sort`, `compress`, `sort&compress`, `sectionbib` of a repeat load do nothing (natbib's binding does not sort
   or compress; `sectionbib` takes effect only on the first load); hyperref's repeat setter applies after any first load
   (unchanged; hyperref's kvoptions clash in TeX). r5: MRM's binding had loaded natbib optionless before
   MRM.cls:2441-2442's `\usepackage[numbers,super]{NJDnatbib}`, so 2506.14995 was author-year where its PDF has
   superscripts; the binding no longer loads natbib, the class's copy does, binding-in-original-space). The defaults the
   PDF shows, by NJDnatbib's version (r5; the class-family rule's dispatch on a conflict): a v5 copy (md5 277c41da:
   2602.03829, 2408.07575, 2609.08425) heads a chapterless class's bibliography "REFERENCES" (:1052
   `\bmsection*{…{{REFERENCES}}…}`), an amsart one `\refname` (:1065); a v2 or MRM copy (2fa96b7a: 2101.06297,
   2211.16474; 6838c57e: 2411.11493, 2206.08798; 4b333a37: 2506.14995) natbib's `\section*{\refname…}` (probe
   njd_direct_v2: pdflatex "References"), so MRM's is its class's `\refname`, "REFERENCES". The version is WileyNJDv5's
   class or the copy's own `\bibsection` set by v5's `\bmsection` (its overlaid meaning, `state::stand_in_copy_meaning`,
   read by the binding's `\AtEndOfPackage` after the copy); "chapterless" is decided by `\chapter`, as the fork's
   `\@ifundefined{chapter}` does (r6, `state::class_defines_chapter`): a stand-in copy that (re)declared `\chapter` (its
   overlay, or declined by the lock: ws-rv9x6.cls:499), a `\chapter` of the document's world or a binding's own, or the
   kernel's under book or report — not LaTeXML's kernel `\chapter`, which the OmniBus base keeps defined under every
   class binding today, and not a `chapter` counter, which WileyNJDv5.cls:5728 and MRM.cls:2160 declare
   (`\newcounter{chapter}[part]`) with no `\chapter` (the reviewer's probe njd_v5_ctr, pdflatex "REFERENCES"). Where a
   chapterless class leaves `\chapter` undefined (the separate `\chapter` batch 72b), the answer is
   `\@ifundefined{chapter}`'s. A copy's counter is declared for real (r6, `state::copy_provides_keeps_counter`,
   `new_counter`): the binding keeps its numbering only for a counter its load declared (`\c@<ctr>`) or numbered (the
   `\the<ctr>` of an existing counter); OmniBus's `\thechapter` autoload stub with no `\c@chapter` does not count, so
   the Wiley classes' and ws-rv9x6.cls:399's `\newcounter{chapter}` declare it (2301.03442's two Warnings, "Counter
   'chapter' was not defined", "'\c@chapter' is not a register", gone; its chapter "1", sections "1" and "2" and
   subsection "2.1", and 1602.07982's chapter "1" and section "1.1", as their PDFs, r5 "Chapter 0"). The kernel's
   `\appendix` (latex_constructs `begin_appendices`) numbers within chapters only where the class has `\chapter` by the
   same rule, not by a `chapter` counter alone (WileyNJD-v2.cls:2410's bookmark counter: 2211.16474 "Appendix A", not
   "0.A"); appendix.sty's and titlesec's chapter tests still read the counter (`has_chapter_counter`). Every version's
   superscript carries its postnote inside, ", p. 5" (:366-368), through natbib's `NATBIB_SUPER_POSTNOTE_INSIDE` switch
   the fork's binding sets. ws-rv-har.sty (World Scientific's natbib derivative, :16 `\ProvidesPackage{ws-rv-har}`;
   2301.03442, whose 28 citations were "(?)", pdflatex "(Mayor et al. 2011)"; 1602.07982 ships it, loads ws-rv-van) is
   bound the same way (`ws_rv_har_sty.rs`), with its own heading: a class with `\chapter` (:676, the same
   `state::class_defines_chapter`) `\bibname` (:681-685; ws-rv9x6.cls:91 "References"), else `\refname`; amsart
   `\refname` (:686-687). A copy's `\newcommand` of a text default (rule 1) defines it only where the real class lacks
   the name: the copy loads no base class (ws-rv9x6.cls:91 `\newcommand\bibname`), or no base class it `\LoadClass`es
   defines it (article.cls has no `\bibname`). What a base class defines is told by its load, not its text (r7, #732:
   `state::ClassLoadFrame`): the macros its load frame assigned, a class loaded while the copy's `\LoadClass` is open
   included. A name the base class defines is the real class's already: LaTeX's "Command … already defined" Error, the
   first definition kept (r6, `state::copy_provides_text_default_clashes`, sect08.rs; the reviewer's probes newcmd_base
   and nc_chain: pdflatex 2 errors, "References", "Figure 1"). A name made `\relax` is definable, as LaTeX's
   `\newcommand` finds it (the copy's own `\let\refname\relax` before its `\newcommand`, or a raw base class's; r7).
   `\def`/`\renewcommand` redefine as before. A copy's own load of a package its stand-in binding loaded on its behalf
   (`<file>:loaded_by_stand_in`, the innermost stand-in binding whose load made the first load — a `.sty`, `.cls` or
   `.tex` stand-in's, `StandInBindingName`, the last since 77w r3: mssymb.tex's amsfonts; the request's copy,
   read before the load's provides-mode suspension, `requested_by_copy`, is that binding's — `state::copy_provides_binding`)
   is that load, which TeX sees alone: its options apply, at Info, with no "Option clash" (77w; a modified elsarticle.cls
   copy's `\RequirePackage[square,…]{natbib}`, 1811.10063). Another stand-in's copy repeating the load with other
   options meets LaTeX's "Option clash", as in pdflatex (77w r2; the review's finding 6, guard
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::another_copys_repeat_load_clashes`; the `.tex` stand-ins' record,
   `tex_stand_in_names_its_package_loads`).
12. *The declaration route* (77w, user ruling 2026-10-20, extending 2026-10-17's "a binding always wins over a shipped
   copy"). A `.sty` or `.cls` the paper ships under a name with no binding of its own that declares itself another file
   a binding stands for is that binding's request (content.rs `provided_binding`, from `input_definitions_impl` ahead
   of the raw read of a file found while interpreting definitions, Step 2, and of the versioned fallback, Step 3, which
   reads no copy): `\usepackage{natbib_vw}` whose file `\ProvidesPackage{natbib}` loads the natbib binding,
   `\documentclass{qm2008_abs}` whose file `\ProvidesClass{revtex4}` the revtex4 binding. The declaration is the file's
   first `\Provides(Expl)?(Class|Package|File)` outside a comment (`file_declaration`, shared with rule 0 (a), the
   declared-macro form included; a later one does not count: qm2008_abs.cls embeds textcase.sty's
   `\ProvidesPackage{textcase}`, :3680), read up to the file's first top-level `\endinput` (a code line of it alone
   outside a brace group, where TeX stops: a declaration in a documentation trailer after it is not the file's — 77w r2,
   the review's finding 8; `file_declarations`); not a bundle — a file declaring three or more distinct files is several
   files in one, read raw as before (77w r2, main-session decision 2026-10-20: 1312.3078's cauchy.sty declares theorem,
   exscale, epsfig and apacite; routed to the theorem binding, theorem.sty's load guard
   `\@ifundefined{theorem@style}{}{\endinput}` ended the read, 8 undefined apacite `\BB…` Errors; qm2008_abs.cls's two
   stay routed; guard `perfect_kernel_batch77w::provides_route_skips_bundles_and_trailers`); of the request's kind (a `.sty`'s `\ProvidesPackage` or `\ProvidesFile{X.sty}`,
   a `.cls`'s `\ProvidesClass` or `\ProvidesFile{X.cls}`); naming another file, compared without regard to case; whose
   binding is the registry's, matched as a request is without regard to case, or the one its versioned fallback reaches
   (`aistats2023` → aistats). The binding loads with the request's options as a versioned fallback's does
   (`fallback_request`/`fallback_target`; `\ver@<request>` is the binding's), its load a stand-in load
   (`StandInLoadGuard`; `fallback_provides` names it, `loading_for_a_provides_route`), and the copy is read after it by
   rules 1-11, identity by the declaration (rule 0 not asked); `<binding>:options_of_a_renamed_copy` is set for the load
   (rule 11). Info `fallback`: "The paper's natbib_vw.sty declares itself natbib: loading the natbib.sty binding, then
   the copy as its stand-in's". Not routed: a request with a binding of its own; a file the search paths do not find
   in the paper's source (a TeX Live file, e.g. TL's dated rollback copies `multicol-2019-10-01.sty`, keeps the
   versioned fallback); a copy naming itself (NJDnatbib, bmvc2k_natbib, ws-rv-har, hbnatbib, aistats2e: their own
   bindings, or raw); another kind (a `.sty` that `\ProvidesClass{revtex4}`); a name no binding answers. No per-name list
   is replaced: the renamed natbib forks with bindings (NJDnatbib, bmvc2k_natbib, ws-rv-har) and aistats2e/aistats2eM
   declare their own names, so their registrations stay. Census (77w): of the 1,677 shipped `*natbib*.sty` (1,509
   papers), 389 declare `natbib` under another name (90 new routes: modnatbib 21, natbib_vw 16, natbib_jrm 11,
   my_natbib 7, natbibsty 6, …; 299 the versioned fallback reached before, natbib209 137, natbib2 134, whose copies are
   now read too); over a 3 % corpus sample (87,937 papers) 491 papers (≈0.56 %) request a shipped file that the rule
   routes, 186 of them reached by the versioned fallback before (by binding: aastex 102, neurips 42, IEEEtran 24,
   longtable 23 — aalongtable.sty —, rotating 22 — rotating_pr.sty —, jheppub 22, aa 16, article 13). Perl: `FindFile`
   finds no `.ltxml` for the request (Package.pm:2113-2133; `FindFile_fallback` reduces by name only, :2141-2210); by
   default it reads no raw style, warns the file missing and loads the bindings its dependency scan names (natbib: the
   citations resolve, the copy's extras are lost), and under `--includestyles` it reads the copy raw, whose citations read
   `\b@<key>`, which no `\bibitem` writes: "?" and a "Citation undefined" Warning per citation (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
   #1014; 0802.4100 142 Warnings, 1003.3017 62, astro-ph0512042). Residual: a binding loaded already is not run again
   and its copy is not read (its options reach it, rule 11); a file whose first declaration follows a long stretch of
   its own code is routed by it all the same (adassconf.sty, astro-ph0101121: html.sty's embedded
   `\ProvidesPackage{html}`, :1374, after 391 definitions of its own, so it routes to the html binding; it converts
   cleanly, +17 words; main-session decision: leave, SYNC row); where the
   copy departs from the binding's class the binding's markup stands (2209.10785's cidr.cls comments out acmart's
   `natbib=true` default, so the acmart binding's natbib meets the document's `\usepackage[numbers]{natbib}`: LaTeX's
   "Option clash" Error, where pdflatex loads natbib once; 1401.1086's confSt.cls, an aamas2013 copy, and 2312.16264's
   arxiv.cls, an egpubl copy, meet those bindings' author-block gaps, 4-6 Errors and a merged creator, as a copy under
   the binding's own name does; 2605.07897's bytedance_seed binding raises its honest "merged_creators" Error on a
   parboxed author row). A/B (77w r3, base 529dc1b543, 471 papers: 161 natbib-census papers requesting their copy,
   280 sampled routes, 30 witnesses; plus 200 random ships/controls, byte-identical): Errors 144 → 123, Fatals 0 → 0,
   Warnings 12,652 → 8,787, words +1.5 %, "?" 2,608 → 109, "Citation undefined" Warnings 3,707 → 39; title
   +37/−11, creator +29/−2, contact +66/−14 papers (the losses: raw classes' duplicated frontmatter now printed
   once, 2210.16202 82 "Japan" → 10 as its source); 4 papers worse in Errors: the three above and 1312.3078's
   bundle, read raw again since r2. Guards
   `perfect_kernel_batch77w::*`; repros `tools/perfect_kernel/repros/stand-in-copies/provides_route/`.
13. *A standard-class derivative* (77w r2; user rulings 2026-10-20: "a shipped class declaring a LaTeX standard class
   stays routed; fix the bindings so the route loses nothing", then "call out arXiv overrides of standard classes in the
   sections patching them"). A class the paper ships that declares one of LaTeX's own classes — its file in the
   format's base distribution, `tex/latex/base/` (article, report, book, letter, proc, slides, minimal; content.rs
   `is_latex_base_class`) — is not that class but an arXiv-side override of it: aip-cp.cls:24 `\ProvidesClass{article}`
   (AIP Conference Proceedings, not in TeX Live; 1506.04050, 1604.08112), mf.cls (0709.4467), antonio.cls (1808.10740),
   articlegm.cls, articlefederico.cls, HERON.cls and mbook.cls (`book`: 1903.06504, nucl-th0703058), avh.cls
   (`report`). Every section of the copy that differs patches the kernel's class, which the binding models with two
   kinds of names: the class's text (`\refname`, `\figurename`, `\@ptsize`), which the copy may change, and LaTeXML's
   structural markup of it (`\appendix` → `<ltx:appendix>`, book's `\frontmatter`/`\mainmatter`/`\backmatter`, the
   sectioning, the counters' ids), which the copy's equivalent code cannot give (user refinement 2026-10-20: honor the
   derivative's patches "without losing the entire binding support for high quality XML such as frontmatter"). The
   provides mode of rules 1-11 kept the binding's meaning for each and lost the patches, silently: aip-cp's
   accumulating `\author[aff1]{…}` (aip-cp.cls:235-258) kept the last of five authors under the locked kernel
   `\author`, its `\affil` list was lost, mf.cls's size file left no nominal font size, HERON.cls's and mbook.cls's
   affiliation contact went. So the copy is read after the binding's load as a raw
   class is (`read_standard_class_derivative`, Info "The paper's X derives from a LaTeX class: read as a raw class over
   its binding"), and its patches are recognised by the raw-class mechanisms, section by section:
   - *frontmatter setters* — a locked kernel name it redefines (`\author`, `\title`, `\maketitle`, `\abstract`, …) is
     refused with the records a raw class's takeover leaves (`\lx@dropped@<name>`, `<name>:redefined`; state.rs
     `install_definition`): the kernel `\author` appends each call (#253, `\lx@add@authors@adaptive`) and replays the
     class's own setter for its flags and stores (#482, #534), its `\maketitle` deposits what the frontmatter does not
     carry (#265: aip-cp's `\aipaffil`), and the title-page stores reach the frontmatter API (K11,
     `\lx@class@loaded@raw` at the binding load's end; `store_setters::mark_raw`);
   - *the class's text names* — its `\newcommand` (or `\providecommand`) of a declared text name (rule 14's list: the
     kernel's `state::COPY_TEXT_NAMES` and the names a binding declares) that the standard binding assigned in its own
     load defines it, the derivative being read in the class's place (`state::standard_class_binding_name`,
     latex_constructs `is_definable_latex`) — aip-cp.cls:875-878 "REFERENCES", "FIGURE 1"; HERON.cls:682
     `\bibname{References}`; Lowx2013.cls:629 `\abstractname{ }`; article_saj.cls:631
     `\newcommand\refname{\noindent\tenrm REFERENCES\vskip-.5cm}` (2212.09079, 2402.12725). Its body is not checked
     (rule 14's safety check is the routed copy's, whose definition otherwise gives way to the binding's): the
     derivative is read as a raw class, whose `\def` and `\renewcommand` of the same name stand unchecked (applied here,
     the check fails closed on `\noindent`, a constructor, and prints article's "References"). Every other `\newcommand`
     of a name the binding defined is "Ignoring redefinition" (78h r2, user ruling 2026-10-21): a caption format (a
     derivative's `\newcommand\fnum@table{TABLE~\thetable}` keeps the article binding's "Table 1"; 78h r1 let every name
     that only prints yield, "TABLE 1"), book's `\@chapapp`, and the four names 77w r3 let yield as bodies without

14. *A routed copy's text names* (78h; user rulings 2026-10-21, memory `feedback_rulings_2026_10_21` item 9, refined the
   same day: "The bindings should always win in terms of semantic markup, as they hold the ground truth for the XML
   spec. The slight typographic variations in the raw .cls or .sty file are often ignorable, and if we can preserve and
   reuse them that should be via a generic mechanism that is set in the binding with a reasonable default"). A copy rule
   12 routed to its binding supplies only the *text names its binding declares*. The list classifies by name: the
   kernel's default, `state::COPY_TEXT_NAMES` — the standard classes' and LaTeX's `\…name` macros `\abstractname`,
   `\appendixname`, `\bibname`, `\chaptername`, `\contentsname`, `\figurename`, `\indexname`, `\listfigurename`,
   `\listtablename`, `\partname`, `\proofname`, `\refname`, `\tablename` —, which a binding extends with the names it
   defines, where it defines them (`state::declare_copy_text_names`, the one declaration point: a value
   `<name>:copy@text`, as a lock is `<name>:locked`; aas_macros_sty.rs declares its 65 journal abbreviations,
   ieeetran_cls.rs `\IEEEkeywordsname` and `\IEEEproofname`). The safety check reads the copy's own definition and fails
   closed: a declared name the binding owns (rule 1) is kept aside as any owned name (rule 2), and when the copy's read
   ends (`state::leave_copy_provides_frame` → `copy_text_names_stand`) the copy's meaning stands for the document only
   if it is a macro without parameters whose body reads as text (`state::copy_text_refusal`, `text_body_refusal`:
   every macro it reaches, at most 32, is followed, a robust `\protect\X` through `\X` and LaTeX's inner `\X `; what
   reads as text is characters, a `\let` or `\chardef` character (`\&`), a conditional (both branches), a primitive
   that prints a character or selects a font by its definition (`\it`, a `\font` selector) or prints a space (`\ `,
   `~`'s `\lx@NBSP`, `\lx@nobreakspace`), LaTeX's font selection commands (`\fontfamily`, `\fontseries`, `\fontshape`,
   `\fontencoding`, `\fontsize`, `\selectfont`, `\usefont`, `\not@math@alphabet@@`, `\lx@normalfont@base`, not
   followed: a font switch's robust command reaches them, `\let\jnl@style=\rm` in the AASTeX copies) and an empty
   body; everything else is refused — a constructor, `\par`, `\csname`/`\endcsname`, an undefined name, a macro whose
   expansion is LaTeXML's code (`\begin`), any other primitive (`\noindent`, `\hbox`), a register, a locked command
   that reads arguments), else the binding's comes back (Info "… defines this text name as more than text (<the
   refused token>)", once per name: aastex63_bren.cls:879 `\def\abstractname{\textbf{Abstract}}`, whose `\textbf`

### 732. → #731 (article, report and book assign their classes' names in their own load; what a base class defines is told by its load frame)

### 733. → #731 (A raw file's own repeat load of natbib after a binding's early load is the load TeX sees)

### 734. A `\chapter` call in a class without chapters is LaTeXML's numbered chapter, with one Warning; the name stays undefined (TeX: undefined control sequence; Perl: the kernel's `\chapter`, `undefined:\thechapter`)

**Perl behavior**: `\chapter` is defined in every class (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:557), so a call in an article
digests LaTeXML's chapter, whose counter does not exist: "Counter 'chapter' was not defined", `\c@chapter` "is not a
register", and `Error:undefined:\thechapter` in each tag (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #962).
**Rust behavior**: `\chapter` is undefined after a class without chapters loads (#179). At `\begin{document}`, after the
begin-document hooks have run (a package's `\AtBeginDocument` test gets TeX's answer), a `\chapter` still undefined is
given a stand-in, `\lx@chapterless@chapter` (sect01.rs `supply_chapter_fallback`, `kernel_autoload::name_undefined_fallback`):
the name stays undefined — `\@ifundefined{chapter}`, `\ifdefined` and `\meaning` in the body answer as TeX does
(blindtext.sty:243 `\blinddocument` makes no chapter under scrartcl) — and where the undefined token is met
(`kernel_autoload::undefined_fallback`, at the gullet's and the stomach's undefined-CS sites; a thread-local flag
answers at once until a stand-in is named) the stand-in is read in its place: LaTeXML's ordinary numbered chapter
(`\lx@kernel@chapter`, the pool:557 definition) with a chapter counter of its own where the class made none
(`NewCounter('chapter')`, without report's reset of the sections), and on its first use one `Warning:undefined:\chapter`
(`kernel_chapter_with_warning`, sect04.rs). Its text: "The class defines no \chapter, so TeX stops here with an
undefined control sequence; LaTeXML's \chapter is used"; when the class was answered by a binding not its own (a prefix
alternate or a versioned fallback: neither `<class>.cls.ltxml_loaded` nor `<class>.cls_raw_loaded`, recorded at
`\documentclass` as `\chapter:class@stood@in`), "The binding answering class <class> defines no \chapter; LaTeXML's
\chapter is used", which claims nothing about TeX: the real class may have chapters (0909.2812's mn_thesis.cls has them
through mnphd.cls → report, bound by the prefix alternate `mn`; its report now comes from the dependency scan).
The chapters carry LaTeXML's labels ("Chapter 1", refnum, typerefnum, toc title), which the PDF never shows: pdflatex
stops at the call and sets the title as text (user ruling 2026-10-17: the fallback is LaTeXML's ordinary numbered
chapter). The user ruling supplies LaTeXML's chapter "at `\begin{document}`"; it is supplied there as a stand-in rather
than as the definition (main-session ruling: `\chapter` stays undefined after `\begin{document}`, only a call reads it),
so that body-time tests (blindtext, hvfloat's test documents, the #179 witnesses) keep TeX's answer. Edge cases: a call
in the preamble or in a begin-document hook meets the undefined name as TeX does (one `Error:undefined:\chapter`, the
title as text) and its undefined-error stub is cleared at `\begin{document}` (`\chapter:error@stub`), so the body's calls
read the stand-in (repro sectioning-frontmatter/chapter_in_the_preamble_errs_and_the_body_chapter_converts);
`\csname chapter\endcsname` in the body (and `\expandafter\ifx\csname chapter\endcsname\relax`) makes `\chapter`
`\relax`, as in TeX, and a later call sets its title as text without a diagnostic (the hypbmsec, splitidx, chemscheme,
examplep and wrapfig2 test shapes); `\let\mychap\chapter` copies the undefined meaning, so `\mychap{…}` is
`Error:undefined:\mychap`, as TeX; a body `\edef` holding `\noexpand\chapter` makes a chapter where TeX stops.
**Why**: the author meant a chapter, and the content is kept (the OD #721 precedent: the author's reading plus one
Warning, never silent, never an Error); pdflatex stops at each call ("Undefined control sequence") and sets the title as
text. The Warning stays though TeX (and Perl, for the unstarred call) err (user 2026-11-11: no author-facing value; the
recovery is semantic, reach tiny — 1 of 300 article papers that call `\chapter` reaches the stand-in, 1112.4337; an
Error would flip a paper's conversion status). A binding standing in for a class not its own is a Warning on both
counts: TeX's class may have chapters (0909.2812: pdflatex "CHAPTER 1", no `\chapter` error).
**Witnesses**: 1403.2269, 1511.03874, 1606.03650, 2504.00704 (1 → 0 `undefined:\chapter`); 0909.2812 (1 → 0, its
report's chapters); 0907.3938's pre.cls `\let\chapter\part` after `\LoadClass{article}` is the class's own chapter, kept by #179
(a), where it was retracted; 0802.3014 and 1507.01872 call it inside an undefined preamble macro's argument (pretex's
`\UInewAction`), before the stand-in exists.
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batch72b::{chapter_in_a_chapterless_class_is_the_kernel_chapter_with_a_warning,
a_preamble_chapter_errs_and_the_body_chapter_reads_the_stand_in, a_raw_class_meets_chapter_undefined_while_it_loads,
appendices_follow_the_class_chapters}`; `error_boundary::perfect_kernel_error_boundary` (both sides, each row with
its pdflatex and Perl oracle: article `\chapter`, `\chapter*` and jmlr at 0 errors 1 Warning where pdflatex errs;
report, book, report `\chapter*`, amsbook, scrbook and a document's own `\chapter` at 0/0; 0909.2812's shape, a shipped
raw class over report answered by the prefix alternate `mn`, at 0 errors 2 Warnings); repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{chapter_call_in_a_chapterless_class, chapter_undefined_in_a_chapterless_class,
chapter_in_the_preamble_errs_and_the_body_chapter_converts, appendix_after_a_chapter_in_a_chapterless_class,
chapter_star_in_a_chapterless_class, chapter_in_a_class_a_prefix_binding_answers_warns}.
**Upstream**: not filed.

### 735. jmlr's article `\chapter` is LaTeXML's chapter, with the class's error text as one Warning (TeX: the class's error; Perl: no jmlr binding, the kernel's `\chapter`)

**Perl behavior**: no jmlr binding; OmniBus and the kernel's `\chapter` (pool:557), numbered by no counter
(`undefined:\thechapter`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #962).
**Rust behavior**: jmlr_cls.rs defines `\chapter`, as jmlr.cls:743-745 does (`\artchapter`, `\let\chapter\artchapter`;
:950-959 `\jmlrbookcommands` switches to `\bookchapter`), so a package's `\@ifundefined{chapter}` takes the chapter
branch, as TeX's (pdflatex "X=C."). A call in an article reads LaTeXML's numbered chapter through
`kernel_chapter_with_warning` (#734's), with one `Warning:latex:\chapter` "Class jmlr Error: Chapters not permitted in
articles; LaTeXML's \chapter is used"; the class's chapter counter (:732) is made at the call, marked as the stand-in's
(`\chapter:stand@in@counter`; `has_chapter_counter` ignores it, for every binding that reuses the helper), so the
article's `\appendix` letters the sections as jmlr.cls:720-729 `\artappendix` (`\let\appendix\artappendix`) does:
pdflatex "Appendix A. AppSec", ours "Appendix A" (72b r2: "Appendix 1.A", numbered within the stand-in's chapter).
**Why**: the OD #721 / #734 precedent: TeX's error is the class refusing what the author wrote; the author's chapter is
kept, with a Warning that names the class's error (user 2026-11-11: no author-facing value in an Error; the recovery is
semantic, reach tiny).
**Witnesses**: the 72b review's jmlr probes (jmlr.cls TL 2025; rev72b/r2/jma for the appendix); no arXiv paper calls it (3 jmlr papers of the 72b A/B,
unchanged).
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batch72b::bindings_whose_class_has_chapters_define_them`,
`error_boundary::perfect_kernel_error_boundary`.
**Upstream**: not filed.

### 736. → #731 (A stand-in class binding loads the base class its real file loads; the copy's one class slot is the net)

### 737. The KOMA classes, read raw, get the standard classes' semantic layer: ids, `\appendix`, and a quiet sectioning check

**TeX**: `\documentclass{scrartcl}` (scrreprt, scrbook) is KOMA-Script's class: its `\newcounter`s (scrartcl.cls:5045-5127,
scrreprt.cls:5530-6051), its `\appendix` (scrartcl.cls:4842-4867: counters reset, `\thesection` = `\@Alph\c@section`,
`\appendixmore`; scrreprt.cls:5305-5335 and scrbook.cls:5284-5314 at the chapter level, `\@chapapp` = `\appendixname`),
and a check that the kernel's `\@startsection` and `\@sect` are still latex.ltx's (scrartcl.cls:3292 + :3326, :3520 +
:3552), which passes: pdflatex writes no Class Warning for a minimal document.

**Perl**: no KOMA binding; the class is "missing" and OmniBus (article) loads (`Can't find binding for class scrartcl
(using OmniBus)`), so a KOMA paper has the article's ids (`S1`, `S1.E1`, `S1.F1`) and `<appendix>` elements, and none of
KOMA's own commands.

**Rust** (72a r10; main-session call, row (p) option b): the classes are raw-read (scrartcl_cls.rs, the memoir
precedent, batch 53) and koma_script.rs adds the semantic layer the article, report and book bindings give:
1. *Ids* (`koma_counter_ids`): after the raw load, each sectioning and float counter the class declared gets the ids of
   the standard class's binding (article_cls.rs:86-107 for scrartcl, report_cls.rs:94-130 / book_cls.rs:100-136 for
   scrreprt and scrbook: `idprefix`, `idwithin`, `nested`), through `counter::dialect::define_counter_ids`, the id half
   of `new_counter` split out; the registers and reset lists stay the class's. Before: `section1`,
   `section1.subsection1`, `equation1`, `figure1` (124 of 126 ceurart/atlasdoc papers of 2506+2509 under 72a r9, every
   KOMA paper under 67int21).
2. *Appendix* (`koma_appendix`): `\appendix` is `\@appendix` — `start_appendices("section")` for scrartcl, `("chapter")`
   for scrreprt/scrbook, as article_cls.rs:148-152 and report_cls.rs:178-182 — then KOMA's own, whose lettering,
   `\@chapapp`, one-time hook and `\appendixmore` stand. Before: more `ltx:section`s, their ids colliding with the body's
   (`section1a`), in 26 of the 27 ceurart/atlasdoc papers with an appendix (2509.11496, 2506.00694).
3. *The sectioning check* (`koma_pre_load`): KOMA's copies of the two kernel workers (`\scr@saved@startsection`,
   `\scr@latex@sect`) are set to the kernel's — LaTeXML's native `\@startsection` (sect04.rs) and `\@sect` router
   (latex_constructs_rust_only.rs) — and locked against the class's definitions of them, so the class takes pdflatex's
   branch and writes neither "`\@startsection' has been changed" nor "Unexpected definition of \@sect!" (both on every
   KOMA document since the classes were raw-read; CONTROL repro sectioning-frontmatter/koma_sectioning_check_warns of
   batch 60m, which judged them true). Neither copy is called on that branch: the dispatcher KOMA puts over
   `\@startsection` is refused by its lock, and `\scr@startsection` is LaTeXML's `\@startsection` (`koma_post_load`).
4. *Front matter* (`koma_book_matter`, scrbook only; int23, 72a review r7 SHOULD 1): scrbook's `\frontmatter`,
   `\mainmatter` and `\backmatter` (scrbook.cls:5272-5283) switch `\if@mainmatter`, by which KOMA numbers a chapter
   (:5573-5576); LaTeXML's sectioning numbers by `no_number_sections`, which `\frontmatter` and `\mainmatter` now also
   set before KOMA's own code runs, as book_cls.rs's do (Perl book.cls.ltxml:112-118). Before: 2506.17485 "Chapter 1
   Abstract", "Chapter 2 Introduction", every number one too high; now "Abstract", "1 Introduction", as its PDF.
   Residual: the flag unnumbers every level, where KOMA unnumbers only the chapter outside the main matter and keeps
   a section's number without the chapter's (scrbook.cls:6030-6036 `\if@mainmatter\thechapter.\fi`), so `\backmatter`
   is left to KOMA: a back-matter chapter is numbered (2508.01496's appendix
   "Appendix A", PDF "Appendix"), its sections keep KOMA's numbers ("13", as scrbook.cls numbers them; with the flag
   set there, every reference to them lost its number: -201 words); a section inside a front-matter chapter is
   unnumbered (KOMA "1"). book_cls.rs's `no_number_chapters` (78a, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1016) does not serve here: an
   unnumbered KOMA chapter still resets the counters within it (scrbook.cls:5573-5600, `\cl@<chapter>` with
   `\@stpelt` from v3.15), which the kernel's unnumbered unit does not, so 2508.01496's appendix figures would number
   on from the last main chapter (16 figures off by one; PDF "Figure 1" … "Figure 16").
Divergence from Perl: KOMA's own commands are defined (the raw class), and under scrreprt/scrbook the ids are report's
(`Ch1.S1`), not Perl's article ids. With it, ceurart's `\title[mode=<mode>]` (ceurart.cls:381-500: the optional
argument is a key list; `mode=sub`, and `\subtitle`, the subtitle) maps onto the frontmatter (ceurart_cls.rs: `title` the
main title, `sub` `ltx:subtitle`, `trans`/`transsub` notes as acmart's `\translatedtitle`, `alt`/`ascii` the notes
`alternativetitle`/`asciititle`: ceurart.cls:435-483 prints them as further title lines in styles of their own, an
alternative title and the title in ASCII, so they stay apart from the main title), where the kernel `\title`
took the keys for a short title and the last call won (19 of the 112 ceurart papers of 2506+2509: 2509.11492,
2509.11496); and OmniBus declares book.cls:53's `\if@mainmatter` with its `\mainmatter` (omnibus_cls.rs), which
scrlayer.sty:102-110 expects ("\mainmatter defined without \if@mainmatter!" on 111 of the 112 under 72a r9, where OmniBus
is provided over scrartcl; pdflatex quiet). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch72a::{koma_classes_take_the_kernel_branch_without_warnings,
koma_ids_and_appendix_follow_the_standard_classes, ceurart_title_mode_sub_is_the_subtitle}`,
`perfect_kernel_batchint23::scrbook_front_matter_chapters_are_unnumbered`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/scrbook_front_matter_chapters_are_unnumbered`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/koma_ids_and_appendix_{scrartcl,scrreprt,scrbook}`, `koma_sectioning_check_warns`,
`stand-in-copies/class_slot/ceurart_title_mode_sub`.

### 738. Text TeX writes to an auxiliary file and typesets only when it is printed is digested only where it is printed — index, nomenclature and glossary entries, a `\bibitem` label's reference forms (user ruling 2026-10-18; Perl: digested at the command) — absorbs #750

**Rule (user ruling 2026-10-18).** An entry or form TeX writes to an auxiliary file and typesets only when a list or a
reference reads it back is kept as tokens under an id (`latexml_core/src/stomach.rs:2778 defer_print`), with the anchor
`\lx@deferred@print{id}` where it was made, and digested in document order when its list is printed or its key cited
(`:2828 resolve_deferred_prints`, from a low-water mark, so each entry is scanned once); once printed, a later entry is
digested at once; never printed, it typesets nothing. **Perl** digests every phrase at the `\index`/`\nomenclature` (pool
`\index`; Perl's nomencl is raw and prints no list), `\glossary` only outside `ltx:p` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #281), and a
`\bibitem` label with every form at the `\bibitem` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4096-4102). A label's own reference text
(`\@currentlabel`) is not deferred today: #418, #748, #778, #845 build it at the step — the DG question of the OD
rationalization (C, DEFER).

- **Index, nomenclature, glossary** (73a). `\index` writes its entry `\@sanitize`d and `\protected@write`-expanded to the
  `.idx` (latex.ltx:17710-17726), `\glossary` after `\makeglossary` to the `.glo` (:17727-17741), `\nomenclature` to the
  `.nlo` (nomencl.sty:208-245); `\printindex`/the `.gls` input/`\printnomenclature` read makeindex's `.ind`/`.gls`/`.nls`,
  with all the entries, later ones too. Without a print command an entry's `_` or `\|` is no TeX error. The tokens are
  kept expanded as the write expands them (nomencl's with `\theequation` fixed); the prints are `{theindex}`,
  makeidx/imakeidx `\printindex`, the `.ind`/`.gls` stand-in `\lx@makeindex@output`, nomencl's `\printnomenclature`; the
  anchors absorb the marks, so a list keeps its marks where the entries stood. A list never printed gives no
  `<ltx:indexmark>`/`<ltx:glossarydefinition>` and no HTML head keywords from index phrases — the accepted cost (main
  session 2026-10-18; raw undigested marks declined); `\glossary` likewise (main-session call 2026-10-18). A nomencl entry
  makeindex would reject (a second `|` or `@` in its prefix, symbol, description, or table-mode unit and note,
  nomencl.sty:228-232; "Extra `|'", the `.ilg`) is left out with a Warning. Streaming (and the adaptive eager phase's soft
  yield) digests every pending entry at a yield, as Perl does: a streamed conversion holds marks of an unprinted list,
  and a printed list's entry is digested under the definitions in force at the yield (`\index{\x}`, `\x` "FOO" then
  "BAR" before `\printindex`: streamed "FOO", eager "BAR") — the second documented exception to `--streaming`
  byte-identity besides #456 (the `--streaming` help text; `streaming_sweep::STREAMING_DIVERGENT_FIXTURES` compares
  `cluster_regressions/verb_in_index.tex` without its `<indexmark>`s;
  `114_streaming_cluster_regressions::streaming_yield_typesets_pending_index_entries` asserts it). Witnesses 1112.3972 (20
  → 0 Errors), 2506.02168 (1 → 0, `\printnomenclature` ahead of the entries). Repros
  index/{index_entry_typeset_only_when_printed, printed_index_keeps_its_entries,
  nomenclature_entry_typeset_only_when_printed, glossary_entry_typeset_only_when_printed},
  index-bib/index_entry_ampersand_is_literal_list_printed_first; guards
  `perfect_kernel_batch73a::{index_entry_is_typeset_only_when_printed, printed_index_keeps_its_entries,
  nomenclature_entry_is_typeset_only_when_printed, glossary_entry_is_typeset_only_when_printed,
  index_entry_ampersand_is_literal_list_printed_first, nomentbl_unit_with_a_bar_is_rejected}`.
- **A `\bibitem` label's reference forms** (ex-#750, 70c; rc_struct4 row C1). `\@lbibitem` (latex.ltx:17746-17749)
  typesets the label as `\item[\@biblabel{#1}\hfill]` and writes `\bibcite{key}{label}`; only a `\cite` expands `\b@key`
  (:17761-17771). `\lx@bibitem` (sect11.rs) reads `[label]` undigested and splits the tags (`tag_forms`,
  base_utilities/util_text.rs): the role-less `\fnum@@bibitem` = `{\@biblabel{\the@bibitem}}` is digested at the
  `\bibitem` through the class's `\@biblabel`; refnum, typerefnum, autoref and the cleveref forms are deferred under `b@key`,
  resolved when a `\@@bibref` names the key (`sect11.rs:2475 cite_prints_keys`: the kernel's `\cite`, natbib's, biblatex's,
  the `.bbl` styles'), at once when one already has. `\nocite` prints nothing; the streaming yield typesets pending forms at
  the spill, as Perl. Under mn2e/mnras without `usenatbib` (their bindings define the class's `\def\@biblabel#1{}`,
  mn2e.cls:1370, mnras.cls:1636) a `\bibitem[\protect\citeauthoryear{…}{…}]{key}` errs only when cited (pdflatex 0 uncited,
  1 per citation). An uncited or keyless entry has no refnum tag; the bibliography XSLT shows the role-less tag, else the
  refnum. Unchanged: natbib's entries (`\lx@NAT@lbibitem`), unlabelled `\bibitem{key}`, and any `\bibitem[label]` while natbib
  (or a renamed copy: `\NAT@ifcmd`, natbib.sty:809) is loaded — natbib parses the label at the `\bibitem`, so it is digested
  there once (a copy's delimited `\citeauthoryear`, natbib.sty:1014, read raw ran past the label: 1003.3017's natbib_vw.sty;
  repro `index-bib/mn2e_natbib_copy/natbib_copy_citeauthoryear_label_cited`, pdflatex and Perl 0). An autoload the label
  calls loads before the entry is read (`\lx@bibitem@autoloads`): crckapb's `\citeauthoryear` is natbib's (#731), whose
  parser loaded inside the tags took `\the@bibitem` as its number (astro-ph0007279; guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch77r::bibitem_label_autoload_loads_before_the_entry`). Witnesses 0812.1037, 1105.2318, 1306.6339,
  1805.00040. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch70c::*`; repros `index-bib/mnras_bibitem_label_{uncited,nocite_only,cited_before,cited_after}`,
  controls `index-bib/bibitem_numeric_label_cited_and_uncited`, `index-bib/mnras_usenatbib_bibitem_label_cited`.

### 739. AASTeX 6+'s `\tablecaption` before `\begin{deluxetable}`, or in a `{longrotatetable}` around a plain `tabular`, is kept on the table, unnumbered (user ruling 2026-10-18)

**TeX**: aastex701.cls:8417-8418 (aastex631.cls alike) `\def\tablecaption#1{\gdef\@tablecaption{#1}}` stores the caption,
`\deluxetable` empties the store at the table's start (:11303-11304 `\let\tablecaption\deluxetablecaption
\deluxetablecaption{}`) and `\startdata` prints it above the tabular only when it is not empty (:11391-11399); a long
table (`\startlongtable`, or a deluxetable in `{longrotatetable}`, whose `\global\startlongtabletrue` holds until a long
table ends, :11609) prints its numbered caption always, empty or not (:11568/:11575). A caption given before the table
is lost in the PDF and the table takes no number; in a `{longrotatetable}` (:12245-12286) around a plain `tabular` the
store is never printed, and its `\label` names the last numbered unit (2204.03327's aux: `tab:allesFitted` = 4.1.5).

**Perl**: `\let\tablecaption\caption` (deluxetable.sty.ltxml:77) — outside a float an Error ("outside any known float").

**Rust** (73a): `\tablecaption` is stored outside a float (deluxetable_sty.rs `\lx@deluxe@tablecaption`; scoped to its
group, the class's store is `\gdef`, so a caption a group closes on is not left for an unrelated table) and directly in
an aastex `{longrotatetable}` (aas_support_sty.rs, `in_longrotatetable_body`). The next deluxetable takes the store at
its start; at its print point (`\lx@deluxe@print@caption`, `\startdata`, above the tabular) it sets its own caption,
numbered, else the kept one — **unnumbered** (`\lx@deluxe@unnumbered`, the kernel's starred caption: no counter step,
no list entry), so every later "Table N" and `\ref` is the PDF's (main-session call 2026-10-18; 2204.03327's
`tab:wasp43_res` is 3) — or, in a long table, numbered, kept or empty, as the PDF numbers it. A kept caption holding
a `\label` takes an id step (`\lx@deluxe@id@step`, Perl `RefStepID`: no counter, no list entry; main-session call
2026-10-18), so that `\label` — which pdflatex never runs ("??") — names the table, not the document or section (Perl
`floatToLabel` takes the nearest ancestor with an id); a `\ref` to it shows what Post CrossRef `generateRef` finds
walking up from the table (CrossRef.pm:686-695: the requested `refnum` on the table, then its parents, the title only
when none has one), i.e. the enclosing section's number, linked to the table. A kept caption without a `\label` takes
no id, so a `\label` written after the stored caption names the last numbered unit, as TeX's (2204.03327's aux:
`tab:allesFitted` = 4.1.5). The first `\begin{tabular}` directly in a `{longrotatetable}` sets a caption still stored,
unnumbered; one no `\begin{tabular}` took (a `tabular*`, `tabularx` or `longtable` in it, or a `\tablecaption` after
the tabular) is set at the longrotatetable's end, in its group (`\lx@lrt@end@caption`; a held longtable keeps its own
number and id); the longrotatetable is then that table's float; around a deluxetable (or a `{table}`) it is the page's setting, the
deluxetable its own table; a `\tablecaption` stored there and not taken by the held table is lost, as in the PDF
(an overwritten store behaves the same way). In a `{longtable}` the `\tablecaption` is the caption only while the longtable has none —
numbered, the longtable's own `\caption` (tag and list entry), as the PDF counts the longtable (`\ref` 1, the next
table 2); after a `\caption` it is stored, never printed there (1903.10014, #740). In another float it is the float's `\caption`, as Perl. The author's caption is kept where the PDF
loses it, content before PDF fidelity; the numbering stays the PDF's. The emulateapj and AASTeX 5 stores are TeX's
(#740). Witnesses 2204.03327 (2 → 0, its two `{longrotatetable}` captions kept), 1511.09213 (the deluxetable's `[h]`
placement read again). Repros class-bindings/{aastex_tablecaption_before_deluxetable, tablecaption_inside_the_table_wins,
stored_tablecaption_scoped_to_its_group, longrotatetable_around_a_tabular_is_its_table,
longrotatetable_tablecaption_goes_to_its_table, kept_tablecaption_is_unnumbered, longtable_keeps_its_printed_caption,
longrotatetable_caption_without_a_tabular, kept_caption_label_names_the_table, longtable_tablecaption_is_numbered};
guards `perfect_kernel_batch73a::{aastex_tablecaption_before_deluxetable, tablecaption_inside_the_table_wins,
