longrotatetable_caption_without_a_tabular, kept_caption_label_names_the_table, longtable_tablecaption_is_numbered}`.

### 740. emulateapj's and AASTeX 5's stored `\tablecaption` is printed by every table's head (Perl: an Error outside a float)

**TeX**: emulateapj.cls:1293-1294 (1010.4329's copy :1217-1218) `\gdef\@tablecaption{#1}` stores the caption globally and
never empties it; every `{deluxetable}` prints the store, numbered, at its `\tablehead` or `\startdata` (:1325, :1333;
the copy's :1249, :1257), so a `\tablecaption` before or in the table (before its head) is its caption and a table
without one repeats the last (pdflatex: "TABLE 2 / Stored One."). AASTeX 5's aastex.cls:1280 `\gdef\pt@caption` is
emptied only `\AtBeginDocument` (:1305) and printed by every deluxetable's `\startdata` (:1507), empty or not.

**Perl**: `\let\tablecaption\caption` (deluxetable.sty.ltxml:77) — outside a float an Error ("outside any known float").

**Rust** (73a): the store (`\lx@deluxe@caption`, `\iflx@deluxe@persistent`, the default) is the classes' own: every
`\tablecaption` stores it globally — outside a float, in a table, in a float (which also sets it as its `\caption`, as
Perl) — and every deluxetable prints it at its print point (deluxetable_sty.rs `\lx@deluxe@print@caption` at
`\startdata`; emulateapj_cls.rs where the data opens, at `\tablehead` or `\startdata`), numbered, above the tabular;
an empty store is the number alone, set at the table's end (#664). A caption given in the data, after the print
point, is stored for the next table and kept for this one's end, unnumbered (#664); the next table without a caption
of its own prints it again, as pdflatex, but without its `\label` (`\lx@deluxe@shown`, `\lx@deluxe@caption@nolabel`):
the label names the table that shows the caption first, where pdflatex's names the repeat (it runs only there), and no
label is defined twice. A store printed by two tables from outside both (`\tablecaption{…\label{t1}}` before them)
defines its label twice, as pdflatex ("Label multiply defined"; ours warns nothing). In a `{longtable}` a `\tablecaption` is the caption only while the longtable has none, else
stored (1903.10014's AASTeX 5 longtable keeps its printed `\caption{Observing Log…}`, and "Summary of targets", never
printed, is not set); emulateapj's is numbered there, its `\tablehead` printing it (1810.10130). Witnesses 1010.4329
(4 → 0, each caption above its tabular), 1903.10014 (1 → 0). Repros class-bindings/{emulateapj_stored_caption_repeats,

### 745. Typewriter whitespace is kept only where an auto-opened element reaches text

**Decision** (int23 fix round 2; narrows #47): `open_text`'s exception for whitespace-only typewriter text (and an
explicit `\ `) applies only where the current element can reach `#PCDATA` directly or through auto-opened elements
(`can_contain_node_somehow`); elsewhere Perl's rule stands and the space is dropped (Document.pm `openText`: initial
whitespace where `#PCDATA` cannot go). An `{algorithmic}` set in `\ttfamily` (WileyNJDv5.cls:6953
`\algrenewcommand\ALG@beginalgorithmic{\ttfamily}`) put the space before its first `\item` straight into the
`ltx:listing`, whose model is `listingline*`: `Error:malformed` in a minimal document, schema-invalid output in
2608.15322, 2602.03247, 2607.19926. fancyvrb's indentation (#47's case, 2605.00468) lands in a paragraph the builder
auto-opens and is unchanged. Guard `perfect_kernel_batchint23::a_typewriter_algorithmic_drops_the_leading_space`; repro
`listings-algorithms/typewriter_algorithmic_drops_the_leading_space`.

### 746. `\setlength` on a non-register runs its code

**Decision** (73b; rc_struct6 row 4): latex.ltx:10253 `\def\setlength#1#2{#1 #2\relax}` is code TeX executes. When what
`#1` begins with, past spaces and `\relax` (and expanded, as TeX's `get_x_token`), is neither a register nor a prefix,
the braced `\setlength` (sect12.rs `assign_braced_length`) puts `#1 #2\relax` back unexpanded and lets it run, where
the `Variable` read reported "A <variable> was supposed to be here" and dropped both arguments. IEEEtran templates' empty
`\setlength` line before an `\item` (2201.08831, 2401.09168) took `\item` and `F` as its arguments: the item lost its
first letter and the conversion an Error; now the item runs (pdflatex 0 errors). The preamble runs it too: what it
typesets there starts a paragraph, whose `\everypar{\@nodocument}` (latex.ltx:9137) is TeX's "Missing
\begin{document}"; LaTeXML fires no preamble `\everypar` (stomach.rs `pending_everypar`), so the code is followed by
`\lx@setlength@nodocument`, which runs `\@nodocument` when the code, begun in vertical mode, left it horizontal
(fancyheadings' `\headrulewidth`, a macro since 2.0: `\setlength{\headrulewidth}{0pt}` prints "0.4pt 0pt" and raises
that Error, pdflatex 1; guard `perfect_kernel_batch73b::setlength_on_a_macro_in_the_preamble_errs_as_tex`). `\addtolength`
keeps the error, as `\advance` reads a variable. An undefined name run this way is LaTeXML's undefined command: its
Error, and an `<ERROR class="undefined">` element where it stood (`\setlength{\bibsep}{0pt}` without natbib: pdflatex 2
Errors, ours 2, "0pt" printed by both). Perl:
latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:4603 `{Variable}` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #971). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch73b::setlength_on_a_non_register_runs_its_code`; repro
`parameter-conditional/setlength_on_a_non_register_runs_its_code`.

### 747. A `\DeclareMathAlphabet`'d alphabet takes one argument

**Decision** (73b; rc_struct6 row 10): `\DeclareMathAlphabet{\cs}{enc}{fam}{ser}{sh}` defines `\cs{}` as the stock
alphabets are bound (`\mathrm{}`, sect07.rs; amsfonts' `\mathbb{}`): a bounded constructor carrying the font of
`lookup_tex_font`, as latex.ltx's alphabet sets its argument alone (`\select@group`). Perl's `DefPrimitiveI(cs, undef,
undef, font => …)` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2686) is a switch to the end of the group: `\mathfoo{AB}c` set `c` in the
alphabet too, and under mathalfa's `bb=ams` (mathalpha.sty:116 `\DeclareMathAlphabet{\mathbb}{U}{msb}{m}{n}`, after
`\let\mathbb\relax`) `\frac{\mathbb{W}_c}{w}` read `c` in msbm, where it sets nothing: "Missing sub/superscript
argument" (1810.09080). `\@fontswitch` (`{\foo XY}` for a `\DeclareOldFontCommand`) reads the font from the definition
as before (sect13.rs `math_alphabet_font`); in text the alphabet warns "should only appear in math mode", as the stock
ones. KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #972. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch73b::declared_math_alphabet_takes_one_argument`; repro
`fonts-nfss/declared_math_alphabet_takes_one_argument`.

### 748. A counter stepped in math whose label text cannot set is labelled as math

**Decision** (73b; rc_struct6 row 5): `label_stepped_counter` (counter/dialect.rs) digests the step's refnum and tags
(Package.pm:770 `DigestText(T_CS("\\the$ctr"))`, then `\lx@make@tags`) as text. TeX keeps `\@currentlabel`
unexpanded (latex.ltx:14963-14967) and typesets it only where `\ref` prints it. For a step made in math, the text digest
is held (`DiagnosticsHold`); if it raised an Error, it is discarded and the label digested again with `\the<ctr>` as
`\ensuremath{\the<ctr>}`, local to the label. `\renewcommand{\theconsta}{{\kappa_{\arabic{consta}}}}` with
`\refstepcounter{consta}` in a formula raised three "Script _ can only appear in math mode" per step (1609.03070: 93,
1904.00290: 57). A label text sets keeps Perl's digest, byte-identical (an equation stepped in math keeps its text tags).
Not the 70c timing redesign (labels digested only where printed): a mechanism-local fallback. Part of the surpass: a
`\ref` to such a label in text now prints the math label, where TeX typesets `\@currentlabel` (`{\kappa_{1}}`) in text
and errs ("Missing $ inserted"). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #973.
Guard `perfect_kernel_batch73b::refstepcounter_in_math_sets_a_math_label`; repro
`macro-state/refstepcounter_in_math_sets_a_math_label`.

### 757. A class's append to a locked command it redefined extends the class's own definition (Perl: lost)

When the lock refuses a redefinition that is the locked binding's replacement text with tokens appended or prepended
— etoolbox's `\appto`/`\preto` (`\edef#1{\expandonce#1…}`) and latex.ltx's `\g@addto@macro` build it from the meaning
they read — and the class's own refused definition of the name is on record (`\lx@dropped@<name>`, #265), the record
becomes the class's definition with the same tokens appended or prepended (state.rs `extended_refused_definition`), as
in TeX, where the class's definition is the meaning the append reads. wiley-article.cls:420-466 renews `\maketitle` and
:576 `\appto`s to it: the record held the kernel's body and the append, so the replay ran nothing of the class's title
page (1911.06213, 31 sample papers logging the refusal twice); vmsta.cls:691's `\appto\maketitle{\hypersetup…}` after
its own `\maketitle` (:534-545) likewise (1506.02940, 1801.00977: the received/revised/accepted/published dates, the
affiliation and the keywords the class alone prints are now kept). Parameterless token bodies only; any other
refused definition is recorded as before. Residual: vmsta's title page also prints its journal header with the
values the document did not set left empty — "Modern Stochastics: Theory and Applications () 51–65 / DOI:" and an
empty `<ref href="http://dx.doi.org/">` (1506.02940; the shape the `\submitted` entry of #758 was withheld for, page
furniture by ruling; SYNC_STATUS 75a row (d)). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch75a::maketitle_class_append_extends_class_body`;
repro `sectioning-frontmatter/class_title_page/maketitle_class_append_extends_class_body`.

### 759. What a refused setter's replay added to the class's own record reads as empty in the title-page deposit (Perl: never run)

The #482 replay of a refused class `\title`/`\author` keeps the class's lists; what the body added to a list for the
call's argument — vmsta.cls:296-315 `\g@addto@macro\@@@authors{…\name@m@front{#2}…}` — is the class's record of the field
the kernel's frontmatter carries. For each macro the kept replay changed (its assignment journal with the value before,
state.rs `AssignmentJournalGuard::assigned`) that is now a parameterless token list, the part the replay added — the
tail appended to the value before, the head prepended, the text inserted between the old value's common head and
tail (before a list's end sentinel), or the whole value when the replay overwrote the macro — joins
`lx_replay_records` when it holds the argument (sect05.rs `note_replay_records`), and `\lx@replay@records` takes each
recorded part out of its macro, locally, in the `\@maketitle` deposit and the `\maketitle` replay, as they null
`\@author`. What other code put in the same list stays: a class `\workplace` appending to the author list keeps its
text, in either call order, whether it appends or inserts before a sentinel. Once #757 let vmsta's own `\maketitle` replay, it printed the author and affiliation a
second time (1506.02940, 1801.00977). Residual, awaiting a ruling (SYNC_STATUS 75a row (e)): a record that does not
hold the argument — vmsta 2018+'s `\csxdef{author\the\c@author}` and its list of names — is not found, and its title page
prints the author line beside the creators, and its e-mail line — recovered content, kept nowhere else — twice (it is
built in the toks register `\email@author@toks`, vmsta.cls:1226/1248, not a macro; 1806.03850, 1810.09667, 2012.03249). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch75a::{maketitle_replay_reads_class_author_list_as_empty,
maketitle_replay_keeps_other_setters_in_shared_list,
maketitle_replay_keeps_other_setters_in_sentinel_list}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/class_title_page/maketitle_replay_{reads_class_author_list_as_empty,keeps_other_setters_in_{shared,sentinel}_list_*}`.

**77i.** The records are now read before a clean replay puts the stores back, so a store the body itself defines that
holds the argument is a record too and stays set (#482's 77i addendum; a document's `\gdef\myauth{#1}` read in the
body); the kernel's `\@author`/`\@shortauthor` are put back and are no records.

### 760. A document's `\halign` redefinition runs where a binding's alignment reaches `\halign` (Perl: never runs)

In TeX every amsmath alignment environment and every `\ialign`-based one (latex.ltx `\@array` for array/tabular/
tabularx, plain `\ialign` = `\everycr{}\tabskip\z@skip\halign`, `\eqalign`, `\matrix`, `\oalign`, eqnarray, longtable,
amscd, blkarray, IEEEtrantools, numcases) executes the token `\halign`, so a macro `\halign` runs just before the
primitive it finally reaches. Our bindings build those alignments in Rust (`\lx@begin@alignment`) and never executed
`\halign`; only those bindings run the prelude below — a document's or raw-loaded package's own `\ialign` does not, since
`\ialign` is `\let` to `\halign` (plain_base.rs, as Perl's plain_base.pool.ltxml:118). `\lx@begin@alignment`'s before-digest (tex_tables.rs `run_halign_redefinition_prelude`) now digests the
redefinition's expansion in the group the alignment starts in, just before it, and treats the primitive it ends with as
the alignment already being built. latex.ltx's `tabbing` builds its lines from boxes and never executes `\halign`: its
alignment carries `ALIGNMENT_WITHOUT_HALIGN` (latex_constructs `tabbing_bindings`) and runs no prelude. Only the
conservative shape runs: a parameterless macro whose expansion ends with a token meaning the primitive — a constructor
declared `halign_primitive` (core `Constructor::halign_primitive`): the primitive itself under any name (cryptocode.sty:950
`\let\@pc@halign\halign`) or, inside a pgf picture, its SVG stand-in `\lxSVG@halign`, which `\lxSVG@installcommands` lets
`\halign` to. A redefinition that does not end with the primitive, reaches it only through another macro (one macro
level only; pdflatex runs the two-level shape — a deliberate limit, guard
`halign_redefinition_not_ending_with_the_primitive_is_not_run`), or reaches it in mid-expansion is not run at all. Global
side effects of a redefinition run once per binding alignment, against TeX's measure-then-set: amsmath's measured
environments run their `\halign` twice (align, gather, gather*, multline, flalign, alignat; `split` in an equation four
times). Material the expansion typesets precedes the alignment, as on TeX's
list (pdflatex typesets it with 0 errors); in math contexts it is digested as math where TeX sets it as text in the
alignment's `\vcenter` (`aligned`, `matrix`, `split`: content kept, its mode differs). Where the alignment is the display
itself (`$$\halign`: amsmath's align/gather families, eqnarray, IEEEeqnarray — `ALIGNMENT_IS_DISPLAY`) TeX errs
"Improper \halign inside $$'s" and deletes it (tex.web §776 `flush_math`): a Warning names it and it is dropped.
cases.sty's `numcases` is not one: its `\halign` is inside a `\vbox` (cases.sty:73-75), and the material is kept.
amsmath's `multline` is a display too but is not marked (exception): its material is kept in the formula, the safe
direction.

cryptocode.sty:950-957 (and its `mode=text` branch :760-770) redefines `\halign` inside `\pseudocode` to bind `\@pc@lb`
to the alignment's `\\` and `\\` to its line-numbering wrapper. Without the prelude every pseudocode line after the
first lost its number, silently, and `mode=text` erred `undefined:\@pc@lb` (its `\@pc@modeend` closes the `{varwidth}`
holding the text-mode `\@pc@lb` before the wrapper calls it). Run 340: 27 papers with `undefined:\@pc@lb` (witnesses
1804.05141, 2106.03626, 2107.06049, 2108.04600, 2202.07253; 2107.05054 in TikZ nodes, 11 errors → 0; 2410.11134 95 →
481 numbered lines): all 27 now 0 Errors, every pseudocode row its own numbered row, words unchanged. Perl does not load
cryptocode.sty at all (raw loading off), so it has neither the numbering nor the error. Six amsmath/tabular-heavy papers
without cryptocode convert byte-identically. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch76a::*`; repros
`kernel-alignment/{cryptocode_halign_redefinition_numbers_lines, halign_redefinition_skips_tabbing_and_keeps_material}`.
**Why**: the author's content — every line number pdflatex prints — and an error-free log, by the TeX semantics of
`\halign` rather than a cryptocode special case.

### 761. → KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1263 (Only a titlepage with ink hides the document title in HTML (Perl: any titlepage hides it))

### 762. biblatex `\printbibliography` applies its entry filters (Perl: ignores the optional argument)

`\printbibliography[type=…]`, `nottype=`, `subtype=`, `notsubtype=`, `keyword=`, `notkeyword=`, `category=` and
`notcategory=` narrow the `.bbl`'s datalist as biblatex does (biblatex.sty:9526-9615 `\blx@key@type` …
`\blx@key@notcategory`): the entries of an `entry` datalist are filed by type, `entrysubtype` and comma-split keyword
while the `.bbl` is read (:8707-8711, :8385-8390); the filters apply in the order given and AND together, keeping
datalist order. **Repeated keys**: a key given twice is two filters (`keyword=author,keyword=latent` keeps the entries
with both; witness arXiv 2406.11014), except that `type` and `subtype` share one toggle (`blx@tempb`, :9532-9566): the
second of them is biblatex's error "'type' used multiple times" (or 'subtype') and an empty list. A positive filter
whose value no entry has is biblatex's Warning ("Type 'online' not found") and an empty list; an unknown `not*` value
is a no-op; an empty list is LaTeX's Warning "Empty bibliography" (`\blx@warn@bibempty`, :1511) and prints nothing, not
even its heading (:9866-9868). **Categories**: `\DeclareBibliographyCategory` (:11207) and `\addtocategory`
(:11218-11244) keep global lists (primitives, with biblatex's two errors). biblatex files a category's keys through the
`.aux`, so pdflatex prints every list with the categories the whole previous run filed; the binding decides category
membership once the whole document is digested, and digests no entry a list does not keep: each entry of a list
filtered by categories is deferred where it stands (`\biblatex@defer@entry`, the deferred-print mechanism of #738,
list `biblatex@category`) and built at the end of the document, before the hidden list, if it passes
(`\biblatex@select`), from the data its refsection's `.bbl` gave it, with its bibliography's `xml:id` prefix and its
font; the list's heading is built in place, wrapped in `\biblatex@if@selected[list]`, and a list that keeps no key is
"Empty bibliography" (an `\addtocategory` after the list counts). Under `--streaming` a fragment's yield builds the
pending entries with the keys filed up to then (guard
`114_streaming_cluster_regressions::streaming_builds_a_category_list_when_absorbed`). **Hooks**: an `\addtocategory` in code the binding never runs — a hook
or bibmacro (`\AtEveryCitekey`, `\AtEveryBibitem`, `\AtDataInput`, `\(re)newbibmacro`, …), a declaration
(`\DeclareBibliographyDriver`, historian.bbx/publist.bbx; `\DeclareFieldFormat`, `\DeclareIndex{Name,List,Field}Format`;
`\defbibcheck`; `\DeclareCiteCommand`'s code, musuos.cbx) — what they were given is kept and scanned, with the macros
it calls, as hgbbib.sty:113's `\@AssignToBibCategory`; a category name that is a macro parameter
(`\addtocategory{#1}{…}`) may be any. Such a category is unknown: a filter on it is not applied (one Info per category
and document), and a `\bibbycategory` with such a category prints the one unfiltered list — fail-safe: the list may
hold entries pdflatex leaves out (probe 6 of the 77a r2 review: pdflatex prints that list empty, its driver filing the
keys as the list prints), never an empty one pdflatex would fill. **Numbers**: an entry's label number is biblatex's:
with `defernumbers=false` its place among the numbered entries of its refsection's datalist (biblatex.sty:8891-8923
`\blx@bbl@labelnumber`: every entry but a `skiplab`/`dataonly` one or one with a `shorthand`), so it has one number in
every list of its refsection (`\printbibliography[type=book]` then `[nottype=book]`: Books [1][2], Articles [3][4],
citations "[2, 3, 1, 4]", as pdflatex) and its own in another refsection's; with `defernumbers=true` (package option or `\ExecuteBibliographyOptions`) the next
number of the refsection when the entry is first built, kept by every later list (:9216-9283 `\blx@addlabelnumber`),
`resetnumbers=true`/`<n>` restarting the count for entries not yet numbered (:9759-9765; without `defernumbers` it is
biblatex's Warning and ignored). Each built `ltx:bibentry` carries it as `ltx:bib-data` `labelnumber`
(`\biblatex@bbl@number`), which MakeBibliography prints and cites by in a biblatex bibliography (make_bibliography.rs
`given_number`, read from the list's own copy of the entry — a key several refsections print is numbered in each; a
`.bib` field `labelnumber` under natbib is no label; the list keeps its order); its own count restarted at 1 in each `ltx:bibliography`, so the filtered lists of one `.bbl` gave
two entries one label (witness arXiv 2406.00136: "[5,…] [7,…] [1,…] [1,…]" where pdflatex prints "[9,…] [11,…] [5,…]
[1,…]"). An author-year style numbers nothing. An entry with a `shorthand` takes no number: in a biblatex bibliography the
shorthand is its label (:8920 `\let\abx@field@labelnumber\abx@field@shorthand`; make_bibliography.rs `given_label`),
cited by it (2406.00136's keyword list is [HTT] [HA] [SAG] [Ker]; the other list [1]-[17]), on both routes: on the
`.bib` route (no `.bbl`, no `labelnumber`) the list numbers only the entries that print a number, each keeping its own
id (make_bibliography.rs `number_entry`; it printed `[Balbes & Dwinger] [2]`-`[5]`, pdflatex [1]-[4]). Only biblatex's: the
handlers that digest the label fields `shorthand` and `labelalpha` are the biblatex binding's (defined with its
loading of the BibTeX pool), and `given_label`/`given_number` read a label only in a biblatex bibliography — under
natbib/BibTeX those `.bib` fields are raw `ltx:bib-data` as in Perl and no label (`shorthand={\undefinedmacro TB}`
raised `Error:undefined`, a `labelalpha={Knu84}` printed [Knu84] and was cited "[, 1]"; pdflatex + bibtex 0 errors,
[2, 1]). **`\bibliographystyle`** is ignored, as biblatex does (blx-compat.def:13-17, loaded by biblatex.sty:16416), its error
"'\bibliographystyle' invalid for 'biblatex'" reported as a Warning (ignoring it keeps the labels; 64zf's honesty rule): the kernel's, left after `\printbibliography` by a natbib
template, rewrote the list's `bibstyle` to the `.bst`'s name, so the list was no longer a biblatex one and printed
[1]-[5] for `[Knu84; Böt01; Balbes & Dwinger; Goo94a; Goo94b]` (77a r5 review probe bs/a_alphabetic; pdflatex 1
error). **Entries no list prints**: once a list leaves out an entry of its
datalist, the entries no list of a refsection printed are built at the end of the document in a hidden
(`ltx_nodisplay`) bibliography — only those: each list records the entries it prints as it is digested
(`\biblatex@printed`, `\biblatex@select`), so none is built again in the hidden list (an entry two lists keep is
typeset twice, as in pdflatex) — numbered as above (0
with `defernumbers=true`, the label biblatex gives an entry it never numbered, :8898-8909): biblatex reads the whole
`.bbl` at `\begin{document}`, so pdflatex labels their citations and prints their `\fullcite` (cs-techrep's
`notcategory=selfref` with "Please cite as: \fullcite{selfref}", arXiv 2405.19762). **`\bibbycategory`** (:9955-9998) prints `\printbibliography[<options>,
category=<name>,heading=<name>]` per declared category: a category with no keys is skipped silently, none with keys is
"Empty bibliography", none declared "No categories found"; a non-void category whose keys the refsection never cites
prints nothing (biblatex prints its heading). **Headings**: `heading=<name>` titles the list with the argument of the
sectioning command of the author's `\defbibheading{<name>}[<title>]{<code>}`, `#1` the `title=` or the heading's
default; biblatex.def's own headings, and code with no sectioning command, keep the default title; an undefined
heading is no error here (biblatex's "Heading '…' not found"). **Refsections**: a `\printbibliography` prints its own
refsection's list (`section=`, else the current one, :9827 `\blx@tempe`), refsections numbered as biblatex numbers
them (`\refsection`/`\newrefsection` from 1, back to 0 at `\endrefsection`, :10776-10778, :10874; a citation after
`\end{refsection}` links to refsection 0's list; the `refsegment` environment and `\newrefsegment` open a segment
only `segment=` reads, no-ops here); a `.bbl` with none
of its own number, and refsections opened at headings (`refsection=section`, not counted), print every refsection's
list as before. A citation refers to its own refsection's entry (biblatex: a `\cite` in refsection <n> is to that
refsection's entry, with its number): refsection <n>'s lists are `lists="refsection<n>"` and its citations
`inlist="refsection<n>"` (`CITE_UNIT`, the chapterbib/bibunits mechanism), falling back to the default list as every
unit list does (#59); refsection 0 and refsections opened at headings keep the default list (probe r1 of the 77a r3
review: "A [1, 2]" linking to its own list, where the citation linked to refsection 2's [3]; witnesses arXiv
2308.00515, 2507.16315). Before, every call printed every entry at 0 errors (silent-loss inventory #21); the ar5iv Perl binding
(biblatex.sty.ltxml:857-862) declares `\printbibliography[]` and ignores the argument (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #983). Witness
arXiv 2406.00136 (`[keyword=alph]` then `[notkeyword=alph]`): 21 + 21 entries → 4 + 17, as pdflatex. **Not modelled**:
refsections opened at headings (`refsection=chapter|section`, biblatex's `\blx@refpatch@sect` heading patch, a no-op
here) are not counted, so each `\printbibliography` prints every refsection's list and their citations go to the
default list (arXiv 2406.01695: 8 calls → 96 lists, 566/566 citations outside their chapter's list; SYNC row 21);
`check=`/`\defbibcheck`, `filter=`/`\defbibfilter`, `segment=`, a `\printbibliography[sorting=…]` (its own
refcontext's datalist; the default one prints), `omitnumbers`, `prefixnumbers`/`labelprefix` (and the `resetnumbers`
they imply), biblatex's
Warning "Split bibliography detected", the package-level `sorting=` on the `.bib` route (no `.bbl`; `sorting=none` still lists alphabetically), any filter on
that route, where a filtered list never repeats
the previous one, so `\bibbycategory` prints one unfiltered list (titled by its first heading); the hidden list also
holds `\nocite`d entries no list printed, not `skipbib` ones, and building them raises the errors their data raises,
which pdflatex never typesets (pinned: `biblatex_filtered_out_entries_errors`, 2 errors, pdflatex 0); a citation of an
entry several lists of one refsection print links to the last of them; the `.bib` route numbers a `style=alphabetic`
list where biber gives alphabetic labels (predates 77a); a key two refsections file with different data
is built in a category list from its own refsection's (a snapshot), but a crossref'd parent from the last one read. Code `biblatex_sty.rs` `bbl_filter`, `bbl_print`, `blx_selected`, `blx_unmodelled_categories`,
`blx_unprinted_bibliography`, `blx_heading_title`, `blx_target_refsection`, `blx_refsection_list`;
make_bibliography.rs `given_number`, `given_label`, `number_entry`, `get_bib_entries`; repros
`index-bib/biblatex_printbibliography_filters`,
`biblatex_category_filter_timing`, `biblatex_bibbycategory_headings`, `biblatex_category_hook_filled`,
`biblatex_category_errors`, `biblatex_filter_repeated_keys`, `biblatex_bibbycategory_empty`,
`biblatex_bibbycategory_no_bbl`, `biblatex_filter_refsections`, `biblatex_filtered_out_fullcite`,

### 763. → Bindings beyond Perl's tree: an.cls, apa.cls, cclayout.sty (`an_cls.rs`, `apa_cls.rs`, `cclayout_sty.rs`)

### 764. A shipped class's pre-2020 `\@pushfilename` is read with the pop of its era (TL 2025 pdflatex: errors; Perl: OmniBus)

pasa.cls (2013/04/01 v1.0, Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia; shipped, not in TeX Live) redefines
`\@pushfilename` at :45-52 with the LaTeX2e kernel's body before 2020-10 and calls it once, bare. latex.ltx's 2020-10
`\@pushfilename` also pushes the default hook label and the file path (`\@expl@push@filename@@`,
`\@kernel@currpathstack`; its last token, `\@expl@push@filename@aux@@`, reads the three tokens that follow — the
`\xdef\@currname{…}` of `\@onefilewithoptions`) and its `\@popfilename` pops both, so every package loaded after the
class — its own `\usepackage{graphicx}` at :1339 first — popped a hook label nobody pushed: "LaTeX hooks Error: Extra
\PopDefaultHookLabel" once per load, 13-39 Errors per paper and nothing else (pdflatex on TL 2025 stops with the same
and "File ended while scanning use of \@p@pfilepath@aux"; the class compiled cleanly on the LaTeX of its era). The
kernel's push cannot stand in for the class's copy, because the bare call at :52 would feed its last token
`\newlength\trimwidth`. The pasa binding (pasa_cls.rs, an author-file stand-in) therefore reads the class with the pop
of the same era (`\expandafter\@p@pfilename\@currnamestack\@nil`, locked while the class is read) and restores the
kernel's push and pop after it, so every load balances: the 13 sample papers (1307.3127, 1501.02922, 1510.05346,
1703.06635, 1802.01188, 1407.1937, 1607.08620, 1602.04538, 1401.2223, 1705.02067, 1609.00634, 1511.02959, 1703.03169)
go from 13-39 Errors to 0, word counts unchanged. Packages the class loads get the class's hook label rather than their
own (no hook label is pushed for them, as on the LaTeX of the era). Repro `loader/pasa_era_pushfilename_balanced`
(with a pasa.cls stub); guard `perfect_kernel_batch77c::pasa_era_pushfilename_balances_package_loads`.

### 765. → #993 (Author-name separators beside a control word, a line break or a mark, and in a mark's math (Perl: " and " between spaces only))

### 766. A paragraph break inside an inline-only frontmatter item is a line break (Perl: the paragraphs run together)

A frontmatter item is digested in text mode (Perl `digestFrontmatterItem` → `DigestText`), where `\par` closes no
paragraph, so an item whose element holds only inline content — `Inline.model`: no `ltx:p`, but `ltx:break` —
ran its paragraphs together into one text: apa.cls's `\acknowledgements{We thank …\n\nCorrespondence to …}` (#763)
read "…agency. Correspondence…". By user ruling (2026-10-18) such a paragraph break is a line break of the item.

Mechanism: the item's text is digested in a mode frame of its own (`digest_frontmatter_item`; the body of a keywords or
classification environment, `\lx@add@frontmatter@until`, in the frame it began in), and the field and that frame's depth
(the number of frames binding `MODE`) are noted there (`note_frontmatter_paragraphs`). A `\par` digested at that depth
records the field on its whatsit (tex_paragraph.rs `\lx@normal@par`, `frontmatter_paragraph_field`); a box, an
alignment cell or math inside the item begins a deeper frame, where the `\par` is the ordinary one — in a box or a `c`
cell it ends nothing, as in TeX (tex.web §1096 `end_graf`: `\date{\begin{tabular}{c}D1\par D2\end{tabular}}` "D1D2") —
while a group (`{\bfseries …}`) begins none. At construction, where the schema is loaded (Perl too reads the model only
when it builds the document; WISDOM #100), the `\par`'s constructor (base_utilities/frontmatter/queue.rs `frontmatter_paragraph_break`)
walks up from the insertion point to that field's element; when the element is inline-only and no element on the way
holds paragraphs of its own (a minipage, a note), it inserts a marked `ltx:break` when the item's content so far ends
in other content — not before its first content, not after another such break (a run of `\par`s, in a group too) —
and closes nothing. When the item element closes, the marked breaks left at its end are dropped
(`drop_trailing_paragraph_breaks`). Otherwise the `\par` is the ordinary one: an `ltx:abstract` (`Block.model`) keeps its
`<p>`s, an `ltx:note` its one run of text, a box absorbed outside its item (a reused title) is untouched. No token of the
item is changed.

Where it shows: `ltx:acknowledgements`, `ltx:keywords`, `ltx:classification`, `ltx:pubnote`, `ltx:contact`, `ltx:date`
and `ltx:title`. In the standard classes `\title` and `\date` are not `\long` — pdflatex stops with "Paragraph ended
before \date was complete" — so those two are reached through `\long` setters (apa's), bindings, or an `\endgraf`. An
author's name is digested in a frame of its own inside its `ltx:creator` item, so a `\par` in it ends nothing, as before.
A macro whose string body is a single space tokenizes as an empty line, `\par` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #984): amsppt's
`\usualspace`, biblatex's `\bibnamedelimi` and axessibility's `\auxiliaryspace` (the Perl/ar5iv bodies), and the
Rust-only bindings' `\And`/`\AND`/`\Ands` (colm2025_conference, jmlr, jmlr2e) are explicit space tokens now (colm's
`\Ands` had made "Carol <break/>Dan"; `X\bibnamedelimi Y` had split a paragraph). Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/inline_item_paragraphs_are_line_breaks`,
`sectioning-frontmatter/class_notes/apa_acknowledgements_paragraphs_are_lines`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77f::{inline_item_paragraphs_are_line_breaks, apa_acknowledgements_paragraphs_are_lines,
single_space_macros_are_spaces}`. **Why**:
the author's line structure is content; merging two paragraphs into one sentence run misreports it.

### 767. What a raw class's title page prints is decided by a speculative run of that title page; the static class-code readers are the fallback — absorbs #413 #416 #432 #634 #643 #662 #741 #756 #758 #791 #936 #939 #940 #941 #955

**Rule.** A raw class's title-page stores, contact setters and registers reach the frontmatter API by name (the surveyed
setter table) when their body is a pure store, and whether each is printed is judged by a speculative run of the class's
own title page with sentinel values; an off-table store no kept run typesets is handed on. Where no run can be made, the
static readers of the class code decide.

**Perl.** Drops every such store: its class bindings and OmniBus's table (OmniBus.cls.ltxml:62-247) are its only route,
bypassed under raw loading; the class's `\@maketitle` never runs under the locked `\maketitle`. **TeX.** The class's
`\@maketitle` prints its stores (ptptex.cls:616 `\gdef\@inst{#1}`, jpsj2.cls:841-847).

**Sub-rules** (`latexml_engine/src/frontmatter_stores.rs` module doc)
- *The table*: `latexml_core/src/binding/store_setters.rs:22 STORE_SETTERS` (655 TL classes surveyed; a synonym table,
  never a name pattern); a setter a binding defined is the binding's.
- *The run*: `frontmatter_stores.rs:4897 before_title_page_runs`, `:4513 sentinel_runs` (letters and digits sentinels;
  a numeric context consumes the digits), confirmed with the document's values; the `\maketitle` replay gate reads the
  class body as TeX runs it (`latex_constructs/sect05.rs:2241`; formerly #756).
- *Static readers* (the fallback, retiring post-cutoff, ruling 9): `:1423 prints_as_a_value`, `:1480
  glued_to_class_text`; a default handed only when the title page or page styles print it (formerly #662).
- *Shapes*: keywords a class's abstract defines (formerly #634); a setter by its name with side definitions (formerly
  #643); in-place contact setters (`:2772 reroute_in_place_contact_setters`; formerly #936); a register only a page style
  prints (formerly #939); a raw package's stores (formerly #940); a mark before a pure store (formerly #941); displaced
  affiliation text (formerly #955); a class-numbered `\institute` by numbers (formerly #791); neurips's
  `\@projectpage` (formerly #741); wiley-article and CSML (formerly #758).
- *A labelled off-table store* (QA61, DG 2026-11-15; BM Q3.13): one the run prints right after the class's own label, in
  a line holding no other value and not glued to the class's text, is an `ltx:pubnote` named by the label even where the
  deposit or replay typesets it; they read it as empty and take the label out, from the line the label was read in
  (`decide_moved_offtable_stores`). The line runs between line breaks in the innermost group around the store that is
  no argument a face or box prints (`\texttt`, `\mbox`, `\href`'s text), or in the macro's body: `\texttt{\@x} \@y\par` and `E-mail: \@x, tel.\ \@y\par` stay
  (`store_lines_among`; the other readers of `store_lines` keep the innermost group). The class
  prints its title and names bare, so an unlabelled store stays where the deposit typesets it (SelfArx `\PaperTitle`,
  2011.01685), as one glued to its text (fundam `FI-\@publyear`, 2006.07415) or read by its `\title`/`\author`/`\@author`.
- *Page furniture* (FURN): a one-shot eso-pic overlay is the title page's picture (`eso_pic_sty.rs`; formerly #413);
  textpos blocks are placed where written (`textpos_sty.rs`; formerly #416); a copyright line only a page foot prints
  is a frontmatter note (formerly #432).

**Witnesses** 1805.12376, 1303.3004, 1310.0585, 1202.2889 (astlb `\email`), 2607.06973 (googlecloud), 2307.16262
(medima.sty), 0712.1312 (copernicus), 1206.6940. **Guards**
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::a_class_body_calls_a_setter_through_one_token`,
`perfect_kernel_batch94b::a_contact_in_running_text_stays_the_class`,
`perfect_kernel_batch95d::a_date_with_no_label_read_keeps_its_default_only_where_printed`,
`perfect_kernel_batch77i::offtable_store_typeset_by_the_title_page`. RED:
`mark_then_store_email_read_by_a_refused_abstract_red`. **Upstream.** Not offered (Perl runs no raw class title page).
Residuals: `\ifnum`-tested and `\romannumeral` stores (`frontmatter_stores.rs:4380-4390`). Records: [the archive](../archive/OD_FRONTMATTER_RECORDS_2026-11-15.md).

### 768. A tcolorbox listing environment's box title is the listing's title (Perl: raw tcblistings, the box not read back)

tcolorbox prints a listing box's `title=` in the box's title bar (tcolorbox.sty:162-163 `\tcbtitle`, :214
`title/.store in=\kvtcb@title`); `\newtcblisting`/`\NewTCBListing` environments and `\newtcbinputlisting` commands are
boxes around `\tcblisting{…,options@for=name}` / `\tcbinputlisting{…}` (tcblistingscore.code.tex:301-378). **Perl**
raw-loads them (tcolorbox.sty.ltxml:27). **Rust** delegates them to listings (OD #410), which typeset the listing
without the box and had dropped every box option but the counter, the mode and the listing file — the "Example N: …"
or "Listing N: …" of each box was lost with no diagnostic (silent-loss row #16).

Now the box options are set in a group as the box sets them (`tcolorbox_sty::tcb_resolve_listing_mode`, for the
environments and for `\newtcbinputlisting`; inside another box, where tcolorbox's `every box on layer N` is `reset`, the
enclosing box's title is cleared first), the resolved `\kvtcb@title` is parked (`tcb_pending_title`) and the listing
takes it as its listings `title=` when it has none (`listings_sty::lst_process_display_with` → `\lstlisting@maketitle`):
an unnumbered `ltx:float class="ltx_lstlisting"` whose `ltx:caption` (and `ltx:toccaption`) is the title, always above
the code — the box's title bar is above whatever listings' `captionpos` says (the box gobbles `\lst@MakeCaption`, so
`captionpos` never reaches it; 2409.11413 setup.tex:86 and 2402.13846 headers/lqa/listing.tex:35 set `captionpos=b`). Not in the list of
listings (tcolorbox reads the body back `nolol`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #988). The box's `listing remove caption`
(tcblistings.code.tex:69-72, on by default through `reset@listings`, :88-93) is honoured the same way: it gobbles
`\lst@MakeCaption`, so listings' own caption, title and list entry are not made — the box title is the only one
(2409.11413's `\lstset{title=\lstname}` had emptied all 13 "Listing N: …" titles; a raw box's read-back runs with
`\lst@MakeCaption` = `\@gobble`, which `lst_process_display_with` reads as such). The box frame and colours are not
drawn; a box with `detach title` (title not in the bar) keeps none. `\newtcbinputlisting`'s `[init]` options go through
tcolorbox's own init processor under the command's name (`\__tcobox_process_newtcolorbox:nn`, tcblistingscore.code.tex:359; a
tcolorbox without it, `\tcb@proc@options@init`: `tcolorbox_sty::tcb_process_init`), and each use runs the counter `code=` it left
in `\tcb@opt@<name>` (tcolorbox 6.10 moved it to expl3, tcolorbox.sty:2428-2444), so
`use counter=` gives each use `\thetcbcounter`, and a box without a counter has an empty `\thetcbcounter`
(tcolorbox.sty:2335-2337 `\tcb@proc@counter@no`, key `no counter` :2258; 2605.21082's `title={\textbf{code~\thetcbcounter}: #2}` prints "code : …",
`tcolorbox_sty::tcb_counter_step_code`). `\newtcbinputlisting` also carries the box's phantom code (a per-use `label=` /
`hypertarget=`, at the listing's first line as for the environments) and follows the box's mode as `\tcbinputlisting`
does (tcblistingscore.code.tex:195-220, `tcb_pending_layout`): `listing and text` (the default) typesets the file again
after the listing, `text and listing` before it, `text only` alone, `listing only` not. An absent begin-line argument
stands in the options as xparse passes it: an `O{}` its empty default (an empty `\def` splices to nothing;
neoschool.cls:5168-5214 `\ifx\relax#3\relax` had titled all 40 `{code}` boxes, and its unspliced stand-ins raised 44 of
its 141 pgfkeys errors), a LEADING `O{default}`/`D[]{default}` its default and a leading `o`/`d[]` xparse's no-value
marker (the `\lstnewenvironment` arity's default is the slot's stand-in, `tcb_xparse_listing`; its empty default had
made `\IfNoValueTF{#1}{Code}{Code: #1}` "Code: " and `O{Default}` empty). The raw `{tcblisting}` environment is
unchanged: it draws the box (a picture), title included.

Residuals: `blend into=listings` (its `before title` "Listing N: " prefix), `before title=` and `attach title to upper`
are not captured; `adjusted title`'s `\vphantom` renders as a hidden span with width; a `text only` listing
environment still shows its code (the delegation always displays it; `\newtcbinputlisting` honours the mode); a
`text only` input listing has no listing to carry its title (a paragraph before the text) or its label (dropped); the `comment` modes' comment
is not typeset; `captionpos=tb` keeps Perl's `eq 't'` reading for a listings title (bottom only). A box `label=`'s
`\ref` prints the enclosing section's number, not the box's counter (Perl identical; `perfect_kernel/SILENT_LOSS_INVENTORY.md`, the SYNC silent-loss row "tcolorbox
box label").

Witnesses 2405.01480, 2405.02221, 2405.02462, 2405.03285, incgraph-doc (and the same template shipped unused by the

### 769. A caption is a paragraph of a vertical box, read as its macro argument (Perl: `PBoxContents` read live; the trailing `\label` last)

A float caption is set as a paragraph in a vertical box: latex.ltx's `\@makecaption` sets `#1: #2\par` in a `\vbox`
when it does not fit one line, amsart.cls:1386-1392 always (`\vbox{\noindent…}`), so `$$…$$` in a caption is display
math. **Perl** builds `\@@caption` and `\@@toccaption` from `PBoxContents` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3368-3371;
TeX_Box.pool.ltxml:200-213: `readBoxContents` in `internal_vertical` with `\lx@enterhorizontal` in front). **Rust** had
`\lx@@caption{}` / `\@@toccaption{}` with `mode => "text"` — restricted horizontal, where `$$` is an empty formula
(tex.web §1138) and the formula's `_` text: "Script _ can only appear in math mode" ×2 per caption, the display lost
(1005.1555, 1907.01498, 2310.11556, 1404.2359). Now both take the ported `PBoxContents` (tex_box.rs, with
`\lx@enterhorizontal`), so the display is an `ltx:equation` in an `ltx:inline-block` of the caption, the text after it
an `ltx:p` there; Perl's output puts the `ltx:equation` straight in the caption and its list copy (`<ltx:equation>
isn't allowed in <ltx:caption>` and `… in <ltx:toccaption>`, 4 Errors on the repro).

Departures from Perl's reading, each for a caption the engine set as text before: (1) the material is the braced
argument, digested from a mouth of its own (as `HBoxArgContents` digests an unbraced one), not read live up to the
box's own `}`: the caption is always a macro's argument (`\@caption@@@`, `\lx@format@caption@@`), tokenized before
`\lx@@caption` reads it, and a formula it leaves open ends with it — an author's `$` in a math `\qty` unit (2512.12866:
`$t \approx \qty{29000}{fm/$c$}$`) made the live reader take the caption's `}` as the formula's and read on through the
float and the document (10 → 17 Errors). (2) The box's mode is `inline_internal_vertical`, which ends no paragraph
around it with a `\par`, and `\lx@enterhorizontal` fires no `\everypar` (`stomach::enter_horizontal_without_everypar`,
as Perl's `enterHorizontal`, Stomach.pm:422-433): in an aas `\references`, whose `\par` opens an entry and whose
`\everypar` would too, a caption in a float made phantom entries ("<ltx:bibitem> isn't allowed in <ltx:table>";
LaTeX's floats reset `\everypar`, latex.ltx `\@floatboxreset`). (3) A `\label` after `\caption` goes in front of the
caption's material as `\lx@caption@postlabel` (`\@caption@postlabel`), where Perl appends a `\label`
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3175): the paragraph ends with a final display's `ltx:equation` open, which the label took
(2310.11556, 1404.2359 lost the figure's label), while LaTeX's `\label` names what `\caption`'s `\refstepcounter`
stepped (latex.ltx:17391-17393), the float; under its own name the scan for the caption's own labels does not take the
caption's text as its argument (a stray `\fi` there closed the scan's `\ifx`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #641), and the toc copy
drops it. A `\label` the author writes inside the caption right after a display is the residual Perl shares: LaTeX's
`$$…$$` steps no counter, so `\@currentlabel` is still the float's and the reference reads its number (as ours does),
but the label lands on the unnumbered `ltx:equation` it follows (`floatToLabel`, the nearest labelled element still
open), so the link targets the display, not the float — Perl the same, in a caption as in running text (review probe
cap2 `fig:inner`; moving it is a change to `\lx@label`'s target rule, not this caption's).
(4) `\@@add@caption@counters` reads the list extension (`\ext@<type>`) by expansion, as it reads `\@captype`: digested,
its letters began a paragraph in the float's vertical list whose horizontal mode outlived the counters (every float
body after its caption was in horizontal mode).

The caption's size is now Perl's: a paragraph of the current `\hsize` (`repack_paragraph`'s `width`, Perl #2798), where
it was the natural width of one line or the leaked paragraph around it. Floats sized from it change: panels side by
side whose caption widened them past the line no longer break the row (2107.02579's 0.3\textwidth subfigures), a
caption in a minipage no longer opens the paragraph the capture pruned (`ltx_pruned_first` gone), and rotated floats
take the caption's paragraph height (graphrot.xml's `sidewaystable`, `perfect_kernel_batch65a`'s transforms).
Residual: a tabularray `talltblr` caption is set at the float's `\hsize` (tabularray_sty.rs `\lx@tblr@caption`) where
tabularray sets it at the table's width (tabularray.sty:6444-6452, :6481-6492), so a talltblr beside another table in
one float is now a row of its own (`perfect_kernel_batch57::tabularray_tall_table_in_a_{captionless,captioned}_float`;
pdflatex: side by side). Giving `{lx@tblr@box}` the table's width as its size (`cached_width` in its `after_digest`) does
not reach `arrange_panels`, which sizes the panel from the box node's own content; reach ~0 (3 of 6,000 projection
papers use talltblr/longtblr, none side by side, all byte-identical).
Repro `captions-floats/caption_display_math_is_display_1005.1555`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77k::{caption_display_math_is_display, caption_without_display_is_one_text_run}`.

### 770. A revtex `\preprint` number the class does not print is metadata (Perl: always a pubnote)

`\preprint` stores the number for the title page, which prints it or not by the class family's own rule. **Perl** makes
every call a displayed pubnote (revtex4_support.sty.ltxml:71 `\lx@add@pubnote[role=preprint]{#1}`). **Rust** follows the
class (user rulings 2026-10-06 display toggles, 2026-10-09 unprinted metadata → RDFa), choosing the branch before it
reads the argument (revtex4_support_sty.rs `\preprint`, `preprint_printed`):
- REVTeX 4.1/4.2: the title page prints the store (aps4-1.rtx:216-221 `\ps@titlepage`, aip/aapm/sor alike) under
  `\preprint@sw` — `preprintnumbers`/`nopreprintnumbers`, an unset switch following the `preprint` style (`preprint`,
  `manuscript`, `checkin`; revtex4-2.cls:5927-5930, revtex4-1.cls alike) — and `\frontmatter@init`, a document hook
  (revtex4-1.cls:2094, :2517-2519), empties it, so a preamble `\preprint` is not printed.
- REVTeX 4.0 (revtex4.cls; `revtex@preprint@v4.0`, set by revtex4_cls.rs, which also serves revtex4-2): the store is
  emptied once at load (:4618-4619), so a preamble call is printed too, and the `preprint` style forces `\preprint@sw`
  on after the options (class init hook, :3811-3812), so `nopreprintnumbers` does not hide it there.
- REVTeX 3/3.1 (revtex3_support_sty.rs, also under aipproc): aps.sty:965-968 defines `\@preprint` only under
  `\ifpreprintsty` and `\@maketitle` prints it (:1006-1010), with no reset — printed in the preprint style wherever it
  is called (305 of 8,247 REVTeX 3 papers of 9601-0001 are preprint style with a `\preprint`), decided in TeX by
  `\ifpreprintsty`.
A printed number is Perl's pubnote, its argument read as TeX reads it (`Fe$_{2}$YZ`, `DESY~11--210` as on the page;
a text `_` errs as in pdflatex). An unprinted one is an `ltx:rdf property="dcterms:identifier"` per `\\`-separated number
at the argument's top level (a `\\` in a group or an environment — a `\parbox`, FERMILAB's `{minipage}` with
`{flushright}` — is the block's own), read as an identifier (Semiverbatim, in the identity encoding), KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#990. The class options are recorded by revtex4_cls.rs and revtex4_1_cls.rs (`revtex@preprintsty`,
`revtex@preprintnumbers`), REVTeX 3's by revtex3_support (`\global\preprintstytrue`). Witnesses 2408.13616,
1912.04576, 2110.00437 (unprinted, 4.1), 1207.6705 (unprinted, 4.0), 1205.1463 (a preamble `\preprint` dropped, two
printed); repros `sectioning-frontmatter/revtex_preprint_number_is_an_identifier_2408.13616`,
`…/revtex3_preprint_style_prints_the_number`, `…/revtex_printed_preprint_is_read_as_tex`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77k::{revtex_preprint_number_is_an_identifier, revtex_printed_preprint_is_read_as_tex,
revtex_unprinted_preprint_splits_only_top_level_lines, revtex3_preprint_style_prints_the_number,
revtex40_preprint_numbers_follow_the_class}`.

### 773. A second `\documentstyle` raises LaTeX's error and loads no class (Perl: applies latex209 and the class again)

latex.ltx:18617-18618 `\documentclass` makes itself `\@twoclasseserror` (:18944-18947, "Two \documentclass or
\documentstyle commands", the rest gobbled), and `\documentstyle` (:18622-18624) ends in `\documentclass`, so a second
class declaration only errs. Perl's `\documentstyle` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:97-129) loads the class every time.
Now the document's first `\documentclass` or `\documentstyle` sets `lx@class@declared` (sect01.rs `CLASS_DECLARED`)
and a later `\documentstyle` raises the LaTeX error and loads nothing; a second `\documentclass` is unchanged (it still
loads, sect01.rs `retract_chapter_before_class_load`). A first declaration no binding and no file answered — the
OmniBus fallback (tex_job.rs `\lx@documentstyle@impl`'s last branch; after `\documentclass`, OmniBus newly loaded
and the class's own `.cls_loaded`/`.cls_raw_loaded` unset) — does not count (main-session ruling 2026-10-19): the real
`\documentstyle` after it loads. astro-ph9812142's line 1 is `#\documentstyle[psfig,epsf]{/disk/3/roud/home/Texstuff/aa}`
— the `#` is no comment: pdflatex says "You can't use macro parameter character #", runs that `\documentstyle`, and
stops at the missing class (no PDF; TL 2025 has no aa.cls either) — and its line 2 `\documentstyle[psfig,epsf]{aa}`
gives aa's `\thesaurus`, `\offprints` and bibitem tags (1 Error, the stray `#`; 3,433 words, as 67int19b). latex209.def's
definitions (`\lx@latex@ix@definitions`, since 70b) apply once per document: applied again, they saved the settled
`\normalsize` as `\original@normalsize` and the two called each other (Timeout:Convert); a second class load after the
fallback runs again under the 2e-command traps' `\@gobble` until its own `\@documentclasshook`. Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/documentstyle_twice_loads_one_class`, `sectioning-frontmatter/documentstyle_after_a_missing_class`;
guards `perfect_kernel_batch77r::{documentstyle_twice_loads_one_class, documentstyle_after_a_missing_class_loads_the_class,
documentstyle_after_a_missing_documentclass_loads_the_class}`.

### 774. A siunitx unit's own `\DeclareSIUnit[<options>]` apply where it is a command's whole unit (Perl: stored, ignored)

siunitx.sty:6684-6694 keeps a unit's options from `\DeclareSIUnit[<options>]{\unit}{…}` and applies them when that unit
is the whole unit argument of `\qty`/`\SI`/`\unit`, before the command's own options. Perl's siunitx binding stores the
options and never reads them, so a unit declared with `number-unit-product={}` keeps the default thin space. The Rust
binding applies them (`six_begin_processing_for_units`), and an explicit empty value for a token-list key is empty, not
`true`: 2504.05919's `\DeclareSIUnit[number-unit-product={}]\%{\char`\%}` prints "85%" as pdflatex does; 1501.03532's
per-unit `number-unit-product = \ ` puts its interword space before nm/dBm. 77r r2; repro
`package-bindings/siunitx_unit_named_by_its_own_char_code`; guard `perfect_kernel_batch77r::siunitx_*`.

### 777. T4, X2 and OT2 have font maps; a text symbol of an encoding with no map warns when dropped (Perl: no maps, the letters lost)

**TeX**: t4enc.def (fc, the "African Computer" fonts) declares the African Latin letters as composites of its own
commands — `\DeclareTextComposite{\m}{T4}{y}{175}` (:164) — and `\m`'s own body is an `\errmessage` ("Non existent
modified letter", :36-39) for a letter it has no slot for. x2enc.def and ot2enc.def put Cyrillic letters in the Latin
letters' slots (X2's extended Cyrillic: `\CYRAE` 65 … `\cyrizh` 122; OT2's wncyr transliteration: `A` А, `C` Ц, `Q` Ч).

**Perl**: no t4/x2/ot2.fontmap.ltxml, and its LaTeX.pool `\DeclareTextComposite` is ignored, so the encodings fall back
to OT1 (`Couldn't find font encoding`): `\m{y}` reaches t4enc.def's `\errmessage` and the letter is lost (2405.01972:
44 Errors in Rust before this, Perl's `\errmessage` a Note; pdflatex 0), an X2/OT2 `\DeclareTextSymbol` defines
nothing (`\cyrje` prints nothing, no diagnostic), and Latin letters typed in OT2 text print themselves where pdflatex
prints Cyrillic ("Moskva" for Москва).

**Rust** (77u): `t4_fontmap.rs` — the lower half T1's (the fc fonts are EC-shaped), the upper half fccoding.mf's glyphs
as fc.rme's Appendix D "T4-to-UCS correspondence" maps them, its slips corrected (139 Ń, 150 Ʒ, 152 Ė, 162 ɛ, 172 ʃ,
173/174 ŋ/ʋ), the letters Unicode has no character for as combining sequences (E̱, Ɛ̃ …) and fj as two letters;
`x2_fontmap.rs` — T2A's upper half and accents, x2enc.def's letters in the Latin slots (Unicode from x2enc.dfu; Ԛ/Ԝ/Ԩ/Ҏ
where it has none); `ot2_fontmap.rs` — wncyr10's glyphs (wncyr10.afm) with ot2enc.def's letters, and the fonts'
ligature program (wncyr10.tfm's LIGTABLE, 78 pairs: `sh` ш, `shch` щ, `ya` я, `e1` э, `N0` №, `[[` «, run as TeX
runs it, the result read again with the next character), so OT2's transliteration reads as the PDF prints it
(1405.1988, 2510.25931 "sh"; letter by letter it was "сх"). A `\DeclareTextAccent` whose slot holds a combining mark
(T4's `\G` 159, `\U` 188, `\I` 191) uses that mark, T2A/X2's `\C` (slot 19, ‶) the double grave, and one for a
command another encoding's file already declared as a text command still defines this encoding's command (OT2's
`\U{i}` й after X2's or T2A's `\U`; latex.ltx's `\DeclareTextCommand` always does). A `\DeclareTextSymbol` of an encoding that still has no map
(tipa's T3 until 77x, #781) keeps its empty body but warns once per symbol where it is used, naming the encoding
(`\lx@unmapped@text@symbol`, sect08.rs) — the loss is no longer silent. Witness 2405.01972: 45 Errors → 1 (the
`substitutefont.sty` TL 2025 lacks), "weeɓitanay", "jooɗodi", "o ƴetti" in place; its `\textipa{\textltailn}` (T3) now
warns. Repros `fonts-nfss/{t4_modified_letter_help_is_not_expanded, t4_african_letters_print,
x2_ot2_cyrillic_symbols_print, x2_ot2_cyrillic_letters_and_composites, ot2_transliteration_ligatures,
text_symbol_of_an_unmapped_encoding_warns}`; guards `perfect_kernel_batch77u::{t4_modified_letter_prints,
t4_african_letters_print, x2_ot2_cyrillic_symbols_print, x2_ot2_cyrillic_letters_and_composites,
ot2_transliteration_ligatures, second_encoding_accent_composes, text_symbol_of_an_unmapped_encoding_warns}`.

### 778. A `\p@<counter>` reference form is applied to the expanded number, as `\refstepcounter` stores it (Perl: typed unexpanded at the step)

**TeX**: latex.ltx:14963-14964 `\refstepcounter` stores `\protected@edef\@currentlabel{\csname p@#1\expandafter
\endcsname\csname the#1\endcsname}`: `\p@<counter>` is expanded once, with the expanded `\the<counter>` after it, inside
the definition's braces, and a robust command in it stays; a `\ref` prints the stored text.

**Perl** (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1001): the reference form is typed at the step unexpanded (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:1028
`\lx@@therefnum@@` `{\normalfont\csname p@#1\endcsname\csname the#1\endcsname}`, :1081-1085 the typeref forms), so a
`\p@` that takes arguments reads the `\csname the…` tokens themselves: 1902.09345's `\renewcommand{\p@equation}{\gobblesomeargs}` (a
robust nine-argument command keeping the ninth) read `\csname`, `t`, `h`, … and past the tag (18 errors in Rust, the
first SI equation lost; pdflatex 0).

**Rust** (77u): `\lx@@p@the@@` (base_utilities/defs/tags_refnums.rs), shared by the refnum and typerefnum forms, expands latex.ltx's form
as `\protected@edef` does (`with_unexpandable_protect` + `do_expand_partially`: an `\edef`'s expansion, which keeps
`\protected` macros, bounded by the form's braces) and returns the text: "Equation S1" → refnum "S1", as pdflatex's
`\ref`. Only a `\p@<counter>` that does something is applied so: with the kernel's empty one (`\@definecounter`,
latex.ltx:10144) the number is typed as written, as before — an itemize's `\tikz` bullet, a number LaTeX never stores,
does not survive an `\edef`. The common forms are the same text as before (`\p@enumii` = `\theenumi`, `\labelformat`'s
argument-taking `\p@`). Residual: the form is still TYPESET
at the step, where pdflatex typesets it only at a `\ref`, so a form that cannot typeset (a nine-argument `\p@` before a
one-token number) still reads past its tag — our argument reader takes a `}` as an undelimited argument (Perl
Gullet.pm:732-744 alike; tex.web §395 stops at it, "Argument of \x has an extra }"), SYNC_STATUS C11. Repro
`parameter-conditional/p_form_applies_to_the_expanded_number`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77u::{p_form_applies_to_the_expanded_number, p_forms_of_the_kernel_keep_their_reference}`.

### 779. → #288 (`\normalfont` and `\reset@font` select the document's `\familydefault`, `\seriesdefault`, `\shapedefault` and `\encodingdefault` (Perl: `\rmdefault`, `\mddefault`, `\updefault`, the encoding kept))

### 780. A formula's token fonts are written relative to the text default, not to the enclosing text element, and MathML reads the context font inside the formula only (Perl: written against the enclosing text element, that relative font read whole)

**TeX**: a formula is set in the math fonts of the current math version (fontmath.ltx: `\mathversion{normal}`'s CMMI
letters, CMR operators and digits, `\mathsf` CMSS), never in the text family, series or shape around it: `$y$` in
`\emph` of a `\renewcommand\familydefault{\sfdefault}` document is CMMI10, `\mathsf{G}` in `\textit` CMSS10, `$y$` in
`\textsf{\emph{…}}` of a serif document CMMI10 (pdflatex, `pdffonts`). Size and colour do reach the formula.

**Perl** (Core/Document.pm:385-410 `finalize_rec`): every node's font is written relative to the font declared on its
nearest written ancestor, so a token is written against the text element enclosing the formula — in a theorem body
`y` gets no `font` and `+` `font="upright"`. Post/MathML.pm:278 then takes the enclosing text element's `font` as the
context (`find_inherited_attribute`), and :677 reads a token's own `font` whole, falling back to that context. The two
halves agree only while the text family is serif: against `sansserif italic` the italic `y` is written `font="serif"`
(the shape matches, the family differs) and read as upright serif, `mathvariant="normal"`; `\mathsf{G}` is written
`font="upright"` and loses its sans (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1002).

**Rust** (77u r3): `finalize_rec` (document.rs) resets the declared family, series and shape to the text default's
(serif, medium, upright) at an `ltx:Math`, keeping size and colour, so a formula's tokens are written the same wherever
it stands — `y` is `font="italic"`, `+` has none, inside `\emph`, a theorem body or a plain paragraph alike. An
`XMText` (`\text`, `\mbox`) is text, set in the font around the formula (amstext's `\text` takes `\f@family`,
`\f@series`, `\f@shape`): its content is written against that font, as Perl writes it. `math_context_font`
(latexml_post mathml/mod.rs) reads the tokens' presentation and content context font only between the `XMath` and its
`ltx:Math` (where none can be written), so a token without a `font` is upright serif, not the text around; an
`m:mtext` falls back to the text font around the formula (`ctx_text_font`, Perl's `$LaTeXML::MathML::FONT`). In a serif
document an italic context's letters were plain `<mi>` by inheritance and now are by their own `italic`; the MathML
changes in two cases, both to TeX's fonts. A `\bm`/`\boldsymbol` letter or a `\boldmath` formula in italic text is bold
italic where Perl's MathML read the bare `bold` as bold upright (1503.06160 `\bm{B}` in lemmas, pdflatex CMMIB10). A
formula in a text element nested in another — `\textbf{Momentum:} $m_t$` in a theorem body is written
`<text font="bold italic">Momentum:<text font="medium">$m_t$</text></text>` — took the nearer element's relative
`medium` alone as its context, so its letters were upright (`mathvariant="normal"`); they are italic, as TeX sets them
in CMMI (2601.02609, 30 letters; 2608.12539, 24; 2603.28663, 2603.28316, 2607.18880). The XML of a formula in italic or
bold text differs from Perl's (theorem goldens re-blessed). 77u r2's sans
`\normalfont` (#779) made the Perl shape hit every sans-default document's italic and bold text: 2608.14133 (1,890
letters upright), 2608.31026, 2605.03549, 2604.00146, 2607.19982, 2606.05381 (theorem bodies), 2604.16675. Repros
`fonts-nfss/math_fonts_do_not_follow_a_sans_text_font`, `fonts-nfss/math_fonts_in_sans_italic_text_of_a_serif_document`;
guards `perfect_kernel_batch77u::{math_fonts_do_not_follow_a_sans_text_font,
math_fonts_in_sans_italic_text_of_a_serif_document}`, `perfect_kernel_batch56::letters_in_an_italic_context_stay_plain_mi`.

### 781. tipa's T3 has a font map, its diacritics are combining marks and its tone letters Unicode's; a text accent's default is its encoding's (Perl: no T3 map, the IPA lost; `\DeclareTextAccentDefault` ignored)

**TeX**: t3enc.def (tipa, FUKUI Rei) declares the IPA symbols at the tipa fonts' slots (`\DeclareTextSymbol\textschwa
{T3}{64}` …), and tipa's input convention makes the ASCII slots IPA letters (digits, capitals, `@ : ; " |`; tipaman §3:
`\textipa{[D@"lIm@]}` is [ðəˈlɪmə]); tipa10.tfm ligates `""` to ˌ and `||` to ǁ (tipa.mf:66-67). Its diacritics stack a
slot of the font on the letter: `\upper@accent`/`\lower@accent` (t3enc.def:268-294) put `\hbox{#2\char#4}` above or
below `\hbox{#5}`, `\ipaclap` and `\ipabar` (:330-354) overlap a glyph or rule a bar; in T3 the kernel accents are
t3enc.def's (:489-516, a `*` form below the letter: `\~*{a}`, `\r*{n}`), and tipa.sty:387-464 adds `\|`, `\*`, `\:`,
`\;`, `\!` composites. tone.sty draws a contour from tone-letter parts (slots 128-145, :37-58). tipa.sty:283-344
`\DeclareTextAccentDefault{\textsubring}{T3}` makes the accent usable in other encodings: latex.ltx:9985-9986, `\?\cs` →
`\UseTextAccent{T3}\cs`, which (:9958-9965) sets the accent in T3 and its argument back in the caller's encoding.

**Perl**: no T3 fontmap and no tipa binding (tipa.sty is not read by default: `\textipa` undefined); with the raw file
the symbols are empty and the input letters OT1's ("D@”lIm@"); `\DeclareTextAccentDefault` is ignored
(latex_base.pool.ltxml:361-362) and `\UseTextAccent` reads two arguments (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1004).

tipasym1-4, tipagerm, tipasc, tipatone `cmchar` names), as the IPA letter Unicode has for it by t3enc.def's command

meaning part, the slot is the IPA meaning, as tipauni.sty maps it (user ruling 2026-10-20, 77x r2): `!` the alveolar
click ǃ U+01C3 (tipapnct.mf draws an exclamation mark; tipaman2.tex:1105 "(post)alveolar click"; 2606.11542 "!Xoon"),

no-audible-release mark U+031A (2601.02906, 2609.04232), `\textsubbar` (slot 9 below, `\b` in T3) the minus sign below
U+0320 ("retracted", tipaman2.tex:1461); the open corner 95, which tipauni.sty does not map (tipaman gives it another
meaning), stays the spacing ˹ — so a `\textopencorner x\textcorner` bracket pair (2604.00122's Quine corners) is ˹x̚.
Kept as drawn: `|` `{` `}` the click letters ǀ ǁ ǂ (tipasym1.mf's pipes), the baby gamma 200 the ram's horns' ɤ
(U+0264's former name), 175 ꭢ (tipasym4.mf:299 "Open O-E Ligature"). The marks t3enc.def:213-219 sets after the letter
they modify — `\textrthook` 36, `\textpalhook` 37, `\textcorner` 94 — are the bare combining marks
(`DeclareFontMapMultichar`), which attach to that letter (`t\textrthook` t̢, `k\textcorner` k̚), not to the no-break

the hooktop 35, the tone-letter parts 128-145 and stem 191, the left-hooktop long i/y and Viby i/y 166, 167, 182, 183.
`t3enc_def.rs` reads t3enc.def raw, then sets the `a` form of `\upper@accent`/`\lower@accent` as the slot's combining
mark above or below (`t3_accent_mark`: the tilde 3 is U+0303 above, U+0330 below; the round cap 16 U+0311/U+032F; the
stroke 34 below the syllabicity mark U+0329; the tone accents 152-159 U+1DC4 U+1DC5 U+1DC8 U+1DC9 U+030D U+030E U+1DC0
U+1DC1), decoded in the font `#2` selects and applied as the kernel's `\accent` (`\lx@applyaccent`: `\'a` á,

U+0334, `\ipabar` the stroke overlay U+0335 over a character run (`\textbarc` c̵, `\textcrg` ɡ̵; over another

### 782. A binding may port a non-`\long` TeX macro as one: its arguments stop at a `\par` (Perl: every binding macro reads `\long`)

**TeX**: a macro not declared `\long` stops reading its arguments at a `\par` — "Paragraph ended before \x was
complete", the call dropped, the `\par` read again (tex.web §392, §396; #442). amsppt.sty:799-818's `\footnote` and
`\footnotetext` read their text so (`\nextiv@##1`, `\DNii@[##1]##2`).

**Perl**: every `DefMacro`/`DefConstructor` reads its arguments across paragraphs (Expandable.pm stores `isLong` and
never reads it); amsppt.sty.ltxml:268's `\footnote[]{}` constructor took every paragraph after a note whose `}` never
came (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1014).

**Rust** (77v): `ExpandableOptions::short` — a binding's macro made with `short => true` checks its arguments for
`\par` as #442's TeX-declared macros do, wherever it is made (`Expandable::checks_par`, expandable.rs). amsppt_sty.rs's
`\footnote` and `\footnotetext` are such macros, handing the text to the note constructors. 79m: ams_support_sty.rs's
`\title`, `\subjclass`, `\keywords`, `\dedicatory`, `\translator` (amsart.cls:457/551-568, amsbook.cls, amsproc.cls:
`\renewcommand*`, `\newcommand*`, `\def`), so a `\subjclass{…` whose `}` never comes stops at the paragraph's end
(KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1150; 2212.11488). No other binding is changed: a binding's macros stay `\long` unless the
original's non-`\long` reading is the point. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch77v::amsppt_footnote_argument_runs_past_par`,
`perfect_kernel_batch79m::an_unclosed_subjclass_ends_at_the_paragraph`.

### 783. A document's `\newtheorem` replaces a binding's theorem of the name, also where the real class declares it (Perl: replaced, every `\newtheorem` redefining)

**LaTeX**: `\newtheorem{X}` of a defined `\X` is refused (latex.ltx `\@nthm`, amsthm.sty:78-80 `\@ifdefinable`):
"Command \X already defined", the first declaration kept. Under llncs.cls (`\spnewtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}…`), a
document's `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]` is refused and its theorems print "Theorem 1.".

**Perl**: `\newtheorem` refuses nothing; every declaration replaces the previous one.

**Rust** (77v r2/r3): a second `\newtheorem` is refused, as in LaTeX, only when the document's world (the document, a
raw file it loaded) made the first; a binding's declaration — and a binding's guess made while the document is read,
through `\lx@guess@newtheorem` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1008) — claims no name, so the document's replaces it. A binding's
theorem set is in general more than its class declares (elsart_support's `{rem}` under arxbj, 1205.2947; tac's under
2407.21129's `\newtheoremrm{examples}…[section]`), where the document's declaration gives the theorem the title pdflatex
prints (its number need not match: tac.cls's `\@@newthm#1[#2]#3[#4]` drops both counter arguments and numbers every
theorem on the one `\subsection` sequence, "0.1. Theorem", "0.2. Proposition", which the tac binding does not model —
SYNC row); telling the class's own theorems apart per binding is not done. Where the real class does declare the name, the document's
declaration wins here and LaTeX's refusal is lost: llncs + `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]` gives "Theorem 11"
(the declaration as llncs's kernel numbers it, its `\@thmcountersep` empty: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1111; "Theorem 1.1"
before 78q r2) where pdflatex prints "Theorem 1." with an error. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch77v::llncs_document_newtheorem_replaces_the_class`
(repro class-bindings/llncs_document_newtheorem_over_class).

### 784. A jfm copy's caption: its own `\@makecaption`'s label format, or caption with its options (Perl: no jfm binding, article's "Figure 1:")

**LaTeX**: the jfm.cls copies without caption set `{\normalfont\scshape #1\ifrem@fullpt\else .\fi} #2` (0712.2739's
:953-958, ~41 of 49 sampled jfm papers): "Figure 1." with the label in small caps, `\removefullpoint` dropping the
period once; the newer copies load caption with their own options (2608.01828's :1837 `labelsep=period`).

**Perl**: no jfm binding; OmniBus (article) prints "Figure 1:".

**Rust** (78a): jfm_cls.rs requires caption through `shipped_class::require_shipped_packages`, with the copy's
options (a bare `RequirePackage!("caption")` dropped them); a copy whose `\@makecaption` uses `\ifrem@fullpt` gets its
label format as the figure's and table's title format (`\format@title@<type>` = `\lx@tag[][. ]{…}`, as amsart's
ams_support binding) and its label font as `\fnum@font@<type>` (`\scshape`), with `\removefullpoint`. The copy's own
`\@makecaption` stays declined (the kernel's caption), so its layout (centred short captions, `\small`) is not
modelled. The label format and font are installed at `\begin{document}` only where caption is not loaded
(`\AtBeginDocument{\@ifpackageloaded{caption}{}{…}}`; `\ifrem@fullpt`/`\removefullpoint` are defined either way): the
document's caption package — or subcaption's or subfig's, which load it — replaces the class's `\@makecaption` in
pdflatex ("Figure 1:" in the text font, the sub-captions' "(a)" at their size; 10 of the 40 copies with their own
`\@makecaption` in the 78a census, which is not complete — a 40k-zip sample found 23 more: 1711.01065, 2205.10181,
2507.07213 subcaption, 1805.00129 and 1612.03374 subfig, 2008.04616 caption), the old subfigure package does not, nor
floatrow, which loads caption's kernel alone (floatrow.sty:39 `caption3`; 2312.13002, 2111.12004): caption3 falls back
to the caption binding, which then defines `\lx@caption@kernel@only` (caption_sty.rs), and the class's format stays;
nor `\usepackage[caption=false]{subfig}`, which loads `caption3` too (subfig.sty:129-141; subfig_sty.rs, 78a r3).
subcaption (subcaption.sty:43) and subfig without that option (:129-139) load caption even after floatrow's `caption3`,
so they clear the mark (78a r3). Residual: a document's own `\usepackage{caption}` after a `caption3` load — floatrow's,
or `[caption=false]{subfig}`'s — keeps the class's format, as the caption binding is not run again (RED
class-bindings/jfm_caption/jfm_copy_caption_package_after_subfig_without_caption, the rev78a3 re-review's finding 1). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch78a::{
jfm_copy_captions_end_the_label_with_a_period, jfm_copy_caption_package_keeps_its_options,
jfm_copy_caption_yields_to_caption_loaders, jfm_copy_caption_kept_with_subfigure, jfm_copy_caption_kept_with_floatrow,
jfm_copy_caption_kept_with_subfig_without_caption, jfm_copy_caption_yields_to_caption_loaders_after_floatrow}`.

### 785. An unnumbered heading runs its title format's after-code (Perl: the title font alone, titlesec's after-code dropped)

**LaTeX**: titlesec typesets a starred title with the same `\ttlf@<sec>` as a numbered one, without the label: the
format, `<before>{title}` and the after-code (titlesec.sty:740-818). tufte-common.def:1613-1619's `\chapter` format
opens `\begin{fullwidth}` in the format and closes it in the after-code.

**Perl**: `\@@unnumbered@section` digests `\lx@format@title@font@@{type}` before the title
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:666-670); titlesec.sty.ltxml:42-57 drops the after-code.

**Rust** (78a): the starred title runs `\lx@format@title@font@@{type}` before it (as Perl; the port had lost it, a
Rust-only defect — SYNC "Rust Error Fixes") and `\lx@format@title@after@@{type}` after it (base_utilities/defs/tags_refnums.rs:
`\format@title@after@<type>` when defined). titlesec_sty.rs defines `\format@title@after@<sec>` as its after-code
(empty for `rightmargin`/`wrap`/`drop`, and for an `explicit` after-code that names the title): the format's
`\begin{fullwidth}` is closed in the title (the tufte manuals: 0 errors, the starred titles in the class's italics).
Guards `perfect_kernel_batch78a::{unnumbered_section_takes_the_title_font,
titlesec_after_code_closes_an_unnumbered_title}`.

### 786. biblatex's `\citeauthor` and a numeric style's `\textcite` print the name, and a nameless entry in a textual numeric citation keeps its brackets, natbib's too (Perl: no biblatex binding; CrossRef.pm:541 drops every bracket of the citation)

**biblatex**: `\citeauthor` prints `\printnames{labelname}` in every style (biblatex.def:2497-2506); numeric.cbx's and
alphabetic.cbx's `\textcite` print the name, then the bracketed label ("Hampe [1]").

**Perl**: no biblatex binding (the contrib binding ports the upstream draft's `_cite_fallback`, which sends both to the
plain `\cite` outside an author-year style: "[1] showed it").

**Rust** (78a): biblatex_sty.rs's `\citeauthor` is the author-year form (`\@@bibref{Authors}`) in every style; a
non-author-year `\textcite`/`\Textcite`/`\citet` is natbib's numbers-mode textual citation (Perl natbib.sty.ltxml:161-171,
`Authors Phrase1NumberPhrase2`, the pre- and postnote inside the brackets). An author-title or verbose style's
`\textcite` prints "Name [1]" too, where biblatex prints the title. Witnesses 2402.17192 (style=ieee), 2410.22329.
Guard `perfect_kernel_batch78a::biblatex_citeauthor_and_textcite_print_the_name_in_a_numeric_style`.

An entry with no name (no author, editor or key tag) under such a textual numeric citation keeps the brackets around
its number, for that entry alone (latexml_post crossref.rs `nameless_numeric_show`, 78a r2): biblatex "No Author Misc
[2]" (numeric.cbx:23-41 prints the `labeltitle` before the bracket) is "[2]", natbib numbers mode's "Smith [2], ano [1]"
(plainnat's key-prefix label) "Smith [2], [1]". Perl's CrossRef.pm:541 turns the whole citation's `show` to `refnum`
("2"; "2, 1"). Residuals: the biblatex `labeltitle` (and natbib's key-prefix) is not printed; `\citeauthor` of a
nameless entry prints its number ("3"), where biblatex prints nothing. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78a::biblatex_numeric_textcite_without_author_keeps_its_brackets`,
`bibref_show::natbib_numbers_citet_merges_same_authors`.

### 788. `\pdfxform` keeps its box as the form, `\pdfrefxform` places it (Perl: `\pdfxformname` only)

**pdfTeX**: `\pdfxform <box>` makes a form XObject of the box (voiding it) and numbers it in `\pdflastxform`;
`\pdfrefxform <n>` places the form, as often as it is referenced (pdfTeX manual §`\pdfxform`, §`\pdfrefxform`).

**Perl**: pdfTeX.pool.ltxml:96 defines `\pdfxformname`; neither primitive.

**Rust** (78a): pdftex.rs's `\pdfxform` keeps the box (global value `pdfxform@<n>`) and `\pdfrefxform` returns it, as
`\copy` does. xsavebox's `\xsbox`/`\xusebox` (xsavebox.sty:120-122, :298, :325 through pdfbase's
`\pbs_pdfxform:nnnnn`/`\pbs_pdfrefxform:n`) printed an empty box of the content's size (biblatex-ext's open-access
symbols, biblatex-ext.tex:3938-4022). Guard `perfect_kernel_batch78a::xsavebox_saved_box_prints_its_content`.
### 789. A class's author name markup as its title page prints it: vmsta's `\fnm`/`\snm`/`\inits`

vmsta.cls (Modern Stochastics: Theory and Applications, VTeX; shipped, not in TeX Live) defines the name parts only
where its `\@@author` prints the author list (vmsta.cls:278-291): `\name@m@front` stores `\fnm{…}` and `\snm{…}`, drops
`\inits` and `\suffix`, and prints `\@fnm~\@snm` — "Yuliya Mishura" for `\author[a]{\inits{Yu.}\fnm{Yuliya}\snm{Mishura}
\corref{cor1}}`. The kernel's locked `\author` replaces the class's, and OXIDIZED_DESIGN #647's search found the class's
`\name@m` identities, OmniBus's `\inits` printing: 1508.02842's creator "Yu.YuliyaMishura". Perl has no vmsta binding
(`\fnm` undefined). Ours: a vmsta binding (latexml_contrib vmsta_cls.rs) reads the shipped class raw and sets
`\lx@author@markup@class`, `\lx@author@markup@provide` calls that `\lx@author@markup@begin` (base_utilities/defs/frontmatter_fields.rs) runs
first for the author content, before OmniBus's identity meanings — `\fnm` stores, `\snm` prints `first~surname`, the
initials and suffix dropped, for the author content only and undefined after it, as the class defines them only in its
title code. A first name no `\snm` follows is printed after the content (flushed with the markup's restore list), as
`\@fnm~\@snm` prints it there: `\fnm{Ivan}~Voronov` "VoronovIvan" (vmsta.cls errs on its undefined `\@snm` there; no
corpus paper has the shape). 71 vmsta papers (1508.02842, 1411.4499, 1601.01109). The 68v repro of #647
(`vmsta_name_parts`) now reads its cut-down class as `vtexnames.cls`, which no binding answers. Repros
class-bindings/vmsta/vmsta_title_page_name_parts_red, vmsta_first_name_without_surname_red; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch77t::{vmsta_title_page_name_parts, vmsta_first_name_without_surname}`.
