### 793. IEEEtran's `\appendix` keeps the title of the `\section` that follows it

IEEEtran.cls:5719-5745 `\appendix[<title>]` is one appendix: it prints the heading "Appendix" (or "Appendix \\* <title>")
through the kernel's `\section*`, steps the section counter once (`\ref` "A") and redefines `\section` so that an
unstarred one throws its argument away (`\@IEEEdestroythesectionargument`, :5711-5713, a terminal warning only): the
common `\appendix` `\section{Proof of Theorem 1}` prints "APPENDIX" and loses the title. Ours (ieeetran_cls.rs): the
optional title is the appendix's (an `ltx:appendix`, refnum "A", tag "Appendix" as the class prints it). Without one, the
first unstarred `\section` after `\appendix` — past blank lines, spaces, comment lines, empty groups (2002.07641's
`\appendix{}`) and `\label`s, the labels then the appendix's — makes the appendix, its title kept; anything else next
(`\section*`, `\subsection`, text) follows an appendix with an empty title, the "Appendix" heading pdflatex prints
(witnesses 1903.01287, 1103.2068, 2002.03484, 2410.15995, 2401.07123: a blank line after `\appendix` had made the titled
section a second appendix "B"). Residual: a non-printing command or a float between `\appendix` and the `\section`
(2404.01875's `\setlength{\jot}… \allowdisplaybreaks`, 2007.07179's figure; 3 of ~140 IEEEtran `\appendix` files, rev78d2)
takes the heading path too, so the titled section is "Appendix B" and refs to it read "B" where pdflatex's read "A"
(int45b had one appendix "Appendix A" with that title). A later
unstarred `\section` is another appendix with its title, tagged by its refnum, "Appendix B", "Appendix C" (2401.07123),
where pdflatex prints nothing of it and a `\ref` to a label in it prints "A" — ours reads "B", "C". `\appendices`
after `\appendix` numbers its appendices from "A" with their letters, as the class (pdflatex "APPENDIX", "APPENDIX A",
"APPENDIX B"). Authored content first: the destroyed argument is the author's text. Repro
sectioning-frontmatter/ieeetran_appendix_with_a_title_is_one_appendix; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78d::ieeetran_appendix_with_a_title_is_one_appendix` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1022).

### 805. A separately printed address goes to its owner by one chain: its own mark, the author it spells, author order when the list is the authors', the group's only author, elimination, the one marked corresponding author, else the block — absorbs #140 #159 #465 #808 #809 #901 #908 #932 #938 #956 #966 #970 #972 #984 #992

**Rule.** A contact the block or a class list prints apart from its author is owned by its own mark, else the author it
spells (base letters and transliteration), else author order when the list is the authors', else the group's only
author, else by elimination (an address no name spells to a name no address spells, where one of each is left or the
spelled addresses' order confirms it; a role mailbox is no person's), else the one author marked corresponding, else
the block (resolver rule 7; user ruling R10). An e-mail printed inside an affiliation entry is that entry's addresses,
placed by the same chain; one contact per print event.

**Perl.** The n-th piece of a comma split goes on the n-th author, or the address stays in the affiliation's text and is
copied onto every holder; iopart's `\ead` goes to the last author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1031). **TeX.** The class prints
the list where its `\@maketitle` puts it (iopart.cls `\ead`, ijcai.sty `\emails`); the PDF shows no owner but the spelling.

**Sub-rules**
- *The chain*: `observer/resolver/mod.rs` rule 7; `resolver/owners.rs:860 entry_address_owners`; elimination
  `owners.rs:768 owners_by_elimination` (`classify/links.rs:359 is_role_mailbox`; formerly #52(j), (o)); spelling by
  `resolver/mod.rs:1198 base_letters`, `labels.rs:258 tex_letters`, `:1511 surname_owners` (formerly #970);
  `place.rs:291 marked_corresponding_author` (formerly #809).
- *Class lists*: ijcai's `\emails`, cas's `\address[label]` (formerly #908); each iopart `\author` a group (iopart.cls:225-231),
  its `\ead` under its address's mark RED (`iopart_ead_under_its_address_mark_red`; formerly #808); llncs's and aa's sole `\institute` every author's unless `\inst{n}` picks it
  (formerly #901, #932; the Perl side KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1195); the amsart up-front grid (formerly #140); `address_lists.rs:33 distribute_address_lists`.
- *Inside an affiliation* (the Kind and Link steps): the API kinds an entry's lines and notes of addresses once
  (`defs/frontmatter_api/kind.rs:29 kind_entry_addresses`), and one Link chain places every e-mail of an entry
  (`insert.rs:941 kind_link_and_grade_contacts`, `:2293 kind_address_lines`); the emitter keeps only the entry's own
  text (`emitter/address_cut.rs:812 entry_cuts`, `:899 cut_mail_call`) (formerly #938, #956, #966, #984); AASTeX's `\affil`
  e-mail lines go as written and the steps place their addresses (formerly #992); a list one contact prints for several
  people is each address's on its owner, a math brace the brace it prints (formerly #972).
- *The block's own*: an address or affiliation no author owns goes once to the block's own creator, below all authors
  (formerly #159; `address_lists.rs:24`, `emit.rs:6395 block_creator`).
- *A name line's trailing address* is the author's e-mail (formerly #465).

**Witnesses** 2505.15472, 2410.04091, 2609.24668, 1710.01968, 2011.14024 (svjour3 `\at`), 1504.05444. **Guards**
`perfect_kernel_batch104d::a_cas_unlabelled_affiliation_is_every_authors`,
`perfect_kernel_batch107c::a_sole_or_glued_marked_authors_address_is_never_the_blocks`,
`perfect_kernel_batch107g::a_repeated_author_block_copies_no_address_onto_the_last_author`. RED:
`iopart_ead_under_its_address_mark_red`, `ijcai_binding_emails_in_author_order_red`,
`email_own_call_printed_under_both_stays_on_both_red`. **Upstream.** iopart's `\ead`: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1031.
**Code.** The chain is spread over the resolver, the API's Kind/Link steps and `insert.rs`'s DOM steps; one Kind pass
and one Link chain is the post-cutoff CODE row (SYNTHESIS (D) 1). Records: [the archive](../archive/OD_FRONTMATTER_RECORDS_2026-11-15.md).

### 807. An `\inst` mark after a comma is the name's before it

llncs.cls:894-896 `\def\inst#1{\unskip$^{#1}$}`, `\def\fnmsep{\unskip$^,$}` (aa.cls:759-760 the same with
`\unskip\hbox{…}`): the mark takes back the space before it and stands on the name before the comma, so `\author{Clara
Dehman,⏎\inst{1}\fnmsep\inst{2}\fnmsep\inst{3}\fnmsep\inst{4}\thanks{Email: …} Mario Centelles,\inst{5}\fnmsep\inst{6}
\and Xavier Vi\~nas…}` prints "Clara Dehman,¹,²,³,⁴⋆ Mario Centelles,⁵,⁶ and Xavier Viñas⁵,⁶,⁷". The author split
(Perl inst_support.sty.ltxml:33-35 `\lx@splitting{\lx@add@author}{\and\And,}`; ours `split_author_line`) cut at the
comma, so the marks and note opened the next piece: 2401.16957's four affiliations and e-mail note went to Mario
Centelles and his institutes 5-6, a piece of marks only, to no one (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1032). The kernel's
`marks_before_glued_commas` already moved a mark glued to the comma before it (`Ann Able,\textsuperscript{a}`); it did
not know `\inst`, and kept a mark after a space on the next name (`Ann$^1$, $^{*}$Bob`). Ours: `\inst` and a
`\fnmsep`/`\fnsep` between two marks are leading marks there (`leading_inst_marks_end`), and an `\inst` after the
comma's spaces or ties moves too, the spaces it takes back dropped — only where `\inst` is the convention's mark,
decided by its meaning (`inst_takes_back_space`, 78f r2): it starts with `\unskip` (a raw llncs.cls/aa.cls/svjour3.cls),
or it is the request the convention's bindings give it for that definition (`\lx@request@frontmatter@annotation`:
llncs_cls.rs, inst_support_sty.rs, sv_support_sty.rs; inside author content the one `\lx@author@withinst` saved); a class
that defines `\inst` only inside its title, where the names print, has its binding declare that meaning as
`\lx@title@inst`, which decides first (epl_cls.rs, epl2.cls:725 `\def\inst##1{\unskip${}^{##1}$…}`: 1201.1900's
`\author{Zhen Wang,\inst{1,2} Attila Szolnoki,\inst{3} …}`, each name its own marks).
Beamer's `\inst` (beamerbasetitle.sty:169 `\textsuperscript{#1}`) and a document's own `\newcommand{\inst}[1]{$^{#1}$}`
take back no space: `Ann Able\inst{1}, \inst{2}Bob Baker` keeps Bob Baker's 2 (rev78f probes c08, c09). Names that open
with their `\inst`s (`\inst{1}Ann Able, \inst{2}Bob Baker`) keep each its own, as leading superscripts do (`marker_leads`;
rev78f probe c01). Census (26,323 papers of sel78d's 30k): 15 aa/llncs
papers write `,\inst`, `, \inst` or `,~\inst`; A/B 7 of them changed, each now as its PDF (1604.07826, 1811.07968,
2011.09991, 2309.00573, 2404.01383, 2502.20626, 2503.07779: each author's institutes and note its own, where every one
after the first comma had moved one author on; no nameless creator; 1811.07968's B. Nikiel-Wroczyński, whose `,$^{8}$`
is no `\inst`, keeps the mark shown without an institute, where he had held the next author's), the other 8 unchanged. Repros
sectioning-frontmatter/{llncs_comma_before_inst_is_the_name_before, llncs_inst_leading_marks_keep_their_names,
inst_without_unskip_keeps_the_next_name_red}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78f::{llncs_comma_before_inst_is_the_name_before,
llncs_inst_leading_marks_keep_their_names, inst_without_unskip_keeps_the_next_name}`.

### 810. A label's spacing parts it also as digested

A class's optional `\author[*\,b,c]{…}` labels reach the frontmatter digested, the thin space a U+2009 character, which
`clean_frontmatter_labels` read as part of one label `*_b` (OD #52(o) parts the labels at the spacing as written:
`\,`, `~`, `\quad`), so Paul J. Steinhardt (2404.00867) lost his affiliation b and the `*` of his
`\note[*]{Corresponding author: …}`. Ours (`SPACING_IN_LABEL`, base_utilities/frontmatter/queue_digest.rs): the no-break, en to thin, and narrow
no-break spaces (U+00A0, U+2002-U+2009, U+202F) part labels as their commands do. Perl's cleanFrontmatterLabels parts at
commas only. Repro sectioning-frontmatter/jheppub_note_mark_apart_from_the_names; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78f::jheppub_note_mark_apart_from_the_names`.

### 813. A `\label` names what `\@currentlabel` holds where it is made — the object of the step in scope, numbered as the kernel or amsmath numbers it (Perl: the nearest ancestor that may carry `labels`, every row numbered) — absorbs #847 #856 #865 #875 #877

**Rule.** LaTeX's `\label` writes the `\@currentlabel` of the last `\refstepcounter` in scope and hyperref's anchor of
that step (latex.ltx:14963-14967): a label goes to the element that step numbered, taking the step's number when the
element has none, and climbs from where it is made when a group has undone the step; an equation row or an `{equation}`
is numbered by the switch the kernel (`\if@eqnsw`) or, where loaded, amsmath keeps. **Perl** (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3782,
Document.pm:1098-1127 `floatToLabel`) climbs from the current node's last child to the nearest ancestor that may carry
`labels`, and `\ref` prints that element's `refnum`; it numbers every eqnarray row without `\nonumber` and gives every
`{equation}` amsmath's `\nonumber`.
**Code.** `latexml_core/src/document.rs:7823 float_to_label_for`, `:7836 float_to_label_scoped`, `:7937
take_raw_refstep_number`, `:7988 note_raw_refstep_object`, `:8006 release_earlier_label_holders`, `:8078
merge_raw_refstep_tags`; `binding/counter/dialect.rs:785 current_raw_refstep`, `:1002 label_follows_an_undone_step`, `:722
hold_raw_refstep_for_display`, `:754 leave_display_for_parbox`; `latex_constructs/mod.rs:2549 rearrange_eqnarray`, `:2856
eqnarray_eqncr_numbering` (the rule's one statement), `:2976 eqnarray_next_number_tags`; `sect07.rs:58
prepare_latex_equation_counter`.

- **A raw counter step names its object (78g).** A step no constructor takes numbered no element, so its labels landed
  on the section (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1038). tcolorbox's `\newtcbtheorem`, `\newtcolorbox[auto counter]` put
  `\addtocounter{\tcbcounter}{-1}\refstepcounter{\tcbcounter}` and the `label=` key's `\label` in the box's phantom code
  (tcolorbox.sty:2311, :998, :1154-1161), inside the frame picture (:1925 `\pgftext`). (1) The kernel's `\refstepcounter`
  records its step with the tags LaTeXML makes for every step (sect08.rs `\lx@refstepcounter@label`, dialect.rs
  `note_raw_refstep`; local, as `\@currentlabel`); a `\label` made while `\@currentlabel` is still that step's
  `\the<counter>` carries them (with the step's serial). (2) It may stop at an `ltx:picture` (the box the step is made
  in), not at an object another raw step numbered (`_raw_refstep`); the schema gives `ltx:picture` `Labelled.attributes`
  and an optional leading `ltx:tags` (LaTeXML-picture.rnc/.rng, LaTeXML.model). (3) The object takes the step's tags when
  it has no number and is not a unit numbered by its heading (an unnumbered `\section*` or theorem stays unnumbered); the
  role-less display tag is dropped. (4) Under cleveref, tcolorbox's `label type` (`\label[<box>]`, :955-968, `crefname`
  :2270) gives the box the type's forms (cleveref_sty.rs `\lx@cleverref@labeltype`, numbering the box first). (5) The SVG
  post-processor keeps a labelled `picture`'s id, `labels` and `ltx:tags` around its SVG (svg.rs). (6) A listing's start
  forgets the step (`forget_raw_refstep` in `\@@listings@block`'s `before_digest`; lstmisc.sty:1228 `\lst@Init`, :1225);
  a tcolorbox listing box notes it again in its first line (`\lx@lst@renote@raw@refstep`, `renote_forgotten_raw_refstep`):
  a `\newtcblisting`/`\newtcbinputlisting` labels its first line with the box number. (7) An amsmath display's `\label`
  (`\lx@ams@display@label`, wrapping the replaced `\label`, `mark_display_label`) names the step held where the display
  starts (`hold_raw_refstep_for_display` in `ams_rearrangeable_bindings`/`ams_alignment_bindings`): amsmath's
  `\label@in@display` (amsmath.sty:1230-1236) is made in the tag cell after the cell group restored `\@currentlabel`
  (:1240-1252); `{gather}` tags every row (:1621-1627), so a `{gather*}` row's label after a step in its cell is the
  section's (pdflatex 7), after a step before the display the step's, an `{aligned}`/`{split}` in `{equation*}` names the
  step before it (44, 45); the align family and `{multline}` hold no step (`\math@cr@@@align` tags only under `\iftag@`,
  :1833-1843: an untagged row's label is the next tagged row's, `\df@label`, or `??`, never a held step: review probe rev78g2 al2.tex). A paragraph box in a display
  (`{minipage}`, `\parbox`, `\@arrayparboxrestore`) leaves it (`\label` restored to `\ltx@label`, :1237-1238; pdflatex 42).
  A saved kernel `\label` (`\AtBeginDocument{\let\originallabel\label}`, 2310.19138's `\labelrel`) labels at once. (8)
  `\eqno` on a display a raw step numbered joins its `ltx:tags`: `$$ \refstepcounter{foo}\label{x2} c=d \eqno(B) $$`
  shows "(B)", `\ref` 42. (9) Never inside an `ltx:Math` (`within_math`): it climbs to the display, which takes the step's
  number (pdflatex 41, 43), or past an inline formula to the section (pdflatex 42, ours 7, Perl the same).
  Residuals (decided main session 2026-10-21: the section fallback stays, no `ltx:g` schema change; `Labelled.attributes`
  on `ltx:g` and an `id` on `svg:g` remain the future path): an unnumbered listing's line label prints the section's
  number (listings steps `lstnumber` per line); a second raw step in one picture (`\put(0,0){\refstepcounter{foo}\label{p:a}…}
  \put(50,0){…\label{p:b}…}`) labels the section (pdflatex 42); an untagged `{align*}`/`{flalign*}`/`{multline*}` row's
  label (pdflatex `??`, "Multiple \label's"); a saved `\oldlabel` in a later `{align*}` row (`u&=v
  \refstepcounter{foo}\oldlabel{o2} \\ w&=x \oldlabel{o3}`: ours 45, pdflatex 7; rev78g2 obs.tex o3); a `$$…$$` label after
  an `{align*}` whose cell stepped (`\begin{align*} u&=v \refstepcounter{foo}\\ w&=x \end{align*} $$ a=b \label{d3} $$`:
  ours 7, pdflatex 42; leak2.tex d3); a label after an `\eqno` (`$$ \refstepcounter{foo} c=d \eqno(E) \label{x5}$$`: "(E)",
  pdflatex 43; eqno.tex x5); an object's own number wins (`\begin{equation} p=q \refstepcounter{foo}\label{e4}\end{equation}`
  pdflatex 42; an `\item`; `\begin{align} a&=b \refstepcounter{foo}\text{\begin{minipage}{2cm}\label{y7}x\end{minipage}}
  \end{align}` pdflatex 48, ours 1; rev78g3 pb2.tex y7, cr.tex w2); a raw step in running text labels the section
  (`ltx:para` holds no `ltx:tags`); cleveref's `\label[]` in an `equation` gives "condition 1" where pdflatex prints `??`;
  a box whose listing numbers its lines keeps the label on the first line. A/B (sel78d's 150 `tcb_label_ref` papers + 100
  random): 8 papers changed references, all 44 labels with pdflatex's `.aux` number; 2 gained numbers on unreferenced
  boxes; 0 Error/Fatal changes. Witnesses 2505.20088, 2311.09542, 2509.17784, 2602.03411, 2606.06976, 2402.06608 (`[blend
  into=figures]`), 2506.01072 (`\newtcbtheorem`), 2609.20563 (`\newtcblisting`). Repros tools/perfect_kernel/repros/cross-references/;
  guards `perfect_kernel_batch78g::{tcb_box_label_takes_the_box_number, tcb_listing_box_label_takes_the_box_number,
  picture_step_label_takes_the_step_number, tcb_theorem_cref_names_the_box_type, listing_label_names_no_step_before_it,
  amsmath_row_label_names_the_display_step, unnumbered_display_label_takes_the_step_number,

- **A step a group undid** (ex-#856, 78p; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1092). `\refstepcounter` sets `\@currentlabel` locally, so
  after an `equation`, theorem, caption or list closes it reverts. Every step records its serial in scope and as the
  latest made (global, `label_stepped_counter`); a label where they differ climbs from the current node, not its last
  child (`\lx@label`'s `after_undone_step`). A label in the step's own scope is unchanged (`\caption{…}\label`, `\item…\label`).
  A LaTeXML wrapper group around a step LaTeX makes in the current group does not undo it (`\lx@refstep@outlives@group`,
  `keep_latest_refstep_in_scope`): caption's `\captionof` (caption.sty:390-391; 2402.05535). With no ancestor able to take
  it, Perl's fallback (last child, else the root) stays — the root taking lastpage's `\AtEndDocument{\label{lastpage}}`
  renumbered every `idN`. A label after a closed table, figure, equation or list names the enclosing section's (theorem's,
  item's) number (math0107195: PDF "Theorem 5.3", Perl and ours before the equation's 16); after a `subequations`
  block's inner `align` the block's (2505.03288 `eq:GNG` "13"); after `\subfloat{…}\label{…}` the figure when its
  `\caption` precedes the subfloats, where pdflatex names the section when it follows (1504.02206 `fig:2c`: pdflatex 5.1,
  ours 2; rev78p). cleveref's `\lx@cleverref@labeltype` places by `float_to_label_scoped` (78j r5; guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch78j::cleveref_label_type_after_a_closed_float_names_the_object_in_scope`). Repro
  cross-references/label_after_an_inner_equation_names_the_theorem; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78p::{
  label_after_an_inner_equation_names_the_theorem, label_after_a_closed_step_names_the_step_in_scope,
  label_after_captionof_names_its_float}`.
- **eqnarray numbers by `\@@eqncr`'s `\if@eqnsw`** (ex-#847, 78n r3). latex.ltx:15750-15797: a row is numbered only if it
  ends through `\@@eqncr` (`\\`, `\\*`, `\\[len]`, `\end{eqnarray}`) with no `\nonumber` (`\global\@eqnswfalse`, :15775)
  since the last one (:15795 `\if@eqnsw\@eqnnum\stepcounter{equation}\fi \global\@eqnswtrue`); a raw `\cr` neither
  numbers nor resets; `\@currentlabel` is `\p@equation\theequation` (:15752), so a label names the number the next
  printing `\@@eqncr` prints. Perl's `\eqnarray@row@after@` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2226) runs `afterEquation` for
  any row end. Ours: `\lx@eqnarray@number@check` (expanded by `\\` and `\end{eqnarray}`) records `EQNARRAY_EQNNUM` from
  `EQNARRAY_EQNSW`; `\nonumber` clears it; `\eqnarray@row@after@` retracts unnumbered rows' preset numbers and marks them
  (`UNNUMBERED_EQNCR_ROW_ATTRIBUTE`); `rearrange_eqnarray` moves their labels to the next numbered row. Opt-in numbering key
  `eqncr=1`: latex.ltx's `eqnarray`/`eqnarray*` (not iopart's `\eqnalign`, subeqn's or subeqnarray's `subeqnarray`). A number
  printed on an empty row under an unnumbered one (`x &=& y \cr \end{eqnarray}`, `… \cr &&\\`, `\label{e} x = y, \nonumber\\
  \end{eqnarray}`) is that equation's (`NUMBER_ROW_PROPERTY`; the empty numbered row joins the equation above, tags and id
  with it, single-column too); an empty numbered row under a numbered equation (`a &=& b \\ \end{eqnarray}`) is removed,
  its number consumed as in LaTeX. A label with no numbered row after it in its group (an `eqnarray*`, a trailing
  `\nonumber` row) names the counter's next value (78r; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1106): `\lx@eqnarray@label` marks the row
  (`EQNARRAY_ROW_LABELLED`), `eqnarray_next_number_tags` digests that value's `tag_forms` (refnum, typerefnum, autoref,
  cleveref forms; no printed tag), and the row stands as its own equation (split from a numbered equation), except in a

  676 → 702 of 704 (the misses no eqnarray's: 1508.00199, gr-qc0201061). 212 papers in the fidelity3 scan of 9,829
  eqnarray papers had a `\cr` row; nucl-th9903062 ((1) our 2, (6) our 12), nucl-th9807024. Repros

  REVTeX 4.x 370 → 560 of 561); 13 census papers 92 → 273 of 274. Residual: a `\nonumber` in an `aligned`/`split` of an
  `{equation}` still removes its number (amsmath's local `\let\print@eqnum\@empty`; 2407.10017 `eq:chainMapHam`, PDF 41).
  Repros cross-references/{equation_nonumber_without_amsmath_keeps_the_number, equation_nonumber_with_amsmath_removes_the_number};
  guards `perfect_kernel_batch78r::{equation_nonumber_without_amsmath_keeps_the_number,
  equation_nonumber_with_amsmath_removes_the_number, mnras_equation_nonumber_keeps_the_number}`.
- **amsmath `{equation}` + `\nonumber` + `\label`** (ex-#875, 78t; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1128). amsmath's `{equation}`
  (amsmath.sty:2913-2932) steps at its start (`\incr@eqnum`, `\refstepcounter`); its `\nonumber` (:1269-1275) steps back only
  while `\if@eqnsw` holds; the label is made at the end (`\label@in@display`, `\endmathdisplay@a` :2821-2830), so it names
  the stepped number; `\tag{X}\nonumber` prints "(X)". Perl retracts and labels the unit (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2025-2057),
  and its `\nonumber` after `\tag` retracted the tag. Ours: `AMS_EQUATION` marks it; `\lx@equation@nonumber` digests the
  stepped number's forms (`eqnarray_next_number_tags`) before retracting, does nothing once gone; the equation drops them
  without a label (`NEXT_NUMBER_EQUATION`). `{equation*}` and `\[…\]` step nothing. The #865 residual's `aligned`/`split`
  label names pdflatex's number. Witness 1306.2116 (`eq:covariate`, PDF 17, int57a "3.1"; 75 → 77 of 77). Kept quirk:
  pdflatex's `\cref{e2}` prints "eq. (1)" (cleveref.sty `\cref@currentlabel` after the step back,
  `\newlabel{e2@cref}{{[equation][1][]1}…}`) where `\ref`/`\eqref` print 2; ours "(2)" for both. Repro
  cross-references/ams_equation_nonumber_label_names_the_stepped_number; guard
  `perfect_kernel_batch78t::ams_equation_nonumber_label_names_the_stepped_number`.
- **algorithm2e's lines** (ex-#877, 78t; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1129). algorithm2e.sty:1657-1667: `\nl` is
  `\refstepcounter{AlgoLine}\gdef\@currentlabel{\theAlgoLine}` (with hyperref `\stepcounter{AlgoLine}` and
  `\algocf@nl@sethref{\theAlgoLine}`), then `\algocf@printnl`, so a label names the line until the next number (`stmt\;
  \label{x}`, `\While{c}{\label{x} …}`). Perl's line carries only the printed number (algorithm2e.sty.ltxml:180-221).
  `\algocf@printnl@i` records the line as its step's object (`note_raw_refstep_object`, `RAW_REFSTEP_MARK`), global as the
  `\gdef` (`\lx@refstep@global`, `globalize_raw_refstep`), forgotten in the next algorithm's group (`\@algocf@init` steps
  `algocfline`, algorithm2e.sty:2560-2561; 2010.00626's `alg:F_cycle`, PDF 2); with hyperref `\algocf@nl@sethref` records
  `\lx@refstepcounter@label{AlgoLine}` when the number is `\theAlgoLine`; the line takes the forms
  (`take_raw_refstep_number`), `renumber_algo_lines` (algorithm2e_sty.rs:173) renumbers with the printed number. Witnesses
  2406.05437 (`step1`, `step2`: PDF 14, 17; 37 → 39 of 40), 1602.05866 (`algline:mainloop`, PDF 8). Residuals: `\nlset{text}`
  lines take no form; a labelled line's id is made at its close (`algorithm1.1` in `algorithm1.5`); each listing restarts at
  1 where a paper continues the count (1311.7635: PDF 9-11, ours 2-4); `\enl` (:1671-1679) never calls `\algocf@printnl`, so
  its label names the algorithm.
- **The later `\label` of a key wins** (ex-#877, 78t r2; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1131). LaTeX's last `\newlabel` wins
  (latex.ltx `\@newl@bel`: `\global\@namedef{r@key}`, "Label multiply defined"), while the post scan registers in document
  order, outer first (Perl Scan.pm:196-203, scan.rs `register_scanned`): 2001.00288's `\label{algo2}` at a block's start
  and after `\caption` gave a line (pdflatex "Algorithm 2"; `.aux` 13 → 14 of 19). A label placed takes the key from the
  earlier holders that contain it or that it contains (`release_earlier_label_holders`, from `\lx@label`, only for a key
  placed before); holders apart keep it (the scan takes the later already); the streaming build may have spilled the
  earlier, so streaming and eager agree (`114_streaming_graphics`: graphrot's two tables `tb:tab3`). Perl keeps both, the
  inner winning (`\caption{Panel}\label{x}` in a `{subfigure}` then `\caption{Main}\label{x}`: Perl "1(a)", pdflatex 1). In
  the 1,608-paper A/B 15 earlier holders in 10 papers gave their key up (1908.05655's `fig:rule_example`), none left the
  document; `.aux` matches over 144 papers 6,582 → 7,095. Witnesses 2001.00288, 1611.06737, 1711.00112, 1804.00071,
  2010.05861, 2209.06323, 2511.10625, astro-ph0512093. Residuals: algorithm2e's caption box (`\global\sbox\algocf@capbox`,
  algorithm2e.sty:2305-2336: bottom for `plain`/`boxed`, top for the ruled family) writes its `\label` there, so 2511.10625's
  caption `\label{alg:general_astar}` names the algorithm in pdflatex (1), ours the line (13); a deferred float's
  `\newlabel` is written when placed and wins (`\begin{figure}[p]\caption{Deferred}\label{k}\end{figure}\section{Two}\label{k}See
  \ref{k}.`: pdflatex "See 1.", ours "See 2."; rev78t2's lb2; SYNC_STATUS row). Repros
  listings-algorithms/algorithm2e_line_label_names_the_line, cross-references/the_later_label_wins; guards
  `perfect_kernel_batch78t::{algorithm2e_line_label_names_the_line, the_later_label_wins}`.
- Related: #491 (IEEEeqnarray's columns), #360 (a duplicated label in streaming vs eager), KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #46 (#54, #888).

### 823. biblatex's own `.bib` fields are read by the biblatex binding only

The `.bib` reader's handlers for biblatex's field names (biblatex manual §2.2.2: `journaltitle`, `location`, `urldate`,
`titleaddon`, `addendum`, `maintitle`, `mainsubtitle`, `maintitleaddon`, `booksubtitle`, `booktitleaddon`,
`issuetitle`, `issuesubtitle`, `eventtitle`, `eventtitleaddon`, `venue`, `eventdate`, `editora`-`editorc`,
`annotation`, and the per-type variants that nest them in a host or event: 47 in all, batches 56ie, 56ii and 57) were
defined in the BibTeX pool (bibtex.rs), so every route read them — under natbib or the classic styles too, where a
`.bst` declares a closed field list without them (plainnat, apsrev4-1) and bibtex(1) never writes them to the `.bbl`.
Perl's pool has none of them (they are `\bib@field@default@default` data, BibTeX.pool.ltxml:346). A paper with no
`.bbl` printed what its PDF does not have: "Accessed: 2025-08-15" (2606.11822 [9]; 2602.10008's 54 apsrev4-1 entries),
"Note: <addendum>", the main title before the title, and a `journaltitle={\undefinedmacro Jt}` raised
`Error:undefined` where pdflatex has 0. Ours (78i, bibtex.rs `define_biblatex_fields`): the handlers are defined by
the biblatex binding after its `LoadPool!("BibTeX")` (biblatex_sty.rs, beside 77a r5's `shorthand`/`labelalpha`), for
both of biblatex's routes (a `.bbl`'s entries, a `.bib` rendered without biber), and on the BibTeX route only for the
fields the document's style declares in its `.bst`'s `ENTRY` list (`bst_declared_fields`: the `\bibliographystyle`
recorded as `BIBSTYLE`, the `.bst` found on the search path) — what bibtex(1) copies for the style to print:
ACM-Reference-Format.bst:38 `location` (printed after the event, :1318-1342; 2603.25517, 2601.12610), sn-mathphys.bst
and mdpi.bst `urldate` (2607.28080, 2511.08819, 2608.12223). multibib's `\bibliographystyle<suffix>` only writes to its side aux
(multibib.sty:234); its binding (multibib_sty.rs) records that style per suffix: `\bibliography<suffix>` reads its own in a
group around the list, so `\bibliographystyle{alpha}\bibliographystyleweb{plain}` gives `alpha` on the main list and `plain`
on `web`, as pdflatex's `[Zet01]` and `[1]` (opticajnl.cls:288's and osajnl's full-reference list: 1908.11477, 2006.07118,
2008.09542, 2205.11481, 2308.15957, 2607.03975), and quantum.bst's `urldate` prints as `accessed`
(quantum-bibliographystyle-demo; `perfect_kernel_batchm1::a_multibib_style_reaches_the_bst_fields`,
`::each_multibib_list_reads_its_own_style`). The `.bst` fields are read once per document: the main list's style, with none
the first declared. Limits: a `\bibliographystyle` after a suffix list takes that list's attribute (the kernel's `\bibstyle` sets
the first `ltx:bibliography`, sect11.rs; RED index-bib/multibib_main_style_after_a_list_stays_off_that_list_red), and a suffix
style after its own list reaches `BIBSTYLE` only. Where natbib took `\bibstyle`, a list records its style's name and order
(`CITE_SORT`) as `\bibliographystyle` does (`record_bibstyle`; `06_cluster_bibliography::cluster_bib_order_is_the_styles_sort_fact`'s
multibib rows); every list holds every cited entry (RED index-bib/multibib_lists_hold_every_entry_red, post-merge MBAL). Elsewhere the fields are raw `bib-data`, as in Perl. OD #289's `annotation` and 56ie's biblatex names (the entry for the subtitle and host rows) are biblatex-only
accordingly. Repros index-bib/natbib_biblatex_only_fields_are_raw_data (red int47a) and its twin
index-bib/biblatex_prints_its_own_fields, index-bib/bst_declared_biblatex_field_is_printed; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78i::{natbib_biblatex_only_fields_are_raw_data, biblatex_prints_its_own_fields,
bst_declared_biblatex_field_is_printed}`, `06_cluster_bibliography`'s biblatex field guards.

### 824. hyperref's PDF information strings are expanded when `\hypersetup` sets them

hyperref sets `pdftitle`, `pdfauthor`, `pdfsubject`, `pdfkeywords` (and the rest of its information keys) by
`\pdfstringdef\@pdf<key>{#1}` (hyperref.sty:3543-3600): expanded at once with the document's markup made harmless, the
string its characters. Perl records the value's source text (hyperref.sty.ltxml:133 `ToString`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#1050), so `pdftitle={\mytitle}` was the metadata `<rdf content="\mytitle" property="dcterms:title"/>` (1210.7805
`\OfficialTitle`; resphilosophica.cls:311/:324 `pdftitle=\@title`, `pdfauthor=\authors` in every paper of that class).
Ours (78i, hyperref_sty.rs `pdf_string`): the value of `pdftitle`, `pdfauthor`, `pdfsubject`, `pdfkeywords` and
`pdfcopyright` is expanded by `\lx@pdfstringdef` — hyperref's `\pdfstringdef` in brief (:386-560): `\protect` empty, the
font and size commands their argument or nothing, `\\`, `~` and the other spaces a space, `\texorpdfstring` its PDF
branch, labels, index entries and error messages gobbled, then the document's `\pdfstringdefPreHook` — and, as for
hyperref's own `pdfusetitle` title (`\Hy@UseMaketitleString`, :6248-6266), `\thanks` and the note commands gobbled,
so that expanding the title makes no second note; the result's characters are kept (a control sequence still
unexpanded, a brace, a math shift, a script mark dropped: `$x^2$` is "x2" as in the PDF); puenc.def's text glyphs are
their characters in `\lx@pdfstringdef`'s group (`\DeclareTextCommand{\ss}{PU}{\80\337}` …: `\ss` ß, `\i` ı, `\j` ȷ,
`\o`, `\O`, `\ae`, `\AE`, `\oe`, `\OE`, `\l`, `\L`, `\dh`, `\th`, `\ng`, `\dj`, `\ij` and their capitals, `\SS` "SS",
latex.ltx:564's `\aa` å) and so are its text symbols (78i r3: `\textendash` :1082 –, `\textemdash` —, `\textsection` :184
§, `\textparagraph` ¶, `\textdagger` †, `\textdaggerdbl` ‡, `\textcopyright` ©, `\textregistered` ®, `\texttrademark`
™, `\textsterling` £, `\textellipsis` …, the `\textquote*` and `\quote*base` quotes, `\guillemot*`/`\guillemet*`,
`\guilsingl*`, `\textdegree` °, `\textbullet` •, `\textexclamdown`, `\textquestiondown`, with the kernel's names `\S`,
`\P`, `\dag`, `\ddag`, `\copyright`, `\pounds` and hyperref.sty:416-418's `\ldots`, `\dots`; each `\string`s its
character, which the utf8 input encoding makes active as the very command), `---`, `--`, `` !` ``, `` ?` `` are the
dashes and inverted marks hyperref substitutes in the expanded string (hyperref.sty:620-623; r2 "AB, 2, , , …",
"Pre--post---end", pdfinfo "A–B, §2, †, …", "Pre–post—end"), the text accents composed on the next character as the PU encoding composes them (`\"o` "ö";
on `\i` and `\j` the dotted letter, puenc.def:172-264 `\DeclareTextCompositeCommand{\'}{PU}{\i}{\80\355}`, so
`Mart\'{\i}nez` is "Martínez" and `\.{\i}` "i"), and the logos spelled (`\TeX`, `\LaTeX`: our logos are locked
constructors, which `\pdfstringdef`'s `\def\TeX{TeX}` cannot reach). The expansion happens when the key is
set, hyperref's own timing: `\hypersetup{pdftitle=\@title}` before `\title{…}` is the kernel's `\@title` as in the PDF
("title" — `\@` then the letters), one after it is the title, and a class's `\hypersetup` inside its `\maketitle`
(resphilosophica) sees its local definitions. Beyond hyperref: a `\and` in a PDF string is "; ", the separator of
hyperref's own `pdfusetitle` author (:6255), where `\pdfstringdef` makes garbage of it (pdfinfo "Ann Able [t]cBob
Baker"). The `\@pdf<key>` macros keep the value's tokens, as before (packages read them as text: nlctuserguide.sty's
`author={\@pdfauthor}`). Repros sectioning-frontmatter/{hyperref_pdfinfo_expands_macros (red 60m),
hyperref_pdfinfo_drops_notes_and_markup, hyperref_pdfinfo_text_symbols}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78i::{hyperref_metadata_is_expanded, hyperref_metadata_drops_notes_and_markup,
hyperref_metadata_text_symbols}`.

### 825. An AMS-TeX paper's own style is read raw unless it builds on another style

amstex.tex:1731 `\def\documentstyle#1{\W@{}\input #1.sty\relax}`. Perl's `\documentstyle` loads only a binding
(AmSTeX.pool.ltxml:71 `notex => 1`) and falls back to amsppt (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1051), so a paper's own style was
never read: amams.sty (Annals of Mathematics; math0402285, math9806089) defines `\annalsline`, `\received`,
`\startingpage` and a one-argument `\title`, which met amsppt's `\title … \endtitle` and read the whole paper as the
title (Fatal:Mouth:EoF, 0 words); 1412.7214's phd.sty its `\ThesisTitle`, `\Committee` and `\Contents` (16 Errors, 97
words). Ours (78i, amstex.rs): a style with no binding that the search path finds is read raw, as `\input` reads it —
unless it `\input`s another style (`\input amsppt.sty`, `\input ams-p.sty`: `inputs_a_style`), when it is a variation on
that style, whose changes are to internals of the style it builds on (gr-qc9507042's fic.sty redefines amsppt's
`\titlebox@`, `\thethanks@`; read raw over the amsppt binding it ended in a Fatal pushback runaway and 16 Errors), or
its parent is missing (math0406145's grubb-p.sty and 0803.2668's conm-p-mod.sty `\input ams-p.sty`, not in TeX Live):
then the amsppt binding stands in, as before. amstex.tex's `\Invalid@` (:251-252), with which such a style marks the
commands it disallows, is defined. amams.sty redefines `\ifdefined` (amams.sty:1099, a three-argument label test,
as pre-e-TeX styles did); LaTeXML's own macros test with the kernel's `\lx@ifdefined` (etex.rs, `\let` to e-TeX's
primitive: `\lx@latin@name`, the frontmatter stores' nulls, `\makeindex`, `\makeglossary`), which the redefinition
cannot reach; `\loggingall` and `\tracingnone` keep the public `\ifdefined`, as latex.ltx:662/:679 and Perl
plain_base.pool.ltxml:40/:56 do (78i r2; math0402285 3 → 0 Errors; repro parameter-conditional/kernel_ifdefined_survives_a_document_redefinition,
guard `perfect_kernel_batch78i::kernel_ifdefined_survives_a_document_redefinition`). The errors these papers still
raise are our emulation's, not the style's (`tex` converts math9906120 clean): amams's `\everydisplay{\lookforbreak}`
(amams.sty:585-590) over amstex's `\multline` (math9906120: 43 "Use \Bbb only in math", 43 "Script ^/_ can only
appear in math mode", Fatal:TooManyErrors, from JohanssonArchive.tex:250), its `\split` over amstex.tex internals the
AmSTeX pool does not have (`\ifinany@`; math9806089's 9 split errors); SYNC_STATUS "AMS-TeX papers read through their
own amams.sty". Repro
amstex/amstex_local_style_is_read (with a stand-in amslocal.sty written from scratch: amams.sty states no licence);
guard `perfect_kernel_batch78i::amstex_local_style_is_read`.

### 829. thmtools names an unnamed theorem by its environment, case-modified as its options say

thm-kv.sty:359 names a `\declaretheorem{<env>}` without `name=`/`title=`/`heading=` `\thmt@modifycase <env>`, which is
`\protect\MakeUppercase` by default and `\MakeLowercase` or nothing under thmtools' `lowercase`/`anycase` options
(thmtools.sty:35-39 passes them to thm-kv, thm-kv.sty:30-42): `\MakeUppercase` takes the first token only, so `{defn}`
is headed "Defn 1.2". Perl hardwires `\MakeUppercase` (thmtools.sty.ltxml:80-82) and ignores the options; ours had no
name at all ("1.2", typerefnum " 1.2"; 1505.04294's 90 theorems, 70 papers of the census without a name key). Ours
(78k, thmtools_sty.rs): the binding declares thm-kv's three options and defaults the name to `\thmt@modifycase` before
the environment's name. Repros package-bindings/{thmtools_unnamed_theorem_is_headed_by_its_environment,
thmtools_lowercase_option_lowercases_the_unnamed_theorem}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78k::{thmtools_unnamed_theorem_is_headed_by_its_environment,
thmtools_unnamed_theorem_follows_the_case_option}`.

### 830. bibentry's store mode: `\nobibliography` keeps each `.bbl` entry for `\bibentry`

bibentry.sty:42-66: `\nobibliography{<db>}` and `\nobibliography*` read the `.bbl` with `{thebibliography}` and
`\bibitem` redefined so that each entry's text up to its blank line is stored as `\BR@r@<key>` (`\BR@c@bibitem#1 #2
\par`) and nothing is printed; `\bibentry{<key>}` `\nocite`s the key and prints the stored text without its final
period (`\BR@nodot`). Perl has no binding (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1059); read raw, our kernel's locked `{thebibliography}`
refuses the redefinition, so `\nobibliography*` printed the whole list and each `\bibentry` nothing (2505.07606: 29 empty
entries, two lists; 2210.16098: 48 lines "."). Ours (78k, latexml_contrib bibentry_sty.rs): `\lx@BR@store` reads the
`<jobname>.bbl` itself (the file `\bibliography`'s bbl route reads), tokenizes it under the standard catcodes and stores
each `\bibitem[<label>]{<key>}`'s tokens up to `\par`, the next `\bibitem` or the list's `\end` (where TeX's delimited
read would run on into the next entry when no blank line separates them); the stored text is digested where
`\bibentry` stands. A paper with no `.bbl` (only its `.bib`) stores nothing; each `\bibentry` then reports its key in a
Warning (pdflatex: its `\nocite`'s undefined citation). bibentry's `\def\bibliography` wrapper (bibentry.sty:74-75),
which resets the star's flag, is refused by the locked `\bibliography`, so the `\AtEndDocument` warning for a
`\nobibliography*` without a later `\bibliography` (:76-79) asks the kernel's count of `\bibliography` calls
(`lx_bibliography_calls`, sect11.rs `\lx@ifusebbl`) instead. bibentry's `\BR@b@bibitem`, `\BR@c@bibitem` and `\BR@nodot`
are defined as there for code that redefines them (tufte-common.def:876-882, whose margin citations are `\bibentry`s).
Repro index-bib/bibentry_prints_the_stored_entry; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78k::bibentry_prints_the_stored_entry`.

### 831. bibentry's `\nobibliography{<db>}` without the star keeps the list its citations resolve to

In TeX, `\nobibliography{<db>}` prints no list, but its `\bibitem`s (the original `\BR@bibitem`, bibentry.sty:49-53)
still write the `\bibcite` labels every `\cite` resolves to. Our citations resolve to the `ltx:bibitem`s of a
bibliography in the document: without a list every `\cite` would be a "Missing Entry for citation" (2210.16098's 33
`\cite`s, AAAI's `\nobibliography{aaai23}` idiom). By the charter's order (semantic markup before PDF fidelity), the
starless form stores the entries for `\bibentry` and builds the list where it stands, as before: the PDF's list-less
page differs; the starred form (followed by a `\bibliography`) builds none, so one list stands as in the PDF. Repro
index-bib/bibentry_nobibliography_keeps_the_list_its_citations_resolve_to; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78k::bibentry_nobibliography_keeps_the_list_its_citations_resolve_to`.

### 834. tabularray's `\SetCell[c=<n>,r=<m>]` spans columns and rows

tabularray.sty:2542-2615: `\SetCell[<outer>]{<inner>}` sets a cell's `r=`/`c=` span (`cell/outer` keys, :2611-2615) and
its style (`cell/inner`, :2617-2642); the author leaves the covered cells empty and tabularray typesets the spanned cell
over them. Perl's ar5iv stub maps `tblr` to `tabular` and has no `\SetCell`; ours had it as a no-op (#384), so "Wide"
(`c=2`) sat in one cell beside a stray empty `<td/>` and "Tall" (`r=2`) spanned no row. Ours (78l, tabularray_sty.rs
`tblr_span_cells`): `\lx@tblr@env` reads the table body whole, as tabularray's `+b` argument holds it (:3463; before,
only for `evaluate=`/`expand=`), and when it holds a `\SetCell` at a cell's start, after any row-level rule command, at
the body's own level (tabularray's extractor takes every table command at a cell's start, with its `[…]`/`{…}`
arguments, among the cell's own tokens unexpanded, :3770-3860 — `\hline`, `\hline[1pt]`, `\cline{1-2}`, `\midrule`,
`\cmidrule[…](lr){…}`, `\SetRow{…}`, `\SetHline`, …; the `*` and `[<space>]` of the row end before it, `\\[2pt]`;
2308.16907's 11 `\hline \SetCell`, 2507.01654, 2305.00635, 2502.18449, 2404.12789, 2601.16161, 2604.10925, 2606.09108, a 78l r1
draft taking only a first-token `\SetCell`; never one in braces or in a cell's environment), rewrites that cell (a body without one is put back as read): `r=<m>` becomes `\lx@tblr@cell@span{<m>}`, the row span `\multirow` sets (multirow_sty.rs
`\lx@multirow@setup`), and `c=<n>` turns the `n-1` column separators after the cell's text into the primitive `\span`
(`\lx@span`, as `\multispan` spans), so the cell keeps its columns' templates — their rules and the first one's
alignment, as tabularray's spanned cell keeps the first column's `halign`. A covered cell's text, if the author wrote
any, stays in the spanned cell (tabularray hides it; authored content is kept, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2). The inner keys stay
unrendered, `halign` (`l`, `c`, `r`, `halign=`) included: a `\multicolumn{<n>}{<halign>}` would replace the columns'
templates and drop their rules, which tabularray draws apart from the cell (`colspec={Q[l]|l}` with
`\SetCell[c=1]{c}`, 2408.02133; `\SetCell{c, gray9}` in a `c |` column, 2403.06461; both lost a `border` in a 78l
draft), so `\SetCell[c=2]{c}` over `l` columns is left-aligned where pdflatex centres it. `\SetCells` (every cell,
:2510) and the inner spec's `cell{i}{j}={r=…,c=…}{…}` spans are not modelled. Residuals: a row span over a cell below
that holds text is not applied — the cell below keeps its own cell and the spanned one spans no row (`\SetCell[r=2]{c}
T & … \\ Below & …`, where tabularray hides "Below" under "T"; the text stays, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2); a math table's
`tex=` reverts a spanned row with its `\span`s as `\hfil\hfil` (`\SetCell[c=2]{c} mx & \\` in a `$…$` tblr:
"mx\hfil\hfil\\"). Probe `tblr.tex` (sel78k; 25 sample papers call `\SetCell`/`\SetCells`); 78l review probes `tb.tex`,
`tb2.tex`. Repros alignment-bindings/tblr_setcell_spans_columns_and_rows, alignment-bindings/tblr_setcell_after_a_row_rule_spans;

### 844. A citation's ordering is a class on its `ltx:bibref`, applied where the numbers are known

natbib's `sort`/`compress`/`sort&compress` (natbib.sty:267-271; `\NAT@sort@cites`, :377 and :1185-1200; the run
compressed in `\NAT@citexnum`, :401-421) and cite.sty (sorts and compresses unless `nosort`/`nocompress`, cite.sty:95,
:272-297, :412, :415) order a citation's numbers when they typeset it, from the `.aux`. LaTeXML numbers the bibliography
after the document, so the order is applied by the post stage: the `\@@bibref` constructor (sect11.rs
`cite_order_class`) writes the package's choice, the values `CITE_SORTCITES`/`CITE_COMPRESS` (not Perl's `CITE_SORT`, the
style's list order, #116: read as this one, a `\bibliographystyle{plain}` before the citations sorted them, "[1, 3]" for
pdflatex's "[3, 1]"), as `class="ltx_cite_sort
ltx_cite_compress"` on the `ltx:bibref` (the schema's `Common.attributes` class: no new attribute; the bibref is
replaced by its citation in post, so the class never reaches the HTML), and `make_bibcite` (crossref.rs) sorts the
entries by number (those without a whole number after them, in their order, as natbib's `\NAT@nonsort@list`) and, for a
bare-number citation (`show` Number/refnum/Super: `\citep`, `\cite`, a superscript one; not natbib's textual `\citet`,
which natbib does not compress), joins each run of three or more consecutive numbers with an en dash, a run of two with
the separator ("[1–3]", "[1, 2]"; a superscript range inside its superscript). Who sets the values: natbib's options
(also on a later `\usepackage[…]{natbib}` after a binding's early load, `\lx@natbib@repeat@options`; a cite.sty loaded
first is natbib's `sort`, natbib.sty:272-274); cite.sty's binding (its 16 options declared, `nosort`/`nocompress`
acting); revtex4/4-1/4-2 (`\PassOptionsToPackage{sort&compress}{natbib}`, revtex4.cls:5480, revtex4-1.cls:7021,
revtex4-2.cls:7042); achemso.cls (:1396-1398, the binding passes `sort&compress` alone: its numeric style is not the
binding's yet); acmart, whose own `\setcitestyle` (acmart.cls:306-345) reads the ordering words that natbib's ignores
(`natbib@setcitestyle@orders`), so its default `\citestyle{acmnumeric}` sorts and compresses; jheppub and
quantumarticle, which already passed `sort&compress`. cite.sty prints a key it cannot sort (a label not a number, an
undefined key) at once, before the sorted ones (cite.sty:205-230 `\@cite@dump@now`, `\@cite@gobbledump@now`): its
binding adds `ltx_cite_unsorted_first` (`CITE_UNSORTED_FIRST`, which natbib's load clears), "[Knu84, Lam86, 1]".
Under that class the entries sort by cite.sty's own sort numbers (crossref.rs `cite_sty_sort_key`, cite.sty:127-222): a
number `n` is `256n`, a `[prefix]number[suffix]` label one character each `(16384p + n)·256 + s` ("2a" between 2 and 3:
"[1, 2a, 7]"), number-separator-number `((16384p + n)·256 + sep)·4096 + m`; a run compresses by cite.sty's two kinds
(:266-297 `\@compress@cite`): consecutive numbers (256 apart) or consecutive suffixes of one number (1 apart, "[4a–4c]").
Only whole numbers compress, so a label given in natbib's numbers mode ("[Knu84, Lam86, Mil90]", below and natbib_sty.rs
`\lx@NAT@parselabel`) stays a list; such a label is the number only, not the full authors as well (a `\citet{k}`
printed "Knu84 [Knu84]"; it prints "Knu84" as an entry without authors prints its number, natbib's "(author?)" not
reproduced; witness 2608.05327 "[21]" → "[FNW23]"). Perl ignores all of it (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1072). Repros index-bib/{natbib_sort_compress_numbers,
natbib_super_sort_compress, cite_sty_sorts_and_compresses, cite_sty_nosort_keeps_the_order,
cite_sty_prints_unsorted_labels_first, revtex_citations_sort_and_compress, acmart_numeric_citations_sort_and_compress,
natbib_numbers_prints_a_label_given, cite_sty_sorts_numbers_with_a_suffix, natbib_numbers_textual_label}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78j::{natbib_sort_compress_numbers,
natbib_super_sort_compress, cite_sty_sorts_and_compresses, cite_sty_nosort_keeps_the_order,
cite_sty_prints_unsorted_labels_first, revtex_citations_sort_and_compress, acmart_numeric_citations_sort_and_compress,
natbib_numbers_prints_a_label_given, cite_sty_sorts_numbers_with_a_suffix, natbib_numbers_textual_label}`,
`crossref::tests::{compressed_joints_join_runs_of_three, cite_sty_sort_keys_and_runs}`.

### 845. cleveref's label format and the document's reference formats are tag forms built with the target

cleveref formats the number a `\cref` prints with the type's label format, `\cref@<type>@label` from `\creflabelformat`
(cleveref.sty:1270-1272), else `\cref@default@label` (`\crefdefaultlabelformat`, :1264-1265), applied when the reference
is typeset (`\@crefconstructcomponents`, :1329-1334): an equation's "(1)" (:7838-7842). Ours (cleveref_sty.rs): a
`creflabel` tag role (`type_tag_formatter`, `\lx@creflabel@@`) formats the target's refnum with that macro where the
target's tags are built (base_utilities `tag_forms`), as the type names are (OD #131, ruling 7e) — only for a type whose
format does not print the number as it is (read from the format's definition, body `#2#1#3`, so the format is expanded
once, where the tag is built; a plain type has no such tag and its refnum is the form), its diagnostics held until a
reference prints it (`type_tag_deferred`, as hyperref's `autoref`: 2506.11592's malformed, never-referenced
`\creflabelformat{enumi}{label*=\arabic*}` raised 96 Warnings); `\cref`, `\Cref`, `\labelcref` and both ends of
`\crefrange`/`\Crefrange` show it (the range's second end was a `\ref`), the page references (`\cpageref`,
`\labelcpageref`) keep the refnum; the post stage falls back to `refnum` for a target without the tag (crossref.rs
`ref_fallbacks`), and a tooltip treats it as the refnum it formats (`generate_title`'s duplicate test).

A reference format the document sets replaces the whole reference: `\crefformat`/`\Crefformat{<type>}{<format>}`
(cleveref.sty:1851, :1886-1906; `#1` the number, `#2`/`#3` the link's ends, :1047-1071 `\@@setcref`) and the
multi-reference `\crefmultiformat`/`\Crefmultiformat` (:1855-1858, `first`/`second`/`middle`/`last`, each holding its
conjunction, :1000-1018) are what pdflatex prints, with none of cleveref's names or label format; cleveref builds the
format of every other type from its names and label format at `\begin{document}` (:8020-8032 `\@crefdefineformat`),
which is our `creftype~creflabel`. Which formats the document set is noted as they are set (`\@crefformat`,
`\@crefmultiformat`, `\labelcrefformat` wrapped, `\lx@cref@noteformat`, map `cref_doc_format`), cleveref's own
`\begin{document}` code, which builds the defaults, bracketed out (`\lx@cref@building`, a hook before the file's and one
after; the builders themselves are left as they are, which packages patch: clevethm's `\patchcmd\@crefdefineformat`,
2608.12136), the other variant with one when cleveref derives it (:1888-1904, `\cref@othervariant`), and a copy
cleveref makes of one for a sub-type (`\@crefcopyformats`, :8035-8046: the section's `\S#2#1#3` is the subsection's,
`cref_note_copy`); a name `\csname` made `\relax` is undefined, as `\@ifundefined` reads it (`cref_defined`). Each such format is a tag form of its own at the target
(`crefformat`, `crefformatcap`, `labelcrefformat`, `crefmulti{first,firstcap,second,middle,last}`; `\lx@cref@docformat`,
held like `creflabel`; the family's roles registered by the first format the document sets, so a document that sets
none builds none), whole inside the link (pdflatex links only `#1`), the number one group (`{{<refnum>}}`, as
cleveref's `#1` is one macro: the derived `\MakeUppercase#2#1#3` takes it whole; 2307.12991, 2408.03413). A form is the
format's text, which pdflatex typesets at the reference: a format whose commands compute (`cref_format_is_text`: each
must typeset — not expandable, protected, robust `\protect\<cs>`, or a macro made only of such — besides the case
changer cleveref puts first in a variant it derives; 2608.12136's xstring calls on the label being referenced looped
to a Fatal PushbackLimit at the target, a `\cref` in a format) or that typesets a numbered object of its own
(`\crefformat{footnote}{#2\footnotemark[#1]#3}`, a mark with its own tags: a recursion; 1601.06262, 1711.01177,
2005.13962, 2008.04624) gives none, and the reference prints cleveref's default ("footnote 1"); a form makes no forms
while it is typeset (`\lx@cref@inform`). This is the fail-safe of building at the target what cleveref typesets at
the reference. Its diagnostics are the held tag's, raised where a reference prints the form, as TeX raises them at the
reference; a form whose typesetting errs, or that leaves a group open or closes one it did not open, gives none (an
Error naming the format, its type and the target's place: "The cleveref format of the figure (at …) leaves 1 group(s)
open"; `\egroup`, a command let to `}`, is text, so `#2Fig.~#1#3\egroup` gives pdflatex's one error — divergence: the
reference then prints cleveref's default "fig. 1" where pdflatex, which typesets on, prints the author's "Fig. 1"; a held
tag's text that errs on its own raises no second, summary Error, `\lx@tag@intags@held`: rev78j4's n9, an `\autoref`
name `\bgroup Fig`, gives pdflatex's one). The form is
digested in a group of its own, `stomach::digest_in_own_group`, which undoes what its text leaves: the frames it left
open are unwound and the alignment brace count (tex.web's `align_state`) is put back, as the `{` such a text scanned is
not the document's (left counted, a figure's tabular of two captioned minipages read its next `&` as text and moved a
cell into the row above, "Missing } inserted"; rev78j3's k5, k2). Its tag, empty, stays until its target ties the
diagnostics to its labels (`note_empty_held_tag`, sect11.rs `remove_empty_held_tags`), or, for a tag no target closes
over (a caption's tags in a minipage folded into a figure panel, a label type's tags put in place after their target
closed), once the document is built (`settle_empty_held_tags`, before the held diagnostics are replayed; the pending
count is the job's, reset with its deferred diagnostics), tied to its owner's labels only — the element holding its
`ltx:tags`; an owner with no label, a panel no reference names, drops the tag with its diagnostics, as pdflatex never
typesets that format (rev78j4's m1c, m1, m2, m5: a section's or the outer figure's label had replayed the panels'
errors); a held tag whose typesetting raised only Debug messages holds
nothing and is removed where it is built (a plain label format's empty `creflabel`): the derived `\Cref` variant `\MakeUppercase#2\color{blue}Fig.~#1#3` of 2008.12750's and
2604.24399's `\crefformat`, whose `\MakeUppercase` takes `\color` alone (pdflatex errs at a `\Cref`), had left its
group to the tag's `\endgroup` and the figure's mode unended. A stray `&` in a form (`F & #2#1#3`) is dropped, as TeX
drops it, with its Error held (pdflatex 1 error for the one `\cref`, where every figure's two forms raised one each). A reference, when the document set any format
of its family, shows `<format role>|<default>` (`\lx@cref@or`, a text `|`): the post stage prints the first alternative
its target has (crossref.rs `generate_ref_aux`, `show_alternatives`; a show with no `|` is unchanged, so a document that
set no format keeps its output; a document format the target has is the whole reference, with no context sought for
one without a letter or digit, `generate_ref`: siamart's `\crefformat{equation}{\textup{#2(#1)#3}}` with `\tag{$\star$}`
prints "(⋆)", not "(⋆) ‣ section 1", 1905.03839), and between the references of a `\cref` list the conjunction is wrapped
(`\lx@cref@conjunction`, `ltx_cref_conjunction`) and dropped before a reference that printed the document's format, else
unwrapped (crossref.rs `settle_cref_conjunctions`). `\labelcref` prints the document's `\labelcrefformat`, else for a
type whose `\crefformat` the document set the bare number (cleveref builds that type no `\labelcref` format,
:1438-1440, so `\labelcref@default@format` applies), else the label format; a `\labelcref` list likewise prints the
default `\labelcref` format for a type whose `\crefmultiformat` the document set (role `labelcrefmulti`; cleveref.sty
:8028-8030 builds no `\labelcref` multi format for it, :1620-1669 the defaults): siamart's "1 and 3", not "(1) and (3)". 2004.14422 (`\crefformat{equation}
{#2#1#3}`: "1"), 2312.00252 (`#2Equation~#1#3`), 2406.15983 (formats in a `.sty`: "Equation 2").

Under `\label[<type>]` (`\lx@cleverref@labeltype`, placed on the object the label names as the kernel's `\lx@label`
places it, `Document::float_to_label_scoped`: after a closed float, an inner equation or a `\footnote`, the object
whose step is in scope) the label type's forms replace the object's (names, `creflabel`, the
document's formats; an empty one, a plain label format or no format of the document's, removes the object's), with the
object's own number (`\@currentlabel`, `cleveref_label_number`: cleveref.sty:82-96 changes the type of the label it
writes, not its number): an equation labelled `[lemma]` under `\crefformat{lemma}{Lem.~#2#1#3}` is "Lem. 1".
Divergence: the format is the one in force where the target is numbered, not where it is referenced, so a
`\creflabelformat`, `\crefformat` or `\crefmultiformat` between a label and its `\cref` (in a group, set after the
equation, or a `\crefformat{section}{Appendix~#2#1#3}` after `\appendix` for the sections numbered before it) is not seen
for that target: the format in force at the target prints, where pdflatex prints the one in force at the reference
(rev78j2's t1, a `\crefformat` redefined mid-document: ours "C2", "B1", pdflatex "B2", "C1"). Not modelled: `\crefrangeformat`/`\Crefrangeformat` (a range's format holds both numbers,
`\crefstripprefix{#1}{#2}` in 1409.7964 and 1603.08012, which a tag form at one target cannot carry: `\crefrange` keeps
`creftypeplural~creflabel` to `creflabel`), `\labelcrefmultiformat`, cleveref's grouping of a `\cref` list by type and
its range compression (`\cref{e3,e1,e2}`: pdflatex "eqs. (1) to (3)", ours in the order given). The forms are copies
at every target (an `\ensuremath{(#2#1#3)}` format's math in each equation's `ltx:tags`, which takes the first math ids:
1905.03839's `Ch1.E1.m1` is `m8`); a stored tag with markup is its copy (latexml_post scan.rs `has_markup`, Perl
Scan.pm:269 `cleanNode`), so a reference prints the tag's math as a formula ("(P1)" for `\tag{$\mathrm{P_1}$}`, where its
flattened text read "( P 1 )"; 2609.28438, 1905.03839, 2510.06152), a tag of text alone its text as before.
Divergence: a tag's text and its copy reach the reference with their spaces, where Perl's `prepRefText`
(CrossRef.pm:791-793, `trimChildNodes`, Post.pm:1374-1397) trims the copy's first and last text: a tag rarely starts
or ends with a space, but a cleveref position format holds its conjunction (`\crefmultiformat`'s second
`{ and~(#2#1#3)}`), which trimmed would print "Problems (P)and (P1)" (2609.28438). A
format's `#1` is the refnum in `\normalfont` (`\lx@therefnum@@`), where cleveref's is the label's text in the
format's font (`\sffamily\bfseries … theorem~#1` prints the number upright, pdflatex sans bold). KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1073.

### 846. pdfpages' `\includepdf` places the file's pages as graphics

Perl's `\includepdf` (pdfpages.sty.ltxml:30-36) writes the PDF as an `ltx:resource` and the text "See [pages X of]
⟨link⟩"; pdflatex places the pages, each as a page of the document. Ours (pdfpages_sty.rs): each page the `pages` list
names (pdfpages.sty's syntax: `N`, `N-M` descending when `M < N`, `N-`, `-M`, `-`, `last`; `{}` a blank page, which
places nothing; default `1`) is an `\includegraphics[page=N]{file}` in its own paragraph, with the graphicx keys given
(`scale`, `angle`, `width`, `height`, `trim`, `clip`, `viewport`, `keepaspectratio`), as pdfpages includes each page
through graphicx; the post stage renders the page (`page=`, latexml_post graphics.rs). The list and the file name are
expanded first, as pdfpages reads them (a `\foreach` loop's `pages={\x}`, 2605.05847; a name in a macro, 2406.13026). An
open range reads the page count from the file (`read_pdf_page_count`), and a page past the last is an Error placing
nothing, in pdfpages' words ("Page 6 of `five.pdf' does not exist", pdfpages.sty:909-920 `\AM@checkpagenumber`; a count
not read keeps every page). A PDF the graphics search path does not find
(pdflatex: "Cannot find file"), or a list not understood, keeps Perl's link (`\lx@includepdf@link`). pdfpages' layout
keys (`nup`, `frame`, `landscape`, `pagecommand`, `offset`, `fitpaper`, …) are not modelled. The pages are content, as
pdflatex prints them, at their size cost where Perl's link (pdfpages.sty.ltxml:24-29) chose size: a paper that is one
included PDF converts to its page images (1805.02202: 133 PNGs, 23 MB, 1.38 s cold). Repros
singletons/{includepdf_places_its_pages, includepdf_expands_its_arguments, includepdf_page_past_the_last}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78j::{includepdf_places_its_pages, includepdf_expands_its_arguments,
includepdf_page_past_the_last}`, `pdfpages_sty::tests::include_pdf_pages_reads_pdfpages_lists`; the missing-file link
`binding_singletons_56::includepdf_file_name_is_semiverbatim`,
`perfect_kernel_gemini::pdfpages_includepdfmerge_multi_and_opts`.

### 848. A class's `\@xnthm` may print a theorem's within-counter its own way

latex.ltx's `\@xnthm` defines `\the<thm>` as `\the<within>\@thmcountersep\@thmcounter{<thm>}`; IEEEtran.cls:5607-5627
redefines it so a theorem numbered within sections prints `\@IEEEthmcounterinsection{section}` (`\arabic`, "Theorem
2.1" where `\thesection` is "II"; "A" after `\appendix`, `\Alph` after `\appendices`, `A\arabic` under
`romanappendices`, :5737/:5768/:5773). Perl's kernel `\newtheorem` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml `defineNewTheorem`)
always prints `\the<within>`, and its IEEEtran binding has no theorem code: "Example II.1" (1911.01952; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#1079). Ours (78n): `define_new_theorem` reads the mapping `theorem_within_display` (within counter → a one-argument
macro) set by `set_theorem_within_display` (ieeetran_cls.rs, for `section` → `\@IEEEthmcounterinsection`); amsthm's
binding, which ntheorem and theorem.sty borrow, clears it (`clear_theorem_within_display`), as their own `\@xnthm`
replaces the class's in LaTeX. Repro cross-references/ieeetran_theorem_within_section_is_arabic; guard
`perfect_kernel_batch78n::ieeetran_theorem_within_section`.

### 851. A footnote's `[<n>]` is `\thefootnote` at `<n>`; article's title block marks in `\@fnsymbol` and steps the counter; a title mark and a body text pair by the number they stand for

latex.ltx:17652-17657 `\@xfootnote`, :17678-17682 `\@xfootnotemark` and :17694-17699 `\@xfootnotenext` set the footnote
counter to `<n>` in a group and mark the note `\thefootnote` there; article's `\maketitle` (article.cls:203-205; report.cls
:211, book.cls:217, extarticle's copy, all in the `\if@titlepage` false branch — `titlepage` is report's and book's
default) typesets the title, the authors and the date with `\thefootnote` `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote` and resets the
counter after it (:190, :223); its `\thanks` (latex.ltx:17215; `\footnote` is `\thanks` there, article.cls:173, :241)
is `\footnotemark` and the text, a step of the counter, under a title page too. Perl prints `[<n>]` as given and its
frontmatter marks a title-block note as the body does and steps nothing (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1060). Ours (78o,
latex_constructs/mod.rs): `numbered_footnote_mark` prints `[<n>]` through `\thefootnote` at `<n>` (`\lx@note`,
`\lx@notemark`, `\lx@notetext` and the VerbatimFootnotes `@live` forms, which read `[<n>]` undigested,
`OptionalUndigested`, as TeX reads `\c@footnote #1\relax`; a minipage's notes stay `footnote_tag`'s); `<n>` is a number
when it expands to digits (`2`, `\arabic{footnote}`) or is a count register (`\value{footnote}` — digested on its own
it was a register assignment, "Missing number, treated as zero", and the mark printed nothing); a `[<n>]` that TeX's
scan leaves nothing printable of (`\relax`, `\value` of a counter not yet defined, `2\relax`; not a blank `[]`, a text
mark's "no mark", arxstspdf's `\freefootnotetext[]`: RED `footnotemark_blank_is_tex_zero_red`) is read by the
`\setcounter` siblings' reader, `read_braced_value` (GA1f `tex_footnote_number`: the mark TeX's, 0 with its one "Missing
number"; 2407.13730, 2606.19583; guard rows `footnotemark_missing_number_reads_as_tex`,
`footnotetext_missing_number_pairs_with_its_mark`), and any other mark
(`\footnotemark[$\dagger$]`, "Missing number" in LaTeX) is printed as given, as before and as Perl does, with no
diagnostic (main-session decision 2026-10-22: no diagnostic for now, the Warning false-alarmed on classes that read the
mark as text; the faithful counter-definition rule is SYNC row 596's open part); an e-TeX expression
(`[\numexpr\value{footnote}-1]`) is a number since 78u (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1135; the `…\relax]` and leading-space forms not
yet, review rev78u); `given_footnote_number` reads
`[<n>]` for a number once per note, its diagnostics held, and the mark and
`_fnvalue` reuse it, so a `[<n>]` whose expansion errs (`\footnotemark[\the\relax]`) is no number and the mark's
digestion reports the error once, as pdflatex (review probes rev78o2 valerr, val: 78o r2 2 and 3 errors) (read so, a `\footnotetext[<mark>]{…}` no longer drops the space after it, which the digested argument
lost: `perfect_kernel_batch68y::aa_tablefootmark_sets_the_mark_in_text`). `declare_fnsymbol_title_block` (called by the article, report, book, extarticle, extreport, extbook
and siamltex bindings — siamltex.cls:156-175 marks its title block in `\fnsymbol` too — when that class is the
document's — `is_document_class`, recorded by `\documentclass`/`\documentstyle` before the class loads, so revtex4,
IEEEtran, elsarticle, llncs and the other bindings that load the article binding as their base keep their marks)
defines the title's `\thefootnote` hook `\lx@title@thefootnote` (`TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE`, `\@fnsymbol\c@footnote`, unless
the class options set a title page), sets `lx_title_counts_footnotes` and appends `\setcounter{footnote}{0}` to
`\lx@maketitle@body`; `enter_title_footnotes` makes the hook `\thefootnote` for the rest of a title, creator or date
field the frontmatter digests (`lx_frontmatter_item`), and `\lx@title@footnote@step` (frontmatter_fields.rs, first in
`\lx@add@thanks`, `\lx@add@note`, `\lx@add@pubnote` and `\lx@add@pubnote@thanks`) steps the counter for each `\thanks`
and `\footnote` of those fields as the `\maketitle` flush digests them (`lx_frontmatter_explicit`; a flush without
`\maketitle` typesets no title and steps nothing). The hook is the one a binding declares its title's own marks with,
and the frontmatter observer's (#837, `observer/rehearsal.rs` `TITLE_FOOTNOTE_HOOK` is `TITLE_THEFOOTNOTE`), so the
printed marks and the observer's Mark labels agree for a bare `\footnotemark` and a literal `[<n>]` (the observer
evaluates `[\arabic{footnote}]` against the counter unstepped, so its label there is the one before the title's notes —
FM S2a.2's to fix, SYNC). So `\author{A\footnote{…}}\author{B\footnotemark[\arabic{footnote}]}`
gives B "∗" (2201.11183 "Zhenan Fan∗1, Huang Fang∗2", 2111.13260 "Suhani Vora1 *, Noha Radwan1 *"; int51a "0", 78o r1
""), and a bare `\footnotemark` after three `\thanks` "§". A mark and a text are paired by their printed marks as before
(`relocate_footnote`, Perl's `relocateFootnote`); one that finds no such partner and stands in the title block, or
whose partner would, pairs with the opposite notes standing for the same footnote counter value (`_fnvalue`, a
bookkeeping attribute `footnote_pairing` sets on page footnotes; `title_block_partner`: an `ltx:creator`, `ltx:title` or
`ltx:date` ancestor on one side), or when neither prints a mark — `{\renewcommand\thefootnote{}\footnotemark
\footnotetext{…}}`, the unmarked "equal contribution" note, prints the same nothing twice (2606.03847; Perl and int52a
leave them apart, an empty mark matching none). In a class that sets the counter back after `\maketitle`, a note numbered from the counter — no
`[<n>]`, or one that moves with the counter (`\value{footnote}`, `\arabic{footnote}`; read with the counter one ahead,
`FootnoteNumber::from_counter`) — carries `_fncounted` (`footnote_pairing`), and a mark and a text on the two sides of
the reset (one in the title block, one not) pair by value only when neither carries it, and by printed mark unless both
do (`same_count`): the body counts from 1 again, so its "2" is another note — article's "C†" for
`\footnotemark[\value{footnote}]` after two `\thanks` and the body's `\footnotetext[2]` "2 Body text two", report's
(title page) "B2" for a bare `\footnotemark` after a `\thanks` and the body's bare `\footnotetext` "2" answering the
body's own mark (pdflatex; review probes rev78o2 art2, ttp3; 78o r2 moved, and for ttp3 copied, the body's text into
the title's mark). A `[<n>]` naming its number keeps the pairing across the reset: by value `\footnotemark[2]` "†" and
`\footnotetext[2]` "2" (2505.14146), by printed mark a title's bare `\footnotemark` "∗" and the body's
`\footnotetext[1]` under `\fnsymbol` "∗", one note in the PDF too (2507.05750, 1405.7962), and a `[\thealtnum]` of a
counter of its own on both sides (astro-ph9712060). The title block is the document's title, its creators and its
date — a section's `ltx:title` is the body's (1907.00457's `\section{Results\footnotemark}` and the `\footnotetext`
after it, one body note; `in_title_block`, also `title_block_partner`'s predicate). Two body notes that print apart stay apart, as in pdflatex: a `\footnotetext[1]`
under `\fnsymbol` ("∗ Equal contribution") is no answer to a table's `\footnotemark` "1" (review probe rev78o f2; 78o
r1, int52a and Perl moved the text into the table's mark). This keeps the common title-block idiom paired —
`\author{A\footnotemark[1]}` `\maketitle` `\renewcommand{\thefootnote}{\fnsymbol{footnote}}` `\footnotetext[1]{…}`
prints "∗" for both (2412.20504, 2006.14582; siamltex 0903.0014); `\footnotetext[2]` after `\maketitle` without the
renewal prints "2" where the title shows "†", which pdflatex leaves apart and we pair (2505.14146); a class whose title
marks we do not model pairs too (siamltex1213, 1406.0089, 1503.07490); and `\fnsymbol`'s "∥" against `\@fnsymbol`'s "‖"
for 6 (2002.11721; Perl's `\fnsymbol` table, latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:3070, against latex.ltx's `\@fnsymbol` the
kernel runs). Witness 2507.05750 (footmisc `symbol`). 0707.3986 (RR.sty:141 `\RRnote` = `\footnotetext[0]`, under
RR.sty:445 `\def\thefootnote{\fnsymbol{footnote}}`) prints its note unmarked, as the class asks; its TL 2025 PDF's "0"
is pdflatex's error recovery — RR.sty's `\xdef` of the accented theme name (`\RRtheme{\THCog}`, :160-168) raises
"Missing } inserted" and "Too many }'s" in `\makeRR`, which close its group early, so `\thefootnote` is article's
`\@arabic` again when `\@RRnote` runs (:477). Residuals: the frontmatter digests the fields in the order the preamble
set them, so a title `\thanks` set after the `\author` steps after the authors' (pdflatex: the title's first); the
observer's fallback when the hook is undefined (a title-page class) is `\@fnsymbol`, where report and book print arabic.

### 852. → KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1062 (algorithm2e's `noline` block gives its indentation back)

### 853. A minipage holding a `\subcaption` is the sub-figure

subcaption.sty:251 makes `\subcaption` `\caption` under `\@captype` `sub<type>`: in a minipage of a figure it numbers
the minipage "1a", and a `\label` after it names that panel; caption's `\caption@subtypehook` (caption.sty:639-664)
steps the float's counter ahead of the float's own caption. Perl's `\subcaption` (subcaption.sty.ltxml:43-56, with a
TODO for exactly this) changes `\@captype` only: the sub-caption's number is made but no element carries it, and its
label falls to the figure (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1085). Ours (78o): `begin_caption_box`/`end_caption_box`
(latex_constructs/mod.rs) take a box's caption of the float's sub-type as well as of its type (`caption_box_types`), so the
minipage becomes the sub-caption's panel — its id, tags and list entry, the labels its content left, as a `{subfigure}`
has them (#447), and the float's element (`ltx:table` in a `table`, as a `{subtable}` is; blocks.rs
`adopt_box_caption`, 2502.10377); `\lx@subcaption@type` (subcaption_sty.rs) steps the float's counter ahead
once per float as `{subfigure}`'s `before_float` does (`preincrement_float_counter`, not again under `\ContinuedFloat`).
A box holding two sub-captions (2008.05644: two `\includegraphics` + `\subcaption` pairs in one minipage) is not one
sub-figure: it stays as before (`\@@add@caption@counters` counts the captions per type, `CAPTION_COUNT_PREFIX`).
Witness 2011.13897 (PDF "2a"/"2b", before "2"/"2"; fidelity3 N4). Outside a float (`\captionsetup{type=figure}` in a
`center`) nothing changes (the RED `captions-floats/subcaption_before_caption_numbers_its_figure` stays). Repros
captions-floats/subcaption_in_a_minipage_labels_its_panel (and, now green, subcaption_labels_in_scaled_panels_stay_on_their_panels,
continuedfloat_minipage_subcaption_continues_the_letters); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78o::{subcaption_in_a_minipage_labels_its_panel,
subcaption_in_a_minipage_of_a_table_is_a_subtable, subcaption_minipage_panels_in_boxes_and_continued_floats}`.

What packages add to `\caption@subtypehook` runs (fix/windows-suite). Perl defines no such macro: each
`\g@addto@macro` on it warns "\caption@subtypehook is not an expandable control sequence" and the addition never runs; on
TL 2026, whose first aid for subcaption v1.6b adds `\let\ltx@label\label` (latex2e-first-aid-for-external-files.ltx:197-201),
our undefined hook was an Error in every subcaption paper. We follow caption.sty: the binding defines it empty (its own
body, caption.sty:639-664, is the bindings' sub-float model) and entering a sub-type runs it once, in the sub-type's
group, keeping what it typesets — a `{subfigure}`/`{subtable}` (after its minipage opened), a `{subcaptiongroup}`, a
`\subcaption` or `\phantomsubcaption` in a box (subcaption.sty:251-252), not again inside a sub-type (caption.sty:325-330,
`\caption@ifsubtype`, here `\@captype` already `sub…`); `run_caption_subtype_hook` (caption_sty.rs). Not mirrored:
`\subcaptionbox` runs it once where pdflatex runs it twice (caption.sty:465-489 `\caption@iiiibox`'s `#1*` trial in a
group, then in the `\parbox`); and a second `\phantomsubcaption`, or a `\subcaption` after one, in the same group runs it
again where pdflatex does not — `\setcaptionsubtype*` sets `\@subcaptype` for the group (caption.sty:305-327), which our
gate (`\@captype`, never set by `\phantomsubcaption`) does not model (row R PHANTOM2; harmless for idempotent additions such
as the first aid's `\let`). Guards `caption_subtype_hook::{first_aid_adds_to_the_subtype_hook,
subtype_hook_runs_inside_the_sub_float, subtype_hook_runs_once_per_sub_type, subtype_hook_material_is_kept}`.

### 854. acmart makes its theorems at the end of the preamble, each only when undefined

acmart.cls:3460-3489 (TL 2025; 2510.04987's copy :3405-3430) defines `{theorem}`, `{conjecture}`, `{proposition}`,
`{lemma}`, `{corollary}` (style `acmplain`) and `{example}`, `{definition}` (`acmdefinition`) `\AtEndPreamble`, under the
`acmthm` key (default true, :86-93), each `\@ifundefined`, so an author's own `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}` keeps its
numbering and style and an author's `\newcommand{\example}` its meaning. Perl's acmart.cls.ltxml:236-243 makes them at
class load (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1086): the author's `{theorem}` kept the class's within-section counter ("Theorem 1"
twice in 2306.01662, PDF 1, 2), the author's `\theoremstyle{definition}` theorems the class's italic heads, and
2510.04987's `\example` opened a theorem in 14 table cells. Ours (78o, acmart_cls.rs) is the class's `\AtEndPreamble`
block, with `acmthm` read from the class options. Repros class-bindings/acmart_author_theorem_name_wins,
class-bindings/acmart_author_newtheorem_numbers_as_the_author_says; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch78o::{acmart_author_theorem_name_wins, acmart_author_newtheorem_numbers_as_the_author_says,
acmart_acmthm_false_makes_no_theorems}`.

### 855. tabularray's rule keys are drawn as cell borders

tabularray draws its rules apart from the cells (tabularray.sty:1957-2290 `\SetHline`/`\SetVline`, the inner keys
`hlines`/`vlines` :4011-4012 and the child keys `hline{…}`/`vline{…}`, a rowspec's `|` through
`\__tblr_parse_colrow_spec:nn`, :4003). The binding maps `tblr` to the kernel `tabular` (Perl's ar5iv stub the same,
no rules), so only a colspec's `|` and a body `\hline` showed; an all-empty table with `hlines,vlines` (the manual's
`\makeEmptyTable`, tabularray.tex:2859-2870) was pruned whole. Ours (78p, `latexml_contrib/src/tabularray_sty.rs`
`tblr_rule_keys`, `tblr_rule_borders`, `tblr_draw_rules`): each rule key is read as tabularray reads its value
(`{<index>}{<cross>}{<style>}`, `{<cross>}{<style>}`, `<style>`; `\__tblr_set_hline_aux:nn`, :2045-2055), its positions
and cross range through tabularray's child selectors (`tblr_select`: `1,Z`, `2-4`, `odd`, `-`), against the table's
shape (the body's rows and widest row, after `evaluate=`/`expand=` when given: `\lx@tblr@rules@shape`; a last
one-cell row empty but for spaces and `\par`s is no row, :3722-3731), and drawn as the table ends
(`\lx@tblr@rules` in `\lx@tblr@end`, expandable so it starts no row after a last `\\`) as the border letters the
kernel's `\hline` and `|` give: an hline above row `i` is that row's `t` (the last one the row after a final `\\`, or
the last row's `b`), a vline left of column `j` column `j-1`'s `r` (the first column 1's `l`); a second line at a place
(`index` 2) is a second letter, a double rule. A letter the template's `|` already gives is not repeated (`vlines` is
the colspec's first `|`); a body `\hline` after `hlines` is a second line, as tabularray numbers it. `text=` lines and
white ones (`hlines={white}` on coloured rows, 2308.16907) draw none; widths, dashes and colours are not rendered. The
kernel's header guess reads the borders as it does a `tabular`'s. Open: `\SetHline`/`\SetHlines`/`\SetVline`/
`\SetVlines` in the body stay no-ops. Repros alignment-bindings/{tblr_all_empty_table_keeps_its_rules,
tblr_rule_keys_become_cell_borders}; guards `perfect_kernel_batch78p::{tblr_rules_keep_an_empty_table,
tblr_rule_keys_become_cell_borders, tblr_rules_end_a_table_with_a_cmd_column}`.
