### 906. The `\maketitle` replay gate does not run what `\ifx` and its kin only compare or show; the full stop closing an IEEE author block after a grade is no part of its names, and the notes after it stay the block's (Perl: the class body is never run; IEEE grades dropped)

`body_vocabulary_is_defined` (#756) refused a class title page that tests a control sequence TeX never defines:
zaa.cls:166 `\ifx\@dedication\undefined` gave "The \maketitle body was not replayed: it uses \undefined", and the
addresses only its `\maketitle` prints (`\@addresses`, :115-127, in its `\afootnote`, :190; numbered stores K11 does not
take) were lost (1902.07328: "University of Calgary" and the MSC line "Primary 34K20, secondary 34N05", which pdflatex
prints). A token TeX reads unexpanded and never runs is now not checked (`unrun_operands`, sect05.rs): `\ifx`'s two
comparands (tex.web §507, `get_next`), e-TeX's `\ifdefined`'s one (etex.ch `if_def_code`), `\string`'s and
`\meaning`'s (§470-471, `get_token`). A parameter (`#1`) is one comparand; after `\expandafter\ifx` a
`\csname…\endcsname` first comparand's name tokens are checked as any others and the token after `\endcsname` is the
second. Any other first comparand after `\expandafter\ifx` is expanded once (§367), so nothing there is skipped
(`\expandafter\ifx\Hy@pdfversion\relax`). `\noexpand`'s operand is checked as well: in an `\edef`/`\xdef` replacement
text, its main use, the operand is stored and runs when the macro is called (`\edef\x{\noexpand\Hy@SectionAnchorHref{a}}\x`).
Both bodies are refused by the gate, which names the control sequence; 86d's first round admitted them, and the
replay's error net then discarded each body after 1 error. A `\newif` switch in a skipped place is no conditional for
the dead-branch reading (`switch_is_operand`: `\ifx\if@x\undefined` keeps its branches; not after `\expandafter\ifx`),
so the skipped positions stay the body's.
`\@ifundefined{name}` and `\ifcsname` take characters and needed nothing. Both branches of an `\ifx` are still
checked: `\ifx\@foo\undefined\else…\@foo…\fi` with `\@foo` undefined stays refused (the dead-branch reading of
`\@ifundefined` admitted apa7's man-mode title page, the #265/68u dead end). A replayed body that calls the kernel's
`\maketitle` (`\let\@origmaketitle\maketitle` … `\def\maketitle{\ifx\@institute\undefined…\fi\@origmaketitle}`, the
77i probe `relax`, replayed now) runs it with `\lx@maketitle@body` empty (`title_page_replay_tokens`), as it already ran
`\@maketitle` relaxed: that nested `\maketitle` superseded the first and handed the class's keywords store on as a
`<pubnote>` beside the deposit's "Key words: lensing" — pre-existing for any such wrapper the gate admitted
(`\def\maketitle{\@origmaketitle}` gave it on the base, 501e8ba4f1).

The full stop or semicolon closing an IEEE author block right after a grade is no part of its names: IEEEtran's binding
takes it out before the block is read (`without_stop_after_grade`, ieeetran_cls.rs; only what prints no text after it,
and only such material between it and an `\IEEEmembership{…}`: spaces, `\par`, `\\`, `\vspace{…}`, `\thanks{…}`,
`\footnote{…}` and `\IEEEcompsocitemizethanks{…}` notes). `…,\\ and Farshid Alambeigi$^{1}$
\IEEEmembership{Member, IEEE}\thanks{…}.}` (2405.17600): the lone "." left once the grade and the note are set apart
made the last line no names, so its grade was dropped (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #534); in an `\IEEEauthorblockN` the line's
authors became every author's affiliation ("Charlie Zhang, , Xianbin Wang, , Jiangchuan Liu, .", 2405.10825;
2112.14209, 2409.11755, 2510.15773). Every reading of the names after it — the line test (`names_continue`), the block's
cautious split, a grade rejoining its name (`is_name_qualifier`) — took the "." for a word, so the stop is removed once
at the binding, not taught to each test: a rule in the shared `name_count` alone kept 2405.10825's names one author (an
Error), and 1810.08035's `{\em Senior Member, IEEE}.` became a creator of its own. A stop after any other text (an
affiliation's, a grade written `{\em …}`: 1810.08035, whose last line stays every author's affiliation, as before) stays.
The notes between the grade and the end of the block keep the reading the stop gave them. Where the names carry no
marks, the stop had made the last line no names and the notes the document's `<pubnote>`s. The binding now sets them on
a line of their own after a `\\`: a line of notes alone reads as no names and yields the document's notes, as
2510.15773's own `\\`-lines did. So they stay the document's: all six of 2112.14209's (with "L. Qiao, J. Zhang, Z. Gao,
and D. Zheng are with…" and the ICCC presented-in-part note), 2409.11755's one, which covers all five authors ("H. Fukada
and N. Ishikawa are with … H. Iimori, C. Pradhan, and S. Malomsoky are with Ericsson…"; pdflatex prints it as an
unmarked page-1 footnote), and 2510.15773's four (the first had followed the grade; the other three were on `\\`-lines).
Left after the grade, they went to the last author by position alone in 86d's first round: Marco Di Renzo held
2112.14209's six, Naoki Ishikawa 2409.11755's one (the HTML put a † on his name), Chau Yuen 2510.15773's first. Charter
§4 rules that out: IEEEtran journal `\thanks` print unmarked, and nothing ties them to an owner. The stop is removed only where no note changes hands by it, decided by the shared reader's own tests of a mark, three
of them: any mark on the names (`names_any`: `author_mark_position` on the block with its notes taken out, as
`llncs_cls.rs` reads its list; it sees a `\let` alias of `\textsuperscript`, a mark in a group or an `\mbox`); a mark on
the names that reads as a label (`names_labelled`: `leads_with_mark` on the names from one of those marks, the test the
notes are read by — `$^{1}$`, `\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}`, `$^{1,*}$`, not `$^{*}$`, `$^{\dag}$`, `\textsuperscript{*}`);
and a note after the grade leading with a label (`notes_marked`: `leads_with_mark` on each, `$^{1}$…`, `\up{1}…`; a
symbol such as `$^{*}$` is a note's own mark, no affiliation's). Three branches: with neither the names nor a note
marked (`!names_any && !notes_marked`), the stop goes and the notes move to their own line (above); with a label on the
names and a note marked (`names_labelled && notes_marked`), the stop goes and the notes stay in place, read by their
marks as the base reads them with the stop; only the grade is added (2405.17600, whose first marks, `$^{*1}$`, lead with a
symbol; Sarah Go's `$^{1}$` is the label; the guard's `$^{1}$` and `\let\up\textsuperscript` variants; the 86d r2 re-review's m0-m3, m5, m9, m13, the r3 re-review's
a7, a17: the same notes and affiliations as on the base). Every other block is left exactly as the base reads it, stop
and all: marks on the names alone (`Ann Able$^{*}$,… Cat Cole,~\IEEEmembership{Fellow,~IEEE}.\thanks{$^{*}$Corresponding
author.}\thanks{Manuscript received May 1.}`, the r2 re-review's m4 and n4b; the base's notes the document's, where
without the stop both went to Cat Cole), on the notes alone, and names marked only by symbols over a note led by a
number or letter (`Ann Able$^{*}$,… Cat Cole,~\IEEEmembership{Fellow,~IEEE}.\thanks{$^{*}$Corresponding
author.}\thanks{$^{1}$All authors are with X.}`, the r3 re-review's a9, a12: read as both-marked, the correspondence
note went to Cat Cole and the numbered note became a creator with no name; a test that took a symbol for a mark on the
names and not on a note had let them through). r2's literal test of a top-level `^`/`\textsuperscript`/`\IEEEauthorrefmark` read an alias
as no mark and moved marked notes to a line of their own, so they lost their authors (the re-review's B1). Two
pre-existing residuals of the shared reader are not this binding's: a line of notes alone is not read by marks (`Cat
Cole$^{2}$` keeps a printed "2" and both marked notes become pubnotes, base alike), and a correspondence note is not tied
to a non-last author's mark (n4b without the stop: Ann Able's `$^{*}$` note goes to Cat Cole, base alike; RED
`author_ieee_correspondence_note_of_a_non_last_author`, the observer's S2c item, a reader change for its single home).
A note after a `\\` that already
follows the grade is on such a line already. `[journal,compsoc]`'s
`…Fellow,~IEEE}.\IEEEcompsocitemizethanks{\IEEEcompsocthanksitem A. Able is with X.}` keeps Cat Cole (the 86d review's
probe; it had lost her, base alike), the note the document's. Notes after a grade with no stop keep the pre-existing
reading: they go to the last author by position (`…Cat Cole,~\IEEEmembership{Fellow,~IEEE}\thanks{A. Able is with
X.}\thanks{Manuscript received May 1.}}`, both Cat Cole's). Perl does the same: on
`author_ieee_membership_after_closing_stop` it puts the `\thanks` inside Alambeigi's creator. That reading waits for a
ruling; an upper bound of 322 of the 1,801 `ieee86d` papers have a `\thanks` right after an `\IEEEmembership`.
Residual (RED `sectioning-frontmatter/author_ieee_membership_mark_before_closing_stop`, 0 of 1,801 by regex): a mark
between the grade and the stop (`…Fellow,~IEEE}$^{*}$.\thanks{…}`) is not looked past, so the last line stays every
author's affiliation.

Witnesses 1902.07328 (replayed), 2307.11186 and 2507.13469 (cms-tdr.cls:786 `\ifx\cmsMessage\undefined` passes; still
refused at :689's `\ifthenelse{\boolean{cms@pas}}{\cmsContact}{}`, a dead branch the gate does not read), 2406.18171

A/B of the final code (`86d-rel`, the gates' build of this code) against 501e8ba4f1 (`86d-base`), cached harness, 9,329 papers (pop86d2: 3,634 shipping a `.cls` that tests `\ifx…\undefined` in a title-page file, 1,800 IEEE `\IEEEmembership` papers, 544 whose `\author` closes with a stop; pop86d7: 3,351 raw-class papers): 8 changed, none worse, E 8,592 → 8,592, F 25 → 25. Better creators with their grades on 2405.17600, 2405.10825, 2112.14209, 2409.11755 and 2510.15773, their notes the document's as on the base; 2605.22853's two unmarked notes after a closing stop ("The authors are with the Neuro-X Institute…", "Manuscript received…") are the document's now, where the base gave them to the last author; 1902.07328 replayed; 2406.18171 its manuscript `\baselinestretch`. ### 908. → #805 (ijcai's `\emails` section is a class's address list, placed by spelling, else author order, else the block; cas's `\address[label]` keeps its label (Perl: the n-th piece of a comma split on the n-th author; the label dropped))

### 910. A symbol-font argument is read expanded, and a symbol its font cannot decode, declared at its fontmath.ltx or amssymb slot, is the token LaTeXML's own binding makes of the name (Perl: the name read as written, the symbols dropped)

latex.ltx reads the symbol-font name through `\csname sym#3\endcsname` (`\DeclareMathSymbol` :13480,
`\DeclareMathAccent` :13430, `\DeclareSymbolFontAlphabet@` :13725) and `\DeclareSymbolFont` builds
`\csname sym#1\endcsname` and `\csname#2/#3/#4/#5\endcsname` (:13138): each argument is expanded. Perl reads them as
written (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:2645, :2664, :2671, :2697-2699 `ToString($fontkind)`; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1201).
mathdesign declares `\DeclareSymbolFont{\MD@greek@family upright}{OML}{\MD@greek@family}{m}{n}` (mdbch.sty:157) and
its Greek in `{\MD@greek@family}`/`{\MD@greek@family upright}` (:261, :291, :330; `\MD@greek@family` is `letters`,
mathdesign.sty:135): the name found no declaration and was taken for the encoding, which has no map, so every Greek
letter came out U+FFFD or an ASCII stand-in (Ω a newline, ω `!`; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #27) — 703 tokens on
1808.08390, 1910.04228 and 1108.1913. Ours (sect08.rs): `\DeclareMathSymbol`'s font, `\DeclareMathAccent`'s font,
`\DeclareSymbolFont`'s name, family, series and shape (the encoding stays `ExpandedPartially`, as Perl) and
`\DeclareSymbolFontAlphabet`'s name are read `Expanded`, each space token a space (`nfss_name`): a space token keeps
the line end it came from as its text, so 1501.05180's `\DeclareSymbolFont{latex-font⏎msa}` was another font than its
`\DeclareMathSymbol\onto\mathrel{latex-font msa}{"10}` (U+FFFD, now ↠). A series or shape given by a macro is the one
latex.ltx selects (`\mddefault`, `\updefault`: mathtext.sty:103, euler.sty:225): an OML font declared with shape
`{\itdefault}` records `it` and is a math italic font (`math_italic`, its letters italic as their class says;
`Font::specialize_letters`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1147).
(`\DeclareSymbolFontAlphabet` looks up `fontdeclarations@`, plural, as Perl's pool:2673 does, so it finds no font
either way; left as it is.)

A math-font package that redeclares a symbol font as `U` (or `LMS`, `MDA`…) has no map for it (#645): its symbols stayed
undecoded. When the declared font decodes nothing, `\DeclareMathSymbol` now looks the symbol up in the reference slots —
every `\DeclareMathSymbol` of fontmath.ltx (254) and the small variant of its control-sequence `\DeclareMathDelimiter`s
(26, `\|` among them), and those of amsfonts.sty and amssymb.sty (219), with the encoding of the font they name
(`operators` OT1, `letters` OML, `symbols` OMS, `largesymbols` OMX, `AMSa`/`AMSb` msam/msbm). Declared at its reference
slot, the symbol is the token LaTeXML's own kernel/amssymb binding makes of the name: its glyph, and the role, meaning,
`name` and stretchiness the binding gives (a binding's `UNKNOWN`, no role at all, leaves the class's role) — so a paper
using kpfonts gets the symbols a paper without it gets (`reference_symbol`/`reference_glyph`, sect08.rs). `\Cap` is ⋒
ADDOP `double-intersection`, `\mid` ∣ VERTBAR, `\lgroup` ⟮ OPEN `stretchy="false"`, `\jmath` ȷ, `\uplus` ⊎, `\perp` ⟂,
`\setminus` ∖ — where the reference fonts' fontmap entries give a slot glyph (`|`, the OMX extensible piece ⎩, the plain
⊥ ◁ ⊔ `\`) or a Perl-origin slot error (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1202). The table `reference_math_slots.rs` is static and
generated by `tools/perfect_kernel/gen_reference_math_slots.py`: the slots from TL 2025's fontmath.ltx 2025/06/05 v3.0l
and amsfonts/amssymb 2013/01/14 v3.01 (the Computer Modern and AMS layouts, unchanged since LaTeX2e; a conversion should
not parse kernel files to look up fixed layouts), each binding's token captured by converting the generator's own
document (every name typeset, amssymb loaded) with `--nomathparse`; the header names the binary. A name no binding
defines — fontmath.ltx's `\varbigtriangleup`/`\varbigtriangledown`, whose `\mathchardef` LaTeXML keeps raw — falls back
to the reference font's map, as do `,` `.` `;` (set as text by the capture).

A package that puts a kernel or AMS name at the reference slot of its own font draws the reference glyph there:
kpfonts' `\Delta`/`\Omega` in `U/jkpmia` at 1 and 10 (fontmath.ltx:205/214 `operators`; kpfonts.sty:679-681 `\let`s
the name away before redeclaring it, so its old meaning is gone), `\leqslant`, `\Cap`/`\Cup` in an `AMSa` redeclared as
`U/jkpsya` (kpfonts.sty:498, :831/:833; amssymb.sty:101, :144/:146; txfonts and pxfonts likewise), eulerpx's `\jmath`
in `U/zeur` at 124 (eulerpx.sty:276), raw newtxsf's `\lfloor`, `\mid` and `\lgroup` in `LMS/ntxsy`/`LMX/ntxexx`
(newtxsf.sty:95/:150, :242/:261; fontmath.ltx:499 — newtxmath and newpxmath are bound and run none of this). Witnesses
1604.04618, 2008.13643 (kpfonts), 2506.22450 (newtxsf through wiley-article.cls:130), 2501.18458 (eulerpx). The
exception is arev: its bold `mathdesignA` (`mdbchbma`) draws ∟ at `\nless`'s slot 04 and lacks 0x24, 0x26 and 0x36
(pdflatex logs "Missing character"); we print what the author named (≮). Another slot is another glyph and stays
undecoded: a variant swap (`\epsilon` at "22, where fontmath.ltx has `\varepsilon`), and jkpsyb's and txsyb's
`\precapprox`/`\succapprox` at 118/119 (kpfonts.sty, txfonts.sty), where msbm has them the other way round (checked by
rendering) — so the symbol-font name alone (`AMSa`) is no slot contract, and a name no reference declares in an
`AMSa`/`AMSb` font stays undecoded too. A name no reference declares (shuffle's `\shuffle`, stmaryrd's `\boxslash`,
#645; kpfonts' `\neq` in `U/jkpsyc` at 44) stays undecoded too: U+FFFD, with its font's one Warning (#27). A font with a map decodes through it, not the binding (oz.sty's
`U/msa` `\Cap` ⋒ BINOP through `U_msa`), and at a slot its map records as a gap of the font (`U/eur`'s 17, `U/msb`'s
5, generated by tftopl; pdflatex "Missing character") a kernel or AMS name is U+FFFD with the font's Warning too
(`\star` at eur "3F, `\Cap` at `AMSb` "65; 89c, #27); the maps' other empty slots are glyphs with no single
character, which the reference still decodes (msbm's negated pairs, msam's `\dabar@`). The match is slot-matched in
the name and the slot, not the font (`\Cap` at `AMSb` "65 matches amssymb's `AMSa` "65), so the match alone cannot
see a font's gap: the gap record defeats the match at that slot. `\DeclareMathAccent`, undecoded in a declared font with no font map, takes the
binding's token by the name alone, at any slot (89c, #27: an accent's name is its meaning; newtxsf uses other slots,
and mdsymbol's `largesymbols` would — rendered; not reached while `\SetSymbolFont{…}{normal}` is unmodelled). The two
triggers differ because the evidence differs: an equal slot is layout evidence, which holds in a mapped font and is
defeated only at a recorded gap; a name at any slot is not, so the accent rule is confined to fonts with no map, where
an empty slot of a mapped font names nothing the map vouches for. Perl drops all these symbols. The
binding's limits placement (its `scriptpos`/`mathstyle` closures) is not carried: a kernel `\mathop` redeclared this
way (`\sum`, `\bigcup` at their largesymbols slots) sets its display limits as scripts, where the kernel's token sets
them under and over (repro fonts-nfss/redeclared_mathop_takes_display_limits, RED; no corpus witness, the packages use
their own `\sumop`), and carrying it needs a display capture or a role-based rule.

Repros fonts-nfss/{symbol_font_name_expands, u_font_kernel_slot_and_ams_names, font_package_symbols_are_the_bindings,
ams_font_slots_decode_as_msam_msbm_draw, kernel_name_at_another_slot_stays_undecoded}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch89a::{symbol_font_name_expands, kernel_and_ams_names_at_their_reference_slots,
font_packages_get_the_bindings_symbols, ams_font_slots_decode_as_the_fonts_draw,
kernel_name_at_another_slot_stays_undecoded}` (the first two also on the binary, eager and `--streaming`),
`perfect_kernel_batch68v::batch68v_u_symbol_font_without_a_map_stays_undecoded`.
### 911. A mark is read from the digested output — a formula's XMath, a `\ref` list, a hand-printed label — by one reader every consumer shares — absorbs #881 #913 #918 #924 #927 #937

**Rule.** Whether a formula or script in a name or an affiliation is a mark is decided from its digested XMath (as
digested and as parsed) by one reader, and the marks a name shows are its requests (ruling 1): `1,2` → 1, 2; a symbol
run glued to a label two requests; a mark of `\ref`s every key. A labelled entry goes to every name requesting its
label, and an affiliation that opens with marks is the entry they label.

**Perl.** Labels are split by `ToString` of the tokens; a hand-typed mark stays in the name (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:
694-719 superscript-marker arm). **TeX.** latex.ltx:17673-17678 `\footnotemark`/`\@xfootnotemark`, :10224 `\@fnsymbol`:
a mark is what prints as a superscript beside the name.

**Sub-rules**
- *One reader*: `observer/marks.rs:391 read_formula`, `:136 printed_children`, `:467 glued_in_a_word`, used by the
  content check, `relocate::shown_marks` and `name_text::is_name_mark` (`observer/mod.rs` module doc).
- *Labels*: `resolver/labels.rs:67 mark_labels`, `:158 glued_symbol_parts` (a label glued to a symbol parted, formerly
  #924), `:185 label_owners` (Perl's prefix chain); a label several `\and` columns answer is each column's, a compound
  symbol mark all its symbols' (formerly #927).
- *Hand marks*: a numbered entry owned by a hand-printed mark is ruling 1's; one whose lines marks lead is split at them
  (formerly #918; amended by #924: a `_share=authors` entry — llncs's one `\institute`, its number never printed,
  llncs.cls:878-883, and aa's since #932 — is requested only by the class's `\inst{n}`, never by a hand mark, so
  `Ann Able$^{1,2}$` over `\institute{{1} Univ A \\ {2} Univ B}` leaves it the block's, `resolver/post.rs:993
  answer_pending`); a mark-led affiliation is the entry it labels (formerly #937).
- *A glued script is text*: a script a letter or digit prints after in its own formula (an isotope prescript,
  `${\rm ^{3}He}$`, `${}^{87}{\rm Rb}$`) is the formula's text, not a mark, unless a name requests it or, none
  requesting, it opens its line (`events/lexer.rs:561`; 2105.07958, 1006.5052).
- *Notes inside marks*: ijcai's binding takes a `\thanks` out of its mark before the block is read
  (`defs/author_macros/ijcai.rs:441 notes_out_of_marks`, 2512.05464; formerly #881); the emitter digests each note where
  its name's run holds it, its footnote step there (`emit.rs:882 note_steps`).
- *Frontmatter clears* remove the calls before them; a publication note's e-mail calls follow #805's chain (formerly #913).

**Witnesses** 2105.07958 (`$\rm ^{3}$He Lab`), 2203.01892, 2002.12524, 2006.00536. **Guards**
`perfect_kernel_batch92a::a_mark_of_refs_requests_every_key`,
`perfect_kernel_batch92b::a_numbered_entry_owned_by_a_hand_mark_is_ruling_ones`,
`perfect_kernel_batch93a::a_label_answered_in_several_columns_is_each_columns_own`,
`perfect_kernel_batch93a::a_compound_symbol_mark_names_the_names_carrying_all`,
`perfect_kernel_batch90a::a_script_before_printed_ink_or_on_a_base_is_text`. RED:
`llncs_thanks_requested_mark_legend_read_as_affiliation_red`. **Upstream.** Not offered. Records: [the archive](../archive/OD_FRONTMATTER_RECORDS_2026-11-15.md).

### 919. Frontmatter label keys are compared by their printed text (Perl: the operand's source string, `cleanFrontmatterLabels`)

Frontmatter refactor stage 4 (FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 "Frontmatter label keys are compared by their printed text", user
ruling 2026-10-29; `archive/FRONTMATTER_DIGESTED_REFACTOR_2026-11-07.md` "Stages"; inventory row 2.8). Today's output, every family.

- **Perl.** The marks that link authors to affiliations are keyed by the operand's ToString, cleaned by
  `cleanFrontmatterLabels` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:365: `\rm` stripped, split at commas, prefixed): aa's
  `\inst{\ESO}` with `\newcommand{\ESO}{2}` requests `affiliation:\ESO`, which no entry answers (entry 2 is
  `affiliation:2`); `$^{\dag}$` and `$^{\dagger}$` are two labels. The port had grown token-level patches on the same
  reading (`FONT_SWITCH`, the 19 switches; `SPACING_IN_LABEL`; `SYMBOL_COMMAND_RUN`).
- **Now** (`queue_digest::frontmatter_label_keys`, `printed_label`): an operand that prints through a command — a
  macro, a symbol, a font switch, math — is digested in a speculative run of its own (`speculative_label_ink`: in a
  group, in a reading context of its own, assignments undone, diagnostics discarded, as sect05.rs
  `title_page_probe_run`; the field ledger put back, `FieldLedgerScope`, as the observer's rehearsal does) and
  keyed by what it prints (`label_ink`: its characters, a cross-reference as its key
  `\ref{key}`), then parted and prefixed as before; a printed run of distinct symbols (`♣♡`) is each symbol too, as
  the spelled run of symbol commands was, and so is a number or letters a symbol is glued to (`parted_printed_label`:
  `$^{\ICQD,\Phys\ast}$` prints "1,4∗", the 4 and the ∗; 2412.09857) — the printed text alone, never a spelling
  (`clean_frontmatter_labels`' ~30 spelling callers read it as before; review rev92b_r1 S2). Any spacing in the printed
  text parts two labels as a comma does: white space in a box's text and every item `util_text::is_spacing_item` reads
  as spacing, the reader 92e's `first_ink` uses (a box of white space, a box or whatsit Perl marks `isSpace`, but a
  leader: `$^{1\,2}$`'s math glue, a box of a space; `\!`'s zero-width-space box; `\:`, `\>`, `\ `, `\hspace`,
  `\kern`, `\mskip`, `\textsuperscript{1\,2}`) — but what prints no gap (`util_text::is_blank_item`: a box of no
  text, `\-`'s; a zero-width kern, the italic correction `\/`; glue of no width, stretch or shrink, `\hskip0pt`,
  `\hspace{0pt}`, which the author block's `\hspace` rewrite, `author_block::rows::normalize_hspace_separators`, no
  longer turns into a `\quad`): `\textsuperscript{1\-2}`, `1\/2` and `$^{1\hskip0pt 2}$` print the one label 12
  (review rev92b_r3 P1 and rev92b_r4 S1: read as spacing, 1 and 2, the `12` line on a nameless creator). A format character (Unicode Cf: the zero-width space, the joiners)
  is no label and no shown symbol; a combining mark (M) is part of the character before it — `\={x}`'s `x̄` (the
  accents with no precomposed form, `\=` `\~` `\v` `\u` `\H` `\b` `\d`) is one label, never `x` nor a mark of its own —
  and is dropped only with no base (`util_text::keeps_label_char`; `parted_printed_label`, `is_printed_symbol`,
  `insert::unanswered_mark_text`, the observer's `labels::parted_label`, `labels::mark_labels` and its lexer's text
  symbols, `events::lexer`: `\={\dag}`'s `†̄` and `\textcircled{\dag}`'s `†⃝` are no `†`, review rev92b_r3 B1, where
  the shadow gave both `†` lines to both names). A math accent prints its glyph on its base as that combining mark
  (`util_text::accent_combining_form`, from the glyph the accent's constructor carries, `accent`, set for an
  `OVERACCENT` or `UNDERACCENT` operator in latexml_core `transfer_common_constructor_options`: `\bar` U+0304, `\hat`
  U+0302, `\tilde` U+0303, `\dot` U+0307, `\ddot` U+0308, `\vec` U+20D7, `\check` U+030C, `\breve` U+0306, `\acute`
  U+0301, `\grave` U+0300, `\mathring` U+030A; `\underline` U+0332; a glyph with no combining form, `\overbrace`'s,
  none): `$^{\bar{\dag}}$` is `†̄`, no `$^{\dag}$`, and `$^{\hat a}$` `â`, no `a` (review rev92b_r4 S2, a regression
  against the spelling keys: both `†` lines on both names). A pgf/TikZ picture (`\lxSVG@insertpicture`)
  prints only its text nodes, the boxes its `\pgfsys@hbox` calls insert (`util_text::picture_text`): an SVG path's
  data, colours and transforms are no label, a circled `a` (`\tikz…\node[circle,draw](c){a};`) is `a`; LaTeX's
  `picture` environment is read as any material (`\put(0,0){c}`'s `c`). A label only a pgf picture's text prints may
  answer a line (a circled `a`, `\inst{\circled{1}}`'s 1) but is never shown unanswered (`queue_digest::
  frontmatter_label_request`, the creator's `_picturemarks`): the picture is dropped from the name, and its text with
  it (review rev92b_r3 S1: a TikZ ORCID icon's node text "iD" in `$^{1,\href{…}{\orcidicon}}$` and llncs
  `\inst{1\myorcid{…}}` was shown as a mark; Perl shows nothing). The rule is per request: a label the name also
  requests outside a picture (`_plainmarks`) is shown, `Ann Able$^{\circled{b}}$$^{b}$` or `\inst{\circled{b}}\inst{b}`
  in either order (review rev92b_r4 B1, where the picture's hid it). The observer's mark reader
  (`events::script_ink`) reads a script so too. Review rev92b_r2: dropping every combining mark read `x̄` as `x` (a
  wrong owner), and reading a picture as no text lost a circled letter's label. Review rev92b_r1 B1: `$^{1\,2}$`
  printed one label `1_2`, which nothing answered and `unanswered_mark_text` showed none of — each such mark lost

  `$^{1\,\textrm{\Letter}}$` their affiliation; 2601.02539 `$^{1\,2\,\bigstar}$`; 1704.04058 `$^{* \, \dagger}$`);
  `\up{\!1,2}` (2209.14855) an empty superscript holding U+200B on each name; the picture rule keeps 2605.02769's

  run errs or prints nothing, where it cannot open, and for an operand holding a note (`split_mark_notes`). Both

  A mark inside a label's own operand requests and sets nothing (`reading_label`). An unanswered mark keyed by its
  printed glyph is shown as it (`insert::unanswered_mark_text`: `\inst{1,\star}`'s ⋆, 2105.03212, which the
  spelled-name table alone had shown).
- **Residuals of the printed reading** (RED repros pending; no regression against the reading before stage 4 on any

### 920. The author setter stores, replaces or stacks as the class's own `\author` does, and what code appends to `\@author` is the block's continuation — absorbs #253 #405 #406 #922 #996

**Rule.** A binding's `\author` replaces or stacks per call as the class it stands for does (inst_support's keeps
stacking), and a block's owner is the binding whose definition is in force at the call. What is appended to `\@author`
after the setter stored it is read as the block's continuation when the title page prints it, and a later `\maketitle`
typesets the authors set after the last one.

**Perl.** inst_support's `\author` clears on every call; `\maketitle` ends with `\global\let\author\relax`
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1106-1118); appended `\@author` text is never read. **TeX.** latex.ltx:17213
`\gdef\@author{#1}` replaces; a class's own `\author` (aa.cls, llncs.cls) may stack; `\g@addto@macro\@author` after the
call extends what `\@maketitle` prints.

**Sub-rules**
- *Ownership*: the binding whose `\author` is in force owns the block (`observer/ledger.rs` `author_binding`,
  `policy_binding`); a binding's redefinition after a nested binding's owns it (formerly #922: aa).
- *A raw class's own `\author`* with a trailing argument: the locked kernel `\author` absorbs it and appends per call
  (formerly #253).
- *The tail* (formerly #405, #996): rows before the tail's first `\and` continue the last author, authors after it are
  new; read only where the title page prints the tail (`title_page_check.rs` "FX27" Info otherwise).
- *Repeat `\maketitle`* typesets the authors set since the last (formerly #406).

**Witnesses** 1412.6580, 2311.07297, 1606.03167, 2511.03250. **Guards**
`perfect_kernel_batchfx24::a_coauthor_appended_to_author_is_kept`, `…::an_author_tail_the_title_page_prints_is_read`,
`…::an_author_tail_the_title_page_does_not_print_is_not_read`, `…::an_llncs_author_tail_is_kept`. RED:
`article_author_tail_let_and_stays_a_row_red`, `authblk_author_tail_before_a_later_author_is_lost_red`,
`ptephy_author_given_twice_keeps_the_last_red` (ptephy's replacing `\author`: the first call's Univ A lost, 3 Warnings).

### 921. A frontmatter note whose class prints no label has none: an explicit empty `name=` is no label (Perl: the role's default label)

Perl's `getFrontmatterName` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:378-389) treats an empty `name=` as unset (`$name &&
scalar($name->unlist)`) and names the note by its role's default (`\lx@pubnote@<role>@name`), so every note whose class
prints it with no label read as a labelled field: a title's `\thanks{X}` "Thanks: X" (pdflatex: a "∗ X" footnote),
aa's `\dedication` "Dedication: …", a report number set at the top right "Preprint: …", IEEEtran's `\IEEEpubid`
"PubID: pubid: X" (Perl's content prefix too). FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, user rulings 2026-10-30: "keep every note with the
label the class prints, which here is none", and "we still want the 'role' of the note to be kept semantic. That can
be carried to a class in HTML which can be styled via CSS". Ours: `get_frontmatter_name` (queue_digest.rs) reads a
`name=` the call gives as the label, an empty one (`name={}`, or one digesting to nothing) as none — the per-role empty
default (`\lx@contact@orcid@name`) already meant that —, and each binding passes the label its class prints, `name={}`
for none; the role stays (`role=`, the HTML's `ltx_role_<role>`, LaTeXML-common.xsl:538), only `ltx_note_name` goes.
No label: a `\thanks` — the role's default `\lx@pubnote@thanks@name` is empty (LaTeX prints a title's `\thanks` as a
marked footnote; Perl "Thanks:~"), so the kernel's title `\thanks` (`\lx@add@pubnote@thanks`, IEEEtran's `\thanksto`
with it) and amsart's `\thanks` with no `\thanksname` (amsart.cls:836) have none, and a class that labels its thanks
sets the default (resphilosophica's "Acknowledgments", resphilosophica.cls:448); amsppt's `\thanks…\endthanks` and
`\dedicatory` (amsppt.sty:373, :504); the dedications of aa, svjour/svjour3, jheppub (jinstpub with it), JHEP, JINST, elsart, tac,
compositio, epl2, wileymsp; the report numbers of svjour, jheppub, JHEP, JINST, aastex631 `\reportnum`, atlasdoc,
appolb, jinstpub's header and REVTeX's printed `\preprint` (aps4-2.rtx:250-264, a sibling the 92e audit did not
list); the head and slug notes (aa `\headnote`, acmart `\titlenote`/`\subtitlenote`, AASTeX/aguplus `\slugcomment`,
ijcai `\pubnote`, pos.sty `\notes`); the journal lines (aa/svjour `\journalname`, before the class's "manuscript no."
suffix; acmart `\acmJournal`; emulateapj/AASTeX `\journalinfo` and aastex6 `\submitted`; apa7; arximspdf; mn2e;
aastex.cls's gobbled `\journal`/`\volume`/`\issue`); the conference lines (jheppub `\proceeding`, JHEP/JINST
`\conference`, acmart `\acmConference`); the bare DOIs (acmart `\acmDOI`, aamas `\doi`, pnas `\doi`); the volumes
(apa7, mn2e, elsart, ams `\issueinfo`, whose content "Volume 12, Number 3, …" is the class's `\volinfo`); the IDs
(IEEEtran `\IEEEpubid`, its content the ID alone, IEEEtran.cls:6153; PoS's watermark; apa7 `\copnum`); the article
types (iopart `\article`, svjour `\papertype`, elsart `\articletype`), and elsart's `\issue`. The class's own label:
acmart `\acmVolume` "Vol." (the journal formats' running foot, acmart.cls:3088), arximspdf `\volume` "Vol." and
`\issue` "No." (arximspdf.cls:366, :383). Kept as they were: aa's, atlasdoc's and arximspdf's DOI "DOI:", imsart's and
atlasdoc's "arXiv:" (the classes print them), elsarticle/elsart `\journal` and dgruyter's "Dedicated to" (the printed
reading depends on the version or the language: SYNC_STATUS, the 92e row), OmniBus's notes (no class to read). A command
that forwards its optional label as `name={#1}` (the class prints the option before the address) defaults the option
to the role's label (`\email[Default:\lx@contact@email@name]`), so a call without one reads as before and one with an
empty option has none, as the class prints it: REVTeX's `\email`, `\homepage`, `\thanks`, `\altaffiliation`
(revtex4-2.cls:2404-2421 `#1\href…`), quantumarticle's `\email`, `\homepage`, `\thanks`, `\altaffiliation`, aastex's
and emulateapj's `\homepage`, sv_support's `\thanks`, ams_support's `\address`, lmcs's `\address` (in Rust); the body
keeps its frontmatter call first, which the author block reads a class's email command by (`is_email_command`). A
class's own `\@email{}`/`\@homepage{}` call with an empty label (the class prints none) has none. AASTeX's `\keywords`
falls back to `\lx@keywords@name` when the class defines no `\keywordsname`. A label a class defines empty (`\renewcommand\abstractname{}`) now reads as printed:
none. Repros class-bindings/{kernel_title_thanks_note_has_no_label, aa_notes_read_as_aa_prints_them,
ieeetran_pubid_note_is_the_id_alone, revtex_contact_without_its_label_keeps_the_roles}; guards
`perfect_kernel_batch92g::*`; the structure goldens authors.xml and amsarticle.xml (the title's and amsart's `\thanks`,
now no `name`).

### 951. A note inside an `\inst{…}` is the note of the name it is printed on (Perl: the note's text read as a label, the note lost)

**What** (brief 98b; census mechanism D). `\lx@request@frontmatter@annotation` (defs/frontmatter_api.rs), which
llncs's, inst_support's (aa's) and sv_support's `\inst` are, parts its operand as a name's `$^{…}$` mark is parted
(`split_mark_notes`, `\lx@sup@request@affiliation`): the labels are requested from the rest, `\fnmsep` read as a
comma — the one it prints there under aa (aa.cls:807-808, an `\hbox` in `\inst`'s math); under llncs it is a pdflatex
error there (llncs.cls:894-896, its `$^,$` inside `\inst`'s `$^{…}$`; the rev98b review's pdx4), an invalid input
read the same —, and the notes — `\thanks{…}`, `\footnote{…}`, `\footnotemark[…]`, a macro making
one — run after the request, in the name, the note of the author it is printed on (aa.cls:759-760 and llncs.cls:894
set the operand in a superscript, so its `\thanks` runs there).

**Why.** FIDELITY_CHARTER §4: `\inst{1,3,\thanks{NSF … Fellow}}` lost the note (4 census papers); Perl the same
(aa.cls.ltxml:50, the whole operand the label).

**Witnesses** (int126a → 98b): aa 2303.08174 (5 notes), 2311.02521, 2601.20473 (the note, and the institute no longer
on a nameless creator); llncs 1808.09829. 2404.09857's `Kui Wu\inst{3\footnotemark[1]}` shape: the author has
institute 3 (it had been on a nameless creator), the mark a footnote mark in the name (the observer declines it: a
note in a personname is no note of the creator to the writer, `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2r5::
a_footnotemark_inside_a_mark_is_its_own`, its decline reason re-pinned).

**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch98b::thanks_inside_inst_is_the_authors_note`; repros class-bindings/
`aa_thanks_inside_inst_is_the_authors_note`, `llncs_thanks_inside_inst_is_the_authors_note` (RED → GREEN).

### 952. svjour3's text before `\at` is kept where it prints a word no author's name does (Perl: only the institute's owner label)

**What** (brief 98b; census mechanism E). sv_support_sty.rs `\lx@sv@institute@`: a labelled piece's text before
`\at` (its `fuzzy:` owner label, unchanged) is the affiliation's first line, a line break before the address, as
svjour3 prints it (svjour3.cls:506 `\def\at{\\\let\and=\iand}`, in the institute footnote) — when it prints a word
no queued author's name prints (`queued_author_name_prints`, frontmatter/queue_reading.rs: each word a word of a name,
an initial of one, or "and" between names, accents aside): "Contact author:", "Corresponding author", a fuller name
than the author line's, an institution written before `\at` (2010.12315, 2208.01887). A piece printing only its
authors' names adds nothing and stays as before, so the svjour3 writer's declines (#948) and the readings are
unchanged. Decided as `\institute` is read; with no author queued yet (`\institute` before `\author`) the text is
kept. An environment written whole there is left out (`without_environments`: 2008.12867's `{acknowledgements}`, whose
`<ltx:acknowledgements>` in a contact is malformed — its text stays lost, RED
`svjour3_institute_environment_before_at_is_lost`, pathological authoring, deferred).

**A list opened there** (2305.05902, 2306.07927, 2312.14898, 2605.09054: `\institute{\begin{itemize}\item[✉] Name \\
\email{…} \at \item[1] … \end{itemize}}`) is structure, no word of the line: an environment's `\begin{…}`/`\end{…}` prints
no word in `visible_name_text` (frontmatter/classify/name_text.rs), the text every name-shape test reads, as an item's
`\item[…]` label already printed none ("itemize" had kept a line printing only a queued name); and the list's commands
(`list_structure`, sv_support_sty.rs) are left out of the `fuzzy:` owner label (whose `\begin` opened the list in the label's digestion,
an Error). The affiliation keeps the structure explicitly: the list's `\begin` when the address closes it, with the
piece's last `\item[…]` when the address opens with no item of its own; none of its commands when the address does
not close it; and an `\end` the piece did not open (`\begin{itemize}\item A \at X \and \item B \at Y \end{itemize}`) is
dropped. A kept line's `\email` calls stay with the label, which files them (kept in the line too, they were filed
twice). A list whose items spell two or more queued names whole before its one `\at` (`queued_author_names_spelled`,
frontmatter/queue_reading.rs; 2312.14898's seven names) is a list of its authors, no one's: its owner label names no
one (`fuzzy:` empty), its `\email` calls are in the affiliation, each answered by the author it spells, and the list is
placed as an orphan (#159: shared, below the authors); the surname reading had given it the last name's alone. Names a
comma or "and" parts, outside a list, stay each their own owner (`Paulo Rezeck and Hector Azp\'urua \at …`,
2202.12391; 1404.4148, 2108.10893, 2305.05654: the rule without the list condition moved their institute to the block).
Errors int126a → 98b → 98b r2: 2305.05902 5 → 1 → 0, 2312.14898 4 → 1 → 0, 2306.07927 8 → 2 → 0, 2605.09054 14 → 1 →
0; 2305.05902's and 2312.14898's lists the block's, 2306.07927's and 2605.09054's (the later names inside the address,
after the first `\at`) the first author's, as int126a.

**Why.** FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 (3 census papers); "Duplicates the author printed stay duplicated" (§2). Perl
sv_support.sty.ltxml:45-47 keeps only the label.

**Witnesses** (int126a → 98b): 1711.01894 ("Contact author: Erwan Le Merrer" over the address), 2107.13864 (the
affiliation and address now on Xin-long Luo; the address had been on a nameless creator), 1705.01399 ("Leonardo
Anjoletto Ferreira", "Reinaldo Augusto da Costa Bianchi", "Paulo Eduardo Santos"); unchanged: 2609.05466, 1506.02396,
1908.03628, 2007.09912 (declined), 0807.2295, 2405.17600, 1201.0008 (written).

`perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2::fuzzy_labels_by_surname_and_with_their_macros` (the reading's entry "Corresponding author:

**Batch 98b's A/B** (#949-#952; `pop98b.tsv`, 843 papers: the census witnesses, every popint125a_s10k paper of

### 953. A raw class's store that only its own title-page code prints, which no frontmatter owner claims, is a note of the author block (Perl: kept by OmniBus, in another shape)

**What** (brief 98c; the unclaimed-text net, stages A1 and A2; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 "No printed frontmatter word is
lost"). At `\maketitle` the candidates are the control sequences the class's title-page code reads
(frontmatter_stores.rs `net_candidates`: `live_read_order` over the code that runs, from its refused `\maketitle`, its
`\@maketitle`, its own `\@author` and the refused `{abstract}` begin code), never a run's text, so what a class
hard-codes (a letterhead, "Received …", a copyright line) is no candidate. A candidate is a store a setter of a raw
file's or of the document's writes and no macro of the format's, the pools' or the bindings' does
(`stores_raw_code_writes`: not latex.ltx's scratch `\@tempa`, `\toks@`, which smfart.cls's title page reads, 2206.03779;
not a shorthand the document only defines, 2609.05055's `\newcommand\SL{\mathrm{SL}}`): a parameterless macro the
document made (`DefinitionOrigin::Document`; not a raw file's default, not a replayed class setter's store, not one the
begin-document hooks made, `note_document_hooks`) or a token register whose contents differ from those it had when the
raw files before it loaded (`note_raw_register_defaults`) or, for one the begin-document hooks changed, from those the
hooks left (`note_document_hooks`, after `\AtBeginDocument`'s and the `begindocument/end` hook's code, which
`\begin{document}` reads after itself, `\lx@net@document@hooks@done`: a class's `\AtBeginDocument{\setjournal{…}}`
filling its `\jtoks` is the class's text; review rev98c S2); its value holds text of its own (`holds_text`: a character
the code that runs typesets, not `\markboth`'s argument nor a font switch's robust wrapper — oasics.cls:544's
`\@titlerunning`); not blank, not a store K11 or the kernel owns (`frontmatter_owned_stores`), not one holding such a
store, not `\jobname` (the engine's), not an internal `\lx@…`. What the title page prints of them is decided by the
existing sentinel runs (`before_title_page_runs`, joined to K11's runs, which a run the net's sentinels end is made
again without them), a register given its sentinel as `\reg={…}` (`sentinel_definitions`), the refused begin codes run
after the title page in a run of their own (`net_begin_code_tokens`: in the environment, `\@currenvir` set, its `\end`
given and gobbled, read from a mouth of its own, `title_page_probe_run`, isolated) — what only they print is handed on when the
document opens the environment after that `\maketitle` (`hand_net_begin_code_stores`, from `\lx@abstract@class@setters`
after the class's begin code is replayed there), with the values it then has; never opened, or opened before
`\maketitle`, nothing printed it (review rev98c S1: pdflatex prints the title note's mark alone, or an empty footnote) —;
a begin code that reaches a raw macro with
a delimited parameter collects its body and is not run (`collects_its_body`: smfart.cls:510 `\@getgenabstext#1\end #2`,
nrc1.cls:1558; run alone they read on to the document's end, 2206.03779 and 1910.12640 timed out). Each candidate
printed and typeset by no kept deposit or replay is handed on (`hand_net_stores`; its `\label`s taken out,
`without_labels`: a label in a title-page store names nothing of ours, and inside the note it asked for an annotation
no entry answers, review rev98c S3) as
`\lx@annotate@frontmatter{ltx:creator}{ltx:note}[role=note,label=addresses:block,_net=<name>]`: the block's shared
nameless creator below the authors (#159), a sole author's own. When the frontmatter is placed (insert.rs
`keep_unclaimed_net_notes`) a note line (split at `ltx:break`/`ltx:p`) is kept only with 3 or more distinct content
words (the scorer's: letter runs of 2+ outside its stop words, digit runs of 3+, accents dropped) that neither the
document's text set so far (the frontmatter, the deposit) nor the class's own code in the store holds — the raw macros
that name the store and those its value reads, two deep (`net_class_text`: e-jc.sty:100-101's "Submitted: …; Accepted:
…" around 2410.15356's dates; smfart.cls's `\keywordsname` "Key words and phrases", set by its captions when babel
selects the language in the document, 2206.11835) —; a note left with no line goes, with a nameless creator it empties.
Each kept note raises `Warning:frontmatter:unclaimed` ("The title page prints N line(s) of \<store> that no frontmatter
field holds: kept as a note of the author block").

**The class's own `\@author`** (sect05.rs `keep_class_author_reader`): after each raw class or package loaded, its
`\@author` is kept (a state value, not a meaning: `ClassReaders::survey` reads every raw macro) when it is a reader — it
reads a raw file's, a binding's or the document's macro, or a token register — and the file's own `\author` does not
define `\@author`; the speculative run of the whole title page (`title_page_print_tokens`) prints it
(`\lx@class@author@reader`), as pdflatex does. The kernel's `\author` (Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1076-1079
`\def\@author{#2}`) or a binding's (authblk_sty.rs, under oasics.cls) replaces it, though it is the only code printing
copernicus.cls:1329-1352's `\AB@affillist`. Kept at the raw load rather than in the kernel's `\author`: under the
authblk binding the kernel's `\author` never runs (1709.00722). A later raw file's `\@author` that is no reader replaces
the kept one (review rev98c N2). A K11 off-table store printed there is K11's as before;
its author-block rows are not handed on when they only repeat the names (`repeats_creator_names`, which now reads commas
and "and" between the names as separators).

**Why.** FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 (user 2026-11-01): printed frontmatter text that no owner claims is written at the block as
a note with a counted Warning, only for lines of several unmatched words. **This restores a Rust-only loss, not a
surpass** (review rev98c B1, corrected 2026-11-01): Perl does not raw-load these classes; OmniBus keeps the text — `\titlenote` → `\lx@add@pubnote[role=note]` (OmniBus.cls.ltxml:245), so 1206.6940 keeps both title notes as
`<pubnote role="note">`, and authblk-code `\affil` (OmniBus.cls.ltxml:93) keeps the affiliation as a paragraph before

the text too is aaskaii 2606.24738 (Perl 108 lost words).

**105a: the lines below the floor** (brief 105a; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4, every loss counted). A note line with fewer
than 3 unclaimed content words was removed with no Warning. Now `keep_unclaimed_net_notes` reads each line by its
shape: a line of e-mail addresses alone (`resolver::addresses_in` and `only_addresses`, the frontmatter reader's
address-line test) is the e-mail contacts of the note's creator — the block's nameless creator or the sole author
(#159), no invented owner — each address no kept text holds, at any length, whether or not its words are used elsewhere
(a title word in the domain), with no Warning (aaskaiid.sty `\email@toks`: 2606.27706, 2607.25721; 98c's notes of
2606.24738, 2606.25049, 2606.25830 become contacts); a line whose unclaimed words are all a code's or a date's, or that
prints a code no kept text prints (`code_pieces`: digits and letters parted by dots or run together, `98.80.Cq`,
`20N05`, `H.2.4`; `code_or_date_word`/`date_word`: an English month's name, a year), or the label such a line leads
with (`leading_label`: received, accepted, revised, published, submitted before a date's word; MSC, PACS on a line
that prints a code — "Received: 2021", "MSC 2020: 05C12"; not "ICML 2021", "Room 101", "Vol. 3", "Paris 7"), is kept as
the note's line, with the note's Warning; any other line with unclaimed words goes, and its store raises one
`Warning:frontmatter:unclaimed` naming it and the words, distinct, in printed order ("The title page prints \<store>
with N word(s) no frontmatter field holds, too few to keep as a note: …"; sig-alternate-2013's `\tntoks` "corresponding
authors", 2103.14934). A line's words (`net_content_words`) are the scorer's ASCII runs and, beyond them, any script's
letter runs (`Москва`) and each Han ideograph or kana as a word of its own (`unspaced_script`), so a Chinese line clears
the floor (2206.01007's `\address` "北京师范大学天文系，100875，北京", 2601.14329's `\institude` "1)北京航空航天大学
物理学院，北京"); a store whose only letters are non-ASCII active characters (`[T2A]{fontenc}`'s Cyrillic, through
t2aenc.dfu's `\DeclareUnicodeCharacter`) holds text (`frontmatter_stores.rs` `holds_text`), and the class's own text in a store (`net_class_text`) is read by the same character test (`prints_a_character`), a run of active bytes read as the UTF-8 character its macros print (CJKutf8 reads a class file one active token per byte, `作` = `ä½\u{9c}`) and a byte outside a UTF-8 sequence as its own Latin-1 character (`[latin1]{inputenc}`'s `é`), so a class label set in CJK, Cyrillic or Latin-1 (`\gdef\@xa{作者单位：#1}`, `Université de Genève: #1`) is the class's text, not an unclaimed note or a false Warning (review rev105a2 finding 1, rev105a3 finding 2; repros `net_class_label_in_cjk_is_class_text`, `net_class_label_in_latin1_is_class_text`). The class's words are taken from a line as a multiset — each occurrence accounts for one, each setter body read once (a `\let`/`\futurelet` copy such as `\@ifnextchar`'s `\@let@token` is the same code) — so a label's `单位` does not take the document's own `单位甲` with it (rev105a3 finding 1). An `ltx:ERROR`'s text, at
any depth in the line, is no printed word (`text_without_errors`: an undefined `\songti`'s name inside
physics_report.sty's `{\songti\zihao{-4}#2}`, 2601.14329). The floor of 3 stands for prose, and the code keeps the
shaped lines below the charter's tentative floor, pending the user's ruling on FIDELITY_CHARTER §4's floor. **Known
gap:** class-default placeholders are not net candidates, pending the placeholder ruling (2302.11911, 1509.08973;

`net_class_default_placeholder_is_counted_red`); a date in another language's months is counted and not kept (`mars

**106s: the title-page check** (brief 106s; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4 as amended 2026-11-04, every residual loss counted by
a Warning). The net counts only what it hands on; a loss on any other path — a store it cannot name, code it does not
walk, a binding's reader, a dropped deposit or replay — was silent. Now a check, which writes no content and changes no
XML, compares the title page's printed words with the whole output. **The print:** at each `\maketitle` the kernel's
deposit (`\lx@deposit@maketitle`, after `before_title_page_runs`) runs the whole title page once more as pdflatex runs
it (sect05.rs `note_title_page_print`: `title_page_print_tokens`, the class's refused `\maketitle` when replayable,
else `\@maketitle` — a raw file's, a binding's, or LaTeX's printing `\@title`, `\@author`, `\@date`, then `\@thanks` as
article.cls's `\maketitle` does, `\lx@print@thanks`), with `\today` empty (the conversion's date is no document word)
and `\thanks` latex.ltx's (`LATEX_THANKS`: a mark, its text appended to `\@thanks`) unless a raw file defined its own
(kept, or the `\lx@dropped@thanks` the lock left): a note prints, set apart, only where `\@thanks` runs, and nowhere
when the class never runs it (review rev106s B1, probe p3: drcls's unflushed `\thanks{Draft}`, which r1 counted),
inside a `FieldLedgerScope` (a `\usebox` box the fields hand back stays unstamped; without it the box became an `ltx:text` of
its own, `perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2r9`). Its text is read by `ink_word_text` (util_text.rs): a space for a whatsit
that prints nothing, spacing (a phantom's ink, `is_spacing_item`) and a script (`\textsuperscript`, a math script: a
mark); a seam (`INK_SEAM`) at a printing whatsit's and each of its arguments' edges and around each alignment cell (an
accent built as an alignment runs on: combelow's `Babe\cb{s}` is "babes", 2007.07526, which r1 parted to "babe"); no
quantity argument and no environment's required argument (`settings_arguments`: `{CJK}`'s `{UTF8}{gbsn}`); a mark
(`INK_INSERT`) before an `\insert`'s material. A column break ends the words before it: LaTeX's stand-in for
article.cls's `\@maketitle` (TL 2025 article.cls:236-251) runs `\@author` inside `\begin{tabular}[t]{c}…\end{tabular}`
as article.cls:246-248 does, with `\and` as the document has it — the kernel's (`\and`, Perl
latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1071 `DefConstructorI('\and', undef, " and ")`) and its `\let` copies a whatsit printing
nothing, a space, as latex.ltx's `\end{tabular}\hskip 1em \@plus.17fil\begin{tabular}[t]{c}` ends a column in print; a
class's or document's printing a word (`\def\and{\unskip\ und\ \ignorespaces}`) prints it; a document's copy of
latex.ltx's column break closes and reopens the stand-in's tabular, so every column after it, `\@date` and the `\thanks`
texts stay in the print (1409.7028, 2103.04211: the base's words exactly). Until FX25 the stand-in let `\and` to
`\relax`, which leaves nothing: `Inst X\and Bob` read "xbob", and a loss beside it was one unknown word, an Info
`class_text`, uncounted (RR1 gap 24, 2511.15315); FX25 ran `\@author` outside the tabular, and the copy's
`\begin{tabular}` was never closed (FX25b). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfx25::{the_check_print_ends_words_at_a_kernel_and,
the_check_print_keeps_a_class_and_word, a_loss_beside_an_appended_and_is_held_or_counted,
the_check_print_keeps_columns_after_a_document_column_and}`. The print of the latest `\maketitle` before the authors are sealed is
the one checked (a later one supersedes, #406; a supplement's after the seal is none, `frontmatter_entry_sealed`).
**The check** (`Tag ltx:document after_close_late`; base_utilities/frontmatter/title_page_check.rs
`check_title_page_words`): each content word of the print (`net_content_words`, the scorer's) is looked for in the
output — every text node and attribute value of the document (not `_…`), stretches of up to 6 pieces across element
edges joined (`Bob <text>Bak</text>and`), under `--streaming` each spilled subtree's words (`note_spilled_words`, the
spill observer, into a per-conversion thread-local set of distinct words, `SpilledWords`, reset by
`reset_title_page_check`, nothing pinned in the arena; once a title page printed, only the words it wants — review
rev106s B2: r1 copied all the words so far into the arena per spilled subtree, and an 8,000-section `--streaming
--max-memory=1400` document ran out at 1,206 MB, where int133a peaks at 386 MB and r2 at 389 MB; 1605.02624's pass-1
RSS 289 MB on both); a seamed run counts its pieces when the output holds one of them or the whole is no word of the
source; a run the print opens or ends with against no space may run on into the document's text ("SHOWNBody.");
words the net already named are not counted again (`note_net_counted`). A word the output lacks is the document's
when its own source writes it (`source_words` over the files read as content, `binding::content::CONTENT_FILES`, and
the files of the document's own directory read as definitions, `binding::content::raw_read_paths` — a style the author
wrote, probe p7_sty —, their definitions' replacement texts out, `Definer`; UTF-8, else Latin-1, 0802.2579 —
comments, `filecontents` bodies, `\begin`/`\end` names and the keys and options of `keyed_arguments` out
(`\documentclass[draft]`, `\usepackage[…]`, `\label`, `\ref`/`\cref` and kin, `\cite` and kin, file and counter names,
`\hyphenation`: probe p4, au.cls 1205.1106), a control word nothing and the spaces after it skipped and, in a second
reading, a space, an accent nothing, `\o`-style text symbols their letters): named, distinct and in printed order, in one `Warning:frontmatter:unclaimed` ("The title
page prints N word(s) of the document's that its output does not hold: …"). Any other is the class's own text — a
label, a placeholder at its default, a running head's —, tallied in an Info (`frontmatter:class_text`), not a Warning,
pending the placeholder ruling. **Coverage** (the 56 dev20k + 42 long-tail lost-words papers of int133a): before 1
names all its lost words in a Warning (2103.14934; 2410.15356 warns without naming them), 97 silent; after 24 (22
all, 2 some: 15 of the 56 dev, 9 of the 42 long tail — raa 1304.5354, ab 1508.04926, 1511.07638, ametsoc 2004.13105,
2408.12585, amsart 2007.07526, homework 2304.08300, JUSTC 2409.17603, memsait astro-ph0102098, astro-ph9909366,
astro-ph0005436, icrc29 astro-ph0507347, mem 0805.4214, 1311.4988, tADR2e 2312.02510, chjaa astro-ph0609644,
astro-ph0612749, article 2008.02713, 2401.04073, 2404.07719, and three the census tags the scorer's whose output
glues the word — 2504.21411, 2510.12317, hep-th0606194), 74 silent: 19 the scorer's artefacts, 15 with no print run,
40 whose words the print does not reach (or the output holds elsewhere). **False alarms:** none found — on a 500-paper control from `popint125a_s10k` 10 papers gain the
Warning, each a real loss read against pdflatex (or the source where pdflatex fails): cpc-hepnp's `\email` (9:
1504.05444, 1505.01270, 1609.08464, 2010.04386, 1709.02056, 1806.07548, 0912.1248, and by its source 1309.0234,
1906.10531), mnras's `\date` the binding replaces with `\pubyear{\date{year}}` (2506.15059). **Silent still** (the
print does not reach the words): no deposit runs — a binding's own `\maketitle` (daj 1510.08733, 2112.09352,

`\g@addto@macro\document{\maketitle}`, 2302.11911, 2508.08363, 2607.18758, …: our `\document` is no macro, the
append fails — counted since 107d, below: its print noted at `\begin{document}`'s end, repro sectioning-frontmatter/`check_title_page_from_begin_document_is_counted`); the replay does not reach the class's
title-page code (opendatalab's `\let\oldmaketitle\maketitle` copying the locked kernel's, 2601.09733; cccconf's
`\keywords`/`\section`, 1702.07637); a binding's fields outside `\@author` (quantumarticle `\ead`, 2209.07123; IEEEtran
grades, 1511.03982 — both counted by 106t's second source, below); the scorer's artefacts (census132 §3). **Known edge:** a class's literal word equal to a word the
document writes is counted as the document's (77i's "OPEN", which `\svc{open}` writes): the check reads the print's
text, not where each printed letter came from. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch106s::{
a_class_store_the_net_misses_is_counted, a_note_prints_only_where_the_class_flushes_it,
the_documents_own_files_write_its_words, a_binding_losing_author_lines_is_counted,
a_title_page_whose_words_are_kept_counts_nothing, a_word_a_spilled_subtree_holds_is_no_loss}`; repros

(RED int133a → GREEN 106s), `check_unflushed_thanks_prints_nothing`, `check_document_style_words_are_counted` (RED

**106t: the second source — what TeX makes of what the document gave its frontmatter commands** (brief 106t; review
rev106s open question 1; main-session rule (A) of r1's report: digest, never read tokens). The print is read only where
the kernel's deposit runs: a class binding that writes its own frontmatter (daj, elsarticle, aastex, revtex, IEEEtran)
has no print run, and a binding's command may drop what pdflatex prints. **The calls:** while the document's own text
is read (`Mouth::is_document_text`, a content file's mouth; the setter watch's flag set only then,
`origin::watch_document_calls` / `note_document_mouth`, cleared when the frontmatter is first sealed), each call of a
LaTeXML macro (kernel or binding origin) whose arguments are read from that text keeps them, each with whether its
parameter is optional and whether the macro's token body names it, `#n` (`Expandable::watched_call`,
`state::note_document_call`, `DocumentArgument::used`; a closure's arguments count as handed on). When the frontmatter API
queues an entry inside such calls (`queue_front_matter`, `\lx@add@frontmatter@until`:
`title_page_check::note_frontmatter_entry`), they are the document's frontmatter commands; the entries made inside one
call are one record group (`claim_open_document_calls`). **What is wanted, all of it digested** (TeX settles letters
across commands, environment arguments, nested optionals, conditional branches, glue keywords, mark arguments — each a
false alarm of r1's token reading, 42 guards): (1) the entry's own digested content, read by `ink_word_text` as the
print is, when the API digests it (`begin_frontmatter_entry_digestion` / `end_frontmatter_entry_digestion`, matched by
the queued invocation's content; no extra run); (2) the arguments no entry digests (`never_digested`): a required one
a binding's frontmatter command's body never names (quantumarticle's `\ead[]{}` → `\email{#1}` drops the address,
KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1208, 2209.07123), and an optional one an internal command (a name with `@`) reads from the
document's text (`\begin{abstract}[Summary]` → `\lx@begin@abstract[]`, #1209, elsarticle 2104.14704; amsart's
`[R\'esum\'e]`, 1006.5288's shape); (3) the required arguments a binding-made macro (`DefinitionOrigin::is_binding_made`:
binding, fallback, stub, borrowed — never the kernel's selectors) drops while the document's entry digests
(`origin::watch_dropped_arguments`, `state::note_dropped_argument`), when the document wrote them (`writes`: a contiguous
run of the record's arguments — xkeyval's `\@nil`-delimited plumbing under a raw `\ead[label=e1,mark]` is none; digested,
it looped to a Timeout Fatal, 2101.10506): IEEEtran's `\lx@IEEE@membership@drop` over a grade it could not place
(1511.03982; deleted by P5a, the grade the reading's, OD #1016), jmlr's `\titletag[1]{}` over the title's `\thanks` (2211.07413). (2) and (3) are digested once each,
speculatively, when the entry is digested (sect05.rs `speculative_word_run`: `speculative_run_read` in a mouth of its own, read
by `ink_word_text`, a `\thanks` set apart; its state rolled back with the journal it opens, so it leaves no trace).
**Only a binding's drop counts** (106t r3): a kernel macro's drop is TeX's own — the format's `\@firstoftwo{T}{F}`, which
ifthen's `\ifthenelse` ends in, reads both branches from the document's text around its `\title` and abstract and drops
the one not taken, as pdflatex does (2202.08832; r3's first census build counted the untaken branch's "physics") —
so both drop readers take a non-binding macro's required arguments as accounted for (an internal command's optional
argument is read whatever its origin, which keeps the kernel Pool's `\lx@begin@abstract[Summary]`, 2104.14704, counted) (`DocumentArgument::used`,
`DefinitionOrigin::is_binding_made`). **A binding's declared drop** (main-session ruling (b), 106t r2: a binding's by-design drop of an argument that sees the
document's frontmatter text counts as a loss unless the binding declares it; every loss counted, failing toward
flagging): the binding names the arguments on its own definition, `DefMacro!(…, drops => [n, …])`
(`ExpandableOptions::drops` → `Expandable::dropped_by_design`, a bit per `#n`; the expansion unchanged), and both drop
readers take a declared argument as accounted for (`DocumentArgument::used`). Declared only where the real package or
class prints nothing of the argument, or prints it as page furniture (FIDELITY_CHARTER §2), each checked against the
real file: hyperref's `\texorpdfstring` #2 (the PDF bookmark's string; 2306.06741's `{Lg}`, 2306.06006), dmtcs's
`\publicationdetails` #5 (a link target only), lipics's `\volumeinfo` #1, #2, #4-#6 (the copyright line's editors and
pages, 1507.03682's `\copyrightline`), lmcs's `\lmcsheading` #1-#4, #7 (#1 unused, the rest the first page's head:

midl's `\orcid` #1 (a linked logo, midl.cls:106), cas's `\corref` #1 (a key), icml's `\comment` (icml2018.sty:709

`\emailauthor`/`\urlauthor` #2 and `\orcidauthor` (the name's initials and surname beside each address,
2511.11770's ceurart.cls:665-757). **Not wanted:** of a command the document writes (no `@`) its optional
arguments (`\author[a]`, `\email[show]`, `\title[short]`); a command that queues nothing (aas_support's gobbled
`\shortauthors`); `ltx:toctitle`; a record group whose leading entry the API removes (`\lx@clear@frontmatter`,

want are counted once; the source gate, the net's words and the class-text Info are the print's; the Warning says which
source it read ("The document's frontmatter commands were given N word(s) …"). The source reading skips the spaces
after an accent (`Universit{\" a}t`, 2406.18504). **Coverage** (the 98 lost-words papers): 24 → 28 (26 all, 2 some):
2209.07123, 2104.14704, 1511.03982, 2211.07413. **Silent still**, by rule (A) — r1's token reading named them: a raw
class's or `.sty`'s macro that stores what its own title page prints, with no print run (no `\maketitle`: imsart copies
2101.10506, 2203.00070 under `{frontmatter}`; no kept run: docclass_edit 1107.2462 — the print's reach, 106s); a word one
command's argument and the text after it make (aa's `\email jose.cernicharo@…`, an undelimited argument: 2110.09105);
daj's thanks (1510.08733, 2112.09352: the binding keeps the kernel's replacing `\author` where tocbase.cls:644-660
accumulates, a content fix); europhys `\Pacs` (cond-mat9610136, cond-mat9812194, cond-mat9906132), cpcHACK 0706.0578;

(revtex4 107, revtex4-1 77, IEEEtran 74, acmart 45, llncs 26, elsarticle 26, …) and 500 random. A/B (`pop106t.tsv`, 1,097
converted; vs int135e-rel, both on the int135e dumps): the XML byte-identical in every one, E 1,969 = 1,969, F 4 = 4,
Warnings +4 (the 4 above). **Cost** (`instructions:u`, int135e-rel vs 106t r2, 20 bound-class papers): +0.19 % (median −0.05 %, at most +1.80 %, 2507.07700).
**Memory:** a document call's arguments are kept once (`state::CallArguments`, an `Rc<[DocumentArgument]>`), shared by
every entry made inside it — r2 copied them per entry, quadratic in the entries one call makes (rev106t: 3,000 names
