**107d: the print where the class prints its title page from a trigger of its own** (brief 107d; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4,
every residual loss counted). The print was noted only at our `\maketitle`'s deposit; a class that prints its title page
without one had no print, and only the second source was read. A kernel primitive, `\lx@note@title@page` (sect05.rs),
notes the print (`note_title_page_print`: nothing typeset, no deposit, no net) when no print was noted yet
(`title_page_check::title_page_noted`: a later `\maketitle` supersedes it, as a second one does; one before it keeps its
own print, whose fields ours empties), at the trigger the class prints from: (1) a binding's — elsarticle's
`\end{frontmatter}` (elsarticle.cls:1303 `\newenvironment{frontmatter}{}{\maketitle}`; the core's empty primitive, Perl
PR #2767), let to it in elsarticle_cls.rs: 2312.03765's `\subjclass`, `\gdef\@title{\@oldtitle\footnotetext{…}}`, a
title footnote no setter sees; (2) a raw class's — a `\g@addto@macro{\document}{…}` holding `\maketitle` (or a `\let` copy, by meaning: GA5), which our
constructor `\document` refuses as Perl does (the `Warning:unexpected:\document` kept), is recorded
(`lx_title_page_at_begin_document`) and the print noted at the end of `\begin{document}`, after `begindocument/end`,
where latex.ltx runs appended code (sect02.rs; cup-journal.cls:1014: 2207.13252 — the `\alsoaffiliation`, the e-mail,
the DOI and the dates —, 2603.00371, 2302.11911, 2508.08363, 2607.18758). A class whose title page never prints (no
`\maketitle`, no trigger) stays unchecked: the print is never noted at the frontmatter's placement. **The source gate**
(`document_source_words`), which the new prints reach on raw journal styles over the binding (medima.sty's journal
header and its `\printFirstPageNotes` "URL:", 2507.07920, 2201.10981, 2409.09188, false Warnings on the first A/B):
a content file is the document's only when its own directory holds it (a package's `\input` of a TeX Live file —
translations' `translations-basic-dictionary-english.trsl`, "Contents" — is none), and a `.bbl` is read with its
definitions out (`\providecommand{\URLprefix}{URL: }` is its BibTeX style's; its entries stay the document's). **Not this
mechanism** (the print's reach or a content loss, each one paper of dev3; SYNC row 107d): an `\ead` a raw elsarticle
copy writes to the `.aux` (`\immediate\write\@auxout{\string\emailauthor…}`), printed only on pdflatex's second run
(nj_style 1401.7920); a class title page gated on a counter its refused `\author` advances (CUP-JNL-DTM's `\aucount`,
2305.00867); a raw copy of a bound class whose store only its own `\@author@finish` prints (aeb_emulateapj_2010's
`\alt@affil@toks`: the copy's redefinition, :460-468, emits `\affiliation{\the\alt@affil@toks}` and calls revtex's
— under the revtex4-1 binding neither runs, 1011.2770); a style printing its title block from `{abstract}`
(bosonai_techreport.sty, 2605.02209); a class's `\ifthenelse{\authorslen > 1}` over xstring's `\StrLen`
(naverlabseurope, 2408.05088); a grade a document macro hands IEEEtran's drop (`\SeMieee` → `\IEEEmembership`,
2503.14354, not `writes`); and 2310.07393's "Space Robotics" and "Campus", whose first letters (`S`, `C`) our empty `\@listi` lets a
class's `\xdef{… \let\@listi\@listI Campus}` take (two Errors, "pace Robotics" and "ampus"; no net word claimed
and unwritten) — not a Perl parity gap: Perl defines no `\@listi`, ours is a Rust-only stand-in
(`latex_constructs_rust_only.rs:515-524`); TeX's `size10.clo:63` body decides it (rev107d N3). With no
`SOURCEDIRECTORY` (literal or stdin input) every content file reads as the document's, as before (N4). **RED
residuals (rev107d, synthetic only):** a trigger notes a print where `\maketitle` never runs — `\let\maketitle\relax`,
an appended `\if@notitle\else\maketitle\fi` — a false Warning
(`check_title_page_relaxed_maketitle_no_false_warning_red`; S1); a title page `\input` from a sibling directory
reads as a package's (S2: by origin, a TeX installation tree's file is a package's, would fix it). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch107d::{elsarticle_frontmatter_end_notes_the_title_page,
a_maketitle_inside_frontmatter_keeps_its_print, a_title_page_appended_to_document_is_counted,
no_title_page_printed_is_unchecked, package_and_bibtex_text_is_not_the_documents}`; repros sectioning-frontmatter/`check_elsarticle_frontmatter_end_prints_the_title_page`,
`check_title_page_from_begin_document_is_counted` (RED int139a1 → GREEN), `check_elsarticle_maketitle_inside_frontmatter_keeps_its_print`,
`check_no_title_page_printed_is_unchecked` (negative), `check_package_and_bibtex_text_is_not_the_documents` (RED int139a1 → GREEN). dev3's lost-words-counted line (the 21 lost-words papers' logs):
5 all / 0 some / 16 silent → 7 / 1 / 13. A/B: `pop107d.tsv` (3,562: the 10 witnesses, the 2,982 dev3/dev20k papers with `\author`/`\title` and no `\maketitle`, 47 more with `\altaffiltext`, 23 with the net's "kept as a note", 500 random of `popint125a_s10k`; holdout excluded) vs int139a1-rel, both on the int138a dumps: 3,552 converted, the XML byte-identical in every one, E 1,346 = 1,346, F 8 = 8, words equal; Warnings +7, one each, every one a real loss read against the PDF (cup-journal 2207.13252, 2302.11911, 2410.19985, 2508.08363, 2603.00371, 2607.18758; elsarticle 2312.03765); 7 class-text Infos more (elsarticle + medima/jasr journal headers: 2006.08179, 2007.15546, 2201.10981, 2403.04024, 2407.18673, 2409.09188, 2507.07920); no check line of the base changed.

**108b: the third source — what the document's text gives a raw class's setters** (brief 108b; FIDELITY_CHARTER §4; root
cause `agent_reports/2026-11-06_lostwords139c_report.md`). The check's print reads less than pdflatex prints when a raw
setter's store sits behind a gate the rehearsal cannot pass: CUP-JNL-DTM's `\auaddress` (printed under a count only the
class's refused `\author` advances, 2305.00867), aeb_emulateapj's `\alt@affil@toks` (read only by a raw
`\@author@finish` the revtex binding never runs, 1011.2770), a replay the gate refuses (naverlabseurope 2408.05088,
bosonai 2605.02209, sect05.rs "not replayed"), nj_style's `\ead` (only `\immediate\write\@auxout`, 1401.7920). **The
source:** `Expandable::watched_call`, while `origin::store_call_watch` (the current mouth the document's, from the
conversion's start to the title page; off from then on, so a macro call in the body pays nothing, and a macro without
parameters is never asked), keeps the arguments of a setter made in a raw class or a raw definitions file of the
document's own directory, loaded as a package or class (a `filecontents` one too), that it writes into a store
(`Expandable::stored_parameters`, once per definition: `#n` in the value of `WRITERS_OF_NAMES` — `\def` and kin, `\let`,
`\g@addto@macro`, `\@namedef`, etoolbox's; the net's `stores_raw_code_writes` keeps its eight kernel ones,
`KERNEL_WRITERS_OF_NAMES`, so its output does not change — and `\renewcommand`, `\newcommand`, `\providecommand`, of a token
register's assignment, or of a `\write` to a named stream). `\expandafter` is never a store's name. A scratch name
(`SCRATCH_NAMES`, one list: `\@tempa`, `\reserved@a`-`f`, `\toks@`, `\@temptokena` and kin) is no store, as a reader
neither, but what it holds hands on to what it is written into, as a name written earlier in the body does
(`\toks@{#1}\xdef\x{\the\toks@}`, `\gdef\@t{#1}\expandafter\g@addto@macro\expandafter\x\expandafter{\@t}`: SCIS2026.cls's
`\@authoremail`). A definition records no source file (its `locator` is a stub: Expandable.pm's is unported), so
`load_tex_definitions` says whether the file it reads is such a file (`origin::note_reading_own_file`, read by
`Expandable::new` as `made_in_own_file`); a binding's load says no, whichever file requires it (xkeyval_sty.rs under
acmcopyright.sty: `\XKV@s@tkeys` was a setter, 2105.13838). **Not covered:** a setter a file `\input` defines
(`\input{defs}`, `\input{sub/defs}`, `\input{x.sty}`, `\input{x.def}`) and a call from a macro `\AtBeginDocument` runs
(RED catalog `check_raw_setter_input_own_file`); `\usepackage{sub/x}`, `filecontents`, a `.clo` through a class and a call
from `\input{front}` are. The arguments may come back through `\@ifnextchar`, so `reading_document_text` is no test here;
a class's own literal is stopped by the source gate. A later call supersedes the earlier when each write of the setter
replaces a known store and none reads a store written before it (`state::note_store_call`, `StoredParameters::replaces`:
`\def\x{#1}`; acm's `\global\conf={#1}\global\confinfo{#2}`, 1612.06202); an appending one's stay (`\g@addto@macro`,
`\xdef\x{\x #1}`, a `\write`, a temporary then an append), and a `\csname` store's, as its next call's name may be
another's. Not read: a shorthand maker's `\gdef#1{#2}`, a replay's or a deposit's calls. **What the bounds drop is said in
an Info:** past the first 512 calls, `frontmatter:store_calls_dropped` (their number and first setters); an argument no run
could read, `frontmatter:unread_argument` (its setter, size and first tokens; a 16,384-word one aborts).
**A document end in an argument:** `\closing{\end{document}}`, digested by the source's run, ended the real document, the
body lost with no diagnostic. A speculative digestion (`gullet::speculative_digestion`: `speculative_run_read`, the observer's
rehearsal, `speculative_label_ink`) leaves `\end{document}`, `\enddocument`, `\@@end`, `\bye` inert: `gullet::flush` does
nothing, and `\end` and the kernel's end half (`\lx@end@open@frontmatter`, `\lx@enddocument@hooks`,
`\lx@finalize@document`) stop at once. 106t's dropped-argument run shares the path, and base lost the body there too
(`\ead{\end{document}}` under quantumarticle, `\begin{abstract}[\end{document}]`: E=3, E=1, now E=0 with the body); a
document end the real digestion reaches (`\title{\end{document}}`) still ends the document, as in pdflatex.
**Digested** once, at the first of `\lx@deposit@maketitle`, `\lx@note@title@page`, a binding's `\maketitle`'s
`\lx@frontmatterhere` (`title_page_check::digest_raw_setter_calls`, `speculative_word_run`); no title page, or the authors
sealed: none. **What it counts:** the words then go through `unclaimed_words` and the source gate; a word only this
source wants is named apart, `Warning:frontmatter:unclaimed_store` ("stored by a raw class's command, which pdflatex may
not print"), and a word `unclaimed` or the net names is not counted again. **The false-alarm rule** (the brief's control
measure): with no narrowing, 13 of 499 controls (26 per 1,000) and 26 of 498 raw-class papers (52 per 1,000) warned;
read against pdflatex's text, 6 of the 13 named no word it prints, the rest mostly journal furniture. So a store counts
only when code reads it: `StoreReaders` (taken at the title page, before a `\maketitle` nulls its own code; the macros
of the raw class, own files and the document, the refused `\lx@dropped@…` records among them) walks up from the store to
a macro nothing reads that is no page furniture (`\ps@…`, `\@oddhead` and kin, `\markboth`; a writer's name, what is
written into furniture, and the first required argument of `\includegraphics`, `\epsfig`, `\href` are no reads). A store read by none or by furniture alone (`\jvol`, `\issn`, `\pagerange`,
`\issuedate`, `\journal`: 2512.10209, 1202.2064, 1312.3323, 1001.4350), a `\csname` store (no name to find a reader by), an
optional or bracketed argument (a key far more often than text: `\cortext[cor1]{…}`, 1005.1545, 1603.09660), and digits
from an argument that yields no counted word (a volume, a page, 2305.00867's ORCID pieces; a postal code printed with its
address counts: 1011.2770, 2305.00867, 2605.02209) go to an Info, `frontmatter:unread_store`. A store read only by page
furniture that pdflatex does print stays there (a first page's foot, RED catalog
`check_store_read_only_in_first_page_foot`: on 42 real Info papers the words checked were running furniture, one a date
line, 1406.6413).
A `\write` reads as read: its reader is the next run. Known undercount: a body `\newcommand` ignored under a kernel
definition has no record, so its stores read as unread (`\@maketitle` of cjpsuppl.cls:199, hep-ph0402063: an Info, and
SYNC row "108b `\newcommand`", now `perfect_kernel/SILENT_LOSS_INVENTORY.md`). **B (`writes`):** a binding's dropped argument is the document's text also when a macro
of the document's the arguments name holds it, read to 3 levels and 4,096 tokens: `\SeMieee` →
`\IEEEmembership{, Senior Member,~IEEE}` (2503.14354; the drop is Perl's, IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:143, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#534). **C (`\@listi`):** `latex_constructs_rust_only.rs` defined `\@listi`-`\@listvi` empty; a class's non-robust
`\normalsize` ending `\let\@listi\@listI` (size10.clo:53), expanded in a `\protected@xdef` (authblk's `\affil{\normalsize
Campus…}`), then left `\let` to take the next letter as its name: "Missing control sequence", the letter lost
(esapub2005 2310.07393: 2 Errors, "ampus", "pace"). They carry size10.clo:216-249's bodies now, the one XML change here;
Perl leaves them undefined, which stay in the expansion. The reach is any empty kernel macro a class writes after
`\let`/`\def` under an expansion: the other `def_macro_noop`s (`latex_constructs_rust_only.rs`) are no such name. Not in
the dump. **Measured:** A/B `pop108b2.tsv` (2,530 converted of 2,536, 6 with no main file: 19 witnesses, 1,117 raw-class papers of
dev3, 1,394 others; vs int139c): XML byte-identical but 2310.07393, E 1,612 → 1,610 (its 2), F 7 = 7, 31 changed, none
worse. `unclaimed_store`: raw-class 16 of 1,117 (14.3 per 1,000), of which 10 name no word pdflatex prints in the whole PDF
(9.0 per 1,000: 1809.03618, 2602.02974 `\papertype{please specify}` and 2609.38689 `\category` of vgtc's review cover page,
2208.07491 `\CCScatlist`, 1801.08694 `\communicated`, 2311.07658 `\pubvolume{xx}`, 2405.13244 KOMA's
`\RedeclareSectionCommands`, 2609.10714 `\Month`, 2609.39493 `\journal`, 1007.4268 `\conferenceinfo`); 6 print (CMS's
`\cmsNoteHeader` ×4, 1607.06975, 1701.02022, 2008.04422, 2505.20483; rmaa's `\SetConfTitle`, 2312.07699, astro-ph0211252).
Others 8 of 1,394 (5.7 per 1,000), 5 false (3.6 per 1,000: 1101.1174 `\journalcode`, 1401.8205 copernicus dates under a
flag, 1612.06804 `\dates`, 1904.08978 a template's placeholders, hep-ph0402063 an own acronym style's expansions), 0706.1324
and 1704.04814 printed, 0804.4883 unread (no PDF on TL 2025). Scratch names and the binding rule took out `\subject{secondary}`
(1803.03153), `\newtheorem*` (1912.10847), `\setcopyright` (2105.13838), 2505.24263; of the 12 false of the review's 619
raw-class papers, 9 stay: stores read under a switch, by design below. `\@namedef` and the etoolbox writers add no Warning
(a `\csname` store goes to the Info; 1,381 dev3 papers use `\@namedef`, mostly theorem makers). **Cost** (`instructions:u`,
int139c-rel vs 108b2): CMS +3.17 to +3.88 % (200-400 M): all in `check_title_page_words`' whole-document scan, which an
unheld word starts; the third source's run itself pays nothing measurable (1607.06975: candidate 6,470 M, with the check
off 6,266 M, with the digestion off 6,264 M, one build apart, base 6,205-6,278 M). A witness +0.83 %; others −0.05 to
+0.08 %. No one-line cap: the scan is what tells a lost word from a held one. **Still counted only, not
kept:** Perl keeps the words on 2305.00867, 1011.2770, 2605.02209 and the repro of A (SYNC row "108b content", now `perfect_kernel/SILENT_LOSS_INVENTORY.md`). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batch108b::{a_store_the_print_gates_out_is_counted, a_store_of_a_refused_replay_is_counted,
each_writer_of_a_store_counts_and_a_replaced_call_does_not, a_tex_live_packages_setter_or_no_title_page_wants_nothing,
a_bindings_drop_inside_a_documents_macro_is_counted, list_parameter_macros_keep_the_letter_after_them,
a_document_end_in_a_stored_argument_ends_nothing, a_replacing_guess_keeps_each_call_of_an_appender,
a_csname_store_keeps_each_call_in_the_info, an_optional_argument_stored_reaches_the_info,
digits_count_with_a_counted_word_of_their_argument, the_bounds_of_the_third_source_say_what_they_dropped}`; repros
sectioning-frontmatter/`check_raw_setter_store_gated`, `check_raw_setter_replay_refused`,
`check_store_replaced_and_siblings`, `check_binding_drops_document_macro_expansion_red` (now `ieee_membership_grade_in_a_document_macro_is_kept`, P5a),
`list_parameters_macro_in_an_expansion_keeps_the_next_letter` (RED int139c → GREEN 108b),
`check_raw_setter_end_document_in_store`, `check_store_replacing_guess_drops_an_appender`,
`check_store_csname_counter_keeps_each_call`, `check_store_optional_argument_printed`,
`check_store_digits_with_an_address`, `check_store_caps_say_what_they_dropped` (RED 108b → GREEN 108b2),
`check_raw_tex_live_package_setter_unwanted`, `check_raw_setter_no_title_page_unwanted` (negative). **Known false alarm,
by design:** a store code reads under a switch that is off, or in a macro nothing calls, reads as read: the check does not
run that code, and the tag says so. Guards updated for it, their XML asserts unchanged, each now naming the Warning:

**R1: what the check costs** (briefs R1, R1r2; `docs/performance/PERFORMANCE.md` "the pk/P1 levers"). The third source digests
each stored argument even when the title page's print digests it too: uantwerpenexam-example2's `\extrainfo`, stored by a raw setter
and printed by the class's `\maketitle`, was digested three times, 47 % of the conversion. Why the third source exists stands: a
store the print's run does not reach (a gate only the class's refused `\author` opens, 2305.00867; a raw `\@author@finish` the
binding never runs, 1011.2770; a replay the gate refuses, 2408.05088, 2605.02209), or a store only written out (1401.7920). It runs
before the print, as it did. **Settled, one line:** skipping an argument the print seems to hold loses a word uncounted, so nothing
is skipped. R1's `print_holds` (the run expanded the store, the print holds three quarters of the words the argument spells, no
`\thanks` spelled) is removed: `\noted{Noteword one\grant}` with `\newcommand\grant{\thanks{Thanksword}}`, in a class that flushes
`\@thanks` at the end of the document, prints Thanksword in pdflatex and in neither XML, and every word the argument spells is
printed, because a spelling can't tell what a macro prints. It fired on 19 small arguments in 10 of 278 raw-class papers and gave
-0.03 to -0.26 % on 2111.15203 and five third-source witnesses, -0.9 % on 1306.4853, with the watch's gain in both.
**A budget:** no run of the check's reads more than 8,000,000 tokens, and a conversion's at most three times that
(`check_run_budget`, `LATEXML_CHECK_READ_BUDGET`, 0 for none). Reads cost about 450 instructions each, so a run costs a second at
most, and the worst a document can ask of the check about 11 G. Over budget (`gullet::read_budget`, an error nothing logs or latches)
the run is abandoned and rolled back like a failed one, and the document close says what was left out once, in a counted
`Warning:frontmatter:check_budget` naming the setter's argument and its size, or the title page. The arguments run first, so ones
that spend all the conversion's reads leave the print no run, and that is named too ("after 0 tokens read"). The run counts as having
read what it read; its failed reads, its conditionals (`set_if_count`) and an inner context's reset of the count leave no mark, so the
token limit, the conditional limit, the cycle guard and `full_read_at` read as they did; the sentinel runs have no budget.
**Data:** on 299 converted papers with a raw class of their own (seed 7), a print reads 1,185 tokens at the median, 285,224 at the
99th percentile and 487,915 at most (2402.13052); an argument 3,348 at most; all a conversion's runs 1,826,755 at most (1306.4853,
587 runs). The budget stops none of them, and none of the 1,873 of `popZ01`; of the 50 TeX Live manuals of the performance
study it leaves circuitikzmanual's title page, a drawing of 4,480,660 reads, unstopped. **It stops** uantwerpenexam-example2 (164 M
reads a run: each `\selectlanguage` reads the class's language data file again, `uantwerpenexam.cls:84,:99-104`): its print and its
`\extrainfo` both stop at the budget, so a title page's words go unchecked there and the Warning names both. That is all of the
regression's fix.
**A trace it found:** a run stopped inside a `\scantokens` left its own mouth open, as `reading_from_mouth`'s error path closed
mouths until one of its own source's *name*, and both were "Anonymous String", and the next close took the document's text, all of
the body, silently. It closes by depth now, counting the mouth in reading with the stack (`mouth_depth`: `open_mouth` pushes nothing
when none is in reading). A sweep of every fifth budget from 1 to 90,000, past the runs' whole length of 83,504 reads, over the hostile repro (18,000 conversions, `kit/check_budget_sweep.sh`) gives the XML of no budget, no Error. Guards `perfect_kernel_batchr1::{a_thanks_behind_a_macro_in_a_stored_argument_is_counted,
what_a_run_left_out_over_budget_is_named, a_spent_budget_names_the_print_it_never_ran,
a_run_over_budget_counts_no_conditional_against_the_limit, a_looping_stored_argument_is_budgeted, a_run_over_budget_leaves_no_trace}`,
units `gullet::token_limit_tests::{a_read_budget_ends_at_its_read_and_counts_what_was_read,
a_failed_context_closes_its_own_mouths_by_depth, a_failed_context_leaves_as_many_mouths_as_it_found}`; repros
sectioning-frontmatter/`check_store_thanks_by_alias_is_counted`, `check_store_over_budget_is_named`,
`check_budget_run_leaves_no_trace`, `check_store_argument_loop_is_budgeted` (RED 108b → GREEN R1). **The watch:**
`Expandable::may_be_watched` asks inline whether the document-call and store-call watches can see a call (a macro with parameters
LaTeXML or a raw class's own file made), so a package's macro no longer takes the cold path; what they record is unchanged. What they
still cost, against no watch: 0.2 % (Scrabble-doc-fr) to 1.0 % (jwjournal-demo-en) on documents with no `\maketitle` to end them, the
calls they record.

**FX27: the check's two severities, by evidence** (the user's ruling of 2026-11-11; FX27b inverts the default). A lost
word stays a Warning, "The title page prints …", unless the title page in force positively does not print it. A lost
word only text a document appended to `\@author` after the author setter stored it prints, under a title page that
positively does not print that tail, is an Info, `frontmatter:annotated`, "The title page annotates N word(s) that its
output does not hold: …": the author may mean it hidden, so no damage can be claimed, and the word is still named.
The title-page reading's run (TP1, below) marks the part a document appended to `\@author` in its print; where the
title page in force positively does not print it, the words outside that part are the print without it, and a lost word
only that part prints, which the frontmatter commands' text does not name either, is the Info's. The other lost words
keep the Warning, also where one loss has words of both. Positively not printed (`TitlePageReading::tail_printed`):
- A title page of the file's or the document's own that does not reach `\@author`: the run's own print (TP1: a
  document's `\@maketitle` runs as written, so it prints no tail at all — authblk or article under a document's
  title-only `\@maketitle`, no Info and no Warning, as pdflatex prints none), else the walk
  (`own_title_page_prints_author`).
- With no such page, or where article.cls's stand-in ran in it (the kernel's marker), the binding owning `\author`
  declares that the document class's page prints its own author list (`TitlePageDecl::author` `AuthorPage::Own`,
  `ledger::author_tail_declared`): ams_support.sty for amsart, amsproc, amsbook (`\authors`, amsart.cls:460-476, :638,
  :815-817); elsart_support_core.sty for elsarticle (`\elsauthors`, elsarticle.cls:247-288, :805, :848); acmart.cls
  (`\addresses`, acmart.cls:1619-1643, :2240, :2631). Keyed to the document class (the first of the class's bindings),
  not the binding alone: OmniBus's autoload of ams_support.sty, old elsart.cls's elsart_support_core.sty and a class
  over amsart (gen-m-l) are not declared.
- The document class is OmniBus, the fallback's guess for an unknown class (`OmniBus:fallback`), whose real page is
  unknown.

Every other title page counts as printing the tail, so a lost word there stays a Warning: LaTeX's `\author` in force
(the kernel's, a raw file's, the document's); an own title page reaching `\@author` (its tail is then read, TP1); a
binding declaring that its page prints the tail (`AuthorPage::Block`: authblk, llncs); any binding declaring no page of
its own, a binding added later included (IEEEtran, mnras, revtex4-1: pdflatex prints the tail, revFX27's probes; FX27
had made each an Info); and wherever the run ran no stand-in (a raw file's `\@maketitle`, a replayed refused
`\maketitle`, titling's binding `\@maketitle` over amsart or elsarticle, titling.sty:166-180), whose print is its own
evidence (TP1 reads the tail there: titling over amsart and elsarticle, `{amsart,elsarticle}_titling_author_tail_printed_is_kept`,
no Warning). FX26/FX26b's declaration that dropped the tail from the print is parked, its mechanism not merged (revFX26,
revFX26b: it silenced counted losses). Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfx24::{an_amsart_author_append_invents_no_creator,
an_author_tail_the_title_page_does_not_print_is_not_read, an_author_tail_printed_but_not_read_is_counted}`.

**TP1: one title-page reading.** What the class's whole title page prints at `\maketitle` is read once
(`latex_constructs::title_page_reading`, a `TitlePageReading`): one speculative run with the document's own values
(`title_page_print_tokens`, the check's thanks and `\today`), under the check's read budget (`checks_run`), read for its
words (`ink_word_text`) and its text (`ink_text`), and kept while the state is unchanged (`watch_state`, TP1b below,
and the LaTeXML-internal values it reads). The check, the stores'
confirming check (`confirmed_printed`, before: two more unbudgeted runs) and the author tail (`author_tail_calls`, before:
a walk of its own) read it. The run defines `\@author` with marks that print nothing (`\lx@title@page@author`,
`\lx@title@page@tail`, `\lx@title@page@tail@end`, read where they stand by their definitions: sect05.rs `title_page_mark`), notes the `\and`
family's meanings where `\@author` first prints (recorded for the separator query, TP2), and whether article.cls's
stand-in ran. Its source: a replayed refused `\maketitle`, a `\@maketitle` of a raw file's, a binding's or the
document's own, or the stand-in. **The stand-in stands at a marker:** the kernel's `\@maketitle` holds
`\lx@kernel@maketitle` (empty outside the run), where the run puts article.cls's page (TL 2025 article.cls:236-251), so a
document's or a raw file's addition to LaTeX's `\@maketitle` (`\g@addto@macro`) or a `\let` copy of it runs as written
around it, and a document's own `\@maketitle` runs as written — before, the stand-in replaced every `\@maketitle` not of
File or Binding origin (TP0's probe p2: a document's title-only page printed the authors). The sentinel runs build on
the same `title_page_print_tokens`. Binding declarations: `Policy::title_page` (`TitlePageDecl`: `author`
Kernel/Block/Own, absorbing FX24b's `author_tail` and FX27b's `own_author_page`; `title_and`, the classes whose page sets
its own `\and`, aa.cls:866 and svjour3.cls:608, recorded for TP2). Perl reads no title page
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1099-1113). Guard `perfect_kernel_batchfx24::an_author_tail_the_title_page_prints_is_read`.

**TP1b: a `\@maketitle` of the document's or a file's own is the page in force only where the `\maketitle` that runs
runs `\@maketitle`.** That is a replayed refused `\maketitle` (it reaches `\@maketitle` or not as written), else the
document class's, as a binding the class loaded declares it (`TitlePageDecl::maketitle_runs`, read by
`ledger::class_maketitle_runs` for the first of the class's bindings; sect05.rs `own_maketitle`; `MaketitleRuns`):
always — amsart, amsproc, amsbook (ams_support.sty; amsart.cls:600-610, amsproc.cls:576-586, amsbook.cls:1334-1337;
amsart's `titlepage` acts inside its `\@maketitle`, :647), IEEEtran.cls (:4753-4775), mnras (mn2e_support.sty;
mnras.cls:1055-1062); never — elsarticle (elsart_support_core.sty; elsarticle.cls:918-989, `\elsarticleprelims
\pprintMaketitle` and its journal variants) and acmart.cls (:2226-2379); **without a title page only (TP1c, review
revTP1b)** — article, report and book (the kernel's declaration, `WithoutTitlepage`), and extsizes' extarticle,
extreport and extbook (review revTP1c; extarticle.cls:196-281, extreport.cls:198-283, extbook.cls:191-276, defaults
extarticle.cls:28 false, extreport.cls:28 and extbook.cls:12 true): article.cls:169-219,
report.cls:175-225 and book.cls:181-231 define `\maketitle` by their `\if@titlepage`, the `titlepage` form printing its
own page with `\@author` and running no `\@maketitle`. The value is the class's `\if@titlepage` after its options, as
the class reads it to define `\maketitle` (article.cls:50-51 false, report.cls and book.cls:50-51 true; `titlepage` and
`notitlepage` set it), kept per class by `declare_fnsymbol_title_block` (`class_titlepage_key`), not read at
`\maketitle`: a document's later `\@titlepagetrue` changes no `\maketitle` (pdflatex: article still runs a title-only
`\@maketitle`). The bindings declare `\if@titlepage` before their options and let the options set it (Perl's options are
no-ops, its report and book set it false). TP1b left report and book undeclared, which was not "as before TP1": under
`notitlepage` the stand-in printed an appended tail pdflatex does not print (report invented "Bob B"), and article under
`titlepage` ran a document's title-only `\@maketitle` and lost the printed "Bob B" silently. With no class binding (a raw
class) it is taken to run it; under a class no declaration names (REVTeX, whose `\maketitle` is `\frontmatter@maketitle`,
revtex4-2.cls:3130-3134; OmniBus's guess) a document's `\@maketitle` is not taken for its page and a raw file's is, as
before TP1. Where it is not the page in force, the run stands
article.cls's page in and the binding's declaration answers (`AuthorPage`), and the walk (`own_title_page_prints_author`)
does not start from it: under elsarticle or acmart a document `\def\@maketitle{…\@author…}` with
`\g@addto@macro\@author{\and Bob B}` makes no creator Bob B (TP1 made one, review revTP1 B1; pdflatex prints no Bob),
the lost "bob" an Info; one printing the title alone leaves the check reading the stand-in's words, not the title alone
(the mirror of TP0's p2). The reading's key is honest (review revTP1 S1): the reading begins a watch on the state (`watch_state`, a
number never begun before) that every write ends — an assignment, a write in place (the mode, a mapping, a box's `\wd`,
a font's parameter), a group's end that restores values (`pop_frame`) — and a rollback puts back the watch its journal
began with (no ABA); a write tests one flag, a journal's or a watch's (`WRITES_WATCHED`; RK1: a count drawn at every
write cost +841 instructions per `\loop` iteration, study PF160); the LaTeXML-internal values the reading reads,
which the watch leaves out, are in its key (`lx_author_handed`, `lx_author_seen`,
`lx_depositing_class_maketitle`, `lx_class_author_reader`). LaTeX's own `\@maketitle`, its marker and the run's marks are
read by definition identity (sect05.rs `is_latex_maketitle`, `maketitle_is_kernels`, `title_page_mark`), not by name.
**Decision (review revTP1 S2):** over the check's read budget the reading has no text, and the stores' confirming check
keeps the sentinel runs' answer unconfirmed — no unbudgeted run (before TP1 two ran, which the budget exists to bound).
That answer errs toward "printed": a store the page may print stays carried, so no source word the PDF may print is
dropped; what goes unchecked is named by the `check_budget` Warning (repro
`check_store_confirm_over_budget_keeps_the_sentinel_answer`: the XML the unbudgeted one's). The confirming text is the
reading's, whose run empties `\today` and routes LaTeX's `\thanks` through `\@thanks` (before: `\thanks` printed in
place, no inject): a date or a note's text is no store value it confirms. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchfx24::{an_author_tail_the_title_page_does_not_print_is_not_read,
an_author_tail_the_title_page_prints_is_read}` (elsarticle, acmart, the title-only sibling; IEEEtran; TP1c: report
under `notitlepage`, article after a document's `\@titlepagetrue`; article under `titlepage` with and without a document
title-only `\@maketitle`, report's and book's default; extarticle, extreport and extbook under `notitlepage`, extreport's
default),
`perfect_kernel_batchr1::a_run_over_budget_leaves_no_trace`, `00_unit_state::a_state_watch_ends_with_every_change_of_the_state`,
`title_page_reading::tests::a_kept_reading_goes_with_what_it_read`.

**TP3: one builder and one budget for every title-page run.** The stores' sentinel probes — the whole page's letters and
digits runs, the deposit's and the replay's (`sentinel_runs`), the refused begin codes' (isolated), the labels'
(`verify_title_page_labels`), the `\and` numbering's (`note_and_numbering`) and the unset nulls' (`decide_unset_nulls`)
— are made by the reading's builder (`checks_run`, sect05.rs `title_page_probe_run`) under the check's read budget,
which they share with the reading and the per-argument runs; before, they ran unbudgeted (`speculative_title_page_run`,
`speculative_isolated_run`, deleted). Over budget a probe falls back as a run that cannot be made does (the code walk,
`walked_title_page_reads`; no label kept from an argument, no numbering recorded, `\relax` kept for an unset store), and
the `check_budget` Warning names it ("a sentinel run of the class's title page"). The probes keep their own runs: they
substitute values, which the one real-values run cannot (TP0), and a merged run would give one probe's sentinels to
another's stores, which a page testing a value prints differently; the labels' and the displaced stores' runs
(`\lx@store@defaults`) precede the hand-on, the whole page's (`\lx@deposit@maketitle`) follows it. A/B TP3base → TP3
(stage2's 1,434, 400 papers shipping a `.cls` that reads `\@maketitle`, 100 controls; 1,929 converted): XML byte-identical,
Warnings and `frontmatter:` log lines unchanged; 397 raw-class title pages read 2.77 M at most of the conversion's 24 M
(2407.17431, revTP3), the probes now inside `FieldLedgerScope` (`checks_run`: the field ledger put back after each, as the
check's own runs). The trade shows on a synthetic page over a budget of 100 reads
(`check_store_over_budget_is_named`): the walk hands on no `\@corr` from the class's `\thanks`, and the e-mail is lost,
counted (the unbudgeted probes kept it). **QA60 site 2 is kept:** under a class no declaration names
(`class_maketitle_runs` None) the run's tail answer stands, not the walk's, which reads both branches of a test it cannot
evaluate (`evaluated_switch` reads `\if` and `\ifx`) and would invent a creator the PDF does not print (repro
`omnibus_value_tested_maketitle_author_tail_makes_no_creator`: a trial build with the walk first made Bob B). Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchr1::a_run_over_budget_leaves_no_trace` (the Warning names the probes),
`perfect_kernel_batchfx24::an_author_tail_the_title_page_does_not_print_is_not_read` (the OmniBus row).

### 954. A contact holding two or more marked entries is cut at its marks in the frontmatter API, and a legend, a URL or a grade among them is what it is — absorbs #945 #961 #969

**Rule.** The API's Cut step cuts a printed list of contact entries at its marks, one queued contact per entry, for
every binding; an entry whose whole text is a legend is its carriers' note, a URL the block's link, a membership grade
its carriers' grade, and an entry a creator holds twice is held once.

**Perl.** One contact, the marks printed in it; an affiliation per call (`\lx@add@affiliation`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:
645). **TeX.** The marks print as superscripts before each entry; a legend (`$^*$ Equal contribution`) prints as a
footnote-like line, not an institution.

**Sub-rules**
- *Cut*: `defs/frontmatter_api/cut.rs:34 cut_marked_contact`, `:122 place_uncut_copies`, `:66 mark_shown_attr`;
  `defs/frontmatter_api.rs:84 cut_list`.
- *Kind*: `insert.rs:547 kind_legend_contacts` (formerly #961), `:941 kind_link_and_grade_contacts` (formerly #969);
  `resolver/labels.rs:546 is_legend_text`.
- *Reaching the author*: a block entry is cut by its whole span, llncs's one institute cut at its marks stays every
  author's, svproc's `\institute` is sv_support's (formerly #945).

**Witnesses** 2312.02779, 2506.18881, 2009.04283, 2103.04797 (975 authors), 1901.01540 (AASTeX, 1,204 authors).
**Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch106b::a_contact_held_twice_keeps_the_first`,
`perfect_kernel_batch107e::a_legend_after_a_wrapped_run_is_its_carriers_notes`,
`perfect_kernel_batch103c::a_legend_whose_label_prints_no_mark_stays_an_affiliation`,
`perfect_kernel_batch100a::a_deceased_legend_is_a_note_of_its_carriers`. RED:
`cut_acmart_uncut_call_after_a_cut_list_red`, `llncs_institute_macro_marks_tabular_rows_red`.
**Upstream.** Offerable. Records: [the archive](../archive/OD_FRONTMATTER_RECORDS_2026-11-15.md).

### 955. → #767 (A raw class's affiliation or address that its own title page prints into the body is the creators' contact: a setter that stores it among code of its own, by what its call recorded; a setter that prints it with no line break of its own, where its call stands as a line (Perl: the shipped class is not read; OmniBus's setters feed the API))

### 956. → #805 (An e-mail address printed inside an affiliation-kind entry is the entry's e-mail in both engines: its lines and notes of addresses are kinded once at the API, and one Link chain places every e-mail of an entry (Perl: the address stays in the affiliation's text, copied onto every carrier; an `\email` inside an entry one contact on its label's owners; a note in an `\affiliation` a document `<pubnote>`))

### 957. → KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1206 (A line of notes only after an author block's `\\` is the line above's, its notes the names' (Perl: a line of its own, read as an affiliation by the mark inside its first note, its notes the document's))

### 958. → #980 (A boxed author block's re-part writes the e-mails the reading spells out of its rows, and a `\resizebox`'s sizes print no name (Perl: one creator holding the whole `tabular`))

### 959. authblk's `\affil` is locked: a document's or raw class's own `\affil` is refused and replayed, the affiliations stay the binding's (Perl: the redefinition replaces the binding's, its affiliations lost with 6-8 Errors)

**Perl behavior**: authblk.sty.ltxml:57 defines `\affil` unlocked, so a later `\renewcommand\affil` replaces it. The
JOSS template copies authblk's own `\affil` code (paper_joss.tex:162-182, a `\renewcommand{\affil}[2][]` that differs
from authblk.sty:148-167 only in typography); it `\xdef`s `\AB@authors`, `\AB@las`, `\AB@au@str`, which Perl's binding
never defines (authblk.sty.ltxml:22-61): 6-8 Errors, and every affiliation lost. **Rust before**: the binding defines
those names (authblk_sty.rs, run 340), so the copy ran clean and put every affiliation in `\AB@authors`, which only
authblk.sty:168-171's `\@author` prints and the binding replaces: the creators kept no affiliation, with 0 Errors and
0 Warnings (2504.08081, 2310.11002, 2107.08407, 2507.13341, 2604.08855; dev lost-words census mechanism A). The raw
classes that copy it after `\RequirePackage{authblk}` — oasics.cls:610, eurocg25.cls, dagman.cls:696 — did the same,
their `\@author` layout of `\AB@affillist` left to the unclaimed-text net (#953) as a note of the author block with a
`Warning:frontmatter:unclaimed` (1709.00722, 2503.02336; 1701.09007 calls no `\affil`). lipics-v2016.cls:611's copy
is read as its binding's stand-in copy (`copy_provides_refuses_locked`, state.rs), which declines a locked name without
a record, so it is not replayed (1603.00928 unchanged).

**Rust behavior**: `\affil` is `locked => true` (robust, as authblk.sty:148's `\newcommand` is; the inner `\affil␣` gets
`:locked@files`, dialect.rs). A redefinition that takes arguments is refused at every origin, the document's too
(state.rs `install_definition`: only a parameterless value definition becomes the meaning, #500); a `\let\affil…`
still goes through, as Perl's `Let` checks no lock (2208.01579's `\let\affil\MEETaddress` unchanged). The refused body
is kept as `\lx@dropped@affil` and run first by the binding's `\affil` through the kernel's replay
(`\lx@replay@class@setter{affil}{label}{text}`, #482): its output discarded, the frontmatter frozen, its stores and
flags kept (`\def\affil#1{\gdef\lastaff{#1}}`'s `\lastaff`, which the document prints), the accumulators it fills
(`\AB@authors`, `\AB@affillist`) its records, taken out of a class title page's deposit. A binding that loads
authblk and defines its own `\affil` loads unlocked and keeps it (lni_cls.rs, which also re-runs authblk's
`\affil`), and so does a raw file a binding reads with `InputDefinitions` (unlocked, as Perl's `loadLTXML`). The page
prints the same text through either definition (the copy's meaning is authblk's), so keeping the binding's meaning is
the faithful reading of what pdflatex prints. A definition that is NOT a copy is refused the same way (D1, OD #500): its
text becomes the binding's affiliation wherever pdflatex prints it — a `\thanks` footnote or a class's own
`\@affiliations` block (base lost the first and left the second unattached), a small italic paragraph after
`\maketitle` (review rev102a p2: base kept it there; now a contact, its font gone), and a `\def` that prints nothing
under the name (the guard `a_refused_affil_still_runs_for_its_stores` pins that contact, beyond TeX). A wrapper round
the binding's `\affil` through a `\let` alias loses its typography (RED repro
`authblk_affil_copy/wrapper_keeps_its_font`; no wrapper in the 30k census's 1,215 authblk papers). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch102a::{a_documents_copy_of_authblk_affil_keeps_the_bindings_affiliations,
a_raw_class_copy_of_authblk_affil_keeps_the_bindings_affiliations, a_refused_affil_still_runs_for_its_stores}`; repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/authblk_affil_copy/`. **Not reached**: an `\email` built from the same code under a new name
(ACL/NAACL: 2406.11632, 1904.03969; RED repro `authblk_email_from_affil_code`, SYNC_STATUS row 102a).

### 960. An ORCID link in an author's name that prints no word is the author's ORCID contact, its icon no part of the name (Perl: the link and its picture stay in the personname)

**Perl behavior**: hyperref's `\href` inside `\author{…}` is digested as the name's text, so the `\orcidicon` template's
`\newcommand{\orcidA}{\href{https://orcid.org/…}{\orcidicon}}` (a TikZ "iD" badge) after a name puts
`<ref href="https://orcid.org/…"><picture>…</picture></ref>` inside `<personname>`. **Rust before**: the same (census129
cluster 5 (O): 2507.12319 and 2406.08258 revtex4-2, 2503.04867 IEEEtran; 9 dev20k papers).

**Rust behavior**: while an author's content is digested (`\lx@author@withinst`, which the kernel's `\lx@add@author`
wraps every name in) `\href` is `\lx@author@href` (frontmatter_fields.rs; a defined `\href` only, saved once so a nested
author restores the document's). A link whose address, expanded as hyperref expands it, is an orcid.org record
(`orcid_id`: `https://orcid.org/\orcidauthorA` — the template's `\xdef` runs before the iD's macro is defined) and whose
ink prints no letter or digit outside a picture (`ink_prints_text`, queue_digest.rs: plain characters as written,
anything else digested in a speculative run as a label's operand is, the text nodes of a pgf/TikZ picture not counted;
a box, a graphic, a rule) is `\lx@add@orcid{<iD>}`, the kernel's ORCID contact (`<contact role="orcid"><ref
class="ltx_orcid" …>` with the logo), and its ink is dropped. Kept as before: an ink printing a letter or a digit,
printed text — the linked name (`\href{https://orcid.org/…}{T.J.C. Bezerra}`, 2606.03745; 2301.02927, 2312.16289,
2601.06085), the iD printed as its digits (`\href{https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097}{0000-0002-1825-0097}`, with or
without an `X` checksum, review rev103b S1), a plain `iD` —,
`\href`'s options, a link in a note or contact digested inside the name (`creator_name_in_progress`: `\thanks{See
\href{https://orcid.org/…}{his record}.}`), and a link inside a mark (`reading_label`, math: `\inst{1,\href{…}{iD}}`,
`$^{1,\href{…}{\orcidicon}}$`), where a contact made was lost — that mark still shows its text without the link, as
before. orcidlink's `\orcidlink` in a name keeps its `ltx_orcid` link in the personname (Perl the same). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batch103b::an_orcid_link_in_a_name_is_the_authors_orcid`; updated
`perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2r9::the_rehearsal_leaves_the_conversion_unchanged` (its `\usebox` icons in names are now ORCID
contacts; the switch on and off still byte-identical); repro sectioning-frontmatter/`author_orcid_href_icon_is_the_orcid`
(RED → GREEN).

An icon link glued after the marks and notes that follow a name's comma is that name's, as the marks are
(`marks_before_glued_commas` moves it before the comma with them, `leading_orcid_icon_end`, separators.rs): `\href` to
an orcid.org record printing no letter or digit as its tokens read, `\orcidlink{…}`, `\orcidID{…}`, or a macro whose
body is one such link (`\orcidAT`, `\orcidicon{0000-…}`, `\orcidA{}`). `Ashley Hai Tung Tan,$^{1}$\thanks{…}\orcidAT⏎
Christian Wolf,$^{1,2}$\orcidChrisW⏎…` (mnras, 2605.03577) split after the comma gave each author the next one's iD
(review rev103b B1). Not when the names open with their icons (`\orcidA~Ann Able,$^{1}$\orcidB~Bob Baker`: each the name
after it, as 2603.26792's `\href{…}{icon}~{Name}`). Open (review rev103b2, synthetic, RED repros): an icon glued to the
comma with no mark before it (`Ann Able,\orcidA{} Bob Baker,\orcidB{} Carl Cole\orcidC{}`) is the previous name's in the
print, set against its comma, but stays in the next name's piece and becomes that name's ORCID (Bob holds Ann's iD, Carl
both B's and C's; int130a misplaces it as ink alike) —
sectioning-frontmatter/`author_orcid_after_bare_comma_is_the_names`; and the leading-icon test reads the first name
only, so a later name's own leading icon in a list whose first name opens with none (`Ann Able,$^{1}$\orcidB~Bob
Baker,$^{2}$`) moves to the name before (Ann holds Bob's iD; int130a kept it as ink in Bob's name, round 1 Bob's
contact) — `author_orcid_leading_a_later_name_is_its_own`; an icon followed by a tie or glued to the next name is that
name's, per icon. A creator holding one iD twice keeps its first contact of it (`drop_repeated_orcids`, insert.rs:
acmart's `\orcid{X}` beside the name's `\orcidicon{X}` link, 2501.02380, review rev103b S2; Perl keeps a repeated
`\orcid` twice, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:659-660); two iDs are two contacts. Guards (`perfect_kernel_batch103b`)
`an_orcid_icon_after_a_names_comma_is_its_own`, `an_orcid_link_printing_text_stays_printed`,
`a_repeated_orcid_is_one_contact`; repros sectioning-frontmatter/`author_orcid_icon_after_comma_marks_is_the_names`,
`author_orcid_href_printing_text_stays`, class-bindings/`mnras_orcid_icon_after_comma_marks_is_the_names`,
`acmart_orcid_and_its_icon_link_one_contact` (RED → GREEN).

A comma closing an ORCID icon link's printed text is the name list's separator (int131fix): `C. J.~Law$^{5,8}$\href{https://orcid.org/…}{\includegraphics[scale=0.08]{ORCIDiD.png}, }%⏎S. Burke-Spolaor$^{2,6,7}$…`
(2110.07418, nature) prints the comma inside the link, so the line did not part there (int130a: one creator "C. J. Law,
S. Burke-Spolaor" holding both links) and the link's ORCID contact dropped the ", " ("C. J. LawS. Burke-Spolaor"). A
link's printed text is a wrapper for `hoist_wrapped_separators` (names_split.rs), its address passed over, and only a
closing comma moves out after it (a link of a comma or an "and" alone, or a leading comma, stays whole): each name its
own iD. `\lx@author@href` keeps a separator (`,`, `;`) its ink prints after the icon where it prints, for the routes
that do not part the line. Guard `perfect_kernel_batch131fix::orcid_icon_link_closing_with_the_comma_parts_the_names`;
repro sectioning-frontmatter/`author_orcid_icon_link_closing_with_the_comma`, `author_orcid_icon_link_closing_with_a_semicolon` (RED → GREEN). Left (base and int131a
alike): `D. Li$^{1,12}$ \href{…}{\includegraphics{…}\footnotemark[1] },` — the icon set off by a space, its footnote
mark inside the link — is a nameless creator holding the link (2110.07418).

### 965. `\end{X}` over a `\begingroup` opened inside X closes that group and X, and X's group stays open for the next `\endgroup`, as TeX scopes it (Perl: Error "Attempt to end mode", the environment left open)

**What** (batch 98d; SYNC row "The unclaimed-text net" R0, census129 §5 "raa lineage, title deposit dropped").
raa.cls:322-349 `\institutename` is `\begin{flushleft}\begingroup … \end{flushleft}\endgroup` — legal TeX: groups are
untyped between `\begingroup` and `\endgroup` (tex.web §1063-1069), `\end{X}` is `\endX` + `\@checkend{X}` +
`\endgroup` (latex.ltx:15384-15393, `\@checkend` reading `\@currenvir`, still X), so `\end{flushleft}`'s `\endgroup`
closes the class's group and the class's `\endgroup` closes the one `\begin{flushleft}` opened. A DefEnvironment's
`\end{X}` ends X's mode frame (Perl Package.pm:1961-1962 `endMode`), which the plain group above it shadowed: Perl and
we raised `Error:unexpected:\end{flushleft} Attempt to end mode …` (Stomach.pm:544-550, `stomach.rs` `end_mode_opt`)
and left the environment open to the document's end. In a raw class's speculative `\@maketitle` deposit
(`sect05.rs` `\lx@deposit@maketitle`) the held errors then dropped the whole title page — raa's abstract and keywords
lost, with no Warning. On the raa witnesses themselves Perl loads no raw class (raa.cls is "missing", OmniBus
stands in), so it keeps their abstract: the loss was ours alone, through the raw-class deposit; the `\end{X}` Error
is Perl's on the shape itself (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1207).

**Now** (`stomach.rs` `end_environment_over_plain_groups`, called first by the `\end{X}` of every DefEnvironment
that declares a mode — `dialect.rs` `def_environment`'s `endMode` arm; a mode-less one's `egroup` arm is untouched):
when the environment open is X (`current_environment`, the check `\end{X}`'s "Can't close environment" runs), every
frame above X's own is a plain `\begingroup` group (non-boxing, no mode, no environment marker, no
`current_environment` but X — an X this branch ended earlier, nested in X, still records X as `\@currenvir` does) and the first frame below them is the `\begin{X}` of this `\end{X}`
(`lx@env@begin@end`), `\end{X}`
- pops the innermost group only, its local values undone (`\end`'s one `\endgroup`);
- ends X: its paragraph, mode (`BOUND_MODE`/`MODE`/`IN_MATH` unbound in X's frame), boxing level and own
  `beforeAfterGroup` work end there, so X's element closes where `\end{X}` stands;
- keeps X's frame as a plain non-boxing group holding X's other local values (`\@currenvir`, `\\`, a value set before
  the class's `\begingroup`) until the `\endgroup` that closes it — with two inner groups the second `\endgroup` closes
  the outer one and the third X's, pdflatex's scoping. The frame surgery is `state.rs` `unbind_value_in_frame` /
  `replace_value_in_frame` (Perl State.pm:280-286 `valueInFrame`'s offset rule).

An Info (`unexpected`) records it. Not for: another environment's `\end{Y}` (LaTeX's `\@badend`), an `\end{X}` with no
`\begin{X}` frame below the groups, or one over a raw `\newenvironment{Y}`'s `\begin{Y}` (its group records Y, so the
environment open is Y: `\@badend` again) — all keep today's Errors; a box or brace frame between (TeX errs), a math
environment (TeX's `$$` against a semi-simple group errs) or one whose begin code opened a box group (`TexGroup::Box`).
Not for the bare `\X … \endX` form (its `\endX` keeps the batch-66t Warning; no witness). Known gap: X's layout
state does not reach a paragraph ended between `\end{X}` and the class's `\endgroup`, where TeX keeps it until that
`\endgroup` — `\leftskip`/`\@totalleftmargin`, `\centering`, `\raggedright` (`\begin{flushleft}\begingroup
A\end{flushleft} B\par\endgroup`: TeX sets "B" ragged, ours has no `align`; `\begin{center}\begingroup
A\end{center}B\\C\endgroup`: TeX centres "B", ours one `<p>` with a `<break/>`; boxes-groups/`unclosed_nested_environments_keep_their_text`, guard
`perfect_kernel_batch65c::unclosed_nested_environments_keep_their_text`: pdflatex indents "Middle." one level and
"Q2."/"After." two, ours flat). No
witness has content in that gap (raa's `\endgroup` follows `\end{flushleft}` at once). Perl Error: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#1207. **Witnesses** 1404.3644, 1304.5354, 1508.02561, 1509.00139, 2004.06992, 2110.11117, 2306.16795, 1604.05586,
2003.13998, 2102.01352 (raa), 2511.10805 (raa_twocolumn); the long tail's raa ×20, cjaa ×2, chjaa ×2, raa06, raa_rb,
raa_twocolumn. **Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch98d::{end_closes_a_begingroup_opened_inside_the_environment,
end_over_begingroups_keeps_tex_scoping, end_over_begingroup_without_its_environment_stays_an_error,
a_raa_title_page_keeps_its_abstract_and_keywords}` (repros boxes-groups/`end_flushleft_closes_a_begingroup_opened_inside_it`,
`end_environment_over_begingroups_keeps_tex_scoping`, `end_other_environment_over_begingroup_stays_an_error`,
`end_without_its_begin_over_begingroup_stays_an_error`, `end_over_a_raw_environments_begin_stays_an_error`,
`end_nested_same_environment_over_begingroup_keeps_tex_scoping`;
sectioning-frontmatter/
`raw_class_institutes_in_flushleft_begingroup_keep_the_title_page`), RED (int132a1) → GREEN.

### 968. IEEEtran's `\IEEEauthorrefmark{n}` prints the n-th footnote symbol, keyed by its number among its kind and read as the symbol among marks of another form (Perl: no argument, its `{n}` printed as name text)

**Defect** (honest scorer `ieee_refmarks_apart`, 2312.10807; dev20k: 188 papers call the mark, 19 mix it with digit
marks). The binding's `\textsuperscript{#1}` printed the number where IEEEtran.cls:4540-4546 prints the footnote symbol
sequence `* † ‡ § ¶ ‖ ** †† ‡‡`, then lower-case roman numerals (`transmag`: the number, :4541), and every reader keyed
the mark by that number, so a block mixing it with digit marks paired it with them: 2312.10807's `Oier
Mees$^3$\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}` ("Mees3∗") took TUM, the `\thanks{$^1$…}` line, as well as Berkeley, and `Zhenshan
Bing$^1$\IEEEauthorrefmark{2}` took Bosch; the `$^{*}$Equal contribution` and `$^{\dagger}$Corresponding author: …`
legends went to the last author.

**Fix.** The binding prints `\textsuperscript{\lx@author@refmark@printed{n}}`, its symbol declared to the kernel's hook
`\lx@author@refmark@symbol` (ieeetran_cls.rs, the IEEEtran sequence in `\@fnsymbol`'s text forms, `transmag`'s number;
the kernel's default the operand, `\lx@author@refmark@arabic`, which IEEEoj's binding keeps, IEEEoj.cls:3186; ieeeaccess's
own `\authorrefmark` prints the number, ieeeaccess.cls:453). The kernel's `\lx@author@refmark@printed` (author_macros.rs) is the number while a
label is read (`queue_digest::printed_label`) and the symbol otherwise, in `\lx@author@refmark@shown`, which keys the
superscript holding it by the number (`_refmark`): the readers of the marks a name shows (`relocate::sup_marks`,
`insert::author_mark_keys`, the legend Kind step's) read it by its number as its label is — a footnote symbol is no
label mark there (`printed_marks`), so keyed by the symbol a block marked with these alone lost every pairing (A/B
probe: 2311.03600's names, 2205.00125's correspondence line). Within one kind the symbols and numbers are one to one,
so such a block pairs as before and prints as IEEEtran does; a request nothing answers shows the symbol
(`_refmarkshown`, 2408.02464); a legend line it labels is its carriers' note marked with the symbol (`‡`, 2410.12184,
2205.00125, 2504.18719, 2507.23474, 2603.14786). Where a reference mark shares its number with a mark of another form
that labels a line (`\thanks{$^1$TUM}`, `\IEEEauthorblockA{$^{1}$Univ}`), the class's `\author` writes each reference
mark as the superscript symbol it prints (`printed_refmarks`), so the block reads as one labelled by numbers and
annotated by footnote symbols (2312.10807, 2409.20550, 2602.11758's `Jianzhu Ma\textsuperscript{1}\authorrefmark{2}`
"Ma1†", no longer HKUST's); a block whose other-form numbers label no line keeps the numbers (1910.10075's
`\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}\textsuperscript{1}` names over refmark-led blockA lines). The observer keys the mark by its
number too (`\lx@fm@obs@mark`), and the observer writer's legend step, which reads the printed glyph, takes a reference
mark off a name only where its number is a label of the line the legend was (`writer::apply::show_legend_mark`, the
replaced contact's `_label`: `\IEEEauthorrefmark{1}\IEEEauthorrefmark{*}` over an `\IEEEauthorrefmark{*}` legend
keeps the `{1}` mark's `∗`, review rev106b S2; a `{1}` legend's `∗` is taken, 2504.18719; repro
`ieee_refmark_beside_a_starred_legend`, guard `a_refmark_printing_a_legends_glyph_keeps_it`). Without IEEEtran's `\raisebox{0pt}[0pt][0pt]` and `\footnotesize`; `*` in its text form
(`\textasteriskcentered`, Perl's `*`), one key with `∗` (`one_asterisk`).

**Beyond Perl**: Perl binds `\IEEEauthorrefmark` with no argument (IEEEtran.cls.ltxml:154). Measured (A/B `pop106b3.tsv`
vs int134b, 340 papers: the 58 batch witnesses, the 161 dev20k and 119 `popint125a_s10k` papers calling the mark, 2 more
of the selection): 204 changed, all frontmatter; 185 only by the mark printed (`1` → `∗`), the creators and contacts as
on base; 2312.10807 and 2602.11758 paired as printed; 14 the dedupe of #969, 3 its Kind step; E 902 = 902, F 1 = 1,
words −262 (the duplicates); `fm_checks.py` 1-7: no creator merged or lost, no address shared more, no growth, no
fragment, the word types lost the refmarks' digits. **Not reached**: the
observer writer's re-part shows an unanswered reference mark's number (synthetic `ieee_affil_block_after_a_marked_block_of_two`,
"Ann Able 1"; no real paper of the A/B); a refmark ≥ 10 among other-form marks is written as its roman numeral and
read as a letter label, answered and so taken off the name and its note ("Ann Able1x", "x Visiting scholar" in the PDF;
review rev106b N2, synthetic); the writer's legend note under `\thanks{$^1$…}` beside a refmark block keeps a math `∗`
where the names show `*` (rev106b N3); a math toggle by `\(…\)` or `\ensuremath` is not seen by `printed_refmarks`
(N4, suspected); 2409.20550's `\thanks{\IEEEauthorrefmark{1} Corresponding author.}` stays a
document note; a block whose reference marks label lines and whose other-form numbers also label lines with the same
numbers is read by the symbols (none in the A/B). **Guards** `perfect_kernel_batch106b::{a_refmark_among_digit_marks_is_the_symbol_it_prints,
refmark_blocks_pair_and_print_their_symbols}` (repros `ieee_refmark_mixed_with_digit_marks`,
`ieee_refmark_blocks_pair_by_symbol`; the catalog repro `ieee_authorrefmark_prints_its_footnote_symbol` GREEN), RED
(int134b) → GREEN. Re-pinned to the printed symbol (the pairing unchanged): `perfect_kernel_batch64::{ieee_refmark_unanswered_stays_printed,
ieee_refmark_address_and_marks_in_a_line, ieee_refmark_orcid_digits_are_no_name}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch67x::ieeetrantools_under_ieeetran_keeps_class_author_marks`,
`perfect_kernel_batch78v::affiliation_address_run_after_a_trailing_comma`,
`perfect_kernel_batch94a::an_ieee_affiliation_block_after_a_marked_block_is_the_next_names` (first case),
`perfect_kernel_batch103c::an_affiliation_that_is_a_legend_is_its_carriers_note` (the IEEE legend's mark `‡`),
`perfect_kernel_batch104a::a_refmark_led_address_line_is_its_marks_addresses`,
`perfect_kernel_batch106a::a_labelled_line_of_addresses_leaves_its_entry`,
`perfect_kernel_batch63::{author_ieee_blockn_name_list_splits, ieee_grade_comma_before_a_break_continues_names}`,
`perfect_kernel_batch77n::ieee_uppercase_names_split_with_grades`, `regress_2605_clusters::ieeetj_is_ieeetran` (ieeetj.cls
:3166 prints the symbols, 2405.01673's copy).

Guard `perfect_kernel_batchm3::tblr_preto_and_appto_join_the_cell_text` (a row per repro). **Left:** the unwarned losses (an inline expl3 key, an inner two-argument cell key, empty `preto`/`appto`, the `\SetTblrInner` order) are `docs/perfect_kernel/OPEN_ROWS.md` ODR2 (SYNC row R); RED repros `alignment-bindings/tblr_inline_expl_command_in_a_key_red`, `tblr_preto_in_a_two_argument_cell_key_red`.

### 977. l3fp's doors answer natively: what the macro's run leaves, from a port of l3fp's arithmetic

Perl has no native l3fp; every `\fp_set:Nn` is about 40k token reads here as there. `latexml_engine/src/l3fp_native/` answers both doors,
`\__fp_parse:n` and `\__fp_parse_o:n` (expl3-code.tex:17313-17339), which `\fp_set:Nn`, `\fp_eval:n`, `\fp_compare:nNnTF`, `\fp_step_*`,
`\fpeval`, siunitx's raw code and l3draw all go through. A speedup, not a behaviour: the known differences are listed under "What can
still tell" below.

**The hook.** The doors stay the format's macros. Both expand to `… \exp:w \__fp_parse_operand:Nw \c__fp_prec_end_int \__fp_parse_expand:w
<expression> \s__fp_expr_mark \__fp_parse_infix_end:N \s__fp_expr_stop …`, the only calls of that shape. `\__fp_parse_operand:Nw` (:17340) keeps
its body too, and carries a native call (`SpecialCall::Native`, `Definition::native_expansion`), tried only when the gullet expands a call
in full (`invoke_expansion`), before any argument is read: `\meaning`, the prefixes, `\cs_replacement_spec:N`, a one-step `\exp_after:wN`,
`\exp_args:No` of a door or of this macro see the format's definition. Every other caller passes another precedence: one comparison, and the
macro runs. At the door's shape the expression is read off the pushback, braces as they stand (`{1}+1`, which the macro's undelimited
`\__fp_parse_expand:w #1` strips, declines), and nothing is consumed until the answer: `\exp_end_continue_f:w <fp>@ \__fp_parse_infix_end:N`, with
`\s__fp_expr_stop` left on the input, exactly what the macro's run leaves for `\__fp_parse_after:ww`, as a list through the ordinary path, so
`invoke_expansion` stamps a frontmatter field's provenance on it as on any macro's. `<fp>` is `\s__fp \__fp_chk:w <kind> <sign>
{<exp>}{<b1>}{<b2>}{<b3>}{<b4>} \__fp_sep:` (or `0 0 \s__fp_exact`, `2 0 \s__fp_exact`, the `\s__fp_underflow` zero of `round(0.4)`).

**The fail-safe.** On anything not handled with certainty nothing has happened and the macro runs as defined: a tuple, `nan`, `rand`, `randint`,
`em`, `ex`, a word it does not know (so a document's new fp variable or function), every flag or message (invalid operation, division by
zero, overflow, underflow), a conditional or a primitive in the expression, an active character, a brace group. The native path reads in the
macro parser's order (`\__fp_parse_expand:w`: an argument's skip of spaces, then `get_x_token`, expanding until an unexpandable token and
swallowing one space), on a stack of its own, and substitutes only what changes no state and reports nothing: a macro with a token-list body;
`\number`, `\the`, `\dim_to_fp:n`, `\fp_to_decimal:n`, `\fp_use:N` of a plain register, one dimension or a nested expression; the format's own
`\__fp_parse:n` inside an expression, by its definition (`\fp_add:Nn`, `\fp_abs:n`, `\fp_sign:n` put it there), as the macro's run reads it; `\csname` of a name
that already means something (of a new one it defines `\relax`, so that is the macro's). A macro behind a space an expansion left is read
unexpanded by the raw parser (`1\x`, `\def\x{ \y}`), so it declines. A dimension's value comes from the engine's own reader over a text checked to
be `<decimal><unit>` below `\maxdimen` by a margin per unit (`Dimension too large` is the macro's to report, once). A stored form is read only when
canonical (an exponent as `\int_value:w` writes it, four blocks of four digits), since l3fp hands any other on as it stands or does its block
arithmetic on it. An `\outer` token in a macro's argument, a macro a frontmatter watch observes (`state::setter_call_is_observed`), and an
expression past `parse::MAX_DEPTH` (400 levels of `operand` and `one` and a function's commas, about 200 of `(`, whose stack use is 172 KB in a
release build and is `maybe_grow`n) decline as well. The macro's own run then reports or is Fatal as it would: `1^1^…` at 2,000 terms, 1,000,000 of
`(`, rc=1. So does a conversion within 6,000 levels of the expansion limit. A long flat expression (`1+1+…`) is a loop and stays native. So does a tab mark
the macro's run would read at `align_state` 0, which ends the cell (tex.web §342), with the Errors and the value that follow: wherever the parser reads one (the
infix, an operand, a `\csname`, `\one &` and any column end in a macro's argument, a `\let` copy of `&`, `\cr`, `\crcr` and `\span` included, and `\one{&}` by its brace level), by the gullet's own count (`parse::tab_mark_ends_cell`). A `{…}`-wrapped cell, an
`\edef`'s body and anything outside an alignment end nothing and stay native: over the census's 346 manuals a catcode-4 `&` or `|` is read 5,448 times, in 6 of them, and none goes raw.

**While it may answer.** Only while l3fp is what this module ports. `state::watch_meanings` watches `\__fp_…`, `\c__fp_…`, `\s__fp…` and `\c_…_fp`: an
assignment that changes one, however local (a group's end does not undo the verdict), ends the native path for the rest of the conversion. Words
(`\fp_clear_variable:n{pi}`, `\fp_clear_function:n{sin}`, `\fp_new_function:n{cos}`), operators, arithmetic macros, constants, the doors, the marks are
all one rule; so a name the parser knows means what it did at the install. No change: a scope move or a copy onto itself (the lazy LaTeX.pool's
`hoist_top_frame_delta`), a first definition (over the `\relax` a `\csname` made, for all but the `\s__fp…` marks, which are `\relax` by meaning),
what l3fp assigns as it runs (`\__fp_tmp:w`, `\__fp_function_arg_o:w`) and what only a flag's path reaches, which the parser declines
(`\fp_trap:nn`'s targets). Only assignments by a document, a raw file or a format file are looked at: a binding's or a pool's code assigns no such name, and
every conversion's preload is thousands of them. Its cost is a test of a name's second and third bytes per such assignment (`MeaningWatch`, without the interner's guard), the name's own test
only for `\__`, `\c_` and `\s_`, and none per use: figures in docs/performance/PERFORMANCE.md.

**What can still tell.** A document's redefinition of the kernel's or TeX's own control sequences l3fp's macros use (`\exp_after:wN`, `\use_i:nn`,
`\int_value:w`), which the macros would obey and the native path does not read (the door itself would break on most); `\number`, `\the`, `\csname`, `\numexpr`, `\dimexpr`, `\relax`
redefined or let are equal both ways, since the macros use the `\tex_…:D` names. A watched constant's value, which is no meaning: `\int_gset:Nn \c__fp_big_middle_shift_int {0}` before `1/3` is 0 Errors native, 1 Error
and 1 Fatal raw, 25 `!` in pdflatex; no file of TeX Live does this. A hand-written call of
`\__fp_parse_operand:Nw \c__fp_prec_end_int \__fp_parse_expand:w …` is answered like the door's. The token and time budgets see fewer reads.

**The arithmetic is a port, not a reimplementation.** `+ - * /`, `sqrt` and the number reader round correctly to 16 digits in the
TeX (ties to even, `\__fp_round_digit:Nw`), so exact `u128` arithmetic with a sticky digit gives the same digits (`num.rs`).
`exp`, `ln`, `^`, the sines and tangents and their inverses, `fact` do not: their block operations (`\__fp_fixed_mul:wwn`,
`\__fp_fixed_mul_sub_back:wwwn`, `\__fp_fixed_div_int:wwN`, `\__fp_ep_div:wwwwn`, `\__fp_ep_isqrt:wwn`), `\numexpr`'s rounding
division, the Taylor loops, the argument reductions and both intarrays are translated one for one, truncations included
(`fixed.rs`, `func.rs`, `tables.rs`). No `f64` comes near a value. Nothing relies on unwinding (`maxperf` aborts on a panic): no `unwrap` or
`panic!` outside the tests, indices bounded by the digits' widths.

**Years.** Installed at the end of `LoadFormat('latex')`, after the dump's apply: the dumps do not change, and a later raw
`expl3-code.tex` trips the watch. Only over l3fp sources it was held against, by `\ExplLoaderFileDate` and the bodies of the door, the operand
macro and `\__fp_parse_infix_end:N`: 2025-11-06 (TL 2025) and 2026-01-19 (the host's Debian tree), which differ in the door's
`\group_align_safe_begin:` alone. That guard is in the count the tab-mark rule reads, so TL 2025's `1&&1` at brace level 0 of a cell is the macro's, Errors and all, and the same cell on 2026-01-19 is native, as each year's macro has it. Any other year keeps its macros, because before 2025 the separator was `;` and the numerics are unverified here.

`LATEXML_L3FP_NATIVE=0` installs nothing; `LATEXML_L3FP_CHECK=1` runs the macro's own run on every answer and reports an Error naming the
argument where the tokens differ, which cannot see what a run reports; `LATEXML_L3FP_TRACE=1` prints the answers and the fallbacks by reason at the
thread's end.

**The proof.** The self-check over the census, the 346 of 2,374 TeX Live manuals that reach l3fp: 971,116 calls, 0 mismatches, 94.3 % answered natively, and over 52 of 1,995 arXiv papers (seeded from those using `siunitx`, `xfp`, `l3draw`, `pgf-interference` or `\fp`) 97.6 % in the first form of this door. It compares tokens; for what a run reports, `run_doc.sh` over those 346, base P1 against native and `LATEXML_L3FP_NATIVE=0`: Errors, Fatals, Warnings and XML equal on every one but l3kernel/source3, which varies on its own under load and is equal at `--max-memory=0` (SYNC_STATUS "l3kernel/source3", now `perfect_kernel/SILENT_LOSS_INVENTORY.md`). pdflatex as oracle (`kit/l3fp_oracle.sh`, `-no-shell-escape`, TL 2025): 36 families, seeded operations in the shapes that matter (16-digit mantissas, ties, exponent limits, angles next to multiples of pi/4, huge and tiny angles, literals past 16 digits, registers, composed expressions), `\fp_to_tl`, 0 mismatches: 100,000 each in the first form, 20,000 each on this one, 97.9 % native; on the host's expl3 2026-01-19, 1,000 each. Every expression of the review's fuzz that differed, each native vs raw vs pdflatex, is a row of the guards. A/B of 2,495 papers (`popP2`: the census's 2,000 and 500 controls) against P1: 0 changed, E 7,795 = 7,795, F 77 = 77, Warnings equal.

Guards `perfect_kernel_batchp2::{the_hard_values_are_pdflatexs, a_seeded_slice_matches_pdflatex, what_it_declines_is_the_raw_macros,
it_expands_when_the_raw_parser_does, an_expression_in_a_printed_title_stays_a_field, a_dimension_too_large_is_reported_once,
a_changed_name_of_l3fp_is_left_to_the_macros, the_doors_stay_the_formats_macros, a_stored_form_not_canonical_is_the_macros,
a_deep_expression_is_the_macros, a_tab_mark_that_ends_a_cell_is_the_macros}` (repros `expl3/l3fp_*`), each both ways byte-identical and with the native answers counted (`native_counts`), since
the raw macro would pass them alone. **Left, each a fallback (speed only):** `\numexpr` and `\dimexpr` of more than one number; `\pgfkeysvalueof`,
`\arabic` and other native-bodied macros; conditionals; macros with delimited parameters; `\seq_item:Nn`, `\clist_item:nn`.

### 980. The frontmatter pipeline: every author block is read by the observer, resolved, and written by the emitter at the flush as Perl's own API calls — absorbs #52 #837 #923 #925 #926 #928 #942 #948 #958 #978 #979 #982 #988 #991

**Rule.** At each frontmatter flush every `\author`-family block is rehearsed (digested in a rolled-back group of event
bindings), lexed into events, resolved into creators with their names, contacts and notes, and written by the emitter as
the calls Perl's `\lx@add@authors` would make (`\lx@add@frontmatter@now{ltx:creator}`, `\lx@annotate@frontmatter@now`,
`\lx@add@thanks`). A block the emitter cannot write without losing or misowning a name is written as Perl writes it —
whole, or split where Perl splits it — with one counted Warning.

**Perl.** `\lx@add@authors` cuts the block's tokens before digestion: the `{tabular}`/`{minipage}`/`\halign` branch writes
it whole as one `\lx@add@author` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:687-693), else `SplitTokens` at `@authorsplits` /
`@authoraffilsplits` (:679-683, :114-140); `insertFrontMatter` places the queue (:824, :913, :918).
**TeX.** latex.ltx:17213 `\author` stores `\@author`; article.cls:236-252 `\@maketitle` typesets it in `tabular[t]{c}`,
`\and` (latex.ltx:17219) closing one column and opening the next. What TeX prints is the reading's evidence.

**The stages** (`base_utilities/frontmatter/observer/mod.rs` lists the modules):
- *Queue.* Every call queues its block whole (`defs/author_macros.rs:35 whole_block_call`); the ledger records it with
  its stamped position range (`observer/ledger.rs`).
- *Flush.* `place.rs:520 digest_front_matter` rehearses and lexes every block not read yet (`observer/reading.rs`;
  `observer/rehearsal.rs`; each block under the author markup its digestion runs, `reading.rs:254`,
  `defs/frontmatter_fields.rs:901 author_markup_begin`: a binding's class markup, OmniBus's, the title code's
  definitions that read arguments — formerly in #802's and #941's records. What a title-code command assigns besides
  printing, called from the block or in the run a paper's macro reached it in, is no declaration of the block
  (`field_notes.rs:613 keep_declared`, `:686 field_expansion`; the run lasts while its expansion is read, a mouth its
  `\textsuperscript` digests its argument in included, `close_runs`): pdflatex runs it inside the title code's group,
  so its replay apart erred undefined (klmm.sty's `\instref`, 2606.12100, 2606.12130, 2606.12144, 2606.22997,
  2606.26035). Every other definition of that macro, a name built at run time too, is the block's (not one it passes as
  the title-code command's argument: row R REHEARSEARG), replayed under the
  author markup (`emitter/emit.rs:3150 declarations`, `frontmatter_fields.rs under_author_markup`), as pdflatex runs it
  in that group; OmniBus's `\orcid` is bound as a class's own
  `\orcid` (`rehearsal.rs:613`, `\lx@author@orcid`), one contact with its argument whole (2606.13132's `\orcid{orcid.org/…}`
  had lost its iD); `events/mod.rs:2774 lex_with_formulas`
  reads a span's content from the digested list, a speculative run's in-place edits undone — formerly #978), then calls
  `emitter/emit.rs:5001 emit_commands` (place.rs:589).
- *Resolve.* `observer/resolver/mod.rs:1257 resolve` applies the rules its module doc numbers 1-10 under the family's
  declared conventions (`observer/policy.rs:371 policy_for`; the kernel's and an undeclared binding's: `KERNEL`,
  `UNDECLARED`, Perl's `@authorsplits` reading).
- *Emit.* The resolved tuples become Perl's calls; an API creator call holding its own `\and`s is cut at them
  (`emit.rs:4511 creator_call_cut`); a block calling a binding's list setter keeps the setter's call as written, its
  entries the list its marks request (`emit.rs:1304 list_setter_runs`, `:1331 list_setter_call`; formerly #982); a block
  no rehearsal read is Perl's whole-block creator (`fallback.rs:23 whole_block_author`).
- *Declines* (written as Perl writes it, each with one Warning, once per block over the flushes): a name's words lost
  (`emit.rs:3558 written_whole`); a footnote counter moved (`:3577 counter_moved`); a declaration reading past its piece
  (`:3903 declaration_reads_past`, `:3944 printing_read_later`); a shared run printing a note (`:3834 names_overlap`).
  The counter and definition declines write Perl's split (`fallback.rs:101 perl_author_calls`), and whole where that
  split states an owner the marks do not support or loses a name (`emit.rs:4096 split_owns_falsely`, `:4196
  split_loses_a_name`, `:4377 split_decline`; formerly #988). A re-referencing `\footnotemark[n]` keeps the reading, its
  label's loss counted (`:3650 mark_dropped`).
- *Check.* The placed creators are read back against the reading (`emitter/mod.rs:45 check_placed_content`); the title
  page's printed words against the output (#953, `title_page_check.rs:1605`).
- *Families* read whole: eptcs's block and OmniBus's `\authors` list go whole to the reading (formerly #991; Perl:
  `OmniBus.cls.ltxml:74` `\authors{}` prints nothing).

**History** (what each absorbed record's code was, what was deleted, and where its live rules are now; each
record kept in [archive/OD_FRONTMATTER_RECORDS_2026-11-15.md](../archive/OD_FRONTMATTER_RECORDS_2026-11-15.md) under
its number):

### 981. Lost frontmatter content is counted, never silent: a note with no ink is not emitted, a take-out keeps every printed word it did not take — absorbs #803 #916 #944

**Rule.** A frontmatter note nothing in which prints — emptied by the contacts taken out of it, or written empty — is not
emitted; every other word a take-out or a decline removes is kept as a label, left in place, or counted by a Warning.
Where a reading still loses content, the loss is a `_red` repro and a counted Warning, never a silent drop.

**Perl.** Emits the empty note (`\lx@add@thanks`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:661-662; `<pubnote role="preprint"/>` for A&A's
`\offprints{\email{…}}`), its mark over nothing. **TeX.** latex.ltx:17215 `\thanks` prints its mark and its footnote
text; a note with no ink prints a mark only.

**Sub-rules**
- *No ink*: resolver rule 9 (`observer/resolver/mod.rs` module doc; `Event::inkless`): a note whose content all became
  contacts (formerly #803: aa/webofc `\fnmsep\thanks{\email{…}}`), or whose content prints nothing (formerly #916:
  `\thanks{}`; user ruling 2026-10-30, FIDELITY_CHARTER §2, §4). A note whose only ink has no letter or digit (a command's
  text, a math token, a rule, `\colorbox`) is dropped as well, named in the content check's Warning: accepted (DG 2026-11-15,
  old #916's "only a note with no ink" retired).
- *Take-outs* keep what they did not take (formerly #944): aa's `\mail` labelled as the paper's copy prints it
  (aa_support.sty.ltxml:118-119), an emptied entry's label kept, a store's label read before its printed occurrence
  (`resolver/labels.rs:985 address_take_out`, `:1112 take_labels`).
- *Accounting*: the emitter's declines (#980) and the unclaimed-text net (`insert.rs:381 keep_unclaimed_net_notes`)
  and the title-page check (#953) each name the words they could not place.
