### 983. An author block's undefined commands raise their Errors once: in place where a piece holds them, else at the flush (ERR2)

**Perl:** the creator's whole block is digested once (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:691-693); an undefined command raises
`Error:undefined:\cs` at its first use and its stub leaves `<ltx:ERROR class="undefined">\cs</ltx:ERROR>` where it
stands (State.pm:547-551 `generateErrorStub`) — `\author{Ann Able\undefinedprobecs \and Bob\email{b@x.org}}` (article)
gives 2 Errors and the creators `Ann Able<ERROR>\undefinedprobecs</ERROR>` and `Bob<ERROR>\email</ERROR>b@x.org`.
**Was (since the flip, `=2`):** the observer's rehearsal held each block Error and discarded it with its stub
(`observer/rehearsal.rs`, `DiagnosticsHold::discard`), trusting the emitter's digestion of each piece to raise it again.
It was lost (a) when the command's token fell in no piece — it prints nothing, so no event covers it and the piece
before it stopped short of it (after a name, after a mark or a `\thanks` the reading writes apart) — and (b) when its
piece was written as text. The command printing nothing also glued the ink around it: "Bobb@x.org" was read as an
address and made Ann's e-mail, Bob lost (one creator). **Now:** (1) a piece grows over the held undefined commands
right after it (`emitter/content.rs` `Field::past_held_undefined`, told by the rehearsal's `Error:undefined:` record at
the command's position, not by its spelling); (2) a name takes the held undefined commands past its marks and notes, up
to the next separator or name, written after them (`emitter/emit.rs` `block_names`; `event_run_at` returns where the
written tokens end, and a mark or separator written apart counts to where its piece's tokens end, so nothing is taken twice:
`Ann Able\footnotemark\foo{} \and Bob Baker` writes one stub, review revERR2c finding 1; `Ann Able\thanks{…}\footnotemark[1]$^,$\foo\footnotemark[2]`
one, between the marks, review revDEL5b finding 1); (3) an address is declined only where an undefined command glues it: the same word has ink before the
command's Error and ink after it, both before the word's first `@` ("Bob|b@": `Bob\email{b@x.org}` prints "Bobb@x.org",
an address no word of the source spells), told by where `InkTable` says each character prints (`events/mod.rs`
`glues_an_address`, setting `Event::glued_undef` in `mark_held`). A Name the ink table cannot align — no record for its
span and text, or one of another length, as when a mark is glued into it (`Bob Baker\textsuperscript{1}\foo b@x.org`
reads "Bob Baker1b@x.org") — fails closed on its span: an Error strictly inside it with an `@` token of it at or past
the Error's end (end-exclusive, as the ink path's: `…b\foo@x.org` as `…b\foo{}@x.org`, review revERR2c finding 2)
declines it (review revERR2b finding 2: the ink path alone made up the e-mail "Baker1b@x.org"; it also declines
`Bob\textsuperscript{1}b\foo{}@x.org`, whose local part is wholly before the command). In that shape the decline is
no undoing of a glue: the reading without the Error (`\def\foo{}`) makes up the same "Baker1b@x.org" from the glued
mark alone (a pre-existing reading of a superscript mark glued before an address, `Bob Baker\textsuperscript{1}b@x.org`),
so the fallback keeps that reading's creators and their count and declines an address the Error did not make. Such a Name is never
read as an address, by the names line's address extraction (`resolver/lines.rs` `names_without_addresses`) or as an
address line (`resolver/blocks.rs`): Bob stays a creator whose piece is digested from its tokens, as Perl's split at
`\and` makes him. Every other undefined command leaves the reading exactly as without its Error: one past the `@`
(`ann@x.org\IEEEmembership{Member}`, the e-mail `ann@x.orgMember`), one before the word or in another word
(`\texttt{ann@x.org}\foo{} Univ X`, `(ann@x.org\foo)`), and one with the whole local part before it ("ann|@":
`ann\foo@x.org`, Ann's e-mail `ann@x.org` as with `\def\foo{}`; review revERR2b finding 3), each Error raised by the
flush's net. So an undefined command never moves a separator: the creators are those of the reading without its Error,
except that the address it glued, or the fallback's address above, is declined; (4) the

### 984. → #805 (The emitter keeps only an affiliation entry's own text, and the Link step places every inner e-mail of it (Z18c: llncs's old split's rules, in the emitter))

### 985. What the old driver wrote at the flush and the emitter had lost: an svjour3 owner label's `\email`, and a frontmatter setter run inside an author block or an API call (CR2)

Two real losses of the flip's content residual (CR1 classes B and A): pdflatex prints the words, the old driver
(`LATEXML_FM_EMIT=0`, int153m) kept them by digesting the label, block or call at the flush; the emitter, writing from
the reading, digested none of it. The old driver's output is the target. For A Perl keeps the words with 0 errors; for B
Perl keeps the e-mails but files them all under the last author (svjour3's `\email`, sv_support.sty.ltxml:52, is an
unlabelled `\lx@add@email`) and drops both affiliations as orphans (2 Warnings), so B's owner rule is the old driver's,
beyond Perl. (1) **svjour3
`Name (\email{…}) \at Address`** inside `\institute`: the `\email` sat only in the piece's `fuzzy:` owner label, which the
emitter reads as text (`observer/ledger.rs` `label_text`), so no contact was filed and no Warning raised. The binding
now files each such `\email` under the label as its own call, before the affiliation as the line prints it
(`sv_support_sty.rs` `\lx@sv@institute@` → `\lx@sv@institute@email`, `\lx@add@email[label={fuzzy:…}]`), the label
holding the owner's name alone. Witnesses 2206.00320 (3 e-mails), 1307.4424 (2). (2) **A setter run inside an author
block or a call** — `\date` inside `\author` (LaTeX prints its argument as the date: 2503.02741, hep-th0304189), REVTeX
3's two-column `\address{\begin{minipage}…\begin{abstract}…\end{abstract}\pacs{…}\end{minipage}}` (cond-mat9801109,
cond-mat9906335, cond-mat9809277, cond-mat9909213). The rehearsal, the frontmatter frozen, notes each entry the run would
queue as the queue would hold it (`rehearsal::note_frozen_entry`, tag + attributes + command) and each it digests where
it stands (`\lx@add@frontmatter@until`, `rehearsal::note_frozen_digest`); a block keeps them (`AuthorBlock::queued`), and
now a call too (`ApiCall::queued`, `reading::read_at_flush`). At the flush the emitter queues them after its own entries,
so each is its own entry where the schema puts it (`emitter::emit::recover_queued`, once per source): a read block's,
not one written whole (whose digestion runs the setter itself, still counted by `warn_queued_unwritten`); a call's of
which the reading writes nothing and whose command is not already written as queued. A call the reading writes from
recovers nothing, neither queued nor counted: its written contact's digestion at the flush runs every setter in it
(`\address{Univ A, Oviedo, Spain \pacs{71.25.Hc}}` wrote two PACS classifications otherwise, and a false "lost" Warning
beside an `\begin{abstract}` written; review revCR2 finding 2). A call whose run digested an entry in place is written as
queued, the old driver's rule, so its digestion runs every setter in it — with the attributes it was queued with, back at
its ledger position among the emitter's item calls, labelled for its run's creators (`run_labels`: the owners of the item
of its role before it when no author came between, else the creators since that item), so the insertion places its
contact with theirs in queue order. Only one owner's label is given (`labelled`, which drops the call's own `label`,
`annotate` and `owner` keys as `rekeyed` does, `routing_key`); a run of two or more owners leaves the call unlabelled,
placed by its own `annotate=` as the old driver digested it: joined as one `label={author:1,author:2}`, the insertion's exact-label lookup
(`relocate::find_targets`) never found it (an orphaned-annotation Warning, review revCR2b finding 1), and a copy per label
would digest the call's setters once each. The resolver's empty `annotate=run` entry records its run
(`Resolver::empty_entry_holds_its_role` → `record_run`), so the next `\address` is the same run's: `\author{Ann Able and
Bob Baker}` + the minipage `\address` + `\address{Univ A}` gives Univ A to both, as the old driver (it went to Bob alone,
review revCR2b P1). Appended unlabelled, its contact went into each creator before the items' moved
contacts, and cond-mat9809277's e-mails, cut from the first address, landed after the journal line (review revCR2
finding 1); now Address, Email, Address(PRL), as the base, REVTeX 3's print and the old driver. An entry digested in place
in a read block, which no step writes, is counted (`warn_queued_lost`). A setter inside a block read while a flush
digests its queue runs `\lx@add@frontmatter@now`, not the queue: 1411.6693's `\title{…\author{…\date{…}}}`, whose
`\author` runs in the title's digestion at the `\maketitle` flush (the emitter stays out of that flush: no author block),
a late block with a flush of its own (`\lx@frontmatter@late`). Its rehearsal notes the `@now` entry as the command a
queued one is digested by (`queue::now_command`, `rehearsal::note_frozen_entry`; never a creator), so that flush's
emitter queues it as above: the date is kept (it was lost with no Warning, review revCR2 P1). cond-mat9809277
keeps Perl's and the old driver's empty minipage `ltx:contact`, last (RED: `\vskip -0.5in $ $` after the `\pacs` keeps
the minipage's paragraph). Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{svjour3_institute_email_before_at_is_its_owners,date_inside_author_is_the_date,revtex3_abstract_inside_address_minipage,revtex3_minipage_address_keeps_contact_order,revtex3_setter_in_written_address_once,revtex3_minipage_address_first_joins_run_labels,date_inside_author_inside_title_is_the_date}.tex`;
guards `perfect_kernel_batchcr2` (one per path: the owner label, a block's queued setter, a call's in-place digest, the
call's place among the items, a written call), `perfect_kernel_batchcr3::{revtex3_minipage_address_first_one_run` (a run
of several owners), `date_inside_author_inside_title_is_the_date}` (a flush-time `@now` setter).

A date such a late block recovers while an outer flush digests its queue is set as TeX typesets the
block (a date only: `\@maketitle` prints the title before the author line, so a `\title` run there changes nothing printed — `\title{A Title \author{Ann Able \title{Inner}}}` prints "A Title"; CR4/CR4b deferred titles too and printed "Inner", review revCR4b finding 1, guard `perfect_kernel_batchcr4b::title_inside_author_inside_title_keeps_the_outer_title`), after the queue's own entries (`\maketitle` runs the inner `\date` while typesetting `\@author`, after every
`\date` before it): it is queued for the end of the outermost flush (`emitter::emit::defer_to_flush_end`, digested by
`place::digest_front_matter` after its own queue), not digested inside the late flush, so `\title{A Title \author{Ann Able \date{Dinner
One}}}` `\date{Dinner Two}` `\maketitle` gives "Dinner One", as pdflatex (it gave "Dinner Two", no Warning; review revCR3b
finding 2, CR4). The title-page check's "unclaimed: two" there (its run prints the outer `\date`, which TeX never prints)
is a false positive erring the safe way, as with the outer `\date` before `\title`. Repro
`date_inside_author_inside_title_over_later_date`; guard `perfect_kernel_batchcr4::date_inside_author_inside_title_over_later_date`.
CR4 queued it for the next flush, which a `\section` after `\maketitle` (the common case) never ran: the date was
dropped and "Dinner Two" kept, with no Warning (review revCR4 finding 3; int154w alike); placed at the end of the
outermost flush, "Dinner One" holds with or without the section (repro
`date_inside_author_inside_title_section_after`; guard
`perfect_kernel_batchcr4b::date_inside_author_inside_title_section_after`).
**Left** (synthetic, pre-existing): a `\date` set in `\title` itself (`\title{A Title \date{Dinner One}}` `\date{Dinner
Two}` `\author{Ann Able}` `\maketitle`; pdflatex "Dinner One") still loses to the later `\date`, with no Warning: an
`@now` setter inside a queued entry's digestion, no late block.


**A block of no name (CR10b).** A block the reading makes no creator of runs its setters as a read block's do, when it
is in the queue of a block read at this flush (its `epoch`), no later block of that queue replaces it (`replace`) and no
clear removed it (`cleared`): a replaced `\author` is never typeset, nor are the setters in it. jheppub's
`\author{\abstract{We define …} \keywords{defect operator, …}}` after three named `\author[x]{…}` (1211.2861), which
pdflatex prints under the names as the abstract and the keywords (jheppub.sty:69-71 setters, `\maketitle` printing
`\@abstract`, `\@keywords`), lost both with 0 Warnings: the recovery skipped every block of no creator. Repro
`sectioning-frontmatter/jheppub_setters_in_a_nameless_author`; guard `perfect_kernel_batchcr10b::jheppub_setters_in_a_nameless_author`.

**Known REDs (review revCR4b):** a `\date` nested two levels deep (`\title{…\author{…\title{…\author{…\date{X}}}}}`) never runs in TeX (pdflatex prints the outer "Dinner Two") but is deferred and replaces it ("Dinner X", counted by the content check: `date_nested_twice_never_runs_red.tex`).

### 986. imsart.sty is a binding of its own, so a shipped copy declaring itself imsart.sty is read through it (CR3)

The imsart.cls binding (latexml_contrib `imsart_cls.rs`) owns imsart.sty's frontmatter (`\ead`, `\printead`, `\author`,
`\address`, `\thanksref`, `\thankstext`, `\thanksmark`), its keyword blocks and `\arxiv`, defined before it reads
imsart.sty raw. A paper that loads imsart.sty without that class read it raw: a renamed copy that declares itself
`\ProvidesFile{imsart.sty}` — stylefile.sty, loaded by stylefile.cls (`\ProvidesClass{stylefile}`, a renamed imsart.cls;
1905.11425, 2101.10506), imsart_mod.sty beside article (math0608476) — or imsart.sty under its own name beside article
(1301.1466). Its `\ead[label=e1,mark]{…}` inside `\author` typeset nothing the frontmatter kept, so every e-mail and every
`\address` was lost with no Warning (CR1 class C; the old driver glued "label=e1" into the name). Now imsart.sty has a
binding (`imsart_sty.rs`, an author-file stand-in in `author_files.rs`) sharing the class binding's markup
(`imsart_cls::imsart_sty_markup`, `imsart_arxiv`), so the charter's copy rule (a shipped copy goes to the binding whose
file it declares itself, FIDELITY_CHARTER "bindings and copies") and the existing declaration route (`content.rs`
`provided_binding`, #731) read each copy after it as the stand-in's copy. Two additions the route needs: imsart.sty's
author markup (`\degs`, `\fnms`, `\inits`, `\snm`, `\roles`, defined only inside its `\author@fmt`) is the binding's
`\lx@author@markup@class`, since a copy's refused `\author` records no `\author:redefined` for the kernel's own provide
list ("\snm undefined", 2 Errors per witness otherwise); and the sty binding's own `\affiliation` (the run of new
authors, or its label's), since a stand-in's copy is no raw class read for the kernel's class readers, which give the
class path's raw `\affiliation` to the frontmatter (it printed in the body). The class path is unchanged (its
`\lx@author@markup@class` provides what the refused `\author` list provides already). Witnesses 1905.11425, 2101.10506
(e-mails and addresses on each author), math0608476 (URLs, addresses, the `\thankstext` note), 1301.1466 (e-mails and
URLs; its affiliation kept; its three addresses printed at the end, each no author's, as below). An unlabelled `\address`
after `\end{frontmatter}` is no author's (review revCR3 finding 1): under the journal options that set
`\@addressatendtrue` (`aap`, imsart.sty:150 of 1301.1466's copy) imsart.sty stores each block (:1242-1252) and prints
them all at the end of the document (`\printaddresses`, :1269-1290), tied to no author, and the API's default owner, the
last author, took all three of 1301.1466's (crackle.tex:1109-1125, after its `\bibliography`). The shared `\address`
prints such a call where it is called, as `\printaddressnum` sets a block (`\address@size`, `{tabular}[t]{@{}l@{}}`;
the `env/frontmatter/after` hook marks the close); inside `{frontmatter}`, or labelled, it stays a contact. Under the
class binding too (the same markup). Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{imsart_renamed_sty_copy_reads_through_its_binding,imsart_address_after_frontmatter_prints_in_place}.tex`;
guards `perfect_kernel_batchcr3::{imsart_renamed_sty_copy_reads_through_its_binding,imsart_address_after_frontmatter_prints_in_place}`.

**CR4 (review revCR3b findings 1, 3 and NIT 4).** (1) In an address printed in place, no author's contact,
`\printead{e1,u1}` prints what imsart.sty's `\@@printead` prints (:506-519): each labelled address, "e-mail: " or "url: "
before it (none under `*`), `;~` between, in typewriter type, through the API's address reading (`\lx@address@printed`,
#972); `\printead[text]{…}` the text; a label no `\ead` gave "??", as `\saferef`. Inside the frontmatter it stays empty: the
address is the author's contact there. imsart.sty's `\ead` writes its label to the aux file (`\safelabel`) for the next
run's `\printead`, so the order does not matter in TeX; here the binding records each `\ead[label=…]{…}` at the
`\author` call (`record_eads`: the author is digested only at the frontmatter's flush, at the end of the document when no
`\maketitle` comes, after the addresses) and where `\ead` expands (`record_ead`), past any speculative run's rollback
(core `state::assign_value_past_rollback`: a rehearsal and a label's ink run undo every assignment, and TeX never takes
back what it wrote to a file). 1301.1466's three end blocks gain their six "e-mail:"/"url:" rows, as the PDF. (2) The

(3) Under `\@addressatendtrue` the in-place block is deferred to `\AtEndDocument`, as imsart.sty's `\enddocument` runs
`\printaddresses`: one called right after `\end{frontmatter}` prints after the body. Repros
`imsart_printead_in_address_at_end`, `imsart_unlabelled_address_is_the_runs`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batchcr4::{imsart_printead_in_address_at_end, imsart_unlabelled_address_is_the_runs}`;
`perfect_kernel_batchcr3::imsart_address_after_frontmatter_prints_in_place` now holds each block's "e-mail: …" row.

**Left** (pre-existing): imsart's `\and` between `\author`s in `{aug}` prints a stray centred "and" paragraph (int154x
alike).

**Known REDs (review revCR4b finding 2, synthetic):** the per-label attribution's `annotate=run` fallback does not end its run at the `author:N` contacts an earlier cited block made, so an uncited block also reaches authors an earlier block went to (`imsart_address_block_fallback_run_q1_red.tex`), and a block naming three authors but citing only `e2` goes to that one (`…_q2_red.tex`); no word lost.

### 989. A picture in a frontmatter field is kept as markup: inside `\author` a plain note of its own or in its line, inside a note that note's (CR8, CR8b)

**What.** The observer's lexer reads a pgf/TikZ picture (pgfsys-latexml.def's `\lxSVG@insertpicture`) as one Note event
of role `picture` (`events::PICTURE_NOTE`, `Lexer::walk_whatsit`), its text its text nodes' only (`ink_of`), never its
drawing's transforms and SVG path data. In an author block, `events::place_pictures` decides its place by its line: one
on a column's first line (the names') or ending a line goes out of the name, and an image (`\includegraphics`, the
Layout event of a whatsit with a graphic) becomes such a note too; one inside a later line, a run of text right after
it (past a font switch, a spanless Layout event: the first marked line after a bold names line switches back), is joined
to that run (and to the run right before it) as one Name whose span covers it, so the line's entry is written with the
picture in place, in source order. The reading attaches a picture note as any adjacent note (to the
name before it, in source order) and the writer writes it as a plain frontmatter `ltx:note` (`role="note"`, no thanks
class, no mark: `emit::picture_note_call`) holding the picture's tokens whole (`emit::item_call`'s picture branch), so
the `ltx:picture` and its `svg`, or the `ltx:graphics`, are kept. Every picture note is keyed by its place
(`plan::note_key`), and the relocation's one copy per label (`relocate`) compares no picture note (a `role="note"`
holding a picture or an image, its creator's own label) by its text: two pictures printing the same text are two notes;
any other note, a `\thanks` holding a logo too, is compared by its text as before. Inside a `\thanks` it is part of the note's text and is digested
with it. A span is its boxes' (`deep_span`), so it ends before what its call read past its last box and printed nothing
of: `emit::past_unprinted_tail` grows it over spaces, one `;` (`\tikz…;`; none when the span's last token is already
the path's `;`, as a text node's box reaches past it: `\tikz\node{Zebraword};; Bob` prints the second), the `\end{…}` of an environment the span opens
(`\end{tikzpicture}`) and the closers of the groups it leaves open (a `\thanks{…\tikz…;}`'s `}`), up to the next event's
start, never past a brace closing a group it does not open, stopping at the first other command or character (a glued
`\and`, `\\`, `,` is the block's separator, never the note's), trailing spaces not its own. With that tail the rewritten
picture keeps its `;` and the note's argument is balanced.

**Why.** User ruling 2026-11-10: a picture or a page-overlay notice inside `\author` is "a note, kept whole", never
read as a name. Perl (0 Errors on the witness) keeps it inside the personname. That placement is the divergence. pdflatex
prints the notice at the page foot and a drawing where it stands, which the in-line placement keeps.

**Witnesses** (int154t → CR8 → CR8b): 2404.13552 (a creator "1.00.00.01.0" and the notice's 21 words lost, 1 Warning → 6
creators, the notice a note of the last one, holding the picture, 0 frontmatter Warnings; CR8b: a plain note, no longer a
"thanks"). CR5's textless repro: the note "Zebra University M 0 0 L 39.37 0fill:none" ("note no argument") → "Zebra
University" with its picture. CR8b, images dropped silently before, kept: 2503.08161's three institute logos inside their
affiliations (CR8c: `polyu-logo.png`, on the first marked line after the bold names, was lost behind the font switch;
review revCR8b finding 1); 2107.13277's ORCID icons, 2208.11637's logo, 1905.00862's decorative bar, 2409.19094's first ORCID icon as
notes. Review revCR8's shapes: a `\and` glued to a picture was the word "and" in its note; two same-text pictures kept
one; a picture leading an affiliation line moved after it, its markup lost.

**Left** (pre-existing, recorded, not changed): a LaTeX `picture` environment in `\author` is read as text, as before
(`\begin{picture}(10,10)\put(0,0){Qwerty}\end{picture}` → the name "Ann Able Qwerty", the same words pdflatex prints). A
picture inside a name (`Ann \tikz\draw…; Able`) parts it in two creators (the base: 3 creators, 1 Error). An image in
a later line before a mark or an address stays a Layout event nothing writes, counted (below). The HTML of these notes is
#990.

Repros `sectioning-frontmatter/fm_picture_text_in_author_is_a_note`, `fm_picture_textless_in_author_is_a_note`,
`fm_picture_textless_in_thanks_stays_in_note`, `fm_picture_glued_to_a_separator_ends_the_note`,
`fm_picture_same_text_twice_two_notes`, `fm_picture_inside_affiliation_line_stays`, `fm_includegraphics_in_author`,
`fm_image_first_marked_line_after_bold_names`, `fm_picture_text_node_then_two_semicolons`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batchcr8::{picture_in_author_is_a_note_kept_whole, textless_picture_in_author_is_a_note,
textless_picture_in_thanks_stays_in_the_note, picture_glued_to_a_separator_ends_the_note,
two_same_text_pictures_are_two_notes, picture_inside_an_affiliation_line_stays_in_place, includegraphics_in_author_is_kept,
image_on_the_first_marked_line_is_kept, a_text_node_picture_takes_one_semicolon}`.

**A boxed line (CR10b).** color.sty's and xcolor.sty's `\fcolorbox` keeps its text in its `text` property (digested in
its `afterDigest` from an `Undigested` argument, printed by the pattern's `#text`: Perl color.sty.ltxml:108-117,
xcolor.sty.ltxml:878-888), which no reader of a field's ink walked — the lexer, the label and word readers, the
title-page check —, so an `\author` line boxed so printed nothing to the frontmatter: acl's
`\fcolorbox{white}{white}{$\{$\texttt{\href{mailto:…}{ann}, }…$\}$\texttt{@inf.ethz.ch}}` (2211.07344, 2305.15057) lost its
e-mails with 0 Warnings. The readers now walk a whatsit's printed properties (`util_text::printed_properties`: the
`alignment` rows and the `text`) beside its shown arguments and body, so the boxed line reads as the same line unboxed:
each author's e-mail, and the content check's one Warning on the brace-group spelling, the unboxed line's too (repro
`sectioning-frontmatter/fcolorbox_email_line_in_author`; guard `perfect_kernel_batchcr10b::fcolorbox_email_line_in_author`).

**An image before a URL, a mark or an address (IMG1, IMG1b, IMG1c; reviews revCR8c finding 2, revIMG1, revIMG1b).** An image leading a
link on a later line — a `role="url"` Contact event, `\url` or `\href` — past font switches and any gap (a space,
`\quad`, `\hspace{3cm}`, however wide, and fill glue: `\hfill`, `\hspace{\fill}`, `\hskip 0pt plus 1fil`) is that
link's: `place_pictures` grows the contact's span over it (the image stays an event of its own), and the contact is
written from its tokens with the icon before the link, as pdflatex prints it — 2503.08161's `\includegraphics{hf-logo.png} \texttt{\small\url{…}}` (its four URL copies) and 2601.17879's
`\github \quad \url{…}`, both dropped with 0 Warnings before; 2505.21327's `{\github\ \texttt{\url{…}}}` lines, which a
note in place merged into one affiliation (CR8c, reverted), are byte-identical. An e-mail printed as a link
(`\href{mailto:…}{…}`, `\url{ann@x.org}`) is such a link, so a photo before it is written inside its `<contact
role="email">`: the content kept, pdflatex printing the two side by side as for any link (repro
`fm_photo_before_mailto_is_in_the_email`, a known shape, catalog only). Fill glue parts the two in print only by the
column's slack (pdflatex: the image at the line's left edge and the link at its right when a wider line sets the column,
side by side when the image's line is the widest); that offset is a placement detail, so the image stays with the link,
content before placement (review revIMG1b finding 1; repro `fm_image_hfill_before_url_is_kept`). The contact as
written holds a space between the graphic and the `<ref>` for `\hfill` and none for `\hspace{\fill}` or `\hskip 0pt plus
1fil`, so in HTML the image touches the link there; no content is lost (guard `image_parted_from_a_url_by_fill_is_kept`,
its `between` column; revIMG1c). One leading a mark, an e-mail not printed as a link
(`\texttt{ann@x.org}`) or an address has no place: a note there made the mark-led affiliation its plain text (+2
Warnings), and a run printing an address is written as the e-mail's text, so `place_pictures` joins no address run. Such
a picture is counted: an image has no word for the word check (`lost_inks`), so the check has a picture half, span
coverage — `Written::unwritten_pictures` counts every image or picture note of a block whose span lies inside no written
item's span (items a ruling dropped aside; no span, counted), and `emit::warn_unwritten_pictures` raises one Warning per
block ("holds no place for N picture(s) its author block prints; they are lost") unless the block is written whole. An
item's span there is the span the emit writes it from, its entry's (`resolver::words::entry_span_in`, the emitter's
`repart::entry_span` reads the same), read by the emit's own key (`plan::written_keys`: an ORCID by its identifier, a
picture note by its place; review revIMG1b finding 2): an affiliation running on past an image to a link, `Zebra University,
\includegraphics{…} \url{…}`, holds the image (review revIMG1 finding 1: its source span alone gave a false loss Warning).
It reads the items written, not the join: `Web: \includegraphics{…} \url{…}` is written as one affiliation holding the
image, and the link label pass (`insert::kind_link_and_grade_contacts`, `strip_before_link`) then strips it with the
label's text — counted there by its own Warning ("drops N picture(s) printed between the label … and its link"), each
picture once, a `ltx:graphics` inside a `ltx:picture` its picture's (review revIMG1b finding 3); keeping
it in the contact is that pass's change, proposed apart. Routes the check does not see, enumerated from `check_blocks` (it walks
`live_blocks`' `Outcome::Events` author blocks, their top-level events) and from the emit's item writers (`emit.rs`
`item_call`'s text branches): (1) an image a later line's run of text joins (`place_pictures`' Name join) leaves no
picture event, the run's words being the word check's; (2) a picture inside a note's `inner` events (`\thanks{…}`, a
footnote) is the note's, not iterated; (3) a block written whole is not checked (its tokens keep its pictures); (4) an API
call's entries (`\affiliation{…}`, `\institute{…}`, `\IEEEauthorblockA{…}`, any `Outcome` not `Events`) are not walked;
(5) an item written by its text (the e-mail branch, "a macro's span", "span letters differ") is held by its span though
its text drops a picture inside it — a possible under-count, unprobed on a real paper (revIMG1's `\texttt{img addr}` is
counted, as its image is a Layout event outside the e-mail's span). Repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/fm_image_before_url_is_in_the_url`, `fm_image_before_mark_is_counted`,
`fm_image_before_address_is_counted`, `fm_image_before_labelled_url_is_counted`, `author_icon_macro_quad_before_url`,
`fm_image_inside_affiliation_before_url_is_kept`, `fm_image_quad_inside_affiliation_before_url_is_kept`,
`fm_image_glued_inside_affiliation_before_url_is_kept`, `fm_image_hfill_before_url_is_kept`,
`fm_image_hspace_fill_before_url_is_kept`, `fm_image_hskip_fil_before_url_is_kept`,
`fm_picture_holding_image_before_labelled_url_is_counted_once`; guards
`perfect_kernel_batchimg1::{image_before_a_url_is_in_the_url, image_before_a_mark_is_counted,
image_before_an_address_is_counted, image_after_a_url_label_is_counted, image_inside_an_affiliation_before_a_url_is_kept,
image_parted_from_a_url_by_fill_is_kept}`, `perfect_kernel_batch77y::icon_parted_from_its_link_goes_with_it`.

### 990. An unmarked frontmatter note renders inline, with no dagger (CR8c)

**What.** In HTML an author's picture note — an `ltx:note` with `role="note"`, no `@mark`, no untyped tag, holding a
picture or graphics (the meta XSLT's `ltx:creator/ltx:note[@role='note' and not(@mark) and not(ltx:tags/ltx:tag[not(@role)])
and (.//ltx:picture or .//ltx:graphics)]`, `LaTeXML-meta-xhtml.xsl`) — is a span holding its content inline: no
`ltx_note_mark` (†), no `ltx_note_outer`/`ltx_note_content` (which `LaTeXML.css` hides until hover, so the content would be
invisible), no "note: " type label (#989's notes; 2404.13552, 2107.13277). Only those: a leftover-ink note with no mark that
holds text — a `\titlenote`'s "Corresponding author. Email: …" (1003.2281, pdflatex prints ∗ and a footnote), `\pacs` codes
(0803.0204, 1009.5642, printed under the abstract) — stands for a mark pdflatex prints or a line printed elsewhere and keeps
the dagger: the first, broader rule inlined those 51 notes of 5,397 papers (review revCR8c finding 1).

**Perl behavior.** The meta XSLT's `ltx:note` template (`LaTeXML-meta-xhtml.xsl`, `note-mark`) falls back to † for a
note with no `@mark` and hides the content behind it. Perl writes no such frontmatter notes (it keeps a picture in the
personname), so the fallback reached them only here.

**Why.** User ruling 2026-11-10, "No dagger for unmarked notes": pdflatex prints these with no mark, where they stand (an
ORCID icon before a name, 2107.13277; 2404.13552's page-overlay notice). A `\thanks` note (role `thanks`, #156) keeps
its dagger: it stands for the footnote mark pdflatex prints, which the note leaves implicit. jheppub's `\note` is a
contact (`\lx@add@contact[role=note]`), unchanged (1203.0413, 2111.03202: HTML byte-identical).

**Witnesses.** 2404.13552 (the notice's picture note: no †, shown inline); 2107.13277 (five ORCID icons, inline spans).
Guard `perfect_kernel_batchcr8::an_unmarked_frontmatter_note_renders_inline_without_a_dagger`.

### 993. An author call is cut at its separators: the rehearsal reads `\and` and its family, a break, a wide space by meaning; the bindings' token splitters cut by spelling — absorbs #36 #48 #445 #765 #804 #840 #897 #994 #995 #1009

**Rule.** The names of an author block are parted where the rehearsal's digested list holds a separator event: a
`Sep(And)` whatever spells it (literal, held in a macro, a `\let` copy, `\csname and\endcsname`), a line break, or the
horizontal space pdflatex sets between names. A binding asks the same question by meaning through one query, and a
binding's marked list is cut by the API's Cut as the binding declares it. The token splitters a binding calls on its
arguments (`split_tokens`, `\lx@splitting`) cut by spelling, as Perl's `SplitTokens` does: today's code, kept as generic
binding utilities (DG 2026-11-15).

**Perl.** `SplitTokens` matches the separator tokens before digestion (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:114-140, `@authorsplits`
:679-680 `\and \And \AND , " and " \quad \qquad`; `Equals` by meaning, Common/Object.pm:100-103), so a separator a macro
hides, a wrapper prints, or spaces alone set, is not seen; " and " only between two space tokens (:678).
**TeX.** latex.ltx:17219 `\and` ends the author's `tabular` column; a control word swallows the spaces after it, so
`Ann\space and Bob` prints " and " (tex.web §354).

**Sub-rules**
- *The query* (formerly #995): `observer/separators.rs:182 argument_separators` (Rust) and `\lx@fm@separators`
  (`:257`, TeX: `kernel`/`binding`/`raw`, `unread`) read the `Sep(And)` events at nest 0 and whether each meaning is the
  kernel separator's; `:284 kernel_separator_runs`, `:321 split_at_kernel_separators`. The rehearsal binds `\and`,
  `\And`, `\AND` always (`rehearsal.rs:593 ALWAYS_BOUND`), so the meaning is read at the call site, outside it.
- *The cut*: the emitter cuts the rehearsed block, or an API creator call, at its own `Sep(And)` events
  (`emit.rs:4558 cut_at_separators`); a `\let` copy of a separator or a note command is bound by its meaning
  (formerly #994, SEP1).
- *Columns*: `\alignauthor` opens a column (`rehearsal.rs:715`; sig-alternate.cls:283; formerly #445).
- *Space-parted names* (formerly #897, #840, #765): a wide space between names parts them (`resolver/lines.rs:1137
  only_gap_between`, `:1150 name_continues_at_gap`, `:1352 gap_inside_one_command`); a space a name sets before its
  own mark stays the name's; " and " beside a control word, a break or a mark is a separator.
- *Token splits by spelling* (the bindings' utilities and Perl's fallback; DG 2026-11-15: "split_tokens in particular has
  generic utility for bindings", so they stay spelling splitters): `tokens.rs:96 split_tokens` (21 call sites) does not
  cut inside balanced `(…)` (`:39 paren_close_offset`) or before a closing environment (`classify/preprocess.rs:233
  environment_closes_ahead`; formerly #36); `\lx@splitting` at `\\` drops the break's `*` and `[…]`
  (`defs/general.rs:178`; formerly #804). #996's `\@author` tail also cuts by spelling (RED below).
- *Font wrappers*: the reading sees the commas inside `\textbf{A$^1$, B$^1$, C$^1$}` as digested, so no wrapper hides a
  separator from it (formerly #48, whose token rule was the deleted `split_author_line`'s).
- *A binding's marked list* (formerly #1009): `defs/frontmatter_api.rs:84 cut_list`, each mark shown as written.

### 1001. A note an author's name or contact holds is the creator's, beside it (FN1)

**Perl.** `\footnotemark[<n>]` makes its `ltx:note` (`role="footnotemark"`) where it stands, and `relocateFootnote`
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:498-520) fills that node with the `\footnotetext[<n>]` content. After an author's name
the node is inside `ltx:personname`: `<personname>Bob Baker<note mark="1" role="footnote">…Note B.</note></personname>`,
so a reader of the name gets "Bob Baker * * footnote * Note B." Our port did the same on every class route (article,
IEEEtran, authblk, llncs, elsarticle, revtex4-2, OmniBus; RT1's F17; witness 2104.12292).

**Rust.** The `ltx:personname` close, and the close of an `ltx:contact` whose parent is the `ltx:creator`, move each
`ltx:note` they hold (one not nested in another note) out to the creator, right after the name or contact, in order:
its `mark`, tags and id kept, as a `\thanks` note sits beside the name (`queue_digest.rs` `lift_notes_beside`, called
first in `frontmatter_api.rs`'s two hooks). A wrapper that held the mark alone and is left empty
(`Bob Baker{\small\footnotemark[2]}`) is removed, and the text a lifted note or wrapper stood between is joined
(`join_texts_after`), so the whole-name bold rule and the punctuation strip see the name alone and trim its end whole
(`Kent-Andre Mardal \footnotemark[2] \footnotemark[3]`, 1612.03574). A contact still in the `role="pending"` holder of
annotations placed by label is left alone (a note lifted there had no label and was orphaned, three Warnings and the
marks lost on revtex's `\affiliation{\footnotemark[1]Univ A}`, 1607.07280); its clone placed in the creator closes again
and is lifted there. The note is moved, not copied, so `relocate_footnote` still finds it when the text comes after the
names. An unpaired mark (a `\footnotemark` whose text prints another number, or one naming a `\thanks` note) moves
the same way, still `role="footnotemark"`. Reason: semantic markup — the name holds the name; no word is dropped or
added. `\footnote{…}` in `\author` was already the creator's `role="note"` contact (`\lx@add@note`).

Not changed: two authors sharing one `\footnotemark[1]` and one `\footnotetext[1]` still get the text twice, once
per mark (Perl's pairing, and `resolver/post.rs` `answer_note_texts`'s for 1405.4582): a pairing rule, Known RED
`sectioning-frontmatter/author_shared_footnotemark_text_written_twice_red.tex`. ptephy's `\name` token writer's own
marks and labels (`class-bindings/ptephy_*_footnotemark_*_red.tex`) stay RED: its notes are now beside the name, its
label text is not this rule's. `\textsuperscript{\footnotemark[1]}` in an article name prints a mark with no note
(the text a document footnote, as pdflatex prints the two apart). An endnotes mark (`role="endnotemark"`) moves the
same way; a `$^,$` printed between two marks stays at the name's end (`Bob Baker<sup>,</sup>`,
`perfect_kernel_batchne2::a_mark_after_its_names_note_stays_with_it`). Known RED, base's and not the lift's:
`sectioning-frontmatter/{author_href_footnotemark_mark_written_twice_red,author_footnotemark_texts_take_a_sized_marks_size_red}.tex`. The lift's own trade (revFN1 finding 1, kept by the main session): where the name holds printed content after the
note (`Bob Baker\footnotemark[2]$^2$`, pdflatex "Bob Baker†2"), that content now precedes the mark — no word or mark
lost, two marks' order changed (2505.14146, 2203.10939): Known RED `sectioning-frontmatter/author_note_mark_before_sup_order_red.tex`;
the `$^,$` left at the name's end: `author_mark_separator_comma_left_in_the_name_red.tex`. Base's, not the lift's:
`author_footnotemark_mid_name_splits_the_creator_red.tex`, `author_boxed_and_multimark_names_double_a_note_and_drop_a_dagger_red.tex`.

A block written whole (one creator, the Warning saying so) holds its notes after the joint name, in order, each with
its mark (main session's ruling on FN1, 2026-11-11): `perfect_kernel_batchne2::a_mark_on_no_name_writes_the_block_whole`,
`perfect_kernel_batchcl9::overlapping_names_keep_the_macros_marks`, `perfect_kernel_batchcr7::a_split_stating_a_false_owner_keeps_the_block_whole`,
`perfect_kernel_batchpb::a_split_losing_a_name_keeps_the_block_whole`. Twenty guards that pinned the note inside the
name were updated with this reason (FN1b report).

Guards `perfect_kernel_batchfn1::{footnotemark_note_is_the_creators_beside_the_name,
footnotemark_in_an_affiliation_is_the_creators_note_beside_it, footnotemark_in_a_wrapper_leaves_the_name_alone,
footnote_in_the_author_is_the_creators_note_contact, spaced_marks_leave_the_name_end_trimmed}`, and
`perfect_kernel_batchfms2a2r7::a_notes_mark_is_answered_by_its_footnotemark` (the pending holder: 0 Warnings); repros
`sectioning-frontmatter/{author_footnotemark_note_is_the_creators_beside_the_name,author_footnotemark_note_beside_the_name_omnibus,author_footnotemark_text_before_maketitle_beside_the_name,author_bare_footnotemark_beside_the_name,affiliation_footnotemark_note_beside_the_contact,author_footnotemark_in_a_wrapper_beside_the_name,author_footnote_in_the_name_is_the_creators_note,author_two_footnotemarks_name_end_trimmed}.tex`.

### 1002. `\rownum` is colortbl's count, as TeX has it, not Perl's row-number macro (GA1c)

Perl's xcolor binding defines `\rownum` as a macro returning the current alignment row (`xcolor.sty.ltxml:744-748`), so
`\number\rownum` in a tabular without `\rowcolors` prints the row (`a1 c2`). In TeX `\rownum` is colortbl's count
(colortbl.sty:269-275, `\c@rownum` the same register; xcolor.sty's `[table]` loads colortbl and defines no `\rownum`),
stepped only by `\rowcolors`' row hook (colortbl.sty:261), so outside `\rowcolors` it reads 0 (`a0 c0`, pdflatex). Since
GA1c the colortbl binding ports colortbl.sty:269-275 as written and Perl's macro is kept as `\lx@xcolor@rownum`, which
`\rownum` is let to only where no `\rownum` exists (`latexml_package/src/package/xcolor_sty.rs:1604-1631`): one count in
every load order of xcolor `[table]`, colortbl and tabularray (whose `\c@rownum`, tabularray.sty:185, is the same name),
so tabularray's per-cell `\c@rownum` is a register and its cells print as pdflatex (2601.01074, 2409.12172: 55 and 154
`expected:register` Warnings under GA1b). A divergence from Perl, faithful to TeX (review revGA1c). Residual (RED): after
a `\rowcolors` table `\rownum` holds the row count where TeX holds one more. Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchga1::an_undefined_counter_register_is_the_error_tex_raises` (both xcolor `[table]` load orders,
colortbl after tabularray, `colortbl_therownum`).

### 1003. REVTeX's post-`\maketitle` switch-off reaches only a repeated author block, whose new words are counted, not kept (RB1, RB1c, RB1d)

**TeX.** `\frontmatter@maketitle` (revtex4-2.cls:2670-2684, revtex4-1.cls:2649-2662, revtex4.cls:4709-4717) lets
`\affiliation`, `\author`, `\email` and `\thanks` to `\@gobble` and `\and` to `\relax`, so whatever the document gives
them after `\maketitle` prints nothing. **Perl** queues a repeated block's calls after the title block and puts every
repeated contact on the last author (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1220).

**Rust** (revtex4_cls.rs `switch_off_author_block_after_maketitle`, under revtex4, revtex4-1 and revtex4-2 only, not
AASTeX's own switch-off, aastex701.cls:13231-13266). `\maketitle` lets only `\author`, to `\lx@revtex@repeated@author`,
which lets `\and`, `\affiliation`, `\email` and `\thanks` locally (a repeat's `\author` inside a group switches off only
to its end, where TeX's switch lasts) and gobbles its own argument. So:
- a block repeated after `\maketitle` (a supplement's, an erratum's) drops its names and contacts from its first
  `\author` on (2401.15572, 1801.07635, 1812.00931, 2510.13035, 2602.09975, 2307.07324, 2001.07542);
- an `\affiliation`, `\email` or `\thanks` used only after `\maketitle` keeps its text, as Perl and int159b do: authored
  text is kept though pdflatex prints none of it (FIDELITY_CHARTER §2; 1309.4768, 1106.2389, 2304.09163);
- `\title` and `\date` stay the kernel's and print as text (2606.04868); a document's own `\maketitle` (2509.25344) or
  `\frontmatter@maketitle` (2111.12484) wins; the setters' locks lift with the switch, so a later `\renewcommand` takes
  effect as after the class's `\let` (2412.14256); a subfile's group undoes it.

**Counted loss.** Each gobbled argument, names included, goes to `ledger::record_switched_off_call`, which feeds the
frontmatter content check (`Ledger::unrecorded`) only the words and addresses no earlier ledger entry holds, read as the
check reads them: each entry's text both as spelled (`content_text`) and as its rehearsal printed it, an accent or a
dotless letter read past matched by `resolver::placed::reads_as`. A pure repeat, also one spelled through a macro
(`\UX` for `Universit\"at X`) or with braced accents, feeds nothing and warns nothing (the gobbled `\email` reads
its argument Semiverbatim — `_` and `@` other as the live one reads them, `%` a comment as under TeX's `\@gobble` —
so `ann_x@x.org` stays one address); a new name ("Dan Doe"), a new
`\thanks` (1206.0114), the new words of a variant address (1903.12442: "120 C DK Munkegade Ny", not the words it
shares) or a repeated name's initials (2305.19055 "A C J P R", 1903.12442 "M T") raise the check's "N words … missing"
Warning naming them. Keeping them needs the repeat matched to the creators it repeats, a
second mechanism: RED `sectioning-frontmatter/{revtex_repeated_block_new_words_kept_red,revtex_repeated_block_new_author_kept_red}.tex`.
Known RED (pre-existing): a repeat's `\altaffiliation` stays live and lands on the last author, where TeX's
`\@AF@join@error` prints nothing (`revtex_repeated_block_altaffiliation_on_last_author_red.tex`).
Known REDs from review revRB1d (synthetic, uncounted): a new name or address spelled through a macro is not read
(the gobbled argument is read as spelled; `revtex_repeated_block_macro_spelled_new_words_red`); a new name whose words all
print elsewhere is held word by word (`revtex_repeated_block_new_name_of_held_words_red`); a repeat's `\author` in a group
switches off only to the group's end, so a following `\email` lands on the last author
(`revtex_repeated_block_in_a_group_email_on_last_author_red`).

Guard `perfect_kernel_batchrb1::revtex_maketitle_switches_the_author_block_off` (one row per shape, exact Error and
Warning counts, whole creators, the body text).

### 1006. `--verbose` prints the un-featured `Debug:` traces, and every `Debug` line carries a `Debug:<target> ` prefix (DBG1, DBG2)

**Perl.** `Debug($message)` prints the bare message (`_printlines`, `Common/Error.pm` L171-183); its trace calls are
guarded `if $LaTeXML::DEBUG{feature}` (L467), so `--verbose` alone prints no trace and `--debug=frontmatter` prints
`FRONT Add …`.

**Rust.** A `Debug!` record without a feature (`primitive invoke for …`) prints under `--verbose` (`util/logger.rs`
`DEBUG_ALL`), and a feature's record only under its `--debug` (`DebugFeature!`). Each `Debug` line reads
`Debug:<target> <message>` (`Debug:frontmatter FRONT Add …`), as the other severities name their category. Reason:
the un-featured traces are Rust's own instrumentation with no Perl feature to enable them, and the prefix keeps them
apart from `Info:` lines in a log. An undeclared `--debug` feature is named at the end of the run, before the verdict,
as Perl's `CheckDebuggable` (`check_debuggable`, `common/error.rs`); its known list holds only the features Rust
declares (`frontmatter`; Perl's `DebuggableFeature` calls declare 15: `alignment`, `modes`, `size`, `svg`, …), so a
`DebugFeature!` site ported from Perl registers its feature through `debuggable_feature`. A Rhai binding's
`Debug(message)` and `Debug(cat, obj, message)` are `Debug!` (DG 2026-11-14): printed only under `--verbose`, counted
either way, where Perl's `Debug` prints unconditionally. Guards
`cluster_cli::debug_feature_scope::debug_feature_prints_only_its_feature`,
`script_bindings::tests::diagnostics_surface_info_notes_progress_and_fatal`.

### 1007. calc's names inside a pgfmath expression: calc's value and a Warning per parse (EB1)

**TeX.** TL 2025 pgf does not know calc's `\widthof`, `\heightof`, `\depthof`, `\maxof`, `\minof`, `\real`, `\ratio` inside a
pgfmath expression: pdflatex reports "Unknown function" / "Undefined control sequence" (4 to 19 `!` per probe) and computes 0.
**Perl.** Binds the seven names before expanding and returns calc's value silently (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1225). **Rust.** Expands
first, binds the names only where one survives (pgf's order, DTL1g), returns calc's value, and raises one Warning per parse
(`pgfmath_code_tex.rs`). Reason: the staged rule (2) — only TeX errs, and the recovery carries the meaning the author wrote.
Guard `error_boundary::perfect_kernel_error_boundary` (the calc rows and their safe twin).
**Target (DG 2026-11-15, post-cutoff with an A/B; SYNC row R line PGF1007):** follow pgf — "Unknown function" and 0,
`calc_compat_expand` (pgfmath_code_tex.rs:2247) retired; today's code is the above.

### 1008. A `cmd/<name>/<hook>` hook on a command LaTeXML binds does not run: a Warning for the document's code, an Info for a class's or package's (QA47A)

**Perl.** `\AddToHook` is a no-op (latex_base.pool.ltxml:833): no generic command hook runs, none is reported.
**pdflatex.** `\begin{document}` runs `\@kernel@after@begindocument` (latex.ltx:9513), whose
`\__hook_cmd_begindocument_code:` (:6865-6873) patches every delayed `cmd/<name>/<hook>` into the macro and later ones at
once (`\__hook_patch_command:Nnn`, :6888); a non-macro errs "Generic hooks cannot be added to '\mylen'".
**Rust.** `\document` runs both kernel begin-document lists, so hooks on TeX macros run as in pdflatex, and a register
errs as pdflatex. A command LaTeXML binds (a constructor or primitive, a locked or Rust-bodied macro, one reading
LaTeXML's argument types) has no macro to patch until the macro faces (BM Q3.8): the override of
`\__hook_patch_command:Nnn` (`latex_constructs_rust_only.rs`) skips the patch and remembers the hook. Each piece of
code on it is reported once, by its owner: `Warning:hook` for the document's (`\__hook_toplevel~<hook>`, a label naming
no loaded class or package, `\AddToHookNext`'s `\__hook_next~<hook>`), else `Info:hook`, as a class's redefinition of a
locked command is dropped with an Info (`state.rs`). The message names the command without "LaTeXML's binding of" when its definition is
the document's (`\newtheorem`'s `\thm`). `\meaning` prints a macro's prefixes in `\escapechar` (tex.web §1295), which
ltcmdhooks reads (latex.ltx:7011-7016; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1229). Code stored before the patch (the preamble's, patched at
`\begin{document}`) is read at the patch; code stored after it — added from `\begin{document}`'s own hooks or in the body,
where the kernel patches before it stores, or added to a hook already usable, which the kernel never patches again
(latex.ltx:5443-5475) — at lthooks' store steps (`\__hook_hook_gput_code_do:nnn`, :5355ff; `\__hook_gput_next_do:nn`,
:6332). KOMA-Script 3.49 adds `cmd/@startsection/before` from `begindocument/end` under its class's label
(scrartcl.cls:3306-3313, scrbook:3498, scrreprt:3531): an Info on any TeX Live (KOMA1).
**Why**: pdflatex runs the hook code; we cannot without the macro faces, so a lost word of the document's is counted
(Warning); a class's or package's hook (memoir.cls:5832-5833 `cmd/end@float/before`; projlib-author.sty's
`cmd/@author/…`, whose lines the binding carries as contacts) is the binding's business, as its locked-command
redefinitions are.
**Witnesses**: 2602.09577 (`cmd/appendix` runs), 2510.06714, 2411.13565 (changes' `\added`/`\deleted`/`\replaced`: 3
Warnings), 2511.21986, 2603.08400, 2607.15091 (memoir: 2 Infos).
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batchqa47a::batchqa47a_command_hook_rows` (rows `command_hook_on_a_binding_is_counted`,
`command_hook_owner_sets_its_severity`, `command_hook_on_a_register_errs`, `command_hook_added_at_begindocument_end`,
`command_hook_stored_after_its_patch`, `command_hook_a_package_adds_in_the_body`); the memoir pins in `perfect_kernel_batch56`,
`perfect_kernel_batch68x`, `perfect_kernel_batch72b` count no Warning for the class's hooks.
**Open** (post-merge, QAHK): the owner is read from the label, so a document's own hook labelled with a loaded
package's name is an Info and its lost word goes uncounted (RED `macro-state/command_hook_a_document_label_names_a_package_red`).
`\@currname` at the store step is no fix: a class's code added from `begindocument/end` (KOMA-Script 3.49) is stored with
it empty.

### 1011. After caption loads, `\@makecaption` is a shorthand-free wrapper calling the format it replaced (CAP1)

**TeX.** caption.sty:243-250, :270 `\let\@makecaption\caption@makecaption`, whose body ends in caption's own `\caption@@make`; a
class's or the kernel's format is gone, and a `cmd/@makecaption` hook patches a body with no shorthand character (under
babel-spanish the kernel's `>\hsize` cannot be retokenized, latex.ltx:7108-7140). **Perl.** Caption's binding never touches
`\@makecaption` (its `\AddToHook` is a no-op). **Rust.** `caption_sty.rs` copies the replaced macro by value
(`\lx@caption@ORI@makecaption`, once, at caption's first full load — also a full load after caption3 alone, `\lx@caption@full@load`)
and lets `\@makecaption` to a `\caption@makecaption` that calls it, so the hook patch succeeds as in TeX and direct callers (xtab,
sidecap, a document's `\@makecaption{…}{…}`) keep the class's format as before. `\meaning\@makecaption` prints
`…\lx@caption@ORI@makecaption {#1}{#2}` where pdflatex prints caption's `…\caption@nobreak …`. **Why**: caption's `\caption@@make`
is a stub in the binding (it prints only the text), so its body would cost a direct caller the label. **Witnesses**: 2401.04032,
2505.14646, 2507.23020, 2403.14646, 2509.09422, 2508.16476, 2406.02775, 2406.11934, 2304.01093, 2408.05897, 2408.03946 (asmeconf +
spanish: 2 false Errors each gone). **Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batchqa47a::batchqa47a_command_hook_rows` (rows
`command_hook_on_makecaption_*`). **Open**: a plain repeat `\usepackage{caption}` after floatrow's caption3
(`command_hook_on_makecaption_caption_repeat_without_options_red`); code on a `cmd/@makecaption` hook never runs, since LaTeXML's
`\caption` does not go through `\@makecaption` (`command_hook_on_makecaption_code_never_runs_red`, post-merge QAHK).

### 1013. cmpj's `\refaddr` marks print as TeX's second run (CMPJ1)

**TeX.** cmpj's `\refaddr{la,lb}` (cmpj2.sty:557-570; cmpj.sty:443-456, cmpj3.sty:653-669) prints each key's `\ref`
once the .aux has defined `r@<key>`, a bold "?" and a Warning before; `\addresses{\addr{la} … \addr{lb} …}` is one
`enumerate`, each `\addr` an `\item\label` (cmpj2.sty:543-555). **Perl.** No binding: the raw package's first-run
branch, every name "?" (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1233). **Rust.** `cmpj_sty.rs` (registered for cmpj, cmpj2, cmpj3) reads
the real package — the paper's copy first, with the document's options — and redefines only `\@@refadx` as its
second-run branch (`\hbox{\ref{key}}` per key, `,\penalty\@m` between), the converged state LaTeXML models for `\ref`.
The `\@address` store reaches the frontmatter as it did raw (`\lx@package@loaded@raw`, so the inner read handles the
options). **The list cut per `\item` (CMPJ2).** An API entry that is one `enumerate` whose items each step the counter and
hold their own `\label` is cut per item (`events::item_led_pieces`: the lexer's Layout event `item` for an untagged
`\enumerate@item@`, `item[]` for a tagged one; decided on the reading's events of the call for both the resolver's `api` and the emitter,
`split_pieces_as` — the writer's rehearsal at a later flush reads the meanings then, `\ukrainianpart`'s bare `\addr`,
cmpj2.sty:649, 1212.6367): each item an entry keyed by its label (`api:ref-label`), written as the list's opening
tokens, `\setcounter{\@listctr}` to one below the value the digestion stepped the item's counter to, the item, and the
list's close (`emit::list_item_tokens`), so it keeps its number and tag as pdflatex prints them where the list sets or
steps its counter (revCMPJ, CMPJ3: `\setcounter{enumi}{3}` after the opening under `\Alph`, D E F where counting the
items before it gave D B C; a `\stepcounter` in item 1, 1 3 4). The value is the `\enumerate@item@` whatsit's
`counter_value` (not in Perl), the `item` event's label — the list the innermost environment around the items as the digestion's frames say
it (`Field::environments`, a close inside a macro too); an item that is no balanced run is its text, counted (a group
across two items: RED `cmpj_address_list_group_across_items_red`). In an emitted entry a
`\label` naming a counter step made inside the entry (`refstep_in_scope` against the step in scope where
`digest_frontmatter_item` starts) is `\lx@label`, as LaTeX's `\label` names `\@currentlabel`: the item carries
`labels=` and the names' `\ref`s resolve; any other stays the emitter's, dropped (OD #980). A list the cut does not
read (a tagged `\item[a]`, an unlabelled item, ink outside the list) stays one entry, each name requesting part of it
holding it all, counted by the Warning "places an entry holding N label targets … whole"
(`warn_whole_entry_of_keyed_parts`; RED `cmpj_address_list_tagged_item_kept_whole_red`). The renamed copies (cmpj2e.sty
0903.4566, cmp2em.sty cond-mat0511115) stay raw: RED `cmpj_renamed_copy_refaddr_prints_question_marks_red` (their
list, cut too, on the nameless creator). The second title page's own `\addresses` (`\ukrainianpart`, 1212.6367) is not
its names' — RED `cmpj_ukrainianpart_addresses_of_the_second_title_red`. An item placed on several names carries the
same `labels=` on each copy, so an HTML `\ref` links to the last copy (1212.6367: J. Ilnytskyi's "2" to A.
Trokhymchuk's) — kept. Coverage: the cut's generality rests on synthetic probes (amsart, revtex, llncs, elsarticle, a
nested list, unlabelled items, itemize, enumitem, an unknown class) and on the six cmpj witnesses below; CMPJ2's A/B
papers with an `enumerate` in a frontmatter block did not reach the cut.

### 1014. A varwidth box measures its widest line (VARW)

**TeX.** varwidth.sty `\endvarwidth` sets the box at its widest line's natural width, at most the given one. **Perl.**
`\varwidth` = `\minipage` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1234). **Rust.** varwidth_sty.rs's `\varwidth` sets `minipage:natural_width`
(`\lx@vwid@setup`) before `\minipage`, as the package runs `\@vwid@setup` from the minipage's `\@minipagerestore`; the minipage
takes the flag at its begin (so a nested box does not) and, after its body, `minipage_takes_natural_width` sizes the body with
`compute_boxes_size`'s `natural_width` option (the stacked lines' widest width instead of the paragraph width) and sets
`width` to the lesser. Every reader takes that width: `\wd`, `\resizebox`, pgf/TikZ and tcolorbox, and the XML `width`,
which the foreignObject of a TikZ node and the float panel grid read. A box narrower than given also carries `cssstyle`
`width:max-content;max-width:<given>`: the HTML sizes it as varwidth does, from the browser's own text, since a CSS width at
our metric estimate would wrap a line the PDF does not (and `fit-content` shrinks to a `\resizebox`'s scaled width, wrapping
its cells); it rides the lone child a box folds into (a `tabular`, a figure's `block`). **Witnesses**: algxpar-doc (784 → 0 Errors),
2401.12710 (310 → 11, the 299 overflows and 23 empty ▷ gone), 2507.12476 (Table 1's cells drawn at their content, the table
~1.15 times its column in Chrome; VARW drew each cell 345pt wide, the table ~3 times the column). **Guards**:
`perfect_kernel_batchvarw::{varwidth_takes_its_widest_line, varwidth_html_follows_its_content}`. **Open** (post-merge,
`boxes-groups/varwidth_lists_and_displays_measure_red.tex`): a list (itemize, center) inside is measured at its full width;
a display inside draws in HTML at the given width, its table's `max-width:100%` filling the `max-content` box
(`varwidth_display_draws_at_given_width_red`); two varwidth panels under `\hfill` sit together (the panel grid reads the
measured width);
a numbered display and a display opening the box measure without TeX's centring shift; `\hfill` sizes as an interword space.
Also `varwidth_colour_at_its_start_keeps_the_given_width_red` (a leading `\color` keeps the line at the given width in
TeX), `varwidth_inline_box_beside_text_measures_the_line_red` (an inline minipage and the text after it are one line), and
`colour_boxes_measure_their_frame_red` (`\fcolorbox` measures 0pt, `\colorbox` without `\fboxsep`; not varwidth's).

### 1015. "Is this package loaded" is `\ver@<file>`, one answer on every load path (GA2)

**TeX.** latex.ltx:18397-18402 `\@ifl@aded`: `\@ifpackageloaded{X}` is true when `\ver@X.sty` is defined and not `\relax`,
whoever defined it — the file's `\ProvidesPackage`, another file's mark (floatrow.sty:34 `ver@float.sty`, xkvutils.tex:71
`ver@keyval.sty`), a document's `\@namedef{ver@…}` — and false after a removal (fontenc.sty's tail, `\let\ver@X\relax`).
**Perl.** `\@ifl@aded` reads the loader's records, `X.sty_loaded` or `X.sty.ltxml_loaded` (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:946-953, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1236),
which a binding clears so that the next request runs it again (aa.cls.ltxml:57, while `\ver@amsmath.sty` stays): after
today's aa.cls (v9.4 :201 loads amsmath) `\@ifpackageloaded{amsmath}` is false, and a document's own mark counts for
nothing. **Rust.** `state::file_loaded` (with `package_loaded`, `class_loaded`) reads `\ver@<file>`; `\@ifl@aded` and every
binding that asks whether a package is loaded ask it (sect07's amsmath `\nonumber`, with the record: a document's
`\let\ver@amsmath.sty\relax` leaves amsmath's definitions in force; color/xcolor, soul, booktabs, cleveref,
hhline, subcaption, subfig, natbib's `cite`, quantumarticle, sn-jnl, changepage, OmniBus, the kernel's `array` and
`biblatex` tests). The loader's own question — were the definitions read here — keeps the records (`load_recorded`,
`binding_loaded`, `raw_loaded`: the autoload triggers, `\documentstyle`'s fallback, the class dispatch, amsmath's
beyond-original load). Two writes follow: a binding that stands in for a file its original loads marks it as that load
does (`state::mark_loaded`: thmtools's thm-patch.sty, aipproc's aipxfm.sty); revtex4_support's preload of hyperref,
which the real class never loads, undefines `\ver@hyperref.sty` with its record (`state::unmark_loaded`), and so does the
format's preload of textcomp (sect13.rs; Perl latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:5893 leaves it loaded), whose definitions
latex.ltx carries without `\ver@textcomp.sty`: the document's first load runs its file and package hooks (TL manual
biblatex-sbl, `\AfterPackage{textcomp}`; guard `perfect_kernel_batchqa47a` row `afterpackage_of_the_formats_textcomp`), and,
as textcomp.sty v2.1b (:52-75), declares and processes the options only: the symbols are not defined again over the
document's (textcomp_sty.rs reads `binding_loaded`; row `textcomp_after_the_format_keeps_the_documents_symbols`); a request the records skip restores a
mark the document took back (`\let\ver@X\relax` then `\usepackage{X}` leaves X loaded, as LaTeX's reload does; the loader's
records-only skip is the ruling of 2026-10-14) with the file's declared version, as the binding load does. A loader marks
the file unless it is loaded by this rule: a `\relax` left by a query before the load (`\expandafter\ifx\csname ver@X.sty\endcsname\relax`,
`\@ifpackagelater`, `\IfPackageAtLeastTF`) is not loaded, while the raw loader keeps a `\relax` the file set itself
(fontenc.sty:123). A package or class load (binding or raw, `\documentclass`, `\LoadClass`) marks `\ver@<file>` `\@empty`
before the read, as latex.ltx:18840 `\@onefilewithoptions` does (Perl's records are set before the read too,
Package.pm:2328, :2363), so a file asks for its loader while it loads (1411.7188's l3names.sty for expl3; a binding's
`subfigure.cfg`); the version replaces the mark after the read, and a load that reads nothing takes it back. The class-copy check, microtype's babel test and biblatex's overlay ask `file_loaded` too. cleveref's
pretense (Perl cleveref.sty.ltxml:23-27) marks amsmath both ways, in the group (`state::with_pretended_load`), only where it
is neither loaded nor recorded. **Witnesses**: 2501.07980, 1712.01010, 1812.04463 (aa.cls copies
loading amsmath). **Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batchga2::one_loaded_answer_on_every_load_path`, the fence
`perfect_kernel_batche0::one_loaded_query` (a record looked up outside `state.rs` and the loader, floor 0) with its
self-test `a_record_lookup_counts_however_it_is_written`.

### 1017. A dropped `\psfrag` fragment is counted at its graphic's constructor, one Warning per EPS graphic (PSF1, PSF1b)

**TeX.** psfrag.sty:42-62 hooks `\epsfbox` and `\Ginclude@eps`: every EPS a graphic includes in a fragment's scope
(local, psfrag's `\pfg@pcount`) places each saved fragment (`\pfg@hideend`), and under `\psfragscanon` (or `scanall`/209
mode) each `(\\tex…)` string `\pfg@scan` reads from the file; the switch stays on until `\psfragscanoff`
(psfrag.sty:24-25). epsfig's `\epsffile` and `\psfig` include through `\Ginclude@eps`, so they place too. **Perl.**
psfrag.sty.ltxml:24-62 saves the fragments; at begin-document it `\let`s `\@includegraphics`, `\@includegraphicx` and
`\epsfbox` to constructors that turn an EPS with fragments into an `ltx:picture` replaying them; epsfig's `\psfig` and
the `\let` copies made before (`\epsffile`) keep the plain `<graphics>`, the fragment lost silently (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#1237). It resets `psfrag_scan` after each graphic, unobservably: the saved list still replays `\psfragscanon`.
**Rust.** The fragment store is Perl's (`saved_psfragments`, `\lx@delayed@psfrag`); the fragments are not rendered yet
(PSFR, post-merge), so every graphic constructor's after-digest (graphics' `\@includegraphics`, graphicx's
`\@includegraphicx`, epsf's and epsfig's `\epsfbox` with their copies, epsfig's `\psfig`) calls
`psfrag_sty::psfrag_graphic`, which at an EPS graphic emits ONE `Warning:missing_feature:psfrag` naming the graphic and
every fragment it drops in order — each tag, and each scanned `\tex` string as TeX reads it — so the count is the
figures affected (cond-mat0310505: 35 preamble fragments x 25 figures, 25 Warnings). A non-EPS graphic, or a fragment no
EPS graphic reaches, prints nothing in TeX and stays silent. The empty box `\psfrag` left before stays, so `tex=`
reverts it (XML byte-identical). A graphic is EPS as psfrag finds it (PSF1c): a candidate (or a `{filecontents}` file of
the name, or the name with `.eps`/`.ps`) whose header is PostScript (`%!`, or the DOS EPS `C5D0D3C6`), as Perl's
`psfrag_requirepicture` asks `image_type` (Util/Image.pm:74-84) — under dvips any file falls to `\Gin@rule@*` of type
eps (dvips.def:211) and epsf reads any file, so the header is what decides an `.epsi` or `.epsf` (hep-ph0610439: 8
`\psfig{figure=*.epsi}`); a PNG or PDF, a pdflatex graphic, places nothing. A file without that header (a compressed
`.eps.gz`) is EPS by its extension's graphics rule: a declared `\Gin@rule@<ext>` of type eps (`\DeclareGraphicsRule`),
else dvips.def:203-210's eps rules (`.eps`, `.ps`, `.eps.gz`, …); psfrag's scan of compressed bytes finds no label.
Residual: raw epsf.sty loaded before psfrag leaves `\epsffile` unhooked in TeX (no placement), where the binding's
`\epsffile` shares `\epsfbox`'s constructor and warns. **Guard**:
`perfect_kernel_batchpsf1::batchpsf1_dropped_fragments_are_counted` (repros `reversion/psfrag_*`).

### 1018. What a package adds to `\@trivlist` runs through the kernel's `\lx@trivlist@hook`; tabu's lets are bound (TABU2, TABU2b, TABU2c)

**TeX.** latex.ltx's `\@trivlist` (:15862) opens every list but an in-paragraph one: `\list`, `\trivlist`, so
`{itemize}`/`{enumerate}`/`{description}`, `{quote}`/`{quotation}`/`{verse}`, theorems (`\@begintheorem`), amsthm's
`\proof` (amsthm.sty:434), mn2e.cls:864 / mnras.cls:993's `\proof`, and `{thebibliography}` (article.cls:565-571,
natbib.sty:1068). A package adds to it: tabu.sty:2389-2391 `\tabu@trivlist`, run by `\tabu@init` (:705) in every tabu,
lets `\\` back to `\@normalcr` at a list's start, so a list in a `>{\centering}p` cell keeps its line breaks; the same
`\tabu@init` lets `\centering`/`\raggedright`/`\raggedleft` to `\tabu@latextwoe`'s copies ending in `\arraybackslash`
(:2376-2381), so a `\\` after them ends the row; its private `|` reads a line style, `|[1pt]` (:907-911).
**Perl.** No tabu binding (OmniBus reads tabu.sty raw); `\@trivlist` is `\relax`, locked
(latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1673), so an addition to it is lost, and its `\trivlist` and lists are constructors that
never run it. **Rust.** `\@trivlist` stays locked; its package additions go to `\lx@trivlist@hook` (empty, sect06.rs),
which `run_trivlist_hook` digests where TeX opens the list: `begin_itemize` (not for `inline@` lists, which TeX does
not open with `\@trivlist`), `{quote}`/`{quotation}`/`{verse}`, `define_new_theorem`'s begin, amsthm's and
mn2e_support's `{proof}`, `\thebibliography` after its heading and preamble. tabu_sty.rs ports `\tabu@latextwoe` and
`\tabu@trivlist` (adding to the hook) as raw TeX, and `\tabu@init`'s lets, the private `|` included, local to each
`{tabu}`/`{longtabu}`; `{tabu*}`/`{longtabu*}` are their unstarred twins (the body rescan not modelled); `|[style]`
keeps the rule, its width, dash and colour not modelled. 10 witnesses 313 → 0 Errors (2210.07016 95 → 0, 1705.07086
90 → 0); ~880 arXiv papers load tabu. Residuals (post-merge): the private `|` let is inherited by a tabular nested in
a tabu cell, where TeX errs (TABUN, `tabu_vline_style_in_a_nested_tabular_red`); our `{center}`/`{flushleft}` let
`\\` to `\@normalcr` themselves, so in a tabu cell they keep line breaks where TeX ends the row (TABUF,
`tabu_center_env_backslash_red`). **Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batch54::tabu_init_lets_rule_styles_and_starred_environments`
(repros `alignment-bindings/tabu_*`, `array_centering_backslash_errs`).

**TeX.** article/report/book `\input` `size1\@ptsize.clo` (book `bk1\@ptsize.clo`), whose one-column `\textwidth` is
the paper's width less 2in, at most 345/360/390pt for 10/11/12pt, `\@settopoint`ed (size12.clo:101-126); under 2.09
compatibility size1x.clo's 345/360/390pt and bk1x.clo:105's 4.5in/5in/5in (pdflatex 325.215pt, 361.34999pt).
**Perl.** The kernel's `\textwidth` is 345pt (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1038) for every size, `\@ptsize` 0
(article.cls.ltxml:51 "should depend on options..."). **Rust.** `declare_standard_class_page` sets `\textwidth` and
`standard_class_ptsize` gives `\@ptsize` from the options the class was given, `\opt@<class>.cls`, which a class's
`\ProcessOptions` reads alone (latex.ltx `\@process@ptions`): the document's options for the document's class, the
passed ones for a class another loads (elsarticle.cls:113, llncs.cls:47 `\PassOptionsToClass`, `\LoadClassWithOptions`;
none for a bare `\LoadClass{article}`). A loading class's own `\textwidth` stands after it (llncs.cls:55, 347.12354pt);
the elsarticle binding passes the size options as the class does (Perl's declared them no-ops). Two goldens differ from Perl on purpose:
`tokenize/fancyvrb.xml` (12pt, `width="390.0pt"`) and `complex/cleveref_minimal.xml` (a `\rule` sized from it).
Residual (post-merge): in two columns the registers stay 345pt (pdflatex 469pt/229.5pt;
`class-bindings/standard_class_twocolumn_textwidth_red.tex`), and elsarticle's `5p` 390pt at 12pt (pdflatex 522pt;
