### 1025. colortbl's rule colour is each border side's, taken as the rule is drawn (W4, #773)

**TeX.** colortbl.sty:156-192 stores `\arrayrulecolor[model]{colour}` as `\gdef\CT@arc@{\color[model]{colour}}` and
draws every rule as `{\CT@arc@ <rule>}`: `\hline`, `\@cline`, the preamble's `|` (`\@arrayrule`, set as each row is),
`\multicolumn`'s own `|`; booktabs' rules alike (booktabs.sty:101,165). The `|` is `\xdef`ed into the preamble
(array.sty:54 `\@addtopreamble`): a colour set as the preamble is built is frozen there (a `\multicolumn` builds its
own), an unset one (`\relax`) is read as the rule is drawn, a cell's left `|` as the cell starts. `\CT@start`/`\CT@end`
(:119-135) save the colour as a `\@tabarray` table (tabular, tabular*, tabularx, array) starts and restore it, globally,
after its alignment closes (`\endarray`); a longtable or an `\halign` (IEEEeqnarraybox) restores nothing. So a
mid-table change colours the `\hline`/`\cline` rules drawn after it, and the `|` ones when none was set as the table
started; a colour never drawn is never evaluated (1910.02206's unbraced `\arrayrulecolor\hhline{---~~~}`). **Perl.** `\arrayrulecolor` and `\doublerulesepcolor` are no-ops
(colortbl.sty.ltxml:85, :88): every border is the stylesheet's black. **Rust.** The core `Cell` keeps a colour per
side (`border_color`, `Cell::add_border`): `add_line` takes the colour of the horizontal rule being drawn
(`alignment::RULE_COLOR`/`take_rule_color`, local to the rule's `\noalign`), and the `|` extraction (tex_tables.rs
`extract_alignment_column`) reads a vertical rule box's own `border_color`, the last one drawn on each side; every
border move (normalize.rs's spans and pruned rows and columns, emulateapj's head rule) carries its side's colour. The
`<td>`/`<XMCell>` carries the coloured sides its `border` keeps as `cssstyle="border-top-color:#BFBFBF;…"`; black,
the stylesheet's colour (LaTeXML.css `.ltx_border_t`), adds nothing. The binding stores `\CT@arc@` as colortbl does
and evaluates it as each rule is drawn (`\lx@CT@arc@draw`, ahead of `\@@alignment@hline`, `\lx@cline` — `\hhline`
and booktabs' `\cmidrule` too), so an author's raw `\gdef\CT@arc@` colours too. Only a `|` takes the colour, as only
`\@arrayrule` wraps `{\CT@arc@\vline}`: the binding's `|` column type puts `\vrule\lx@CT@paint\lx@CT@arc@<n>` in the
template, `\lx@CT@arc@<n>` a copy of `\CT@arc@` frozen as the preamble (or a `\multicolumn`'s) is read, one per distinct
body, or `\vrule\lx@CT@paint@live` (reading `\CT@arc@` as the rule is drawn) when that is `\relax`; the paint token
sets that colour on the rule box just drawn. The rule box is the template's `\vrule`, as the base's `\vrule\relax`, so a
cell's reversion trims it and a math array's `tex=` stays its source with or without a colour
(`colortbl_bar_array_tex_is_its_source.tex`). The template skip lists (`template_after_fill_defeated`,
`intercol_reachable_in_before`) read the paint tokens by their `\lx@CT@` prefix, as they read `\vrule` by its spelling
(e0's spelling pins +1 each). A `!{\vrule}` or a typed
`\vline` keeps the default ink, and a table nested in a cell leaves the cell's rules theirs. `\CT@start`
saves locally just before `\lx@begin@alignment` of a table `\@tabular@bindings`/`\@array@bindings` set up (a request
local to the table's group), and
`\CT@end` restores after `\lx@end@alignment` (`\lx@CT@restore`), so a last row without `\\` keeps the colour. `\arrayrulecolor` is `\lx@hidden@noalign` material, where
colortbl tests `\baselineskip` for a `\noalign` (so mid-cell in an `l` column, in an explicit `\noalign` or before a
`\multicolumn` TeX errs, ours does not: `arrayrulecolor_mid_cell_misplaced_noalign_red.tex`,
`arrayrulecolor_noalign_and_before_multicolumn_red.tex`, post-merge).
`\doublerulesepcolor` is stored, unrendered (a border has no colour for the gap of `||`). Without `\arrayrulecolor`
the output is unchanged: a table in coloured text keeps uncoloured borders, where pdflatex draws its rules in the
current colour. Residual (post-merge): `\hhline`'s `>{…}` colour codes stay skipped
(`hhline_colortbl_color_code_is_skipped`); a `!{}` rule's own colour (`!{\color{blue}\vrule}`) is not read
(`arrayrulecolor_bang_rule_own_colour_red.tex`). **Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batchw4::arrayrulecolor_colours_the_rules_drawn_under_it`
(repros `alignment-bindings/arrayrulecolor_*`), `perfect_kernel_batch69a::arrayrulecolor_reads_to_the_brace`,
`perfect_kernel_batch60::colortbl_noalign_idiom`, the `alignment/colortbls` golden.

### 1029. A file `\input` under a set `\everyeof` is read as a token list, never answered by a binding (WIN1, WIN1F)

**TeX.** An `\input` made while `\everyeof` holds tokens feeds the reader that set them: the file's tokens, then the
`\everyeof` list (etex.web §362), end a delimited scan opened across the `\input` — expl3's `\file_get:nnN`
(`\__file_get_aux:nnN`: `\tex_everyeof:D` the marker, `\__file_get_do:Nw`, `\tex_input:D`). The LaTeX kernel of
November 2026 reads `glyphtounicode.tex` this way while the format is built (latex.ltx:22952-22957). **Perl.** Such an
`\input` met while definitions are read goes to `InputDefinitions` (Package.pm:2287-2288), its own loop; `\everyeof` is
a bare register never inserted (eTeX.pool.ltxml:258); a binding answers where one exists. **Rust.** Under a set
`\everyeof`, `content::input` reads the file on disk in both modes: during definitions `read_as_token_list` opens a mouth
under the current catcodes ending with the `\everyeof` mark (no definitions loop, no loaded mark, no content-file
entry); in a document the binding dispatch is skipped and the content path reads it. Before, `--init=latex.ltx` on that
kernel raised 137 errors (the scan ran on through latex.ltx under `\ExplSyntaxOff`), and in a document
`\file_get:nnN{ltluatex}` / `{pstricks}` / `{glyphtounicode}` / `{xspace.sty}` raised 7 / 16 / 7 / 7 Errors with `[read] [empty]` where
pdflatex prints `[read][42]Tail.` (0 `!`). An ordinary `\input` keeps its binding: the empty `glyphtounicode.tex`
binding answers `\input glyphtounicode` (`\pdfglyphtounicode` a no-op, the raw read's output the same, at fewer
instructions). **Guards**: `perfect_kernel_batch51::file_get_reads_the_file_whole`, the format build's zero-error gate.

### 1032. → #105 (An aligned column's `columnalign` is the stylesheet's `justify-items` (issues #809, #755))

### 1033. A visible MathML Core category-K operator has no operator space: `/` is K, and an Ord (issue #789)

**TeX.** `/` is an Ord (mathcode "013D), as is `\backslash` (`\delimiter"26E30F`, class 0): `\showbox` of `$a/b$` and
`$a\backslash b$` has no glue. **Core** (TR 2025 and ED, Figure 25) puts infix `/`, `\`, `_`, U+2061-2064 and U+2206 in
category K, zero lspace and rspace. **Perl.** OperatorDictionary.pm:185 lists `/` in B (0.222 em; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
#1240), and the space walk (`adjust_pair`) types an operator by its role, so `/` (MULOP) is a Bin and `\backslash`
(MULOP, math_common.pool.ltxml:97) gets `lspace`/`rspace` 0.222 em; `<mo>/</mo>` is bare, and Chrome 155 spaces it 0.222 em
each side (Firefox none). **Rust.** The dictionary has `/` in K; `is_core_k_glyph`
(presentation.rs) marks a visible infix `<mo>` of category K `lspace="0em" rspace="0em"`, as Perl does for the ZWSP of
`--noinvisibletimes` (MathML.pm:773), and the walk types it Ord when its role is a Bin (MULOP). A class digestion
keeps wins: `\mathrel{/}`, `\mathrel{\backslash}` (RELOP) get 0.278 em each side, `\mathpunct{/}`,
`\mathpunct{\backslash}` (PUNCT) 0 em / 0.167 em, TeX's `\thickmuskip` and `\thinmuskip`. The invisible K operators stay
bare (Format text, Perl L747; Chrome and Firefox give them no space). Residual: `\mathbin{/}` and `\bigm/` lose their
Bin/Rel class at digestion and get zero space too (RED `math-parse/mathbin_slash_keeps_binary_space_red.tex`,
post-merge). Offer upstream. **Guards**:
`perfect_kernel_batchmml2::core_k_operators_have_no_operator_space` (repro
`math-parse/slash_is_an_ord_without_operator_space.tex`), `operator_dictionary::tests::test_opdict_category_k_is_infix_only`.

**Extension (2026-11-14, issue #824): TeX's Bin→Ord rule in the same walk.** The walk's atom types move toward TeX's classes in one
mechanism: the Core-K Ord above, and a sign TeX makes an Ord is tight.
**Principle (real TeX, MathML Core).** TeX converts a Bin atom to an Ord when it is the first atom of its list or
follows a Bin, Op, Rel, Open or Punct, and converts the previous Bin when a Rel, Close or Punct follows or the list ends
(tex.web §728-729, `@<Convert \(a)a bin...@>`); glue is not an atom there. MathML Core spaces an `<mo>` by its inferred
form (§3.2.4.2): a last child is postfix, and `+` and `−` have no postfix entry, so they fall back to infix,
0.2222em each side (B.1). Related: #1040. **Perl.** The space walk (`space_walk`/`adjust_pair`,
MathML.pm:1097-1284) types each atom by its role alone, so a trailing `+` stays a Bin. **Rust.** `space_walk`
(presentation.rs) collects an mrow's visually adjacent atoms first, then types them (`item_atom_type`, Perl's role
table and #1033's Core-K Ord) and applies TeX's conversion over the list (`tex_atom_types`, an `mspace` skipped as
glue; `∇`, `|`, `‖` and `.` read as TeX's Ords, class 0, where the role table says Op or Punct, so `\nabla\cdot B`
keeps a binary `⋅`); `adjust_pair` spaces a pair that touches a converted sign by those types; every other pair keeps the role table's types (Perl's), so `\nabla\cdot B` still lacks TeX's medium space before `⋅` (RED `math-parse/nabla_cdot_is_a_binary_operation_red.tex`). A converted Bin `<mo>` after the list's first atom whose
dictionary spacing is nonzero gets `lspace="0em" rspace="0em"`; a leading one is not marked (Core's prefix form gives
`+` and `−` zero). `\showbox` (pdflatex, TL 2025) agrees on every row: `a+-b` has `\medmuskip` both sides of `+` and
none around `−` (`<mo>+</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo>`); `x\pm-1`, `f(0+)`, `a+ =b` (`\thickmuskip` only
around `=`), `a+b+`, `x+,y`, `a+\,=b`, `\{+,-\}`, `x^{2+}`, `\lim_{x\to0+}`, an align cell ending `=b+`, mhchem's charge
`2-` set the sign tight; `-x`, `(-x)`, `a=-b` keep a bare `<mo>` (the parser's prefix operator, already an Ord).
This replaces a rule keyed on the parser's `limit-from` reading, which also tightened the binary `+` of `a+-b`.
Residuals: scripts keep Bin, Rel and Punct space (TeX inserts none in script style, §764), so a converted sign
after a comma in a script (2003.05751 `\mathcal{P}^{2,+}`) leaves the comma Core's 0.167em
(`math-parse/script_style_rel_has_no_thick_space_red.tex`); a braced `{\mathop{\square}}` is TeX's Ord but the role
table's Op (2012.06541). Offer upstream. **Guard**:
`perfect_kernel_batchmml2::core_k_operators_have_no_operator_space` (repro `math-parse/bin_atom_becomes_ord.tex`).

### 1034. A small PDF figure is converted to SVG, raster-bearing ones too, unless it draws a raster enlarged (after PR 816)

**Perl.** Every PDF graphic is rasterized to PNG (`Post/Graphics.pm:62`, `pdf => { destination_type => 'png' }`).
**Rust.** Beyond Perl, a PDF at most 500 KiB (the auto default, `--graphics-svg-threshold-kb 0`; an explicit `N`
bounds it at `N` KB) first tries the vector converters, `mutool convert -F svg`, then `pdftocairo -svg`
(`Graphics::convert_image_svg`); every failure falls back to the PNG path: neither tool on PATH, a non-zero exit, the
15 s timeout, an SVG over 8 MB, an SVG whose `trim`/`viewport` crop cannot be read. Labels, axes and curves stay
vector, and an embedded raster keeps its own pixels (PERF816, 673 arXiv figures: mutool's SVG -8 ms CPU median per
figure against the PNG, 70 vs 157 MB gzipped; 23 % of the PNGs lost raster resolution). Until PR 816 (amachino) an
image XObject in the first 256 KB gated a PDF off the path; DG ruled on 2026-11-14 that size alone gates it (mutool
first, pdftocairo the fallback; MuPDF, AGPL, only as an unmodified CLI subprocess).

**Enlarged rasters take the PNG path** (DG 2026-11-14, "PNG for enlarged rasters"): an SVG that draws any raster larger
than its own pixels is discarded and the figure takes main's PNG path, with an `Info`, no Warning and no error count;
every other figure keeps the SVG. (A raster drawn at its pixel size or smaller inside the figure stays SVG even when the
page then enlarges the whole figure, e.g. `width=\textwidth`; the browser smooths it then, as it smooths main's PNG of
that figure.) Neither tool marks a raster's rendering, so a
browser smooths an enlarged raster into a blur where the PDF (no `/Interpolate`, as pdflatex writes it) shows hard
pixel blocks, and no static `image-rendering` suits every display size: `pixelated` aliases a raster the page or a phone
shows smaller. `svg_enlarged_raster` reads every placement, inline, under nested `<g transform>`, through `<use>` and
through a soft mask's `<mask>` (both tools draw an alpha channel there), and calls a raster enlarged when it is drawn at
more than 1.01 SVG user units per pixel on either axis on any placement (user units are the PDF's bp, which both tools
keep; 1.01 absorbs the tools' float rounding, pdftocairo drawing images about 2 % smaller than mutool). A 1×1 raster never counts, however it is drawn: a browser cannot blur a single pixel (DG 2026-11-14;
10 of the 21 PNG fallbacks in the 60-paper sample were 1×1 rasters in 1503.05958). A placement it
cannot read counts as enlarged: an image in a `<pattern>` or `<symbol>`, under a `skewX`/`skewY` or a nested `<svg>` viewBox (a shear written as `matrix()` is measured by its axis lengths), past
8 nested `<use>`, or with a size or pixel count it cannot read. The decision runs on every render after the graphics
cache, so a cached SVG is judged too (the cache stores the converter's output, not the decision). `/Interpolate true` no
longer matters (the PNG path renders such a raster as main does). **Guards**:
`graphics::tests::small_raster_pdf_keeps_vector_labels_unless_enlarged` (each converter present, then the pipeline:
`native_raster_vector.tex`, a 64×64 PNG at 48 bp, stays SVG; `mixed_raster_vector.tex`, a 4×4 tile at 1 cm, takes the
PNG path), `graphics::tests::svg_enlarged_raster_reads_every_placement`, `graphics::tests::should_try_svg_path_auto_detect`.

### 1036. `AddToMacro!` on an undefined cs is an Error and defines it with the addition (MACSYNC)

**Perl.** `AddToMacro` (Package.pm:2534-2549) Warns ("not an expandable control sequence") and drops the addition when
the cs is undefined; a later use of the cs is then an undefined-cs Error. **TeX.** latex.ltx:1832 `\g@addto@macro`'s
`\expandafter` raises "Undefined control sequence", then its `\xdef` defines the cs with the addition (pdflatex
`\g@addto@macro\nohook{XY}A\nohook B` → 1 `!`, "AXYB"). **Ours.** TeX's Error (`undefined:\nohook`, as TeX and Perl
both err) and TeX's outcome, the content kept; before, the cs was defined silently. `\AtEndOfPackage` names its hook with
`\csname` (latex.ltx:18896), so it makes an empty hook first and raises nothing. A non-expandable cs keeps Perl's Warning and
is left alone (TeX's `\expandafter` leaves a `\relax` cs unexpanded, so its `\xdef` makes a self-referencing macro).
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batchmacsync::add_to_macro_on_an_undefined_cs_errs` (repro
`macro-state/g_addto_macro_undefined_defines.tex`).

So a binding defines the lists and hooks its real class or package defines, which documents extend (REGBIND, 17 papers
of the 2605/2606 reruns: enumerate's `\@enhook`, threeparttable's `\TPT@defaults`, oup-authoring-template's
`\ps@opening`, and the lists below). Where the class prints such a list with its title page and the binding's own
setters do not fill it, the binding prints it there too, or what a document adds to it is lost without a word (Perl:
dropped, with the Warning above): `\lx@frontmatter@footnotes{<list>}` runs it where the class runs it, each
`\footnotetext`/`\@footnotetext` in it an `ltx:pubnote` (role `note`), what else it prints typeset after the
frontmatter. acmart's `\@titlenotes`, `\@subtitlenotes`, `\@authornotes` at `\maketitle` (acmart.cls:2245-2247;
2605.28175, 2605.16813, 2606.04448); amsaddr's `\emails` as its footnote (amsaddr.sty:102-113; 2606.23853, 2606.25954,
2212.11488, 1801.06576, 2307.06418); elsarticle's `\elsaddress` and `\@cornotes` at `\end{frontmatter}` or
`\maketitle` (elsarticle.cls:766, :806; 2605.22682, cnf.sty's `\cortext` 2605.08232, 2606.15628); REVTeX's
`\prep@absbox`, `\post@absbox`, `\mini@notes` and `\@FMN@list` at `\maketitle` (revtex4-2.cls:2648-2652, :3020-3022;
2606.06621, 2605.00976); and the text a document adds to icml's `\icmlcorrespondingauthor@text`, whose names and
addresses are the contacts (icml2026.sty:529-530; 2605.04712, 2605.21190, 2606.01172). **Guard**:
`perfect_kernel_batchregbind::{bindings_define_the_macros_their_files_define,

### 1027. The no-dump expl3-code.tex reload counts what it mutes (#825)

**Perl.** Perl's raw expl3 load raises none of these records, so it has no such scope. **Rust.** Without a kernel dump
(`LATEXML_NODUMP=1`, or no dump for the tree) `expl3.sty` re-reads expl3-code.tex raw, and `expl3_sty.rs` drops that
load's raw-load-only cascade whole (Perl `IGNORE_ERRORS`, issue #651; 5015 Error records on TL 2025). The scope now
tallies what it drops (`IgnoreDiagnosticsScope::dropped`), and `expl3_sty::report_muted_reload` reports it: one
`Warning:expl3:raw-load` naming the Error and Fatal records dropped when the reload completed (the records the scope
dropped, not the undefined-CS Errors `SUPPRESS_UNDEFINED_ERRORS`, stomach.rs, never emitted), an `Error:expl3:raw-load` when it
stopped early (the expl3 functions after the stop are undefined: on TL 2026 it stopped in l3unicode, leaving
`\regex_match:NnTF`, `\text_lowercase:n`, `\sys_if_shell:TF` undefined and mhchem's `\ce` broken). The dump path never
reloads and is unchanged. **Guards**: `common::error::tests::an_ignoring_scope_tallies_what_it_drops`,
`expl3_sty::tests::a_muted_expl3_reload_is_counted`, `dump_gate_init::nodump_latex_branch_converts_healthily`.

### 1028. A Rhai `Fatal()` ends the conversion as an engine Fatal does; after a Fatal the script itself catches, later errors are printed and counted (#792)

**Perl.** `Fatal` prints when raised, sets the status fatal (`Common/Error.pm:298`, `:312`), then sets `IGNORE_ERRORS`
(`:315`) and empties the token stack (`:327`), so a later `Error()` prints nothing (`:362`) even when an `eval` caught the
Fatal. **Rust.** A `Fatal()` (or `Error()` past MAX_ERRORS) prints its one line and sets status 3; containment does not
swallow it (`script_bindings/wire.rs` `contain` returns the Fatal `take_raised_fatal` finds, PR #829), so it ends the
conversion from a binding's top level, a body, a hook or a binding another binding loads (probe: `Before \wftopmacro\
after.` with a body `Fatal()` keeps no text, "Conversion failed: 1 fatal error"). A Fatal the script catches with
`try`/`catch` was printed at its raise; the script and the conversion go on, and a later error stays its own counted
`Error:script:` line (the user's ruling that every Error is emitted and counted, 2026-11-11); no ignore flag outlives it. DG 2026-11-14 confirmed both halves: a Rhai Fatal stops
processing, and a Fatal the binding deliberately catches may continue, as Perl's `eval` allows. A `DefLigature`
`fontTest` and a register setter may die as Perl's (Document.pm:1227 `&$fonttest($font)`, Register.pm:66 `&$setter`):
`FontTestClosure` returns `Result<bool>`, `RegisterSetterClosure` and `Definition::set_value` `Result<()>`, so their
Fatal ends the conversion: a setter's as a body's, a `fontTest`'s as any build hook's (the build stops and keeps the
document built so far, with its Warning). **Exceptions**, one decision post-merge (propagate the `Result`, or re-raise a logged
Fatal): a register getter's Fatal is dropped and the register reads unset, since `Definition::value_of` returns an `Option`
(catalog `rhai-bindings/register_getter_fatal_continues_red.tex`); a `fontTest`'s Fatal raised while `set_node` closes the open
text (a `\footnote` right after the text) is dropped, since `set_node` discards `close_text_internal`'s Result (Perl's
Document.pm:74 dies there; `rhai-bindings/fonttest_fatal_closed_by_set_node_red.tex`).
**Guard**: `30_script_bindings::a_rhai_fatal_is_logged_once` (the caught-then-thrown, `fontTest` and setter rows).

### 1030. → KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1244 (Rhai glue arithmetic is TeX's `\advance`, not Perl's Glue.pm / MuGlue.pm)

### 1031. A Rhai call named after Perl's keeps Perl's intent on our core's TeX-accurate values; an unreadable `Dimension`/`Glue` spec is an Error (Perl: a silent or warned wrong value) — absorbs #1035

**Rule (rulings 10-13, DG 2026-11-14; one name, one meaning).** A Rhai call lowers to the Rust macros' core call, so it
answers as the core does, and a spec that cannot be read as its type is an `Error:unexpected:<spec>` naming it, using 0;
a Number string keeps Perl's `int()` reading with Perl's Warning. A wrong value read silently is the likelier wrong
output (BM, 2026-11-05). Where a Perl-shaped use changes meaning, it keeps working one release with one deprecation
Warning per load. **Code.** `latexml_contrib/src/script_bindings/values.rs:68 unreadable`, `:73 dimension_of`, `:83
glue_of`, `:112 register_value_of_spec`; `latexml_core/src/common/number.rs:52 from_str_value`.

- **Dimension/Glue** (ex-#1031). Perl's `Dimension('3 furlongs')` reads the leading number as sp (`3sp`, with only
  Perl's `Argument "3 furlongs" isn't numeric` warning), and `Glue('1pt plus')` Warns `Missing Glue specification`. Ours
  errs, for the constructors and the string form of `DefRegister`/`AssignRegister`; a fresh register's unitless string
  (`DefRegister("\\c", "5")`) is the same Error, where Perl's untyped register errs at `\the`; an existing register's
  declared type still reads it (`"5"` for a Number register is 5). Guard `perfect_kernel_batchw3rc::rhai_typed_registers_error_side`.
- **Number** (Number.pm:31-34 `int($number)`): `Number(string)`, a Number register's string form and the core
  `Number::from(String)` are one reader — `"1e3"` 1000, `"1.5"` 1, a non-numeric remainder (`"12abc"`) Warned (`isn't
  numeric`) and its prefix read — where the core read 0 silently.
- **Colours and fonts.** Perl's `MergeFont(color => 'red')` keeps the name (`color="red"`) with or without a colour
  package, and Font.pm `merge` ignores an unknown key. Ours resolves the name to its colour (`#FF0000`) — a base name
  (`red`, color.sty's eight) without a colour package included, dvipsnam.def read only once a package defines
  `\DefineNamedColor` (so `Blue` with no colour package is the lookup's Error and Black, where Perl prints the name); an
  unknown font key Warns.
- **Definitions and boxes.** `LookupDefinition` returns a handle that keeps the meaning it found, so `AssignMeaning`
  installs it after a redefinition (`A:OLD:NEW`); a `DefPrimitive` body's returned box or array of boxes is its output
  (Primitive.pm:78). Perl's diagnostics take `(cat, obj, $where, msg, @details)`.
- **Transition.** `CounterValue` returns a Number as in Perl; its int uses (`+`, `-`, `*`, every comparison with an int or
  float in either order, `roman`/`Roman`) keep working one release with one deprecation Warning per load, since Rhai
  answers an unregistered comparison `false` silently (PR #829 rounds G-H).
- **Glue arithmetic** is TeX's `\advance`: KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1244 (#1030).
- **Guards** `perfect_kernel_batchw3rg::rhai_perl_names_behave_as_perl` (Font.pm keys, ExplodeText's ASCII letters, the
  counter calls, variadic Push/UnshiftValue, `ptValue`'s clamp, LookupDimension's argument forms,
  `getAttribute`/`setAttribute`, returned boxes, the diagnostics' form; Perl 3 W plus the Error, ours 1 W more, the
  unknown key), `perfect_kernel_batchw3rg::rhai_perl_names_review_rows` (no colour package, the kept definition, the
  mixed comparisons, `roman(Number)`, `Number(string)`).

### 1037. An EPUB keeps its log outside the container and never over an existing file (UPS1, upstream #2855)

**Perl.** Since #2855 (1718f89e) `latexmlc` keeps an existing external log under an archive output
(`$keep_log_file`, bin/latexmlc:111-134): a `.zip` packs the log as its `--log` basename (default `<name>.latexml.log`,
LaTeXML.pm:621-629, t/932_zip.t), and an EPUB packs it into the container as `OPS/<log>`. **Rust.** The `.zip` is as
Perl. An EPUB writes its log outside the container (epubcheck would flag a log member under `OPS/`), and when a file of
the log's name already exists it is kept and the log not written ("Log not written: '<log>' exists and is kept" on
stderr; DG 2026-11-14). A conversion that fails before it starts writes its Fatal log under the same rule.
`cortex_worker` packs its own `cortex.log` and is unchanged. **Guard**: `cluster_cli::archive_output_keeps_an_existing_log`.

### 1038. A listing `frame=` naming no side draws no frame (UPS1, upstream #2820)

**Perl.** Since #2820 (7412d564) listings.sty.ltxml:277-287 frames a listing whose `frame=` is not `none`: a named
frame from `%frames`, else the sides its letters name (`t`/`b`/`l`/`r`, either case); a value naming none (`xyz`,
empty) joins to `''`, and `framedProperties` (TeX_Box.pool.ltxml:84) turns that into `framed="rectangle"`. **TeX.**
lstmisc.sty:1387-1399 keeps such a value as `\lst@frame`, and the frame code draws only the sides whose letters it
holds: no frame. **Rust.** `lst_frame_sides` (listings_sty.rs) returns no frame for it, as TeX. **Guard**:
`perfect_kernel_batchups1::fboxsep_pads_fcolorbox_boxed_and_listing_frames` (its `frame=xyz` listing).

### 1041. `<mtable>` carries no default `rowspacing="0pt"` (issue 695)

**Perl.** `pmml_array` writes `rowspacing` from the XMArray's `rowsep` (default `0pt`) on every table of two or more
rows (MathML.pm:478-481). **Rust.** The same, except that a missing or zero `rowsep` writes nothing
(`latexml_post/src/mathml/presentation.rs`, `pmml_array_inner`, `is_zero_length`; DG ruling 2026-11-14); an author's
non-zero `rowsep` (`\arraystretch`, `\jot`) is written as Perl writes it (`rowspacing="10.0pt"`). MathML Core
gives `<mtable>` only the global attributes, so Chrome ignores it (cell contents 6.88 px apart with or without it),
while Firefox and MathJax honour it: issue 695's `array` and a `gather*`-nested `aligned` set their rows touching with
`rowspacing="0pt"` (Firefox, Playwright build 1532: 1.5-3 px between the rows' contents) and without it 8.4-9.9 px
apart (Firefox's default) and about 3.8 px in MathJax 2.1 (HTML-CSS, offline; its 1ex default); an
`\arraystretch{2}` array's `10.0pt` gives 16.3 px in Firefox, a `\jot=6pt` `aligned`'s `6.0pt` 11 px. `columnspacing`
stays: LaTeXML.css keys the aligned-cell padding reset on `columnspacing="0pt"` (#755); `columnalign` stays on `<mtd>`:
LaTeXML.css keys `justify-items` on it (#809). The other non-Core attributes still written, `align` and `width` on
`<mtable>`, are left to their own ruling. **Guard**:
`cluster_cli::aligned_mtable_columnspacing_zero::aligned_emits_zero_columnspacing_and_css_resets_mtd_padding` (the
four whole `<mtable>` elements: two default, two with the author's `rowspacing`); repro
`tools/perfect_kernel/repros/alignment/mtable_no_rowspacing.tex`.

### 1039. A bibliography href drops TeX's escapes (issue 808)

**Perl.** A `.bib` `url` is read `Verbatim` (BibTeX.pool.ltxml:740) and becomes `<ltx:bib-url href='#1'>`, which
MakeBibliography.pm `do_links` copies into the link, so `url = {https://doi.org/10.1162/tacl\_a\_00276}` gives
`href="https://doi.org/10.1162/tacl\_a\_00276"`, a dead link.
**Rust** (DG ruling 2026-11-14, "unescape in hrefs"). `format_links` (make_bibliography.rs, the port of `do_links`,
which turns an entry's `bib-url`/`bib-identifier`/`bib-review` into its link: `url`, aa's `adsurl`, a `doi` or review
href) reads `\_ \% \# \& \$ \~ \{ \}` as the character (`\~{}` as `~`) in the href, since a backslash is never valid
in a URL; any other backslash, and a URL without one, is kept. The XML's `bib-url` keeps the field as the engine reads it (verbatim; a `\~{}`'s braces are already dropped there, pre-existing), and a
`*nat` style, which prints its URLs, prints it as TeX does, escapes included. A `doi` was already clean
(`identifier_data`, bibtex.rs). **Guards**: `06_cluster_bibliography::bib_url_escapes_leave_the_href`,
`make_bibliography::tests::unescape_tex_url_drops_only_tex_escapes`.

### 1042. An equation's tag stays beside its formula in LaTeXML.css (issue #810)

**Perl.** LaTeXML.css gives the tag cell `.ltx_eqn_eqno { max-width:0em; overflow:visible }`: the column takes no
width and the tag overlays the right centring pad (`min-width:2em`), so a formula wider than the line less 2em runs
under its tag (reporter nasser1's `align` with `\tag{C.8.1}`: in Chrome the tag sits on the fraction bar at 768 and
375 px; `(C.8.2)` at 375 px; a long `\tag` over `z=1` at 375 px in Firefox). TeX never overlaps them: tex.web
§1202-1205 centres the display in the full line, recentres it in the line less the number when the gap falls under
twice the number's width, and sets the number on a line of its own when even that does not fit. **Rust.** Two local
deltas. (1) `.ltx_eqn_eqno { max-width:none; }`: the tag is a real column. (2) A one-row centred equation
(`.ltx_equation.ltx_eqn_table`, its row the only child) is a grid `minmax(2em,1fr) auto 1fr` (leqno mirrored), the tag
laid over the pad on its side with a 1em quad: the formula is centred in the full line while the tag fits, and moves
only as far as the tag needs when it does not, a continuous form of TeX's two-step rule (a long `\tag` at 375 px:
4 px left in Chrome, 27 px in Firefox, where TeX's rule gives 75/86); under a minipage or a table cell
(`.ltx_inline-block`, `.ltx_td`) the 2em minimum is 0. The other pad's `width:100vw; max-width:100%` keeps the
shrink-to-fit width the old 50% table columns gave (an equation in a list item is centred in the item's line, now in
Firefox too). Measured in Chrome and Firefox at 1280/768/375 px: a one-row equation 0 px off the line's centre (was
-10 px for `(1)`, -68/-79 px for the long `\tag` at 1280 with (1) alone); a `p{4cm}` cell's `q=r+s+t (14)` fits its
152 px without scrolling, the tag visible (was 179 px, the tag behind the scroll); the accessibility tree is
unchanged (playwright `ariaSnapshot`, Chrome's `LayoutTable` roles). A multi-row table (`align`, `gather`,
`eqnarray`, `subequations`) keeps (1) alone, since its rows share columns: its rows are centred in the line less the
tag column (-10 to -24 px at 16 px). Not reached: a formula plus its tag wider than a narrow box in the browser scrolls
with the tag behind the scroll, where TeX would set the number on its own line (repro
`alignment/equation_tag_hidden_in_a_narrow_minipage_red.tex`). Offered upstream. **Guards**:
`cluster_cli::browser_render_eqn_tags::equation_tags_stay_beside` (Chrome, Firefox with `LATEXML_FIREFOX`; local),
`xslt::witnessed_css_delta::equation_tag_and_mathjax_deltas_stay_present`.

### 1043. MathJax's display margin is zeroed inside an equation cell (issue #475)

**Perl.** A display equation is a `table.ltx_eqn_table` (our #473 delta adds its 1em block margins). MathJax
renders a display `<math>` as a block with a 1em block margin (v3/v4 `mjx-container[display="true"]`, v2
`.MathJax_Display`); inside a table cell that margin cannot collapse with the table's, so consecutive displays sat
about three times as far apart as without MathJax (reporter nasser1; measured with MathJax 2.1 offline in Chrome: the
formulas 53 px apart, natively 18 px; ar5iv.css likewise 54 against 20). **Rust.** A local delta zeroes that
container's block margins in an equation cell, as the table already carries the display skip: 21 px under MathJax 2.1,
native rendering unchanged. The rule matches `.ltx_eqn_table .ltx_eqn_cell`, so it holds for the span-built equation
of a minipage or a tabular cell too. MathJax 3/4 was not loadable offline; its selector is from MathJax's CHTML
stylesheet. Offered upstream. **Guard**: `xslt::witnessed_css_delta::equation_tag_and_mathjax_deltas_stay_present`.

### 1040. An mhchem formula is chemistry math: element atoms, isotope prescripts, counts, a charge on the formula (issue #824, stage 1)

**Perl.** Ships no mhchem binding; the raw package hangs on `\ce`. **Rust (before).** The raw mhchem.sty (TL 2025 v4.10)
ran through its text-mode branch: an element run was one `\text` (`MoO`, `SO` one `<mtext>`), the count and charge
`\text` scripts on `\vphantom` bases, the charge's minus an en dash (`<mtext>2 – </mtext>`), the isotope in an
`<mpadded>` from `\mathchoice`/`\llap`, and a formula of text alone left math (`ltx_markedasmath`). **Rust (now).**
mhchem's own parser still reads `\ce`; its output hook `\__mhchem_output_begin_cf:` (empty, mhchem.sty:1424, run
before the formula's `\ensuremath`) rewrites the formula's output list (`lx@mhchem@formula`, `mhchem_sty.rs`). Each
`\__mhchem_output_coreFive:nnnnnnn` unit (mhchem.sty:2774) becomes, in mhchem's math-mode branch: its element run split
at its capitals when it is letters only, each element an ordinary atom (`\mathord`, so the letter ligature does not
merge `Mo` and `O`; Base_XMath.pool.ltxml:443); the isotope's mass and atomic number prescripts (`{}^{95}_{42}`) on
its first element; the count a subscript and an oxidation state a superscript of its last; the formula's brackets
(`\__mhchem_output_withFont:n {(}`) math fences. A charge on the formula's last unit is a superscript of the whole
formula (`\mathord{…}^{2-}`, minus U+2212) unless the formula is one element (`Li+`, `^{227}_{90}Th+`, `2Na+`); an
amount (`\__mhchem_output_amount:n`, mhchem.sty:2769) is not part of the formula after it (`\ce{3SO4^{2-}}` is
`3\,\mathord{SO_4}^{2-}`, `\ce{2e-}` is `2\,e^-`); an
inner unit's charge is the unit's when the unit is several elements (`\ce{OH^-(H2O)}`, 2405.01836). A unit with no
element (mhchem's count or state on an empty base) scripts the bracket or text it follows (`Fe(CN)6`,
`\ce{\textit{LnPn}2}`, 2602.09975), after a unit the formula so far:
`\ce{H2_{(g)}}` is `\mathord{H_2}_{(g)}` and `\ce{SO4^{2-}_{(aq)}}` `\mathord{\mathord{SO_4}^{2-}}_{(aq)}`, the state after
the charge as pdflatex prints it (an empty `{}` base would leave a floating subscript the math grammar does not parse). A text-mode
`\ce` sets the formula in the text font math was entered from (`savedfont`, Stomach.pm:518; mhchem.sty:2760 prints it
in the text font), as nicefrac's `\nf@mathcopytextfont`; a math-mode `\ce` keeps `\mhchem@option@mathFont`. A formula's
elements and brackets are juxtaposed, not multiplied (DG 2026-11-14): each run of them between amounts and mhchem's own
operators is `\lx@kludged{…}`, the unparsed row Perl uses for adjacency (Base_XMath.pool.ltxml:193, MathParser.pm:530),
so no U+2062 `<mo>` sits between two elements (Firefox spaced it ~0.17em; copy gave "H2⁢O"); the amount's thin space
before its species stays a U+2062 `<mo lspace="0.170em">`. A raw command with its argument (2407.15836
`\ce{\textit{R}2Ir2Al20}`, `\mathrm{Y}`) is an atom of the run, its count on it; another raw token (`\cdot`, `\bond{-}`,
mhchem's own output) parts the run. A charge's sign is tight because it ends its list, TeX's atom rule (#1033); a lone
sign (`e^-`, `Th+`) keeps a bare `<mo>`, as Core adds no space to a script that is one operator (§3.4.1). With `--cmml`
a run is an unparsed row (`<cerror><csymbol cd="ambiguous">fragments</csymbol>…`, Perl's `cmml_unparsed`,
MathML.pm:1361-1375, for any kludged row); the formula's content semantics are stage 2. MathML:
`<msup><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><mrow/><mn>95</mn></mmultiscripts><msub><mi
mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup>`
for `\ce{^{95}MoO4^{2-}}`. This first markup is TENTATIVE (DG's rulings of 2026-11-14) and awaits Bruce Miller's
feedback and refinements; stage 2 adds MathML `intent` on these presentation elements (formula, element, count and
charge each their own element). DG: "We expect further improvements are both possible and needed."
A formula whose output list holds a macro that expands to a math shift (`$`, `\(`, `\)`; 2606.03586
`\ce{\alphasic}`, `\alphasic` = `$\alpha$-\ce{SiC}`) keeps mhchem's output: its parser reads a literal `$` itself, a
macro's reaches the output unread, where only mhchem's text-mode `\text{…}` (mhchem.sty:2934) holds it (REGCHEM; guard
`perfect_kernel_batchregchem::mhchem_macro_math_shift_is_mhchems_own_output`).
Arrows, `+` between species, bonds, states and amounts keep mhchem's output (stage 2, SYNC row MHCHEM), and the
formula's `tex=` is the rewritten math, not `\ce{…}`. Cost (instructions:u): −0.55 % on 2307.12991 (589 `\ce` in its sources),
−0.04 % on 300 synthetic `\ce`, +0.13 % on 2405.01836 (167; with `--nomathparse` −0.08 %: the formulas'
parse is the price). **Guard**: `mhchem_formula::mhchem_formula_units_are_chemistry` (repros
`package-bindings/mhchem_formula_units.tex`, `mhchem_formula_text_font.tex`, `mhchem_formula_state.tex`,
`mhchem_formula_amount.tex`, `mhchem_formula_juxtaposed.tex`; witnesses issue 824, 2206.12015).

Residual (revREGCHEM): the decline's scan follows unprotected macros only, so a *protected* user macro hiding a math shift
(`\NewDocumentCommand`, `\protected\def`) still sets the shift in math and errs ("Missing $ inserted"); the skip is load-bearing
(`\@ensuremath` is protected and its `\else` reaches `\@ensuredmath`'s `$`). Row R MHCHEMPROT.

### 1050. The glue between two paragraphs is `--ltx-skip-before` on the second (QAB8, QA26)

**Principle:** TeX's vertical list decides what lies between two paragraphs; Perl's own comment asks for it
(TeX_Glue.pool.ltxml:89-90: "add appropriate class/css for spacing to preceding element"). It sits on the FOLLOWING paragraph
by DG's design ruling (2026-11-14, design A of the QA26 study): one element carries one gap, the stylesheet decides how to
show it, and nothing is added to or between the blocks. Related: #142 (`\\[dimen]` as `--ltx-break-space`, the same carrier), #422 (glue items flagged `isSkip`).
**Perl.** `\vskip` only closes the open `ltx:p`/`ltx:para` and drops its amount, so a topic break by `\bigskip`,
`\medskip` or `\vspace` leaves no trace (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1246). **Rust.** A `\vskip` (its natural width) met
while its parent's last child is an `ltx:para` is summed, in sp, on that parent (tex_glue.rs `note_skip_after_para`);
the next `ltx:para` opened there takes a positive net as `cssstyle="--ltx-skip-before:<pt>"`, appended to any
`cssstyle`, when its previous sibling is that paragraph (tex_paragraph.rs `apply_skip_before`, streaming
placeholders included); any paragraph's start ends the wait, and an empty paragraph pruned at its close gives its skip
back. So consecutive skips add as on TeX's vertical list (`\bigskip\medskip` 18pt, `\bigskip\vspace{-6pt}` 6pt;
needspace's `\vskip\dimen@ … \vskip-\dimen@` nets 0, mdframed_loads_its_dependencies); a heading, float, theorem or
list between, a skip after a heading, and a net that is not positive carry nothing. By the QA26 ruling (DG 2026-11-14) neither do title pages, boxes
(`ltx:inline-block`, `ltx:inline-logical-block`: a minipage holding paragraphs, 2512.08710) and floats
(`in_unspaced_container`), nor cover paragraphs the frontmatter later moves into a title page (`drop_skip_before` in
titlepage_layout.rs, 2007.05296).
A `\vspace` read inside a paragraph is latex.ltx's `\vadjust` (`\@vspace`, set after its line): it counts only when
the paragraph's `\par` follows at once (the `\par` marks it, `par_follows`); the kernel `\vspace` now marks its
`\vskip` (`\lx@vspace@mark`, which made the float's own `\lx@panel@vspace` redundant: removed). A `\vskip` read in a
paragraph ends it (tex.web §1094) and counts. LaTeXML.css: `.ltx_para[style*="--ltx-skip-before:"] { margin-top:
calc(1em + var(--ltx-skip-before)) }` (collapsing with the `<p>` margins: 32 px for 12pt at 16 px); ar5iv-css
mirrors it as `padding-top` (40 px); the EPUB loads LaTeXML.css. `\addvspace` stays a no-op (RED
`paragraph-mode/addvspace_between_paragraphs_takes_the_larger_red.tex`). Witnesses 2503.04888, 2001.10915,
2408.07944, 1606.03039. **Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batchqab8::paragraph_skips_go_on_the_next_paragraph` (repros
`paragraph-mode/skip_between_paragraphs_goes_on_the_next.tex`, `skip_between_paragraphs_shapes.tex`,
`skip_moved_into_a_title_page_is_dropped.tex`).

### 1048. The kernel hooks run where latex.ltx runs them, where LaTeXML's bindings stand in for its macros (QA47B)

**Principle** (real TeX). A binding that stands in for a latex.ltx macro runs that macro's hooks at latex.ltx's point,
with the state latex.ltx has there; whether a hook holds code is lthooks' own storage (`\hook_if_empty:nTF`,
latex.ltx:6436), read, not expanded. Related: #1008 (QA47A, the `cmd/<name>/<hook>` hooks: the same family), #217 (the
document hooks inline in the galley), #314 (`\shipout` in place).
**Perl.** `\AddToHook` is a no-op (latex_base.pool.ltxml), etoolbox's `\AfterEndDocument` queues code nothing reads and
atveryend's commands are no-ops: every hook's code is dropped.
**Rust.** With the kernel's hooks loaded: `\end{document}` runs `env/document/end` before `\enddocument` (:15386);
`\begin{verbatim}`/`{verbatim*}` run `env/<name>/begin|end` (no DefEnvironment fires them; etoolbox's
`\AtBeginEnvironment{verbatim}` joins the same hook, its private store gone); `\label` runs
`\UseHookWithArguments{label}{1}{#1}` in a group (:14943), with the `\@currentcounter` `\refstepcounter` sets (a local
`\let`, none for `*`, :14958-14962; Perl's `RefStepCounter`, Package.pm:755-779, sets only `current_counter`;
unbtex-example's `\cref@updatelabeldata{\@currentcounter}`, unbtex.cls:485-493, read it empty: a Fatal pushback loop);
`\include` names the file current and runs `include/before`,
`include/<name>/before`, `/end`, `/after`, and `include/excluded` for a file `\includeonly` leaves out (:9609-9627).
The kernel's abstract, a binding macro, runs `env/abstract/begin` inside the abstract's group before `\abstract`
(:15354-15362) — ahead of the abstract's name and the class's replayed begin code, what it typesets heading the body —
and `env/abstract/end` before `\end{abstract}` (:15386); an abstract that is a constructor environment runs both from
its constructor only. `\selectfont` runs `\UseHook{selectfont}` before `\size@update` (:12580), only when the hook
holds code (scrartcl.cls:2673's `\par@update`, everysel.sty:49), read from the hook's slots it names once;
`file/<name>/before|after` are plain `\UseHook`s at every `\input` and load (:19668-19673), and a load's `after` pair
runs before its `\AtEndOfPackage`/`\AtEndOfClass` code and `package/<name>/after` (:18865-18869).
`\begin` defines `\@currenvir` (`verbatim*` its own name) before `env/<name>/begin` (:15350-15352), so the verbatim
constructor runs its begin hooks, the kernel's and etoolbox's `@atbegin` store, after it. `enddocument/afterlastpage`, `/afteraux` and
`/end` (:15262-15277) follow the last page, where pdflatex prints nothing they typeset: the document's own code
(lthooks' top-level slot) runs for its side effects in a dropped box, while a package's code there keeps the `.aux` and
the page model LaTeXML has not (acro's property lists, 2502.06996: a Fatal IfLimit; pageslts' numbering check: a false
Warning; pbalance) and does not run; `enddocument/info` (the kernel's file list and rerun warnings) does not run.
etoolbox's `\AfterEndDocument` adds to `enddocument/end`, atveryend's commands to their hooks as atveryend.sty v1.12. A
label hook's code that prints nothing leaves no box (2501.00173: `\label{…}` + `\ ` before a list opened an empty
paragraph). The storage read (`hook_has_code`: the labelled-code prop, the top-level and next-use slots) replaces an
expansion that cost 0.2-0.4M instructions at every `\label` and environment end; `\include`'s hooks pass over an empty
hook (`\lx@usehook`, `\lx@useonetimehook`: a `\UseHook` cost 0.7M, a `\UseOneTimeHook` 3M in lthooks' preamble mode,
where each use rebuilds its hook; the package, class and file hooks of every load take the same path), an empty one-time
hook only marking itself used (`\__hook_use_once_set:n`; the clear
code lthooks leaves in an undeclared hook's next slot is not kept, which only `\IfHookEmptyTF` on that used hook would
see). The kernel's first aid for cleveref.sty (latex2e-first-aid-for-external-files.ltx:193-270, `package/cleveref/after`
labelled `firstaid`) is not registered under cleveref's binding, which replaces the code it repairs (DG 2026-11-14):
its `label` hook code cost 3.5M instructions a `\label`. It is removed only where the chunk is registered
(`hook_has_labelled_code`; the chunk dates from 2024-03-22, firstaid changes.txt), as lthooks warns "Cannot remove
chunk" for a missing one. Its repair of the raw file's amsmath code, which the binding does read (:257-270, a
`begindocument` chunk under `\IfPackageAtLeastT{amsmath}{2025-05-18}`: cleveref.sty:2620, :2623), is added back with
it: without it an explicit `\ltx@label{l4b}` took `l` as the key and printed "4b" (2605.07565: 3 Double subscript;
guard `perfect_kernel_batchregbind::cleveref_ltx_label_braces_its_key_under_amsmath`), for the release it repairs
only (:194 `\FirstAidNeededT`, `\ver@cleveref.sty` v0.21.4). An older copy's `\ltx@label` (v0.19, 2508.14614) is undone
by amsmath's `\AddToHook{begindocument/end}{\let\ltx@label\label}` (amsmath.sty:1228), which the binding now runs at
`begindocument/end`, after the copy's `begindocument` code, as there (it ran in `begindocument`, before it; guard
`perfect_kernel_batchregbind::amsmath_ltx_label_is_label_after_the_begin_document_code`). **Open** (post-merge, catalog): a note steps its counter after its text is digested
and an align or gather row after its cells (Perl's order), so a label hook there reads the enclosing counter (or, in an
align's later row, the previous row's step) where
latex.ltx's `\@footnotetext` and `\@mpfootnotetext` define it (:17664, :16350) and amsmath has stepped `equation`
(`label_hook_currentcounter_stepped_after_the_body_red`); `\label`'s hook runs after the label is recorded, where
latex.ltx runs it before the `.aux` write, so a hook's `\@currentlabel` does not reach `\ref`
(`label_hook_sets_the_reference_text_red`); a DefEnvironment runs its begin hooks before its `\@currenvir` (Perl
Package.pm:1920-1927; `environment_begin_hook_reads_its_environment_red`: moving it alone raised 2001.02707's
`\AtBeginEnvironment{defn}{\begin{samepage}}` from 29 to 54 errors, so the end side moves with it); no `\begin` path
sets `\@currenvline` (`currenvline_is_never_set_red`); a
document's `\AtEndAfterFileList` is lost (`enddocument_info_hook_red`); `\emph` and the other font constructors call no
`\selectfont`, so its hook does not run there (`selectfont_hook_on_emph_red`, the macro faces); the kernel abstract
sets no class abstract font, so a begin hook's `\large` is not undone by article's `\small`
(`abstract_begin_hook_size_under_the_class_small_red`), and what amsart's begin hook typesets before an abstract
ahead of `\maketitle` stays in the abstract, where pdflatex prints it before the title
(`amsart_abstract_begin_hook_text_before_the_title_red`). **Guard**:
`perfect_kernel_batchqa47a::batchqa47a_command_hook_rows` (rows `enddocument_hooks_run`,
`enddocument_hook_commands_run`, `verbatim_env_hooks_run`, `verbatim_begin_hook_reads_its_environment`,
`label_hook_runs`, `include_hooks_run`, `label_hook_opens_no_paragraph`, `cleveref_firstaid_not_registered`,
`cleveref_firstaid_absent_removes_nothing`, `file_hooks_run_at_every_input`, `file_hooks_order_around_a_package`,
`abstract_env_hooks_run`, `selectfont_hook_runs`, `abstract_end_hook_once_in_a_constructor_abstract`,
`abstract_begin_hook_runs_before_the_name`, `label_hook_reads_currentcounter`).

### 1045. Every box's width, height and depth are the CSS custom properties `--ltx-box-width`, `--ltx-box-height`, `--ltx-box-depth` (Perl: `style="width:…;height:…;vertical-align:…"`, or dropped)

Principle: the HTML/CSS cascade — a presentational value the stylesheet applies, so one rule can override or reuse
it. Related: #20 (colour), #887 (`--ltx-panel-*`), #250 (a section lifted out of a box).

**Perl** writes a Positionable element's `width` as `style="width:<w>"` (LaTeXML-common.xsl `base-styling`), and a
sectioning unit set inside a minipage or a `\parbox` (a real section carrying the box's class, #250; a framed box's
`inline-sectional-block`) loses the box's width: no `Sectional.attributes` admits `width` (LaTeXML-structure.rnc),
and Perl's `<sectional-block class="ltx_minipage">` drops it too (TeX_Box.pool.ltxml `insertBlock`).

**Rust** (QAB57; BM Q2.4 asked for the box's "attributes and classes"; DG 2026-11-14: a dedicated custom property, and
"Move them all now"). One name for every box:
- the lifted unit: `insert_block_as` (`carry_box_width`, block_insertion.rs) writes the box's width as
  `--ltx-box-width:<w>` at the head of its `cssstyle`, so a `width:` the box's own style sets follows it (varwidth's
  `--ltx-box-width:63.4pt;width:max-content;max-width:227.6pt`); a unit lifted through nested boxes keeps the first,
  innermost box's width, the one pdflatex sets it in (a `\section` in a minipage{3cm} inside a minipage{8cm}: 85.4pt);
- every other box: `base-styling` writes `--ltx-box-width:<w>` for an LaTeXML element's `width` (minipage and
  `\parbox` `inline-block`/`inline-logical-block`, the panel `figure` and `p` a minipage becomes, `\makebox`'s `text`,
  a transformed box's outer, a wrapfigure, a `tabular`/`td` width, an `ltx:picture` rendered as an image or as its TeX
  through `add_attributes`), and `add_transformable_attributes` for the inner box's `innerwidth`. The XML keeps
  `width` as Perl writes it; of our stylesheets only the XHTML ones read it (neither the JATS nor the TEI one does).
- every box's height and depth (QAB57d; DG 2026-11-14: "also adding --ltx-box-height and --ltx-box-depth"):
  `base-styling` writes TeX's own values, `--ltx-box-height:<h>` (above the baseline) and `--ltx-box-depth:<d>` (below),
  each only where the attribute is set (a `\raisebox{y}[h][d]`'s `text`, a rotated or scaled box's outer
  `inline-block`), where Perl writes `height:<h+d>` (or `<h>`) and, without a `yoffset`,
  `vertical-align:<-d>`. A `\raisebox{y}[h][d]` keeps its `position:relative; bottom:<y>`; a plain `\raisebox{y}` its
  `vertical-align:<y>`. `innerheight`/`innerdepth` stay unwritten, as in Perl.
- Not boxes, so `width:`/`height:` stay: `ltx:rule` (its ink, as an image's size) and MathML's `mspace`/`mpadded`
  (MathML's own attributes). Graphics (`imagewidth`), a picture drawn as SVG, and `--ltx-panel-width` never reach `base-styling`'s
  width.

LaTeXML.css: `:where([style*="--ltx-box-width:"]:not([style^="width:"], [style*=";width:"], [style*="; width:"])) {
width: var(--ltx-box-width, auto) !important }`. Important and of zero specificity, it ranks where the inline `width:`
ranked: over every normal rule (`.ltx_tabular .ltx_tabular`'s 100 %, `.ltx_framed_verbatim`'s fit-content), under
every other `!important` one. It is off where the element's own style sets a `width:` (varwidth's `max-content`,
#1014; a `\text` minipage's, batch76a). ar5iv-css carries the same rule un-layered, so that its layered rules rank under
it as under the inline style, and caps a lifted section at its container
(`:is(section, .ltx_inline-sectional-block)[style*="--ltx-box-width:"] { max-width: 100% }`, as its `.ltx_minipage`).
The height and depth, one rule per case, as the custom properties inherit and a `var()` fallback cannot test that a
box's own style sets one (a height-only box inside a box with a depth would add the outer depth):
`height: var(--ltx-box-height)` where the style sets `--ltx-box-height:`, `height: calc(var(--ltx-box-height) +
var(--ltx-box-depth))` where it sets both, and `vertical-align: calc(-1 * var(--ltx-box-depth))` where it sets
`--ltx-box-depth:`; each `!important` in `:where()` and off where the box's own style sets that property (an author's
`height:`; for the depth a `vertical-align:` or the `; bottom:` of a `yoffset` shift, Perl's `@depth and not(@yoffset)`).
ar5iv-css carries the three un-layered beside the width's.
A stylesheet overrides one box's width with `.sel { --ltx-box-width: <w> !important }` or `.sel { width: <w>
!important }`, reuses it (`width: min(var(--ltx-box-width), 100%) !important`), and switches every box width off with
`:where([style*="--ltx-box-width:"]) { --ltx-box-width: initial !important }`; the same for the height
(`--ltx-box-height`, `height:`). Every box's height is switched off with `:where([style*="--ltx-box-height:"]) {
--ltx-box-height: initial !important }` (its depth's drop kept) and every depth set to zero with
`:where([style*="--ltx-box-depth:"]) { --ltx-box-depth: 0pt !important }` (its height then h): `initial` on the
depth would void the h+d sum as well.

Cost: a box's width, height and depth now need LaTeXML.css or ar5iv-css. It is lost under `--nodefaultresources` without a stylesheet
carrying the rule, in a reader that does not apply our CSS, and in an EPUB reader without `var()` or `:where()` (the
EPUB ships LaTeXML.css).

Measured (QAB57c): each page of the 63 arXiv papers whose HTML moved (QAB57b A/B), rendered once with inline
`width:` and once with the property under the same stylesheet, has every body element's box identical in Chrome at
1280 and 375 px and in Firefox at 1280 px, under LaTeXML.css and under ar5iv.css; in Firefox at 375 px too, except
six `∙` glyph boxes in 2512.16386's bibliography under ar5iv.css, 2 px shorter, nothing moved. Screenshot ink is
identical where it was compared (every page in Chrome; in Firefox only the pages short enough to shoot). The repro
shapes (side-by-side, figure, nested and over-wide minipages, `\parbox` in text, `p{}` cells, `tabular*`,
`\makebox`, scaled/resized/rotated boxes, varwidth, wrapfigure, framed verbatim, lifted sections) were measured so on
QAB57b; on QAB57c the varwidth section is 131 px wide in Chrome as before QAB57 (QAB57b: 85 px, its heading wrapped)
and the nested one 114 px (85.4pt; QAB57b: 303 px). Not reached, as before QAB57: a framed box holding a section
draws its frame as an empty 2 px box above it (RED `block-model/framed_box_section_frame_collapses_red`, post-merge).
Measured (QAB57d): of 93 arXiv papers (QAB57b's 63 and the 30 heaviest in `\raisebox`, `\smash`, `\parbox[…][h]` of
a census sample; 92 converted, 2609.23556 crashes on both binaries) the HTML of 52 moved, and only in these
declarations (`kit/html_style_diff.py --derive-box`: every other declaration and byte unchanged). Each of the 52 has
every body element's box identical, base against candidate, in Chrome and Firefox at 1280 and 375 px under LaTeXML.css
and under ar5iv.css (one Chrome 375 px difference in 1505.06377's equation cell, gone on its rerun); screenshot ink is
identical where shot, but for 2604.04765 in Chrome at 375 px under ar5iv.css, whose base differs from itself by the
same 22,167 px. So are the repro's and hand-built depth-only, author-`height:`, nested and author-`vertical-align:`
boxes, and the two switch-off recipes render as the declarations they stand for. Not reached, as in Perl: a
`\parbox[t][3cm]` or `minipage[t][2cm]` carries no height to write (RED `block-model/parbox_and_minipage_height_dropped_red`,
post-merge).
Guards
`perfect_kernel_batchqab57::section_in_a_box_keeps_the_box_width` (repros `block-model/section_in_a_box_keeps_the_box_width`,
`section_in_varwidth_keeps_its_own_width`, `section_in_nested_boxes_keeps_the_inner_width`,
`box_widths_ride_the_custom_property`), `perfect_kernel_batchqab57::box_heights_ride_the_custom_properties` (repro
`block-model/box_heights_ride_the_custom_properties`).

### 1046. latexml.sty's `pdfoutput`/`nopdfoutput` options set the output mode over the guess (Perl: no such options)

Principle: Perl's own intent for latexml.sty — its options are the author's switches over how LaTeXML processes the
document, as its X/noX pairs are. Related: #285, #537 (the presented `\pdfoutput` and its cues), #204 (`\ifpdf`).

We present `\pdfoutput=1` unless the source's cues say latex+dvips (#285, #537); Perl presents 0. BM (Q4.2): presenting
a mode "may often be desirable … And/Or possibly that should be an additional latexml.sty switch". **Rust** (QAB57, DG
2026-11-14): latexml.sty's options `pdfoutput` (1, pdflatex) and `nopdfoutput` (0, latex+dvips) — latexml.sty's X/noX
pairs, named for the register they set — assign `\pdfoutput` globally and record `PDFOUTPUT_OPTION`, which
`establish_pdf_output_mode` (core_interface.rs) takes over every cue when the option was preloaded
(`--preload=[nopdfoutput]latexml.sty`; under ar5iv `--preload=[nopdfoutput]ar5iv.sty`, which passes it on). Drivers
read `\pdfoutput` as they load, so the option comes first in the preamble: given after graphicx, graphicx keeps the
driver it chose, as TeX's load order decides. Under a preload of latexml.sty a document's own
`\usepackage[nopdfoutput]{latexml}` is a repeat load whose options are dropped, as for every latexml.sty option (RED
`backend-persona/latexml_option_after_ar5iv_preload_red`, post-merge). Default output unchanged. Perl patch prepared
(`bruce_qa/patches/qa64.patch`: the two options, and TeX's latexml.sty declaring them). Guard
`perfect_kernel_batchqab57::latexml_pdfoutput_options_override_the_mode`.
**Addendum (HOOKINIT): lthooks' document mode.** latex.ltx:15356-15361 `\@execute@begin@hook{document}` runs
`\@expl@@@initialize@all@@` (`\__hook_initialize_all:`, :5854) between `env/document/before` and `/begin`: every declared
hook's code is built once, `\__hook_update_hook_code:n` rebuilds a hook at each later add, and
`\__hook_post_initialization_defs:` (:6380) makes `\hook_use:n` the expandable `\__hook_use_initialized:n` (:6351).
LaTeXML's `\begin{document}` (sect01.rs, both the constructor and a renewed `document`) runs it there once, read from
`\__hook_update_hook_code:n` still being `\use_none:n` (:5853/:5856, every lthooks since 2020-10-01), and `\document`'s
`\@kernel@after@begindocument@before` step `\let`s `env/document/begin`'s code to `\@empty` (:9532-9535). Perl's
`\begin{document}` runs neither and stays in preamble mode: a body `\edef\x{\UseHook{h}}` holds `\hook_use:n {h}`
where pdflatex's holds the code (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1249), and each body `\UseHook` of a hook with code rebuilt it.
Cost: a body add now rebuilds its hook, as pdflatex does, so acro papers (an `enddocument` add per acronym use,
acro.sty:3917) cost +0.6…+5.6 % instructions (2502.06996 +5.65 %, 2205.14872 +1.4 %, 2008.04164 +0.6 %) and others
run faster (2307.05602 −7.7 %, 2605.14422 −10 %; median −6.6 % over 56 papers); 300 body adds to one hook take
pdflatex 5.25G instructions, ours 7.81G (accepted as TeX's own cost, DG 2026-11-14).
**Guard**: `perfect_kernel_batchqa47a::batchqa47a_command_hook_rows` (rows `use_hook_expands_in_the_body`,
`hook_code_added_in_the_body_runs`, `hooks_initialize_once_on_an_older_lthooks`); RED catalog
`show_hook_needs_showstream_red` (`\ShowHook` needs pdfTeX's `\showstream`, post-merge),
`file_hooks_run_at_every_input_red` (content.rs runs `file/<name>/before|after` as one-time hooks, latex.ltx:19669/19672
a plain `\UseHook`; post-merge).

### 1051. A line of the author block under the name is a contact of class `ltx_author_line` (issue #783)

**Principle.** The PDF prints `\author{name\\school\\dept}`'s lines centred under the name (article.cls:246-248, `\@maketitle`'s
`tabular[t]{c}`; book.cls and report.cls the same); where a contact prints is a fact of that contact, so it goes on the contact, in Perl's own keyvals
(`\lx@add@affiliation[…]`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:645). Related: #156 (a `\thanks` is a marked note, untouched), #52
(the author block's reading), #412 (a creator laid out by its role's CSS).
**Perl.** Each `\\` line is `\lx@add@affiliation{line}` (Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:722-726), and since #2767 (`23f3acfa`)
LaTeXML.css shows every author's contacts only in a hover pop-up behind a blue star unless the document is
`ltx_authors_multiline` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1268); the XML cannot tell the line from a setter's `\affiliation{}`.
**Rust.** A contact the emitter writes from the block's own text, where the last line break or column before it is a
line break and no note holds it (`emit.rs` `on_an_author_line`; a printed line holds across its text and its word
"and", and resets only at `\\`, an `\and` command, a column break such as `\alignauthor` — 1602.06359, 2605.17295 — or
one of the reading's names, whose line prints what follows it beside the name: IEEE's grades on a names line continued
past `\\`, 2408.01902, 2408.02464),
carries `class=ltx_author_line`; so does an e-mail the Kind step splits out of such a line (`kind_entry_addresses`,
the class handed to it by the emitter as `\lx@frontmatter@itemkinded`'s e-mail keys, never read back) and each `\\`
line of Perl's split when the reading declines (`fallback.rs`; its address line's e-mail gets none,
`author_lines_783_declined_email_red.tex`). A setter's contact (REVTeX `\affiliation`, `\email`) and a note get none; `\\`
lines inside a per-author class's own `\author{Name\\line}` (REVTeX, amsart) are marked too. A line printed once under
several names (`\author{Ann, Bob, Cy \\ CMU}`) is repeated under each name, each creator keeping its own contacts
(DG 2026-11-14; 2104.07210). LaTeXML.css (local delta after the multiline rules): outside `ltx_authors_multiline`, an
author whose contacts are all such lines or notes is an `inline-block` card with the lines under the name, their labels
hidden; a note contact (`\footnote` in `\author` is `\thanks`, article.cls:241, Perl's role=note contact,
Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:331) keeps the star and shows on hover in the card's flow, so two notes, or a note and the
lines, never cover one another (1112.2930, math0111266), and with no note there is no star; an author
with any other contact keeps the pop-up, its labels shown; a marked `\thanks` note shows under the name, with no mark
unless shared, and an unmarked one keeps its mark and pop-up (#1052). Chrome and
Firefox at 1280/375 px. ar5iv.css already shows every
author's contacts (`css/ar5iv.css:920`, `:940` at ar5iv-css `6dc3e97`; it does not load LaTeXML.css): no change. Offered upstream. **Guards**:
`06_cluster_frontmatter::frontmatter_author_lines_783` (repros `sectioning-frontmatter/author_lines_783_*.tex`),
`xslt::witnessed_css_delta::author_line_delta_stays_present`, `cluster_cli::browser_render_author_lines` (local).

### 1052. A note several authors share prints once: the first copy in full, each other copy a mark linked to it (DG 2026-11-16, rulings 1-2)

**Rule.** "One copy" is a page rule: the XML keeps a full copy of a shared author note on every carrier, each with its
`mark` (Perl's model: `relocateAnnotations`, Base_Utility.pool.ltxml:895-901, and `relocateFootnote`,
latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:503-527, both clone), and the HTML prints it once. Marks follow placement: a note of one
author sits under the name with no mark; a shared note carries its mark on every name and at its head, in the side
margin where there is one; margin notes never overlap. An UNMARKED note is no one author's (review SHREND B1): the PDF
prints it with no mark as a footnote of the paper — IEEEtran's `\maketitle` sets `\let\@makefnmark\relax`
(IEEEtran.cls:4758), so its `\thanks` is the funding or "manuscript received" note — so it never sits under a name: the
margin where there is one, else in flow in the block. Once every note the PDF marks carries `mark` (the kernel
`\thanks` its `\@fnsymbol`, a legend its symbol), the rule is complete; until then a markless kernel `\thanks` goes to
the margin, as in ar5iv-css 0.9.3.
**Perl.** Every copy renders in full with its own mark (`LaTeXML-meta-xhtml.xsl`'s note template), so a note shared by
n authors prints n times.
**Rust.** `LaTeXML-meta-xhtml.xsl` keys `ltx:creator[@role='author']/ltx:note` with a non-empty `@mark` and text —
not an editor's note, which never renders (its first copy would leave the authors' marks linking to no element), not
an image-only note (two would merge, the second image lost), not Perl's leftover `role="footnotemark"` notes, which are
no copies — by the creator's parent block, `@role`, `@mark` and `normalize-space(.)` (`xsl:key
f:shared-creator-note`). The first copy of a group of two or more renders in full with class
`ltx_note_shared`; each later copy is `span.ltx_note.ltx_role_footnotemark.ltx_note_shared` holding only its mark,
linked to the first copy's id. `LaTeXML-structure-xhtml.xsl` puts every marked note in `span.ltx_annotated_personname`
after the name, in document order with an ORCID badge, and there the name drops its trailing newline, so no line breaks
between a name and its mark; unmarked notes (an empty `@mark` too) and the footnotemark leftovers follow the name as
before. LaTeXML.css (local delta after the ORCID wrapper rules): a name with notes is set as text; where the author's
lines show under the name (#1051's card, `ltx_authors_multiline`) its marked notes show there, one author's with no
mark, a shared one headed by its mark; an unmarked note, and every note elsewhere, keeps its mark and pop-up.
ar5iv-css (`fix/shared-notes`): a marked note of one author on a row under the name with no mark; a shared note's marks
shown, its body in the side margin on wide screens; an unmarked note's body in the same margin, with no mark. Each
margin note is placed under the one before by CSS anchor positioning (the last earlier box of the same anchor name), so
none overlaps whatever its height. Phones, and browsers without anchor positioning, keep a shared note in flow under its
first author and an unmarked one after its author's lines, start-aligned as a note. A block with a note under a name
aligns its names on one baseline, as the PDF's top-aligned author tabulars do. It replaces 0.9.3's fixed 10rem slots,
which overlapped (1706.03762).
**Witnesses.** 2606.00446 (authblk `\affil[*]`: two copies, one printed); 2407.07614 (the legend line's `*` and `+`,
three copies each, one printed each; `†` one author's, under the name); 2606.00397 (ieeeconf: `\maketitle` empties `\thefootnote`, ieeeconf.cls:3592, so no `\thanks` gets an automatic
mark; the correspondence note's `*` is the authors' own text on the name and the note, so it is Murali Babu's marked
note once SHMARK lifts that typed `*`, and a plain unmarked `\thanks` stays in the margin); 1510.02728 (IEEEtran: the
unmarked Asilomar/NSF note in the margin, not under Azadeh Vosoughi's name, where it read as her affiliation);
1706.03762 (the tall shared note, in the margin; Chrome and Firefox at 1800 and 375 px). **Guards**:
`integration::a_shared_author_note_prints_once_and_its_repeats_are_linked_marks` (latexml_post),
`xslt::witnessed_css_delta::shared_author_note_delta_stays_present`,
`cluster_cli::browser_render_author_lines::a_shared_note_prints_once_under_its_first_author` (local).

Perl simplification of it, so each is a divergence whose ruler is the TeX source (OD rationalization ruling 7: TEX
entries stay, as family tables with an upstream column). The entry keeps its rule, witnesses and
guards; the table names the Perl reference it departs from and the TeX or package source that decides, as the entry
cites them (`—`: the entry cites none). Kinds: **kernel**, a kernel definition or macro as latex.ltx has it;
**binding**, a binding aligned to its real package's source; **scanning**, argument and token scanning as tex.web does
it. Upstream: each row is a candidate Perl patch; none is filed yet (the #403 row, a
